texts.gen.5.26: And Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and two years, and begat sons and daughters:
texts.gen.5.27: And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.28: And Lamech lived a hundred eighty and two years; and begat a son:
texts.gen.5.29: And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD hath cursed.
texts.gen.5.30: And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters:
texts.gen.5.31: And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy and seven years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.32: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
texts.gen.6.1: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
texts.gen.6.2: That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all whom they chose.
texts.gen.6.3: And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.
texts.gen.6.4: There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in to the daughters of men, and they bore children to them: the same became mighty men, who were of old, men of renown.
texts.gen.6.5: And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
texts.gen.6.6: And the LORD repented that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
texts.gen.6.7: And the LORD said, I will destroy man whom I have created, from the face of the earth, both man and beast, and the creeping animal, and the fowls of the air; for I repent that I have made them.
texts.gen.6.8: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
texts.gen.6.9: These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man, and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
texts.gen.6.10: And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
texts.gen.6.11: The earth also was corrupt before God; and the earth was filled with violence.
texts.gen.6.12: And God looked upon the earth, and behold, it was corrupt: for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.
texts.gen.6.13: And God said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them: and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
texts.gen.6.14: Make thee an ark of gopher-wood: rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
texts.gen.6.15: And this is the fashion in which thou shalt make it: the length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
texts.gen.6.16: A window shalt thou make to the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in its side: with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
texts.gen.6.17: And behold, I, even I do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, in which is the breath of life, from under heaven: and every thing that is on the earth shall die.
texts.gen.6.18: But with thee will I establish my covenant: and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee.
texts.gen.6.19: And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee: they shall be male and female.
texts.gen.6.20: Of fowls after their kind, and of cattle after their kind, of every creeping animal of the earth after its kind, two of every sort shall come to thee, to keep them alive.
texts.gen.6.21: And take thou to thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
texts.gen.6.22: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
texts.gen.7.1: And the LORD said to Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark: for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
texts.gen.7.2: Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens, the male and his female: and of beasts that are not clean by two, the male and his female.
texts.gen.7.3: Of fowls of the air also by sevens, the male and the female; to keep seed alive on the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.7.4: For yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights: and every living substance that I have made will I destroy from the face of the earth.
texts.gen.7.5: And Noah did according to all that the LORD commanded him.
texts.gen.7.6: And Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was on the earth.
texts.gen.7.7: And Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
texts.gen.7.8: Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean, and of fowls, and of every animal that creepeth upon the earth;
texts.gen.7.9: There went in two and two to Noah into the ark, the male and the female, as God had commanded Noah.
texts.gen.7.10: And it came to pass after seven days, that the waters of the flood were upon the earth.
texts.gen.7.11: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
texts.gen.7.12: And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
texts.gen.7.13: In the same day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark.
texts.gen.7.14: They, and every beast after his kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth after his kind, and every fowl after his kind, every bird of every sort.
texts.gen.7.15: And they went in to Noah into the ark, two and two of all flesh, in which is the breath of life.
texts.gen.7.16: And they that entered, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the LORD shut him in.
texts.gen.7.17: And the flood was forty days upon the earth: and the waters increased, and bore up the ark, and it was lifted above the earth.
texts.gen.7.18: And the waters prevailed, and were increased greatly upon the earth: and the ark moved upon the face of the waters.
texts.gen.7.19: And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills that were under the whole heaven were covered.
texts.gen.7.20: Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail: and the mountains were covered.
texts.gen.7.21: And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:
texts.gen.7.22: All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was on the dry land, died.
texts.gen.7.23: And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping animals, and the fowl of heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth; and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.
texts.gen.7.24: And the waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.
texts.gen.8.1: And God remembered Noah, and every living animal, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters were checked.
texts.gen.8.2: The fountains also of the deep, and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained;
texts.gen.8.3: And the waters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters were abated.
texts.gen.8.4: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
texts.gen.8.5: And the waters decreased continually, till the tenth month: in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, were the tops of the mountains seen.
texts.gen.8.6: And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made:
texts.gen.8.7: And he sent forth a raven, which went forth to and fro, till the waters were dried from off the earth.
texts.gen.8.8: Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground;
texts.gen.8.9: But the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him into the ark; for the waters were on the face of the whole earth. Then he put forth his hand, and took her, and pulled her in to him into the ark.
texts.gen.8.10: And he stayed yet other seven days, and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark;
texts.gen.8.11: And the dove came in to him in the evening, and lo, in her mouth was an olive-leaf plucked off: So Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
texts.gen.8.12: And he stayed yet other seven days, and sent forth the dove; which returned not again to him any more.
texts.gen.8.13: And it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was dry.
texts.gen.8.14: And in the second month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, was the earth dried.
texts.gen.8.15: And God spoke to Noah, saying,
texts.gen.8.16: Go forth from the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons' wives with thee.
texts.gen.8.17: Bring forth with thee every living animal that is with thee, of all flesh, of fowl, and of cattle, and of every creeping animal that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly on the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.
texts.gen.8.18: And Noah went forth, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him:
texts.gen.8.19: Every beast, every creeping animal, and every fowl, and whatsoever creepeth upon the earth, after their kinds, went out of the ark.
texts.gen.8.20: And Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and offered burnt-offerings on the altar.
texts.gen.8.21: And the LORD smelled a sweet savor; and the LORD said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake; for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth: neither will I again smite any more every living animal as I have done.
texts.gen.8.22: While the earth remaineth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
texts.gen.9.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.
texts.gen.9.2: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth on the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.
texts.gen.9.3: Every moving thing that liveth shall be food for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things:
texts.gen.9.4: But flesh with the life of it, which is its blood, shall ye not eat.
texts.gen.9.5: And surely your blood of your lives will I require: at the hand of every beast will I require it: and at the hand of man, at the hand of every man's brother will I require the life of man.
texts.gen.9.6: Whoever sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
texts.gen.9.7: And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply, bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
texts.gen.9.8: And God spoke to Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,
texts.gen.9.9: And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you;
texts.gen.9.10: And with every living creature that is with you, of the fowl, of the cattle, and of every beast of the earth with you, from all that go out of the ark, to every beast of the earth.
texts.gen.9.11: And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
texts.gen.9.12: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations.
texts.gen.9.13: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
texts.gen.9.14: And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud:
texts.gen.9.15: And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
texts.gen.9.16: And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.
texts.gen.9.17: And God said to Noah, This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.
texts.gen.9.18: And the sons of Noah that went forth from the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham was the father of Canaan.
texts.gen.9.19: These three were the sons of Noah: and from them was the whole earth overspread.
texts.gen.9.20: And Noah began to be a husbandman, and he planted a vineyard:
texts.gen.9.21: And he drank the wine, and was drunken, and he was uncovered within his tent.
texts.gen.9.22: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.
texts.gen.9.23: And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father: and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness.
texts.gen.9.24: And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done to him.
texts.gen.9.25: And he said, Cursed be Canaan, a servant of servants shall he be to his brethren.
texts.gen.9.26: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.
texts.gen.9.27: God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.
texts.gen.9.28: And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
texts.gen.9.29: And all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years: and he died.
texts.gen.10.1: Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah; Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and to them were sons born after the flood.
texts.gen.10.2: The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
texts.gen.10.3: And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
texts.gen.10.4: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
texts.gen.10.5: By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
texts.gen.10.6: And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
texts.gen.10.7: And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha; and the sons of Raamah, Sheba, and Dedan.
texts.gen.10.8: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
texts.gen.10.9: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD.
texts.gen.10.10: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
texts.gen.10.11: Out of that land went forth Ashur, and built Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah,
texts.gen.10.12: And Resen between Nineveh and Calah: the same is a great city.
texts.gen.10.13: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
texts.gen.10.14: And Pathrusim, and Casluhim, (out of whom came Philistim,) and Caphtorim.
texts.gen.10.15: And Canaan begat Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
texts.gen.10.16: And the Jebusite, and the Emorite, and the Girgasite,
texts.gen.10.17: And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
texts.gen.10.18: And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite: and afterward were the families of the Canaanites dispersed.
texts.gen.10.19: And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon, as thou comest to Gerar, to Gaza; as thou goest to Sodom and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, even to Lashah.
texts.gen.10.20: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their countries, and in their nations.
texts.gen.10.21: To Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to him were children born.
texts.gen.10.22: The children of Shem; Elam, and Ashur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
texts.gen.10.23: And the children of Aram; Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
texts.gen.10.24: And Arphaxad begat Salah; and Salah begat Eber.
texts.gen.10.25: And to Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg, for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother's name was Joktan.
texts.gen.10.26: And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
texts.gen.10.27: And Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah.
texts.gen.10.28: And Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
texts.gen.10.29: And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sons of Joktan.
texts.gen.10.30: And their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou goest to Sephar, a mount of the east.
texts.gen.10.31: These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.
texts.gen.10.32: These are the families of the sons of Noah after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.
texts.gen.11.1: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.
texts.gen.11.2: And it came to pass as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they dwelt there.
texts.gen.11.3: And they said one to another, come, let us make brick, and burn them thoroughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for mortar.
texts.gen.11.4: And they said, come, let us build us a city, and a tower, whose top may reach to heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we should be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
texts.gen.11.5: And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men were building.
texts.gen.11.6: And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.
texts.gen.11.7: Come, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech.
texts.gen.11.8: So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.
texts.gen.11.9: Therefore is the name of it called Babel, because the LORD there confounded the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.11.10: These are the generations of Shem: Shem was a hundred years old, and begat Arphaxad two years after the flood:
texts.gen.11.11: And Shem lived after he begat Arphaxad five hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.12: And Arphaxad lived five and thirty years, and begat Salah.
texts.gen.11.13: And Arphaxad lived after he begat Salah four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.14: And Salah lived thirty years, and begat Eber:
texts.gen.11.15: And Salah lived after he begat Eber four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.16: And Eber lived four and thirty years, and begat Peleg:
texts.gen.11.17: And Eber lived after he begat Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.18: And Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu:
texts.gen.11.19: And Peleg lived after he begat Reu two hundred and nine years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.20: And Reu lived two and thirty years, and begat Serug.
texts.gen.11.21: And Reu lived after he begat Serug two hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.22: And Serug lived thirty years, and begat Nahor:
texts.gen.11.23: And Serug lived after he begat Nahor two hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.24: And Nahor lived nine and twenty years, and begat Terah.
texts.gen.11.25: And Nahor lived after he begat Terah a hundred and nineteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.26: And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
texts.gen.11.27: Now these are the generations of Terah: Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran: and Haran begat Lot.
texts.gen.11.28: And Haran died before his father Terah, in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldees.
texts.gen.11.29: And Abram and Nahor took them wives: the name of Abram's wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor's wife Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.
texts.gen.11.30: But Sarai was barren; she had no child.
texts.gen.11.31: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran his son's son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram's wife; and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan; and they came to Haran, and dwelt there.
texts.gen.11.32: And the days of Terah were two hundred and five years: and Terah died in Haran.
texts.gen.12.1: Now the LORD had said to Abram, Depart from thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, to a land that I will show thee:
texts.gen.12.2: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
texts.gen.12.3: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
texts.gen.12.4: So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken to him, and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed from Haran.
texts.gen.12.5: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went to go forth into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came.
texts.gen.12.6: And Abram passed through the land to the place of Sichem, to the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land.
texts.gen.12.7: And the LORD appeared to Abram, and said, To thy seed will I give this land: and there he erected an altar to the LORD, who appeared to him.
texts.gen.12.8: And he removed from thence to a mountain on the east of Beth-el, and pitched his tent, having Beth-el on the west, and Hai on the east: and there he erected an altar to the LORD, and called upon the name of the LORD.
texts.gen.12.9: And Abram journeyed, going on still towards the south.
texts.gen.12.10: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to dwell there; for the famine was grievous in the land.
texts.gen.12.11: And it came to pass, when he had come near to enter into Egypt, that he said to Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon:
texts.gen.12.12: Therefore it will come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they will say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive.
texts.gen.12.13: Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.
texts.gen.12.14: And it came to pass, that when Abram had come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair.
texts.gen.12.15: The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
texts.gen.12.16: And he treated Abram well for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he-asses, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and she-asses, and camels.
texts.gen.12.17: And the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues, because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
texts.gen.12.18: And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done to me? why didst thou not tell me that she is thy wife?
texts.gen.12.19: Why saidst thou, She is my sister? so I might have taken her to me for a wife: now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.
texts.gen.12.20: And Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him: and they sent him away, and his wife, and all that he had.
texts.gen.13.1: And Abram returned from Egypt, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the south.
texts.gen.13.2: And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.
texts.gen.13.3: And he went on his journeys from the south even to Beth-el, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Beth-el and Hai;
texts.gen.13.4: To the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
texts.gen.13.5: And Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, and herds, and tents.
texts.gen.13.6: And the land was not able to bear them, that they might dwell together: for their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together.
texts.gen.13.7: And there was a strife between the herdmen of Abram's cattle and the herdmen of Lot's cattle: and the Canaanite and the Perizzite dwelt then in the land.
texts.gen.13.8: And Abram said to Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we are brethren.
texts.gen.13.9: Is not the whole land before thee? Separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou wilt depart to the right hand, then I will go to the left.
texts.gen.13.10: And Lot lifted up his eyes, and beheld all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered every where, before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, even as the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as thou comest to Zoar.
texts.gen.13.11: Then Lot chose him all the plain of Jordan; and Lot journeyed east: and they separated themselves the one from the other.
texts.gen.13.12: Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent towards Sodom.
texts.gen.13.13: But the men of Sodom were wicked, and sinners before the LORD, exceedingly.
texts.gen.13.14: And the LORD said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, Lift up now thine eyes, and look from the place where thou art, northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward:
texts.gen.13.15: For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.
texts.gen.13.16: And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered.
texts.gen.13.17: Arise, walk through the land in the length of it and in the breadth of it; for I will give it to thee.
texts.gen.13.18: Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar to the LORD.
texts.gen.14.1: And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel, king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations;
texts.gen.14.2: That these made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
texts.gen.14.3: All these were joined together in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt sea.
texts.gen.14.4: Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
texts.gen.14.5: And in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings that were with him, and smote the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzims in Ham, and the Emins in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
texts.gen.14.6: And the Horites in their mount Seir, to El-paran, which is by the wilderness.
texts.gen.14.7: And they returned, and came to En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and smote all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that dwelt in Hazezontamar.
texts.gen.14.8: And there went out the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, (the same is Zoar;) and they joined battle with them in the vale of Siddim;
texts.gen.14.9: With Chedorlaomer the king of Elam, and with Tidal king of nations, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings with five.
texts.gen.14.10: And the vale of Siddim was full of slime-pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and fell there: and they that remained fled to the mountain.
texts.gen.14.11: And they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their provisions, and went their way.
texts.gen.14.12: And they took Lot, Abram's brother's son, who dwelt in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.
texts.gen.14.13: And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew; for he dwelt in the plain of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner: and these were confederate with Abram.
texts.gen.14.14: And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them to Dan.
texts.gen.14.15: And he divided himself against them, he and his servants by night, and smote them, and pursued them to Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.
texts.gen.14.16: And he brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.
texts.gen.14.17: And the king of Sodom went out to meet him after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings that were with him, at the valley of Shaveh, which is the king's dale.
texts.gen.14.18: And Melchisedek, king of Salem, brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God.
texts.gen.14.19: And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth:
texts.gen.14.20: And blessed be the most high God, who hath delivered thy enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.
texts.gen.14.21: And the king of Sodom said to Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goods to thyself.
texts.gen.14.22: And Abram said to the king of Sodom, I have lifted my hand to the LORD, the most high God, the possessor of heaven and earth,
texts.gen.14.23: That I will not take from a thread even to a shoe-latchet, and that I will not take any thing that is thine, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich:
texts.gen.14.24: Save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their portion.
texts.gen.15.1: After these things the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.
texts.gen.15.2: And Abram said, Lord GOD, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?
texts.gen.15.3: And Abram said, Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and lo, one born in my house is my heir.
texts.gen.15.4: And behold, the word of the LORD came to him, saying, This shall not be thy heir; but he that shall come forth out of thy own bowels shall be thy heir.
texts.gen.15.5: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now towards heaven, and tell the stars, if thou art able to number them: and he said to him, So shall thy seed be.
texts.gen.15.6: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
texts.gen.15.7: And he said to him, I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.
texts.gen.15.8: And he said, Lord GOD, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?
texts.gen.15.9: And he said to him, Take me a heifer of three years old, and a she-goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtle-dove, and a young pigeon.
texts.gen.15.10: And he took to him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each piece one against another: but the birds he did not divide.
texts.gen.15.11: And when the fowls came down upon the carcases, Abram drove them away.
texts.gen.15.12: And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and lo, a horror of great darkness fell upon him.
texts.gen.15.13: And he said to Abram, Know certainly that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;
texts.gen.15.14: And also that nation which they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.
texts.gen.15.15: And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age.
texts.gen.15.16: But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.
texts.gen.15.17: And it came to pass, that when the sun had gone down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces.
texts.gen.15.18: In that same day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, To thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
texts.gen.15.19: The Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,
texts.gen.15.20: And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,
texts.gen.15.21: And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
texts.gen.16.1: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, bore him no children: and she had a handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.
texts.gen.16.2: And Sarai said to Abram, Behold, now, the LORD hath restrained me from bearing: I pray thee go in to my maid; it may be that I may obtain children by her. And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai.
texts.gen.16.3: And Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar her maid, the Egyptian, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife.
texts.gen.16.4: And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived: and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
texts.gen.16.5: And Sarai said to Abram, my wrong be upon thee: I have given my maid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: the LORD judge between me and thee.
texts.gen.16.6: But Abram said to Sarai, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand; do to her as it pleaseth thee. And when Sarai dealt hardly with her, she fled from her face.
texts.gen.16.7: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.
texts.gen.16.8: And he said, Hagar, Sarai's maid, whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go? And she said, I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai.
texts.gen.16.9: And the angel of the LORD said to her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.
texts.gen.16.10: And the angel of the LORD said to her, I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.
texts.gen.16.11: And the angel of the LORD said to her, Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the LORD hath heard thy affliction.
texts.gen.16.12: And he will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man's hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.
texts.gen.16.13: And she called the name of the LORD that spoke to her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?
texts.gen.16.14: Wherefore the well was called Beer-la-hai-roi; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
texts.gen.16.15: And Hagar bore Abram a son: and Abram called his son's name, which Hagar bore, Ishmael.
texts.gen.16.16: And Abram was eighty six years old, when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
texts.gen.17.1: And when Abram was ninety and nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram, and said to him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.
texts.gen.17.2: And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly.
texts.gen.17.3: And Abram fell on his face: and God talked with him, saying,
texts.gen.17.4: As for me, behold, my covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be a father of many nations.
texts.gen.17.5: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee.
texts.gen.17.6: And I will make thee exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of thee; and kings shall proceed from thee.
texts.gen.17.7: And I will establish my covenant between me and thee, and thy seed after thee, in their generations, for an everlasting covenant; to be a God to thee and to thy seed after thee.
texts.gen.17.8: And I will give to thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land in which thou art a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.
texts.gen.17.9: And God said to Abraham, Thou shalt keep my covenant therefore, thou, and thy seed after thee, in their generations.
texts.gen.17.10: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep between me and you, and thy seed after thee; Every male-child among you shall be circumcised.
texts.gen.17.11: And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.
texts.gen.17.12: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male-child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, who is not of thy seed.
texts.gen.17.13: He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised: and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
texts.gen.17.14: And the uncircumcised male-child, whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.
texts.gen.17.15: And God said to Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be.
texts.gen.17.16: And I will bless her, and give thee a son also by her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of people shall proceed from her.
texts.gen.17.17: Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born to him that is a hundred years old? and shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear?
texts.gen.17.18: And Abraham said to God, O that Ishmael might live before thee!
texts.gen.17.19: And God said, Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son indeed; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.
texts.gen.17.20: And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.
texts.gen.17.21: But my covenant will I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to thee at this set time in the next year.
texts.gen.17.22: And he ceased talking with him, and God went up from Abraham.
texts.gen.17.23: And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham's house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin, in the same day, as God had said to him.
texts.gen.17.24: And Abraham was ninety and nine years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
texts.gen.17.25: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
texts.gen.17.26: In the same day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
texts.gen.17.27: And all the men of his house, born in the house, and bought with money of the stranger, were circumcised with him.
texts.gen.18.1: And the LORD appeared to him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day;
texts.gen.18.2: And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and lo, three men stood by him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself toward the ground,
texts.gen.18.3: And said, My Lord, if now I have found favor in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant:
texts.gen.18.4: Let a little water, I pray you, be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree:
texts.gen.18.5: And I will bring a morsel of bread, and comfort ye your hearts; after that you shall pass on: for therefore are ye come to your servant. And they said, So do, as thou hast said.
texts.gen.18.6: And Abraham hastened into the tent to Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes upon the hearth.
texts.gen.18.7: And Abraham ran to the herd, and brought a calf tender and good, and gave it to a young man; and he hasted to dress it.
texts.gen.18.8: And he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree, and they ate.
texts.gen.18.9: And they said to him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent.
texts.gen.18.10: And he said, I will certainly return to thee according to the time of life; and lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.
texts.gen.18.11: Now Abraham and Sarah were old and far advanced in age; and it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.
texts.gen.18.12: Therefore Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am become old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?
texts.gen.18.13: And the LORD said to Abraham, Why did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I certainly bear a child, who am old?
texts.gen.18.14: Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return to thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.
texts.gen.18.15: Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.
texts.gen.18.16: And the men rose up from thence, and looked toward Sodom: and Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.
texts.gen.18.17: And the LORD said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do;
texts.gen.18.18: Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?
texts.gen.18.19: For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they will keep the way of the LORD, to do justice and judgment; that the LORD may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.
texts.gen.18.20: And the LORD said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;
texts.gen.18.21: I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come to me; and if not, I will know.
texts.gen.18.22: And the men turned their faces from thence, and went towards Sodom: but Abraham stood yet before the LORD.
texts.gen.18.23: And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?
texts.gen.18.24: Peradventure there are fifty righteous within the city: wilt thou also destroy and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that are in it?
texts.gen.18.25: That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked: and that the righteous should be as the wicked, that be far from thee: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
texts.gen.18.26: And the LORD said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.
texts.gen.18.27: And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I, who am dust and ashes, have taken upon me to speak to the Lord.
texts.gen.18.28: Peradventure there will lack five of the fifty righteous: wilt thou destroy all the city for lack of five? And he said, If I find there forty and five, I will not destroy it.
texts.gen.18.29: And he spoke to him yet again, and said, Peradventure there will be forty found there. And he said, I will not do it for forty's sake.
texts.gen.18.30: And he said, Oh, let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak: Peradventure there will thirty be found there. And he said, I will not do it, if I find thirty there.
texts.gen.18.31: And he said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak to the Lord: Peradventure there will be twenty found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for twenty's sake.
texts.gen.18.32: And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: Peradventure ten will be found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake.
texts.gen.18.33: And the LORD went his way, as soon as he had left communing with Abraham: and Abraham returned to his place.
texts.gen.19.1: And there came two angels to Sodom at evening; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom; and Lot seeing them, rose to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face towards the ground;
texts.gen.19.2: And he said, Behold now, my lords, turn, I pray you, into your servant's house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise early, and go on your ways. And they said, Nay; but we will abide in the street all night.
texts.gen.19.3: And he urged them greatly; and they turned in to him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
texts.gen.19.4: But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
texts.gen.19.5: And they called to Lot, and said to him, Where are the men who came in to thee this night? bring them out to us, that we may know them.
texts.gen.19.6: And Lot went out at the door to them, and shut the door after him,
texts.gen.19.7: And said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly.
texts.gen.19.8: Behold now, I have two daughters who have not known man; let me, I pray you, bring them out to you, and do ye to them as is good in your eyes: only to these men do nothing; for therefore came they under the shadow of my roof.
texts.gen.19.9: And they said, Stand back. And they said again, This one man came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge: Now will we deal worse with thee than with them. And they pressed hard upon the man, Lot, and came near to break the door.
texts.gen.19.10: But the men put forth their hand, and pulled Lot into the house to them, and shut the door.
texts.gen.19.11: And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great: so that they wearied themselves to find the door.
texts.gen.19.12: And the men said to Lot, Hast thou here any besides? son-in-law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and whatever thou hast in the city, bring them out of this place:
texts.gen.19.13: For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them has become great before the face of the LORD; and the LORD hath sent us to destroy it.
texts.gen.19.14: And Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who married his daughters, and said, Arise, depart from this place; for the LORD will destroy this city: but he seemed to his sons-in-law as one that mocked.
texts.gen.19.15: And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters who are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.
texts.gen.19.16: And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters: the LORD being merciful to him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
texts.gen.19.17: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life: look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain: escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.
texts.gen.19.18: And Lot said to them, Oh, not so, my Lord!
texts.gen.19.19: Behold now, thy servant hath found grace in thy sight, and thou hast magnified thy mercy, which thou hast shown to me in saving my life: and I cannot escape to the mountain, lest some evil should take me, and I die:
texts.gen.19.20: Behold now, this city is near to flee to, and it is a small one: Oh, let me escape thither! (Is it not a small one?) and my soul shall live.
texts.gen.19.21: And he said to him, See, I have accepted thee concerning this thing also, that I will not overthrow this city, for which thou hast spoken.
texts.gen.19.22: Haste thee, escape thither: for I cannot do any thing till thou hast come thither: therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.
texts.gen.19.23: The sun had risen upon the earth when Lot entered into Zoar.
texts.gen.19.24: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
texts.gen.19.25: And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.
texts.gen.19.26: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
texts.gen.19.27: And Abraham rose early in the morning, to the place were he stood before the LORD:
texts.gen.19.28: And he looked towards Sodom and Gomorrah, and towards all the land of the plain, and beheld, and lo, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace.
texts.gen.19.29: And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Lot dwelt.
texts.gen.19.30: And Lot went up from Zoar, and dwelt in the mountain, and his two daughters with him; for he feared to dwell in Zoar: and he dwelt in a cave, he, and his two daughters.
texts.gen.19.31: And the first-born said to the younger, Our father is old, and there is not a man on the earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth:
texts.gen.19.32: Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.
texts.gen.19.33: And they made their father drink wine that night: and the first-born went in and lay with her father; and he perceived not when she lay down, nor when she arose.
texts.gen.19.34: And it came to pass on the morrow that the first born said to the younger, Behold, I lay yesternight with my father; let us make him drink wine this night also; and go thou in, and lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.
texts.gen.19.35: And they made their father drink wine that night also: and the younger arose and lay with him; and he perceived not when she lay down, nor when she arose.
texts.gen.19.36: Thus were both the daughters of Lot with child by their father.
texts.gen.19.37: And the first-born bore a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites to this day.
texts.gen.19.38: And the younger, she also bore a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.
texts.gen.20.1: And Abraham journeyed from thence towards the south country, and dwelt between Kadash and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
texts.gen.20.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, she is my sister: And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
texts.gen.20.3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but a dead man, on account of the woman whom thou hast taken: for she is a man's wife.
texts.gen.20.4: But Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, wilt thou also slay a righteous nation?
texts.gen.20.5: Said he not to me, She is my sister? and she, even she herself said, He is my brother: in the integrity of my heart, and innocence of my hands have I done this.
texts.gen.20.6: And God said to him in a dream, Yea, I know that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore I suffered thee not to touch her.
texts.gen.20.7: Now therefore restore to the man his wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou shalt not restore her, know thou that thou shalt surely die, thou and all that are thine.
texts.gen.20.8: Therefore Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ears: and the men were greatly afraid.
texts.gen.20.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, What has thou done to us? and in what have I offended thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done deeds to me that ought not to be done.
texts.gen.20.10: And Abimelech said to Abraham, What sawest thou, that thou hast done this thing?
texts.gen.20.11: And Abraham said, Because I thought, surely the fear of God is not in this place; and they will slay me for my wife's sake.
texts.gen.20.12: And yet indeed she is my sister: she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.
texts.gen.20.13: And it came to pass, when God caused me to wander from my father's house, that I said to her, This is thy kindness which thou shalt show to me; At every place whither we shall come, say of me, He is my brother.
texts.gen.20.14: And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and men-servants, and women-servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored to him Sarah his wife.
texts.gen.20.15: And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dwell where it pleaseth thee.
texts.gen.20.16: And to Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, he is to thee a covering of the eyes, to all that are with thee, and with all other: thus she was reproved.
texts.gen.20.17: So Abraham prayed to God: and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maid-servants, and they bore children.
texts.gen.20.18: For the LORD had made barren all the females of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
texts.gen.21.1: And the LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as he had spoken.
texts.gen.21.2: For Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
texts.gen.21.3: And Abraham called the name of his son that was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
texts.gen.21.4: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac, being eight days old, as God had commanded him.
texts.gen.21.5: And Abraham was a hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born to him.
texts.gen.21.6: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.
texts.gen.21.7: And she said, Who would have said to Abraham, that Sarah shall nurse children? for I have borne him a son in his old age.
texts.gen.21.8: And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the day that Isaac was weaned.
texts.gen.21.9: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, which she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
texts.gen.21.10: Wherefore, she said to Abraham, Cast out this bond-woman, and her son: for the son of this bond-woman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac.
texts.gen.21.11: And the thing was very grievous in Abraham's sight, because of his son.
texts.gen.21.12: And God said to Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight, because of the lad, and because of thy bond-woman; in all that Sarah hath said to thee, hearken to her voice: for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.
texts.gen.21.13: And also of the son of the bond-woman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed.
texts.gen.21.14: And Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and gave it to Hagar (putting it on her shoulder) and the child, and sent her away; and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beer-sheba.
texts.gen.21.15: And the water was spent in the bottle, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.
texts.gen.21.16: And she went, and sat her down over against him, a good way off, as it were a bow-shot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat over against him, and raised her voice, and wept.
texts.gen.21.17: And God heard the voice of the lad: and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said to her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.
texts.gen.21.18: Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thy hand: for I will make him a great nation.
texts.gen.21.19: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water: and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.
texts.gen.21.20: And God was with the lad; and he grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.
texts.gen.21.21: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran: and his mother took for him a wife out of the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.21.22: And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, spoke to Abraham, saying, God is with thee in all that thou doest:
texts.gen.21.23: Now therefore swear to me here by God, that thou wilt not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son's son: but according to the kindness that I have done to thee, thou shalt do to me, and to the land in which thou hast sojourned.
texts.gen.21.24: And Abraham said, I will swear.
texts.gen.21.25: And Abraham reproved Abimelech, because of a well of water, which Abimelech's servants had violently taken away.
texts.gen.21.26: And Abimelech said, I know not who hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet have I heard of it, but to-day.
texts.gen.21.27: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelech: and both of them made a covenant.
texts.gen.21.28: And Abraham set seven ewe-lambs of the flock by themselves.
texts.gen.21.29: And Abimelech said to Abraham, What mean these seven ewe-lambs, which thou hast set by themselves?
texts.gen.21.30: And he said, For these seven ewe-lambs shalt thou take from my hand, that they may be a witness to me, that I have digged this well.
texts.gen.21.31: Wherefore he called that place Beer-sheba: because there they swore both of them.
texts.gen.21.32: Thus they made a covenant at Beer-sheba: Then Abimelech arose, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.
texts.gen.21.33: And Abraham planted a grove in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
texts.gen.21.34: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
texts.gen.22.1: And it came to pass after these things, that God tempted Abraham, and said to him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.
texts.gen.22.2: And he said, Take now thy son, thy only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and go into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will name to thee.
texts.gen.22.3: And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and cleft the wood for the burnt-offering, and rose and went to the place which God had named to him.
texts.gen.22.4: Then on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.
texts.gen.22.5: And Abraham said to his young men, Abide you here with the ass, and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and return to you.
texts.gen.22.6: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt-offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife: and they went both of them together.
texts.gen.22.7: And Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt-offering?
texts.gen.22.8: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt-offering: so they went both of them together.
texts.gen.22.9: And they came to the place which God had named to him; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order; and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.
texts.gen.22.10: And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
texts.gen.22.11: And the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham. And he said, Here am I.
texts.gen.22.12: And he said, Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing to him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld from me thy son, thy only son.
texts.gen.22.13: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.
texts.gen.22.14: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it will be seen.
texts.gen.22.15: And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven the second time,
texts.gen.22.16: And said, By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thy only son:
texts.gen.22.17: That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand which is on the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
texts.gen.22.18: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: because thou hast obeyed my voice.
texts.gen.22.19: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose and went together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beer-sheba.
texts.gen.22.20: And it came to pass after these things, that it was told to Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she hath also borne children to thy brother Nahor;
texts.gen.22.21: Huz his first-born, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
texts.gen.22.22: And Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
texts.gen.22.23: And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight Milcah bore to Nahor Abraham's brother.
texts.gen.22.24: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, she bore also Tebah, and Gaham, and Thahash, and Maachah.
texts.gen.23.1: And Sarah was a hundred and twenty-seven years old: these were the years of the life of Sarah.
texts.gen.23.2: And Sarah died in Kirjath-arba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
texts.gen.23.3: And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
texts.gen.23.4: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you; give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
texts.gen.23.5: And the children of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,
texts.gen.23.6: Hear us, my lord; thou art a mighty prince among us: in the choice of our sepulchers bury thy dead: none of us will withhold from thee his sepulcher, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.
texts.gen.23.7: And Abraham stood up and bowed himself to the people of the land, to the children of Heth.
texts.gen.23.8: And he communed with them, saying, If it is your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
texts.gen.23.9: That he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which is in the end of his field; for as much money as it is worth he shall give it me, for a possession of a burying-place among you.
texts.gen.23.10: And Ephron dwelt among the children of Heth. And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, of all that entered the gates of his city, saying,
texts.gen.23.11: Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I to thee, and the cave that is in it, I give it to thee; in the presence of the sons of my people I give it to thee: bury thy dead.
texts.gen.23.12: And Abraham bowed himself before the people of the land.
texts.gen.23.13: And he spoke to Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou wilt give it, I pray thee, hear me: I will give thee money for the field: take it of me, and I will bury my dead there.
texts.gen.23.14: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
texts.gen.23.15: My lord, hearken to me: the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver; what is that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
texts.gen.23.16: And Abraham hearkened to Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver which he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.
texts.gen.23.17: And the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the borders round about, were made sure
texts.gen.23.18: To Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that entered the gate of his city.
texts.gen.23.19: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.23.20: And the field, and the cave that is in it were made sure to Abraham for a possession of a burying-place, by the sons of Heth.
texts.gen.24.1: And Abraham was old and far advanced in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
texts.gen.24.2: And Abraham said to his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
texts.gen.24.3: And I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that thou wilt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I dwell:
texts.gen.24.4: But thou shalt go to my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac.
texts.gen.24.5: And the servant said to him, It may be the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land: must I needs bring thy son again to the land from whence thou camest?
texts.gen.24.6: And Abraham said to him, Beware that thou bring not my son thither again.
texts.gen.24.7: The LORD God of heaven, who took me from my father's house, and from the land of my kindred, and who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, To thy seed I will give this land: he will send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife for my son from thence.
texts.gen.24.8: And if the woman shall not be willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath; only bring not my son thither again.
texts.gen.24.9: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning that matter.
texts.gen.24.10: And the servant took ten camels, of the camels of his master, and departed; (for all the goods of his master were in his hands:) and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
texts.gen.24.11: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water, at the time of the evening, the time when women go out to draw water:
texts.gen.24.12: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, prosper me this day, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
texts.gen.24.13: Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:
texts.gen.24.14: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and by that shall I know that thou hast shown kindness to my master.
texts.gen.24.15: And it came to pass before he had done speaking, that behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.
texts.gen.24.16: And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
texts.gen.24.17: And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little water from thy pitcher.
texts.gen.24.18: And she said, Drink, my lord. And she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
texts.gen.24.19: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, till they have done drinking.
texts.gen.24.20: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
texts.gen.24.21: And the man, wondering at her, held his peace, to know whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous, or not.
texts.gen.24.22: And it came to pass as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden ear-ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold;
texts.gen.24.23: And said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room in thy father's house for us to lodge in?
texts.gen.24.24: And she said to him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.
texts.gen.24.25: She said moreover to him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
texts.gen.24.26: And the man bowed his head, and worshipped the LORD.
texts.gen.24.27: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left my master destitute of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren.
texts.gen.24.28: And the damsel ran, and told these things to her mother's house.
texts.gen.24.29: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban: and Laban ran out to the man, to the well.
texts.gen.24.30: And it came to pass when he saw the ear-ring and bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spoke the man to me; that he came to the man; and behold, he stood by the camels at the well.
texts.gen.24.31: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD; why standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
texts.gen.24.32: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the men's feet that were with him.
texts.gen.24.33: And there was set food before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told my errand. And he said, Speak on.
texts.gen.24.34: And he said, I am Abraham's servant.
texts.gen.24.35: And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly, and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and camels, and asses.
texts.gen.24.36: And Sarah, my master's wife, bore a son to my master when she was old: and to him hath he given all that he hath.
texts.gen.24.37: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:
texts.gen.24.38: But thou shalt go to my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.
texts.gen.24.39: And I said to my master, It may be the woman will not follow me.
texts.gen.24.40: And he said to me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father's house.
texts.gen.24.41: Then shalt thou be clear from this my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee one, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
texts.gen.24.42: And I came this day to the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now thou dost prosper my way which I go:
texts.gen.24.43: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw water, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water of thy pitcher to drink;
texts.gen.24.44: And she saith to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman whom the LORD hath pointed out for my master's son.
texts.gen.24.45: And before I had done speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down to the well, and drew water: and I said to her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
texts.gen.24.46: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
texts.gen.24.47: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him: and I put the ear-ring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.
texts.gen.24.48: And I bowed my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master's brother's daughter for his son.
texts.gen.24.49: And now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me; and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
texts.gen.24.50: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, and said, The thing proceedeth from the LORD: we cannot speak to thee bad or good.
texts.gen.24.51: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master's son's wife, as the LORD hath spoken.
texts.gen.24.52: And it came to pass, that when Abraham's servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, bowing himself to the earth.
texts.gen.24.53: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: He gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
texts.gen.24.54: And they ate and drank, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose in the morning, and he said, Send me away to my master.
texts.gen.24.55: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.
texts.gen.24.56: And he said to them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way: send me away, that I may go to my master.
texts.gen.24.57: And they said, We will call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.
texts.gen.24.58: And they called Rebekah, and said to her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
texts.gen.24.59: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.
texts.gen.24.60: And they blessed Rebekah, and said to her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those who hate them.
texts.gen.24.61: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
texts.gen.24.62: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahai-roi; for he dwelt in the south country.
texts.gen.24.63: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at evening: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and behold, the camels were coming.
texts.gen.24.64: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she alighted from the camel.
texts.gen.24.65: For she had said to the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It is my master: therefore she took a vail and covered herself.
texts.gen.24.66: And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
texts.gen.24.67: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
texts.gen.25.1: Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
texts.gen.25.2: And she bore him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
texts.gen.25.3: And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim and Leummim.
texts.gen.25.4: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
texts.gen.25.5: And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.
texts.gen.25.6: But to the sons of the concubines which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son (while he yet lived) eastward, to the east country.
texts.gen.25.7: And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived, a hundred and seventy five years.
texts.gen.25.8: Then Abraham expired, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.
texts.gen.25.9: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre;
texts.gen.25.10: The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.
texts.gen.25.11: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac: and Isaac dwelt by the well Lahai-roi.
texts.gen.25.12: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, bore to Abraham.
texts.gen.25.13: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: The first-born of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
texts.gen.25.14: And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
texts.gen.25.15: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
texts.gen.25.16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.
texts.gen.25.17: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael; a hundred and thirty and seven years: and he expired and died, and was gathered to his people.
texts.gen.25.18: And they dwelt from Havilah to Shur, that is before Egypt, as thou goest towards Assyria: and he died in the presence of all his brethren.
texts.gen.25.19: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham begat Isaac:
texts.gen.25.20: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan-aram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
texts.gen.25.21: And Isaac entreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and the LORD was entreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
texts.gen.25.22: And the children struggled together within her: and she said, If it is so, why am I thus? And she went to inquire of the LORD.
texts.gen.25.23: And the LORD said to her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels: and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
texts.gen.25.24: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
texts.gen.25.25: And the first was born red, all over like a hairy garment: and they called his name Esau.
texts.gen.25.26: And after that his brother was born, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
texts.gen.25.27: And the boys grew: and Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man dwelling in tents.
texts.gen.25.28: And Isaac loved Esau, because he ate of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
texts.gen.25.29: And Jacob boiled pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint.
texts.gen.25.30: And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
texts.gen.25.31: And Jacob said, Sell to me this day thy birth-right.
texts.gen.25.32: And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birth-right bring to me?
texts.gen.25.33: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he swore to him: and he sold his birth-right to Jacob.
texts.gen.25.34: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he ate and drank, and rose and went his way: thus Esau despised his birth-right.
texts.gen.26.1: And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines to Gerar.
texts.gen.26.2: And the LORD appeared to him, and said, Go not down into Egypt: dwell in the land which I shall tell thee of.
texts.gen.26.3: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee: for to thee, and to thy seed I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I swore to Abraham thy father;
