texts.gen.26.4: And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give to thy seed all these countries: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed:
texts.gen.26.5: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
texts.gen.26.7: And the men of the place asked him of his wife; and he said, She is my sister: for he feared to say, She is my wife; lest, said he, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she was fair to look upon.
texts.gen.26.8: And it came to pass when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.
texts.gen.26.9: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, surely she is thy wife: and how saidst thou, She is my sister? and Isaac said to him, Because I said, Lest I should die on her account.
texts.gen.26.10: And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done to us? one of the people might lightly have lain with thy wife, and thou wouldst have brought guiltiness upon us.
texts.gen.26.11: And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
texts.gen.26.12: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year a hundred-fold: and the LORD blessed him:
texts.gen.26.13: And the man became great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great:
texts.gen.26.14: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and very many servants: And the Philistines envied him.
texts.gen.26.15: For all the wells which his father's servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.
texts.gen.26.16: And Abimelech said to Isaac, Go from us: for thou art much mightier than we.
texts.gen.26.17: And Isaac departed thence, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
texts.gen.26.18: And Isaac digged again the wells of water which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
texts.gen.26.19: And Isaac's servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.
texts.gen.26.20: And the herdmen of Gerar contended with Isaac's herdmen, saying, The water is ours: and he called the name of the well Esek; because they strove with him.
texts.gen.26.21: And they digged another well, and contended for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.
texts.gen.26.22: And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they did not contend: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now the LORD hath made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
texts.gen.26.23: And he went up from thence to Beer-sheba.
texts.gen.26.24: And the LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.
texts.gen.26.25: And he built an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac's servants digged a well.
texts.gen.26.26: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.
texts.gen.26.27: And Isaac said to them, Why come ye to me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me away from you?
texts.gen.26.28: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;
texts.gen.26.29: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done to thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou art now the blessed of the LORD.
texts.gen.26.30: And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
texts.gen.26.31: And they rose betimes in the morning, and swore one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
texts.gen.26.32: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac's servants came and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said to him, We have found water.
texts.gen.26.33: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city is Beer-sheba to this day.
texts.gen.26.34: And Esau was forty years old when he took for a wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
texts.gen.26.35: Who were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah.
texts.gen.27.1: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said to him, My son: and he said to him, Behold, here am I.
texts.gen.27.2: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death:
texts.gen.27.3: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison;
texts.gen.27.4: And make me savory meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
texts.gen.27.5: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son; and Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
texts.gen.27.6: And Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak to Esau thy brother, saying,
texts.gen.27.7: Bring me venison, and make me savory meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD, before my death.
texts.gen.27.8: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice, according to that which I command thee.
texts.gen.27.9: Go now to the flock, and bring me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savory meat for thy father, such as he loveth:
texts.gen.27.10: And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.
texts.gen.27.11: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man:
texts.gen.27.12: My father perhaps will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
texts.gen.27.13: And his mother said to him, upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go, bring them to me.
texts.gen.27.14: And he went, and took, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savory meat, such as his father loved.
texts.gen.27.15: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which was with her in the house, and put it upon Jacob her younger son:
texts.gen.27.16: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats on his hands, and on the smooth part of his neck:
texts.gen.27.17: And she gave the savory meat, and the bread which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
texts.gen.27.18: And he came to his father, and said, My father: And he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son?
texts.gen.27.19: And Jacob said to his father, I am Esau thy first-born; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
texts.gen.27.20: And Isaac said to his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought it to me.
texts.gen.27.21: And Isaac said to Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou art my very son Esau, or not.
texts.gen.27.22: And Jacob went near to Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
texts.gen.27.23: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: So he blessed him.
texts.gen.27.24: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.
texts.gen.27.25: And he said, bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he ate: and he brought him wine, and he drank.
texts.gen.27.26: And his father Isaac said to him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son.
texts.gen.27.27: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed:
texts.gen.27.28: Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:
texts.gen.27.29: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee; be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.
texts.gen.27.30: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob had yet scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
texts.gen.27.31: And he also had made savory meat, and brought it to his father; and said to his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me.
texts.gen.27.32: And Isaac his father said to him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy first-born Esau.
texts.gen.27.33: And Isaac trembled exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.
texts.gen.27.34: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceedingly bitter cry, and said to his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.
texts.gen.27.35: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.
texts.gen.27.36: And he said, Is he not rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me twice: he took away my birth-right; and behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?
texts.gen.27.37: And Isaac answered and said to Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now to thee, my son?
texts.gen.27.38: And Esau said to his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
texts.gen.27.39: And Isaac his father answered, and said to him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;
texts.gen.27.40: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother: and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.
texts.gen.27.41: And Esau hated Jacob, because of the blessing with which his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
texts.gen.27.42: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as concerning thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.
texts.gen.27.43: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice: and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
texts.gen.27.44: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury shall turn away;
texts.gen.27.45: Till thy brother's anger shall turn away from thee, and he shall forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and bring thee from thence. Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?
texts.gen.27.46: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life, because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob shall take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these who are of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?
texts.gen.28.1: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said to him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
texts.gen.28.2: Arise, go to Padan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother.
texts.gen.28.3: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;
texts.gen.28.4: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land in which thou art a stranger, which God gave to Abraham.
texts.gen.28.5: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padan-aram, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.
texts.gen.28.6: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan-aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him, he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
texts.gen.28.7: And that Jacob obeyed his father, and his mother, and was gone to Padan-aram;
texts.gen.28.8: And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
texts.gen.28.9: Then went Esau to Ishmael, and took to the wives which he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.
texts.gen.28.10: And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba, and went towards Haran.
texts.gen.28.11: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set: and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.
texts.gen.28.12: And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder set upon the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
texts.gen.28.13: And behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land on which thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.
texts.gen.28.14: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth; and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
texts.gen.28.15: And behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land: for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have declared to thee.
texts.gen.28.16: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.
texts.gen.28.17: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is no other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
texts.gen.28.18: And Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it.
texts.gen.28.19: And he called the name of that place Beth-el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.
texts.gen.28.20: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
texts.gen.28.21: So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:
texts.gen.28.22: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me, I will surely give the tenth to thee.
texts.gen.29.1: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.
texts.gen.29.2: And he looked, and behold, a well in the field, and lo, there were three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and a great stone was upon the well's mouth.
texts.gen.29.3: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the well's mouth and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well's mouth in its place.
texts.gen.29.4: And Jacob said to them, My brethren, whence are ye? And they said, We are from Haran.
texts.gen.29.5: And he said to them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? and they said, We know him.
texts.gen.29.6: And he said to them, Is he well? And they said, He is well: and behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep.
texts.gen.29.7: And he said, Lo, it is yet high day, neither is it time that the cattle should be collected: water ye the sheep, and go and feed them.
texts.gen.29.8: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks are collected, and till they roll the stone from the well's mouth; then we water the sheep.
texts.gen.29.9: And while he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep: for she kept them.
texts.gen.29.10: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother; that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
texts.gen.29.11: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
texts.gen.29.12: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebekah's son; and she ran and told her father.
texts.gen.29.13: And it came to pass when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
texts.gen.29.14: And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh: and he abode with him the space of a month.
texts.gen.29.15: And Laban said to Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for naught? tell me, what shall thy wages be?
texts.gen.29.16: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
texts.gen.29.17: Leah was tender-eyed, but Rachel was beautiful and well-favored.
texts.gen.29.18: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
texts.gen.29.19: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.
texts.gen.29.20: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had to her.
texts.gen.29.21: And Jacob said to Laban, Give me my wife (for my days are fulfilled) that I may go in to her.
texts.gen.29.22: And Laban assembled all the men of the place, and made a feast.
texts.gen.29.23: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in to her.
texts.gen.29.24: And Laban gave to his daughter Leah, Zilpah his maid for a handmaid.
texts.gen.29.25: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done to me? did I not serve with thee for Rachel? why then hast thou deceived me?
texts.gen.29.26: And Laban said, it must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the first-born.
texts.gen.29.27: Fulfill her week, and we will give thee this also, for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years.
texts.gen.29.28: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week: and he gave him Rachel, his daughter, for a wife also.
texts.gen.29.29: And Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, Bilhah, his handmaid, to be her maid.
texts.gen.29.30: And he went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.
texts.gen.29.31: And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he made her fruitful: but Rachel was barren.
texts.gen.29.32: And Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; now therefore my husband will love me.
texts.gen.29.33: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this son also: and she called his name Simeon.
texts.gen.29.34: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and said, Now this time will my husband adhere to me, because I have borne him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.
texts.gen.29.35: And she conceived again, and bore a son: and she said, Now will I praise the LORD: therefore she called his name Judah, and left bearing.
texts.gen.30.1: And when Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said to Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
texts.gen.30.2: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel; and he said, Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?
texts.gen.30.3: And she said, Behold, my maid Bilhah, go in to her; and she shall bear upon my knees, that I may also have children by her.
texts.gen.30.4: And she gave him Bilhah, her handmaid, for a wife: and Jacob went in to her.
texts.gen.30.5: And Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.
texts.gen.30.6: And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore she called his name Dan.
texts.gen.30.7: And Bilhah, Rachel's maid, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.
texts.gen.30.8: And Rachel said, With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.
texts.gen.30.9: When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah, her maid, and gave her Jacob for a wife.
texts.gen.30.10: And Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore Jacob a son.
texts.gen.30.11: And Leah said, A troop cometh: and she called his name Gad.
texts.gen.30.12: And Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore Jacob a second son.
texts.gen.30.13: And Leah said, Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed: and she called his name Asher.
texts.gen.30.14: And Reuben went, in the days of wheat-harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.
texts.gen.30.15: And she said to her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to-night for thy son's mandrakes.
texts.gen.30.16: And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in to me; for surely I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.
texts.gen.30.17: And God hearkened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob the fifth son.
texts.gen.30.18: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.
texts.gen.30.19: And Leah conceived again, and bore Jacob the sixth son.
texts.gen.30.20: And Leah said, God hath endowed me with a good dower; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.
texts.gen.30.21: And afterwards she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
texts.gen.30.22: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and rendered her fruitful.
texts.gen.30.23: And she conceived, and bore a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach:
texts.gen.30.24: And she called his name Joseph; and said, The LORD will add to me another son.
texts.gen.30.25: And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.
texts.gen.30.26: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knowest my service which I have done thee.
texts.gen.30.27: And Laban said to him, I pray thee, if I have found favor in thine eyes, tarry: for I have learned by experience, that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.
texts.gen.30.28: And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give it.
texts.gen.30.29: And he said to him, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how thy cattle were with me.
texts.gen.30.30: For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased to a multitude; and the LORD hath blessed thee since my coming: and now when shall I provide for my own house also?
texts.gen.30.31: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing; if thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again feed and keep thy flock:
texts.gen.30.32: I will pass through all thy flock to-day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.
texts.gen.30.33: So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be accounted stolen with me.
texts.gen.30.34: And Laban said, Behold, I would it might be according to thy word.
texts.gen.30.35: And he removed that day the he-goats that were ring-streaked and spotted, and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted; every one that had some white in it, and all the brown among the sheep, and gave them into the hands of his sons.
texts.gen.30.36: And he set three days' journey between himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Laban's flocks.
texts.gen.30.37: And Jacob took to him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut-tree; and peeled white streaks in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
texts.gen.30.38: And he set the rods, which he had peeled, before the flocks in the gutters in the watering-troughs, when the flocks came to drink, that they should conceive when they came to drink.
texts.gen.30.39: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ring-streaked, speckled, and spotted.
texts.gen.30.40: And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks towards the ring-streaked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban: and he put his own flocks by themselves, and put them not with Laban's cattle.
texts.gen.30.41: And it came to pass, whenever the stronger cattle conceived, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the cattle in the gutters, that they might conceive among the rods.
texts.gen.30.42: But when the cattle were feeble, he put them not in: so the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's.
texts.gen.30.43: And the man increased exceedingly, and had many cattle, and maid-servants, and men-servants, and camels, and asses.
texts.gen.31.1: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's; and of that which was our father's hath he obtained all this glory.
texts.gen.31.2: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and behold, it was not towards him as before.
texts.gen.31.3: And the LORD said to Jacob, Return to the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.
texts.gen.31.4: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah into the field to his flock,
texts.gen.31.5: And said to them, I see your father's countenance, that it is not towards me as before: but the God of my father hath been with me.
texts.gen.31.6: And ye know that with all my power I have served your father.
texts.gen.31.7: And your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times: but God suffered him not to hurt me.
texts.gen.31.8: If he said thus, The speckled shall be thy wages; then all the cattle bore speckled: and if he said thus, The ring-streaked shall be thy hire; then all the cattle bore ring-streaked.
texts.gen.31.9: Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given them to me.
texts.gen.31.10: And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived, that I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the rams which leaped upon the cattle were ring-streaked, speckled, and grizzled.
texts.gen.31.11: And the angel of God spoke to me in a dream, saying, Jacob: And I said, Here am I.
texts.gen.31.12: And he said, Lift up now thy eyes and see, all the rams which leap upon the cattle are ring-streaked, speckled, and grizzled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth to thee.
texts.gen.31.13: I am the God of Beth-el, where thou anointedst the pillar, and where thou vowedst to me a vow: now arise, depart from this land, and return to the land of thy kindred.
texts.gen.31.14: And Rachel and Leah answered, and said to him, Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?
texts.gen.31.15: Are we not counted by him strangers; for he hath sold us, and hath quite consumed also our money.
texts.gen.31.16: For all the riches which God hath taken from our father, that is ours, and our children's: now then whatever God hath said to thee, do.
texts.gen.31.17: Then Jacob arose, and set his sons and his wives upon camels;
texts.gen.31.18: And he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods which he had gained, the cattle of his getting, which he had gained in Padan-aram; to go to Isaac, his father, in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.31.19: And Laban went to shear his sheep; and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's.
texts.gen.31.20: And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he was about to depart.
texts.gen.31.21: So he fled with all that he had; and he arose, and passed over the river, and set his face towards the mount Gilead.
texts.gen.31.22: And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.
texts.gen.31.23: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey: and they overtook him in the mount Gilead.
texts.gen.31.24: And God came to Laban, the Syrian, in a dream by night, and said to him, Take heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
texts.gen.31.25: Then Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mount: and Laban, with his brethren, pitched in the mount of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.26: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters, as captives taken with the sword?
texts.gen.31.27: Why didst thou flee away secretly, and steal away from me, and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee away with mirth, and with songs, with tabret, and with harp?
texts.gen.31.28: And hast not suffered me to kiss my sons, and my daughters? thou hast now done foolishly in so doing.
texts.gen.31.29: It is in the power of my hand to do you hurt: but the God of your father spoke to me yesternight, saying, Take thou heed that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
texts.gen.31.30: And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou didst earnestly long after thy father's house; yet why hast thou stolen my gods?
texts.gen.31.31: And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid: for I said, It may be thou wouldest take thy daughters from me by force.
texts.gen.31.32: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee: for Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
texts.gen.31.33: And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the two maid-servants' tents; but he found them not. Then he went out of Leah's tent, and entered into Rachel's tent.
texts.gen.31.34: Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
texts.gen.31.35: And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
texts.gen.31.36: And Jacob was wroth, and chid with Laban: and Jacob answered, and said to Laban, What is my trespass? what is my sin, that thou hast so eagerly pursued after me?
texts.gen.31.37: Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou found of all thy household-stuff? set it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, that they may judge betwixt us both.
texts.gen.31.38: These twenty years have I been with thee: thy ewes and thy she-goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.
texts.gen.31.39: That which was torn by beasts, I brought not to thee; I bore the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, whether stolen by day, or stolen by night.
texts.gen.31.40: Thus I was; in the day the drouth consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from my eyes.
texts.gen.31.41: Thus have I been twenty years in thy house: I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.
texts.gen.31.42: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac had been with me, surely thou hadst now sent me away empty. God hath seen my affliction, and the labor of my hands, and rebuked thee yesternight.
texts.gen.31.43: And Laban answered, and said to Jacob, These daughters are my daughters, and these children are my children, and these cattle are my cattle, and all that thou seest is mine; and what can I do this day to these my daughters, or to their children which they have borne?
texts.gen.31.44: Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.
texts.gen.31.45: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
texts.gen.31.46: And Jacob said to his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made a heap: and they ate there upon the heap.
texts.gen.31.47: And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed:
texts.gen.31.48: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed:
texts.gen.31.49: And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.
texts.gen.31.50: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives besides my daughters; no man is with us; See, God is witness betwixt me and thee.
texts.gen.31.51: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold this pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee;
texts.gen.31.52: This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
texts.gen.31.53: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us. And Jacob swore by the fear of his father Isaac.
texts.gen.31.54: Then Jacob offered sacrifice upon the mount, and called his brethren to eat bread: and they ate bread, and tarried all night in the mount.
texts.gen.31.55: And early in the morning Laban arose, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them: and Laban departed, and returned to his place.
texts.gen.32.1: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
texts.gen.32.2: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is God's host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
texts.gen.32.3: And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
texts.gen.32.4: And he commanded them, saying, Thus shall ye speak to my lord Esau: Thy servant Jacob saith thus, I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed there till now:
texts.gen.32.5: And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and men-servants, and women-servants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find grace in thy sight.
texts.gen.32.6: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and also he is coming to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.
texts.gen.32.7: Then Jacob was greatly afraid, and distressed: and he divided the people that were with him, and the flocks, and herds, and camels, into two bands;
texts.gen.32.8: And said, If Esau shall come to the one company, and smite it, then the other company which is left, will escape.
texts.gen.32.9: And Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, the LORD who saidst to me, Return to thy country, and to thy kindred, and I will deal well with thee;
texts.gen.32.10: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, which thou hast shown to thy servant: for with my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I am become two bands.
texts.gen.32.11: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he shall come and smite me, and the mother with the children.
texts.gen.32.12: And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.
texts.gen.32.13: And he lodged there that same night; and took of that which came to his hand a present for Esau, his brother;
texts.gen.32.14: Two hundred she-goats, and twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
texts.gen.32.15: Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-asses and ten foals.
texts.gen.32.16: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said to his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.
texts.gen.32.17: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau, my brother, meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither goest thou? and whose are these before thee?
texts.gen.32.18: Then thou shalt say, They are thy servant Jacob's: it is a present sent to my lord Esau: and behold also he is behind us.
texts.gen.32.19: And so he commanded the second, and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying, In this manner shall ye speak to Esau, when ye find him.
texts.gen.32.20: And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.
texts.gen.32.21: So the present went over before him; and he himself lodged that night in the company.
texts.gen.32.22: And he arose that night, and took his two wives, and his two women-servants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford Jabbok.
texts.gen.32.23: And he took them, and sent them over the brook, and sent over that which he had.
texts.gen.32.24: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him, until the breaking of the day.
texts.gen.32.25: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh: and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him.
texts.gen.32.26: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh; And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
texts.gen.32.27: And he said to him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.
texts.gen.32.28: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God, and with men, and hast prevailed.
texts.gen.32.29: And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name: And he said, why is it that thou dost ask after my name? and he blessed him there.
texts.gen.32.30: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.
texts.gen.32.31: And as he passed over Penuel the sun rose upon him, and he halted upon his thigh.
texts.gen.32.32: Therefore the children of Israel eat not of the sinew which shrunk, which is upon the hollow of the thigh, to this day; because he touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh in the sinew that shrunk.
texts.gen.33.1: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children to Leah, and to Rachel, and to the two handmaids.
texts.gen.33.2: And he put the handmaids and their children foremost, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph hindermost.
texts.gen.33.3: And he passed on before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, till he came near to his brother.
texts.gen.33.4: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.
texts.gen.33.5: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children, and said, Who are those with thee? And he said, The children which God hath graciously given to thy servant.
texts.gen.33.6: Then the handmaidens came near, they and their children, and they bowed themselves.
texts.gen.33.7: And Leah also with her children came near, and bowed themselves; and after came Joseph near and Rachel, and they bowed themselves.
texts.gen.33.8: And he said, What meanest thou by all this drove which I met? And he said, these are to find grace in the sight of my lord.
texts.gen.33.9: And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; keep what thou hast to thyself.
texts.gen.33.10: And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand: for therefore I have seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of God, and thou hast been pleased with me.
texts.gen.33.11: Take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough: and he urged him, and he took it.
texts.gen.33.12: And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before thee.
texts.gen.33.13: And he said to him, My lord knoweth that the children are tender, and the flocks and herds with young are with me, and if men should over-drive them one day, all the flock will die.
texts.gen.33.14: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant: and I will lead on slowly, according as the cattle that go before me, and the children are able to endure; until I come to my lord to Seir.
texts.gen.33.15: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee some of the people that are with me: And he said, What needeth it? Let me find grace in the sight of my lord.
texts.gen.33.16: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
texts.gen.33.17: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him a house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
texts.gen.33.18: And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan-aram; and pitched his tent before the city.
texts.gen.33.19: And he bought a part of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for a hundred pieces of money.
texts.gen.33.20: And he erected there an altar, and called it El-elohe-Israel.
texts.gen.34.1: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
texts.gen.34.2: And when Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.
texts.gen.34.3: And his soul cleaved to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spoke kindly to the damsel.
texts.gen.34.4: And Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel for a wife.
texts.gen.34.5: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter (now his sons were with his cattle in the field:) and Jacob held his peace till they had come.
texts.gen.34.6: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to commune with him.
texts.gen.34.7: And the sons of Jacob came from the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel, in lying with Jacob's daughter; which thing ought not to be done.
texts.gen.34.8: And Hamor communed with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you give her to him for a wife.
texts.gen.34.9: And make ye marriages with us: give your daughters to us, and take our daughters to you.
texts.gen.34.10: And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.
texts.gen.34.11: And Shechem said to her father, and to her brethren, Let me find favor in your eyes, and what ye shall say to me, I will give.
texts.gen.34.12: Ask me never so much dower and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say to me: but give me the damsel for a wife.
texts.gen.34.13: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, (because he had defiled Dinah their sister,)
texts.gen.34.14: And they said to them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised: for that would be a reproach to us:
texts.gen.34.15: But in this will we consent to you: If ye will be as we are, that every male of you shall be circumcised;
texts.gen.34.16: Then will we give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
texts.gen.34.17: But if ye will not hearken to us, to be circumcised; then will we take our daughter, and we will be gone.
texts.gen.34.18: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor's son.
texts.gen.34.19: And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob's daughter: and he was more honorable than all the house of his father.
texts.gen.34.20: And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and communed with the men of their city, saying,
texts.gen.34.21: These men are peaceable with us, therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein: for the land, behold, it is large enough for them: let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.
texts.gen.34.22: Only herein, will the men consent to us to dwell with us, to be one people, if every male among us shall be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
texts.gen.34.23: Will not their cattle, and their substance, and every beast of theirs be ours? only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.
texts.gen.34.24: And to Hamor and to Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city: and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.
texts.gen.34.25: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.
texts.gen.34.26: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and went out.
texts.gen.34.27: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city; because they had defiled their sister.
texts.gen.34.28: They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field.
texts.gen.34.29: And all their wealth, and all their little ones, and their wives they took captive, and spoiled even all that was in the house.
texts.gen.34.30: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me odious among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites, and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they will assemble themselves against me, and slay me, and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
texts.gen.34.31: And they said, Should he deal with our sister, as with a harlot?
texts.gen.35.1: And God said to Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dwell there: and make there an altar to God, who appeared to thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
texts.gen.35.2: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments:
texts.gen.35.3: And let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
texts.gen.35.4: And they gave to Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and the ear-rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
texts.gen.35.5: And they journeyed: and the terror of God was on the cities that were round them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
texts.gen.35.6: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan (that is Beth-el) he and all the people that were with him.
texts.gen.35.7: And he erected there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el; because there God appeared to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
texts.gen.35.8: But Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried beneath Beth-el, under an oak: and the name of it was called Allon-bachuth.
texts.gen.35.9: And God appeared to Jacob again when he came out of Padan-aram; and blessed him.
texts.gen.35.10: And God said to him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name; and he called his name Israel.
texts.gen.35.11: And God said to him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a multitude of nations shall spring from thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins.
texts.gen.35.12: And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.
texts.gen.35.13: And God went up from him, in the place where he talked with him.
texts.gen.35.14: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he talked with him, even a pillar of stone: and he poured a drink-offering thereon, and he poured oil thereon.
texts.gen.35.15: And Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him, Beth-el.
texts.gen.35.16: And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labor.
texts.gen.35.17: And it came to pass when she was in hard labor, that the midwife said to her, Fear not; thou shalt have this son also.
texts.gen.35.18: And it came to pass as her soul was in departing (for she died) that she called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin.
texts.gen.35.19: And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth-lehem.
texts.gen.35.20: And Jacob set a pillar on her grave: that is the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
texts.gen.35.21: And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Edar.
texts.gen.35.22: And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: and Israel heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:
texts.gen.35.23: The sons of Leah; Reuben, Jacob's first-born, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun:
texts.gen.35.24: The sons of Rachel; Joseph, and Benjamin:
texts.gen.35.25: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid; Dan, and Naphtali:
texts.gen.35.26: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid; Gad, and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Padan-aram.
texts.gen.35.27: And Jacob came to Isaac his father to Mamre, to the city of Arbah (which is Hebron) where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
texts.gen.35.28: And the days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years.
texts.gen.35.29: And Isaac expired and died, and was gathered to his people, being old and full of days; and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
texts.gen.36.1: Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.
texts.gen.36.2: Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
texts.gen.36.3: And Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebajoth.
texts.gen.36.4: And Adah bore to Esau, Eliphaz; and Bashemath bore Reuel;
texts.gen.36.5: And Aholibamah bore Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah: These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.36.6: And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance which he had acquired in the land of Canaan; and went into the country from the face of his brother Jacob.
texts.gen.36.7: For their riches were more than that they might dwell together: and the land wherein they were strangers could not sustain them, because of their cattle.
texts.gen.36.8: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
texts.gen.36.9: And these are the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites, in mount Seir:
texts.gen.36.10: These are the names of Esau's sons; Eliphaz the son of Adah the wife of Esau, Reuel the son of Bashemath the wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.11: And the sons of Eliphaz were, Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
texts.gen.36.12: And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau's son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek: these were the sons of Adah Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.13: And these are the sons of Reuel; Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: these were the sons of Bashemath Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.14: And these were the sons of Aholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon Esau's wife: and she bore to Esau, Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.
texts.gen.36.15: These were dukes of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the first-born son of Esau; duke Teman, duke Omar, duke Zepho, duke Kenaz,
texts.gen.36.16: Duke Korah, duke Gatam, and duke Amalek: these are the dukes, descendants of Eliphaz, in the land of Edom: these were the sons of Adah.
texts.gen.36.17: And these are the sons of Reuel Esau's son; duke Nahath, duke Zerah, duke Shammah, duke Mizzah: these are the dukes, descendants of Reuel, in the land of Edom: these are the sons of Bashemath Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.18: And these are the sons of Aholibamah Esau's wife; duke Jeush, duke Jaalam, duke Korah: these were the dukes, descendants of Aholibamah the daughter of Anah Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.19: These are the sons of Esau (who is Edom) and these are their dukes.
texts.gen.36.20: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah.
texts.gen.36.21: And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
texts.gen.36.22: And the children of Lotan were Hori, and Heman: and Lotan's sister was Timna.
texts.gen.36.23: And the children of Shobal were these; Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
texts.gen.36.24: And these are the children of Zibeon; both Ajah and Anah; this was that Anah that found the mules in the wilderness, as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father.
texts.gen.36.25: And the children of Anah were these; Dishon, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah.
texts.gen.36.26: And these are the children of Dishon; Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
texts.gen.36.27: The children of Ezer are these; Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Achan.
texts.gen.36.28: The children of Dishan are these; Uz, and Aran.
texts.gen.36.29: These are the dukes, descendants of the Horites; duke Lotan, duke Shobal, duke Zibeon, duke Anah,
texts.gen.36.30: Duke Dishon, duke Ezer, duke Dishan; these are the dukes, descendants of Hori, among their dukes in the land of Seir.
texts.gen.36.31: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.
texts.gen.36.32: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
texts.gen.36.33: And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.34: And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.35: And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad (who smote Midian in the field of Moab) reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.
texts.gen.36.36: And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.37: And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.38: And Saul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.39: And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead; and the name of his city was Pau; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
texts.gen.36.40: And these are the names of the dukes, descendants of Esau, according to their families, after their places, by their names; duke Timnah, duke Alvah, duke Jetheth,
texts.gen.36.41: Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon,
texts.gen.36.42: Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar.
texts.gen.36.43: Duke Magdiel, duke Iram; these are the dukes of Edom, according to their habitations, in the land of their possession: he is Esau the father of the Edomites.
texts.gen.37.1: And Jacob dwelt in the land in which his father was a stranger, in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.37.2: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren, and the lad was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives: and Joseph brought to his father their evil report.
texts.gen.37.3: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colors.
texts.gen.37.4: And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him.
texts.gen.37.5: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.
texts.gen.37.6: And he said to them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:
texts.gen.37.7: For behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves stood around and made obeisance to my sheaf.
texts.gen.37.8: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? and they hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.
texts.gen.37.9: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more: and behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
texts.gen.37.10: And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said to him, what is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?
texts.gen.37.11: And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.
texts.gen.37.12: And his brethren went to feed their father's flock in Shechem.
texts.gen.37.13: And Israel said to Joseph, Do not thy brethren feed the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send thee to them. And he said to him, Here am I.
texts.gen.37.14: And he said to him, Go, I pray thee, see whether it is well with thy brethren, and well with the flocks; and bring me word again. So he sent him from the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
texts.gen.37.15: And a certain man found him, and behold he was wandering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
texts.gen.37.16: And he said, I seek my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, where they feed their flocks.
texts.gen.37.17: And the man said, They have departed hence: for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren and found them in Dothan.
texts.gen.37.18: And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near to them, they conspired against him to slay him.
texts.gen.37.19: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer is coming.
texts.gen.37.20: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit; and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him; and we shall see what will become of his dreams.
texts.gen.37.21: And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him from their hands: and said, Let us not kill him.
texts.gen.37.22: And Reuben said to them, Shed no blood; cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might deliver him from their hands, to bring him back to his father.
texts.gen.37.23: And it came to pass when Joseph had come to his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his coat, his coat of many colors that was on him.
texts.gen.37.24: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty; there was no water in it.
texts.gen.37.25: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a company of Ishmaelites came from Gilead, with their camels bearing spicery, and balm, and myrrh, going to carry them down to Egypt.
texts.gen.37.26: And Judah said to his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood.
texts.gen.37.27: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother, our flesh: and his brethren were content.
texts.gen.37.28: Then there passed by Midianites, merchants; and they drew and lifted Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
texts.gen.37.29: And Reuben returned to the pit; and behold, Joseph was not in the pit: and he rent his clothes.
texts.gen.37.30: And he returned to his brethren, and said, The child is not: and I, whither shall I go?
texts.gen.37.31: And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood:
texts.gen.37.32: And they sent the coat of many colors, and they brought it to their father; and said, This have we found: know now whether it is thy son's coat or not.
texts.gen.37.33: And he knew it, and said, It is my son's coat; an evil beast hath devoured him: Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.
texts.gen.37.34: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
texts.gen.37.35: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave to my son mourning: Thus his father wept for him.
texts.gen.37.36: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh's, and captain of the guard.
texts.gen.38.1: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
texts.gen.38.2: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in to her.
texts.gen.38.3: And she conceived, and bore a son; and he called his name Er.
texts.gen.38.4: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and she called his name Onan.
texts.gen.38.5: And she yet again conceived, and bore a son; and called his name Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bore him.
texts.gen.38.6: And Judah took a wife for Er his first-born, whose name was Tamar.
texts.gen.38.7: And Er, Judah's first-born, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him.
texts.gen.38.8: And Judah said to Onan, Go in to thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
texts.gen.38.9: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his: and it came to pass, when he went in to his brother's wife, that he frustrated the purpose, lest he should give seed to his brother.
texts.gen.38.10: And the thing which he did displeased the LORD: wherefore he slew him also.
texts.gen.38.11: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter-in-law, Remain a widow at thy father's house, till Shelah my son shall be grown; (for he said, Lest perhaps he die also as his brethren did:) and Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
texts.gen.38.12: And in process of time, the daughter of Shuah Judah's wife died: and Judah was comforted, and went up to his sheep-shearers to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
texts.gen.38.13: And it was told to Tamar, saying, Behold, thy father-in-law goeth up to Timnath, to shear his sheep.
texts.gen.38.14: And she put off from her, her widow's garments, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath: for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given to him for a wife.
texts.gen.38.15: When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a harlot; because she had covered her face.
texts.gen.38.16: And he turned to her by the way, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me have access to thee; (for he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law:) and she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayst have access to me?
texts.gen.38.17: And he said, I will send thee a kid from the flock: and she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou sendest it?
texts.gen.38.18: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? and she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thy hand: and he gave them to her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him.
texts.gen.38.19: And she arose and went her way and laid by her vail from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
texts.gen.38.20: And Judah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive his pledge from the woman's hand: but he found her not.
texts.gen.38.21: Then he asked the men of that place, saying, where is the harlot that was openly by the way-side? and they said, There was no harlot in this place.
texts.gen.38.22: And he returned to Judah, and said, I cannot find her; and also the men of the place said, that there was no harlot in this place.
texts.gen.38.23: And Judah said, Let her take it to her, lest we be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
texts.gen.38.24: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told to Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath played the harlot; and also, behold she is with child by lewdness: and Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.
texts.gen.38.25: When she was brought forth, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, By the man whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff.
texts.gen.38.26: And Judah acknowledged them, and said She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son: and he knew her again no more.
texts.gen.38.27: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that behold, twins were in her womb.
texts.gen.38.28: And it came to pass when she travailed, that the one put out his hand; and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.
texts.gen.38.29: And it came to pass as he drew back his hand, that behold, his brother came out; and she said, How hast thou broken forth? this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.
texts.gen.38.30: And afterwards came out his brother that had the scarlet thread upon his hand; and his name was called Zarah.
texts.gen.39.1: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt: and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmaelites, who had brought him down thither.
texts.gen.39.2: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man: and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
texts.gen.39.3: And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
texts.gen.39.4: And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.
texts.gen.39.5: And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake: and the blessing of the LORD was on all that he had in the house, and in the field.
texts.gen.39.6: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand; and he knew not aught he had, save the bread which he ate; and Joseph was a goodly person, and well favored.
texts.gen.39.7: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph: and she said, Lie with me.
texts.gen.39.8: But he refused, and said to his master's wife, Behold, my master knoweth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand:
texts.gen.39.9: There is none greater in his house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
texts.gen.39.10: And it came to pass, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
texts.gen.39.11: And it came to pass, about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his business; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
texts.gen.39.12: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went out.
texts.gen.39.13: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and had fled forth,
texts.gen.39.14: That she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying, See, he hath brought in a Hebrew to us to mock us: he came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:
texts.gen.39.15: And it came to pass, when he heard that I raised my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and went out.
texts.gen.39.16: And she laid up his garment by her until his lord came home.
texts.gen.39.17: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought to us, came in to me to mock me.
texts.gen.39.18: And it came to pass, as I raised my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled.
texts.gen.39.19: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.
texts.gen.39.20: And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.
texts.gen.39.21: But the LORD was with Joseph, and showed him mercy, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
texts.gen.39.22: And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatever they did there, was done by him.
texts.gen.39.23: The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the LORD was with him: and that which he did the LORD made it to prosper.
texts.gen.40.1: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker had offended their lord the king of Egypt.
texts.gen.40.2: And Pharaoh was wroth with two of his officers, with the chief of the butlers, and with the chief of the bakers.
texts.gen.40.3: And he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
texts.gen.40.4: And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them, and he served them; and they continued a season in custody.
texts.gen.40.5: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream; the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.
texts.gen.40.6: And Joseph came to them in the morning, and looked upon them, and behold, they were sad.
texts.gen.40.7: And he asked Pharaoh's officers that were with him in the ward of his lord's house, saying, Why look ye so sad to-day?
texts.gen.40.8: And they said to him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said to them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.
texts.gen.40.9: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;
texts.gen.40.10: And on the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and its blossoms shot forth; and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes:
texts.gen.40.11: And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
texts.gen.40.12: And Joseph said to him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days;
texts.gen.40.13: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee to thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.
texts.gen.40.14: But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and show kindness to me, I pray thee, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:
texts.gen.40.15: For indeed I was stolen away from the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
texts.gen.40.16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, I also was in my dream, and behold, I had three white baskets on my head:
texts.gen.40.17: And in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bake-meats for Pharaoh; and the birds ate them out of the basket upon my head.
texts.gen.40.18: And Joseph answered, and said, This is the interpretation of it: The three baskets are three days:
texts.gen.40.19: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.
texts.gen.40.20: And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh's birth-day, that he made a feast to all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants.
texts.gen.40.21: And he restored the chief butler to his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand:
texts.gen.40.22: But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
texts.gen.40.23: Yet the chief butler did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
texts.gen.41.1: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the river.
texts.gen.41.2: And behold, there came up out of the river seven well-favored cows and fat-fleshed; and they fed in a meadow.
texts.gen.41.3: And behold, seven other cows came up after them out of the river, ill-favored and lean-fleshed; and stood by the other cows upon the brink of the river.
texts.gen.41.4: And the ill-favored and lean-fleshed cows ate up the seven well-favored and fat cows. So Pharaoh awoke.
texts.gen.41.5: And he slept and dreamed the second time: and behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good.
texts.gen.41.6: And behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.
texts.gen.41.7: And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
texts.gen.41.8: And it came to pass in the morning, that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.9: Then spoke the chief butler to Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:
texts.gen.41.10: Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in custody in the captain of the guard's house, both me, and the chief baker:
texts.gen.41.11: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he: we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
texts.gen.41.12: And there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he interpreted.
texts.gen.41.13: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was: me he restored to my office, and him he hanged.
texts.gen.41.14: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came before Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard it said of thee, that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it.
texts.gen.41.16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
texts.gen.41.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the river:
texts.gen.41.18: And behold, there came out of the river seven cows, fat-fleshed, and well-favored; and they fed in a meadow:
texts.gen.41.19: And behold, seven other cows came out after them, poor, and very ill-favored, and lean-fleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness:
texts.gen.41.20: And the lean and the ill-favored cows ate up the first seven fat cows:
texts.gen.41.21: And when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they were still ill-favored, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
texts.gen.41.22: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, full and good:
texts.gen.41.23: And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them:
texts.gen.41.24: And the thin ears devoured the seven good ears: and I told this to the magicians; but there was none that could explain it to me.
texts.gen.41.25: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one; God hath showed Pharaoh what he is about to do.
texts.gen.41.26: The seven good cows are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.
texts.gen.41.27: And the seven thin and ill-favored cows that came up after them are seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind will be seven years of famine.
texts.gen.41.28: This is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh: What God is about to do he showeth to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.29: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:
texts.gen.41.30: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;
texts.gen.41.31: And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of the famine following: for it will be very grievous.
texts.gen.41.32: And for that the dream was doubled to Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
texts.gen.41.33: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.34: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.
texts.gen.41.35: And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh; and let them keep food in the cities.
texts.gen.41.36: And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land may not perish through the famine.
texts.gen.41.37: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
texts.gen.41.38: And Pharaoh said to his servants, Can we find such a man as this is, a man in whom the spirit of God is?
texts.gen.41.39: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shown thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:
texts.gen.41.40: Thou shalt be over my house, and according to thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.
texts.gen.41.41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.42: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
texts.gen.41.43: And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had: and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.45: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him for a wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On: and Joseph went over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.46: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt: and Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.47: And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfulls.
texts.gen.41.48: And he gathered all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field which was around every city, he laid up in the same.
texts.gen.41.49: And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number.
texts.gen.41.50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came: which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bore to him.
texts.gen.41.51: And Joseph called the name of the first-born Manasseh: For God, said he, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house.
texts.gen.41.52: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: for God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.
texts.gen.41.53: And the seven years of plenteousness that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.
