texts.gen.41.54: And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
texts.gen.41.55: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, Go to Joseph; what he saith to you, do.
texts.gen.41.56: And the famine was over all the face of the earth; and Joseph opened all the store-houses, and sold to the Egyptians; and the famine became severe in the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.57: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph to buy corn; because the famine was distressing in all lands.
texts.gen.42.1: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?
texts.gen.42.2: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: go down thither, and buy for us from thence; that we may live, and not die.
texts.gen.42.3: And Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.
texts.gen.42.4: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren: for he said, Lest perhaps mischief shall befall him.
texts.gen.42.5: And the sons of Israel came to buy corn among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.6: And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brethren came, and bowed themselves before him with their faces to the earth.
texts.gen.42.7: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange to them, and spoke roughly to them; and he said to them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.
texts.gen.42.8: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.
texts.gen.42.9: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said to them, Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land have ye come.
texts.gen.42.10: And they said to him, No, my lord, but to buy food have thy servants come.
texts.gen.42.11: We are all one man's sons; we are true men; thy servants are no spies.
texts.gen.42.12: And he said to them, No, but to see the nakedness of the land have ye come.
texts.gen.42.13: And they said, Thy servants are twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is not.
texts.gen.42.14: And Joseph said to them, That is what I spoke to you, saying, Ye are spies:
texts.gen.42.15: By this ye shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother shall come hither.
texts.gen.42.16: Send one of you, and let him bring your brother, and ye shall be kept in prison, that your words may be proved, whether there is any truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye are spies.
texts.gen.42.17: And he put them all together into custody three days.
texts.gen.42.18: And Joseph said to them the third day, This do, and live; for I fear God:
texts.gen.42.19: If ye are true men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go ye, carry corn for the famine of your houses:
texts.gen.42.20: But bring your youngest brother to me; so shall your words be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.
texts.gen.42.21: And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
texts.gen.42.22: And Reuben answered them, saying, Did I not speak to you, saying, Do not sin against the young man; and ye would not hear? therefore behold also his blood is required.
texts.gen.42.23: And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for he spoke to them by an interpreter.
texts.gen.42.24: And he turned himself away from them, and wept; and returned to them again, and communed with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.
texts.gen.42.25: Then Joseph commanded to fill their sacks with corn, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way: and thus did he to them.
texts.gen.42.26: And they loaded their asses with the corn, and departed thence.
texts.gen.42.27: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the inn, he espied his money: for behold, it was in his sack's mouth.
texts.gen.42.28: And he said to his brethren, My money is restored; and see it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this that God hath done to us?
texts.gen.42.29: And they came to Jacob their father to the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell them, saying,
texts.gen.42.30: The man who is the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.
texts.gen.42.31: And we said to him, We are true men; we are no spies:
texts.gen.42.32: We are twelve brethren, sons of our father: one is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.33: And the man, the lord of the country, said to us, By this shall I know that ye are true men: leave one of your brethren here with me, and take food for the famine of your households, and depart:
texts.gen.42.34: And bring your youngest brother to me: then shall I know that ye are no spies, but that ye are true men: then will I deliver to you your brother, and ye shall traffick in the land.
texts.gen.42.35: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man's bundle of money was in his sack; and when they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.
texts.gen.42.36: And Jacob their father said to them, Me have ye bereaved: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away: all these things are against me.
texts.gen.42.37: And Reuben spoke to his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.
texts.gen.42.38: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief shall befall him by the way in which ye go, then will ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.
texts.gen.43.1: And the famine was severe in the land.
texts.gen.43.2: And it came to pass, when they had consumed the corn which they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, Go again, buy us a little food.
texts.gen.43.3: And Judah spoke to him, saying, The man did solemnly protest to us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
texts.gen.43.4: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:
texts.gen.43.5: But if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down, for the man said to us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
texts.gen.43.6: And Israel said, Why dealt ye so ill with me, as to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?
texts.gen.43.7: And they said, The man asked us strictly concerning our state, and our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye another brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: Could we certainly know that he would say, Bring your brother down?
texts.gen.43.8: And Judah said to Israel, his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.
texts.gen.43.9: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not to thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:
texts.gen.43.10: For except we had delayed, surely now we had returned this second time.
texts.gen.43.11: And their father Israel said to them, If it must be so now, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry to the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:
texts.gen.43.12: And take double money in your hand; and the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks, carry it again in your hand; it may be it was an oversight:
texts.gen.43.13: Take also your brother, and arise, go again to the man:
texts.gen.43.14: And God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin: If I be bereaved, I am bereaved.
texts.gen.43.15: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and arose, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
texts.gen.43.16: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the ruler of his house, Bring these men home, and slay, and make ready: for these men shall dine with me at noon.
texts.gen.43.17: And the man did as Joseph commanded: and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
texts.gen.43.18: And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Joseph's house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time, are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bond-men, and our asses.
texts.gen.43.19: And they came near to the steward of Joseph's house, and they communed with him at the door of the house,
texts.gen.43.20: And said, O sir, we came down indeed at the first time to buy food:
texts.gen.43.21: And it came to pass, when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and behold, every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.
texts.gen.43.22: And other money have we brought down in our hands to buy food: we cannot tell who put our money in our sacks.
texts.gen.43.23: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out to them.
texts.gen.43.24: And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.
texts.gen.43.25: And they made ready the present against Joseph should come at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.
texts.gen.43.26: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.
texts.gen.43.27: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spoke? Is he yet alive?
texts.gen.43.28: And they answered, Thy servant, our father, is in good health, he is yet alive: and they bowed their heads and made obeisance.
texts.gen.43.29: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, Is this your younger brother, of whom ye spoke to me? And he said, God be gracious to thee, my son.
texts.gen.43.30: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels yearned towards his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.
texts.gen.43.31: And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.
texts.gen.43.32: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who ate with him, by themselves; because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
texts.gen.43.33: And they sat before him, the first-born according to his birth-right, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men wondered one at another.
texts.gen.43.34: And he took and sent messes to them from before him: but Benjamin's mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.
texts.gen.44.1: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth.
texts.gen.44.2: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn money: and he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
texts.gen.44.3: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they, and their asses.
texts.gen.44.4: And when they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, Arise, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say to them, Why have ye rewarded evil for good?
texts.gen.44.5: Is not this the cup in which my lord drinketh, and by which indeed he divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.
texts.gen.44.6: And he overtook them, and he spoke to them these same words.
texts.gen.44.7: And they said to him, Why saith my lord these words? Far be it from us that thy servants should do according to this thing:
texts.gen.44.8: Behold, the money which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again to thee from the land of Canaan: how then should we steal from thy lord's house silver or gold?
texts.gen.44.9: With whom soever of thy servants it shall be found, both let him die, and we also will be my lord's bond-men.
texts.gen.44.10: And he said, Now also let it be according to your words: he with whom it shall be found, shall be my servant; and ye shall be blameless.
texts.gen.44.11: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
texts.gen.44.12: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
texts.gen.44.13: Then they rent their clothes, and loaded every man his ass, and returned to the city.
texts.gen.44.14: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph's house, (for he was yet there:) and they fell before him on the ground.
texts.gen.44.15: And Joseph said to them, What deed is this that ye have done? knew ye not that such a man as I can certainly divine?
texts.gen.44.16: And Judah said, What shall we say to my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold we are my lord's servants, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.
texts.gen.44.17: And he said, Far be it from me that I should do so: the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my servant; and as for you, go in peace to your father.
texts.gen.44.18: Then Judah came near to him, and said, Oh my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not thy anger burn against thy servant; for thou art even as Pharaoh.
texts.gen.44.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?
texts.gen.44.20: And we said to my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one: and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.
texts.gen.44.21: And thou saidst to thy servants, Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes upon him.
texts.gen.44.22: And we said to my lord, The lad cannot leave his father; for if he should leave his father, his father would die.
texts.gen.44.23: And thou saidst to thy servants, Except your youngest brother shall come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.
texts.gen.44.24: And it came to pass, when we came to thy servant, my father, we told him the words of my lord.
texts.gen.44.25: And our father said, Go again; buy us a little food.
texts.gen.44.26: And we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother shall be with us, then will we go down; for we may not see the man's face, except our youngest brother shall be with us.
texts.gen.44.27: And thy servant my father, said to us, Ye know that my wife bore me two sons:
texts.gen.44.28: And the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I have not seen him since:
texts.gen.44.29: And if ye take this also from me, and mischief shall befall him, ye will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.
texts.gen.44.30: Now therefore, when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not with us; (seeing that his life is bound up in the lad's life)
texts.gen.44.31: It shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants will bring down the gray hairs of thy servant our father, with sorrow to the grave.
texts.gen.44.32: For thy servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, If I bring him not to thee, then I will bear the blame to my father for ever.
texts.gen.44.33: Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad, a bond-man to my lord; and let the lad return with his brethren.
texts.gen.44.34: For how shall I return to my father, and the lad be not with me? lest perhaps I see the evil that shall come on my father.
texts.gen.45.1: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me: and there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brethren.
texts.gen.45.2: And he wept aloud; and the Egyptians and the house of Pharaoh heard.
texts.gen.45.3: And Joseph said to his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.
texts.gen.45.4: And Joseph said to his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you: and they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
texts.gen.45.5: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither; for God sent me before you to preserve life.
texts.gen.45.6: For these two years hath the famine been in the land: and yet there are five years, in which there shall neither be tillage nor harvest.
texts.gen.45.7: And God sent me before you, to preserve for you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
texts.gen.45.8: So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.45.9: Haste ye, and return to my father, and say to him, Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me; delay not:
texts.gen.45.10: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near to me, thou, and thy children, and thy children's children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:
texts.gen.45.11: And there will I nourish thee, (for yet there are five years of famine,) lest thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast, should come to poverty.
texts.gen.45.12: And behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh to you.
texts.gen.45.13: And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen: and ye shall haste, and bring down my father hither.
texts.gen.45.14: And he fell upon his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
texts.gen.45.15: Moreover, he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.
texts.gen.45.16: And the fame of this was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, Joseph's brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
texts.gen.45.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Say to thy brethren, This do ye; load your beasts, and go, return to the land of Canaan;
texts.gen.45.18: And take your father, and your households, and come to me: and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.
texts.gen.45.19: Now thou art commanded, this do ye; take for yourselves wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
texts.gen.45.20: Also regard not your furniture; for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.
texts.gen.45.21: And the children of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
texts.gen.45.22: To all of them he gave each man changes of raiment: but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment.
texts.gen.45.23: And to his father he sent after this manner; ten asses laden with the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses laden with corn and bread and meat, for his father by the way.
texts.gen.45.24: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said to them, See that ye contend not by the way.
texts.gen.45.25: And they went up from Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father,
texts.gen.45.26: And told him, saying, Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And Jacob's heart fainted, for he believed them not.
texts.gen.45.27: And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them: and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:
texts.gen.45.28: And Israel said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.
texts.gen.46.1: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
texts.gen.46.2: And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob: and he said, Here am I.
texts.gen.46.3: And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation:
texts.gen.46.4: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.
texts.gen.46.5: And Jacob rose up from Beer-sheba: and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
texts.gen.46.6: And they took their cattle, and their goods which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed with him:
texts.gen.46.7: His sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and all his seed brought he with him into Egypt.
texts.gen.46.8: And these are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob's first-born.
texts.gen.46.9: And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
texts.gen.46.10: And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.
texts.gen.46.11: And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
texts.gen.46.12: And the sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zerah: but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pharez were Hezron, and Hamul.
texts.gen.46.13: And the sons of Issachar; Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
texts.gen.46.14: And the sons of Zebulun; Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
texts.gen.46.15: These are the sons of Leah, which she bore to Jacob in Padan-aram, with his daughter Dinah: all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty and three.
texts.gen.46.16: And the sons of Gad; Ziphion, and Haggai, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
texts.gen.46.17: And the sons of Asher; Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel.
texts.gen.46.18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter: and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
texts.gen.46.19: The sons of Rachel Jacob's wife; Joseph, and Benjamin.
texts.gen.46.20: And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bore to him.
texts.gen.46.21: And the sons of Benjamin were Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
texts.gen.46.22: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob; all the souls were fourteen.
texts.gen.46.23: And the sons of Dan; Hushim.
texts.gen.46.24: And the sons of Naphtali; Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
texts.gen.46.25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
texts.gen.46.26: All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, who came out of his loins, besides Jacob's sons' wives, all the souls were sixty and six.
texts.gen.46.27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.
texts.gen.46.28: And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to direct his face to Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.46.29: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went to meet Israel his father to Goshen; and presented himself to him: and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
texts.gen.46.30: And Israel said to Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.
texts.gen.46.31: And Joseph said to his brethren, and to his father's house, I will go up, and show Pharaoh, and say to him, My brethren, and my father's house, who were in the land of Canaan are come to me.
texts.gen.46.32: And the men are shepherds, for their employment hath been to feed cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.
texts.gen.46.33: And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What is your occupation?
texts.gen.46.34: That ye shall say, The occupation of thy servants hath been about cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.
texts.gen.47.1: Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.47.2: And he took some of his brethren, even five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.3: And Pharaoh said to his brethren, What is your occupation? And they said to Pharaoh, Thy servants are shepherds, both we, and also our fathers.
texts.gen.47.4: They said moreover to Pharaoh, We have come to sojourn in the land: for thy servants have no pasture for their flocks, for the famine is severe in the land of Canaan: now therefore, we pray thee, let thy servants dwell in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.47.5: And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren have come to thee:
texts.gen.47.6: The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell; and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.
texts.gen.47.7: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, How old art thou?
texts.gen.47.9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years: few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, nor have they attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.
texts.gen.47.10: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.11: And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
texts.gen.47.12: And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father's household, with bread according to their families.
texts.gen.47.13: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very distressing, so that the land of Egypt, and all the land of Canaan, fainted by reason of the famine.
texts.gen.47.14: And Joseph gathered all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.
texts.gen.47.15: And when money failed in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence: for the money faileth.
texts.gen.47.16: And Joseph said, Give your cattle; and I will give you for your cattle, if money hath failed.
texts.gen.47.17: And they brought their cattle to Joseph: and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, and for the flocks, and for the cattle of the herds, and for the asses; and he fed them with bread, for all their cattle, for that year.
texts.gen.47.18: When that year was ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, We will not hide from my lord, how that our money is spent; my lord also hath our herds of cattle; there is not aught left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies and our lands:
texts.gen.47.19: Why shall we die before thy eyes, both we and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh: and give us seed, that we may live, and not die, that the land be not desolate.
texts.gen.47.20: And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them: so the land became Pharaoh's.
texts.gen.47.21: And as for the people, he removed them to cities from one end of the borders of Egypt even to the other end thereof.
texts.gen.47.22: Only the land of the priests bought he not; for the priests had a portion assigned them by Pharaoh, and ate their portion which Pharaoh gave them: wherefore they sold not their lands.
texts.gen.47.23: Then Joseph said to the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is seed for you, and ye shall sow the land.
texts.gen.47.24: And it shall come to pass in the increase, that ye shall give the fifth part to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
texts.gen.47.25: And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find grace in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's servants.
texts.gen.47.26: And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth part; except the land of the priests only, which became not Pharaoh's.
texts.gen.47.27: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen; and they had possessions in it and grew, and multiplied exceedingly.
texts.gen.47.28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the whole age of Jacob was a hundred and forty seven years.
texts.gen.47.29: And the time drew nigh that Israel must die: and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, If now I have found grace in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt:
texts.gen.47.30: But I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying-place. And he said, I will do as thou hast said.
texts.gen.47.31: And he said, Swear to me: and he swore to him. And Israel bowed himself upon the bed's head.
texts.gen.48.1: And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
texts.gen.48.2: And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh to thee: and Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
texts.gen.48.3: And Jacob said to Joseph, God Almighty appeared to me at Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
texts.gen.48.4: And said to me, Behold I will make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a multitude of people; and will give this land to thy seed after thee, for an everlasting possession.
texts.gen.48.5: And now, thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, who were born to thee in the land of Egypt, before I came to thee into Egypt, are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.
texts.gen.48.6: And thy issue, which thou begettest after them, shall be thine, and shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.
texts.gen.48.7: And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan, in the way, when yet there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and I buried her there in the way of Ephrath, the same is Beth-lehem.
texts.gen.48.8: And Israel beheld Joseph's sons, and said, Who are these?
texts.gen.48.9: And Joseph said to his father, They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, to me, and I will bless them.
texts.gen.48.10: (Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see:) And he brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
texts.gen.48.11: And Israel said to Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and lo, God hath shown me also thy seed.
texts.gen.48.12: And Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
texts.gen.48.13: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand towards Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand towards Israel's right hand, and brought them near to him.
texts.gen.48.14: And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh's head, guiding his hands by design; for Manasseh was the first-born.
texts.gen.48.15: And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God who hath fed me all my life long to this day,
texts.gen.48.16: The angel who hath redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac: and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.
texts.gen.48.17: And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he lifted his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
texts.gen.48.18: And Joseph said to his father, Not so, my father; for this is the first-born; put thy right hand upon his head.
texts.gen.48.19: And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.
texts.gen.48.20: And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
texts.gen.48.21: And Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I die; but God shall be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
texts.gen.48.22: Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.
texts.gen.49.1: And Jacob called to his sons, and said, Assemble yourselves, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.
texts.gen.49.2: Assemble yourselves, and hear, ye sons of Jacob: and hearken to Israel your father.
texts.gen.49.3: Reuben, thou art my first-born, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellence of dignity, and the excellence of power:
texts.gen.49.4: Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed; then defiledst thou it; he went up to my couch.
texts.gen.49.5: Simeon and Levi are brethren: instruments of cruelty are in, their habitations.
texts.gen.49.6: O my soul, come not thou into their secret; to their assembly, my honor, be not thou united: for in their anger they slew a man, and in their self-will they digged down a wall.
texts.gen.49.7: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce: and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.
texts.gen.49.8: Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise; thy hand shall be on the neck of thy enemies: thy father's children shall bow down before thee.
texts.gen.49.9: Judah is a lion's whelp; from the prey, my son, thou hast gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion: who shall rouse him up?
texts.gen.49.10: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh shall come: and to him shall be the gathering of the people.
texts.gen.49.11: Binding his foal to the vine, and his ass's colt to the choice vine; he washed his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood of grapes:
texts.gen.49.12: His eyes shall be red with wine, and his teeth white with milk.
texts.gen.49.13: Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for a haven of ships; and his border shall be to Zidon.
texts.gen.49.14: Issachar is a strong ass, couching down between two burdens:
texts.gen.49.15: And he saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant to tribute.
texts.gen.49.16: Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.
texts.gen.49.17: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, that biteth the horse-heels, so that his rider shall fall backward.
texts.gen.49.18: I have waited for thy salvation O LORD.
texts.gen.49.19: Gad, a troop shall overcome him: but he shall overcome at the last.
texts.gen.49.20: Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties.
texts.gen.49.21: Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words.
texts.gen.49.22: Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall:
texts.gen.49.23: The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him:
texts.gen.49.24: But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob: from thence is the shepherd the stone of Israel:
texts.gen.49.25: Even by the God of thy father, who shall help thee, and by the Almighty, who shall bless thee with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lieth beneath, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb:
texts.gen.49.26: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors to the utmost bound of the everlasting hills; they shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.
texts.gen.49.27: Benjamin shall raven as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.
texts.gen.49.28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is it which their father spoke to them, and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.
texts.gen.49.29: And he charged them, and said to them, I am to be gathered to my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite.
texts.gen.49.30: In the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field of Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a burying-place.
texts.gen.49.31: (There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah,)
texts.gen.49.32: The purchase of the field and of the cave that is in it, was from the children of Heth.
texts.gen.49.33: And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he drew his feet into the bed, and expired, and was gathered to his people.
texts.gen.50.1: And Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.
texts.gen.50.2: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel.
texts.gen.50.3: And forty days were fulfilled for him; (for so are fulfilled the days of those who are embalmed:) and the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.
texts.gen.50.4: And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found grace in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
texts.gen.50.5: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.
texts.gen.50.6: And Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.
texts.gen.50.7: And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
texts.gen.50.8: And all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father's house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds they left in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.50.9: And there went with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.
texts.gen.50.10: And they came to the threshing-floor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.
texts.gen.50.11: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abel-mizraim, which is beyond Jordan.
texts.gen.50.12: And his sons did to him according as he commanded them:
texts.gen.50.13: For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a burying-place of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.
texts.gen.50.14: And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brethren, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
texts.gen.50.15: And when Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will perhaps hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did to him.
texts.gen.50.16: And they sent messengers to Joseph, saying, Thy father commanded before he died, saying,
texts.gen.50.17: So shall ye say to Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did to thee evil: and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
texts.gen.50.18: And his brethren also went and fell down before his face: and they said, Behold, we are thy servants.
texts.gen.50.19: And Joseph said to them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?
texts.gen.50.20: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save many people alive.
texts.gen.50.21: Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
texts.gen.50.22: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his father's house: and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
texts.gen.50.23: And Joseph saw Ephraim's children of the third generation: the children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were brought up upon Joseph's knees.
texts.gen.50.24: And Joseph said to his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land, to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
texts.gen.50.25: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.
texts.gen.50.26: So Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

texts.gen.1.1: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
texts.gen.1.2: And the earth was waste and empty, and darkness was on the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters.
texts.gen.1.3: And God said, Let there be light. And there was light.
texts.gen.1.4: And God saw the light that it was good; and God divided between the light and the darkness.
texts.gen.1.5: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning -- the first day.
texts.gen.1.6: And God said, Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it be a division between waters and waters.
texts.gen.1.7: And God made the expanse, and divided between the waters that are under the expanse and the waters that are above the expanse; and it was so.
texts.gen.1.8: And God called the expanse Heavens. And there was evening, and there was morning -- a second day.
texts.gen.1.9: And God said, Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together to one place, and let the dry [land] appear. And it was so.
texts.gen.1.10: And God called the dry [land] Earth, and the gathering together of the waters he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
texts.gen.1.11: And God said, Let the earth cause grass to spring up, herb producing seed, fruit-trees yielding fruit after their kind, the seed of which is in them, on the earth. And it was so.
texts.gen.1.12: And the earth brought forth grass, herb producing seed after its kind, and trees yielding fruit, the seed of which is in them, after their kind. And God saw that it was good.
texts.gen.1.13: And there was evening, and there was morning -- a third day.
texts.gen.1.14: And God said, Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens, to divide between the day and the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years;
texts.gen.1.15: and let them be for lights in the expanse of the heavens, to give light on the earth. And it was so.
texts.gen.1.16: And God made the two great lights, the great light to rule the day, and the small light to rule the night, -- and the stars.
texts.gen.1.17: And God set them in the expanse of the heavens, to give light on the earth,
texts.gen.1.18: and to rule during the day and during the night, and to divide between the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
texts.gen.1.19: And there was evening, and there was morning -- a fourth day.
texts.gen.1.20: And God said, Let the waters swarm with swarms of living souls, and let fowl fly above the earth in the expanse of the heavens.
texts.gen.1.21: And God created the great sea monsters, and every living soul that moves with which the waters swarm, after their kind, and every winged fowl after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
texts.gen.1.22: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply on the earth.
texts.gen.1.23: And there was evening, and there was morning -- a fifth day.
texts.gen.1.24: And God said, Let the earth bring forth living souls after their kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth, after their kind. And it was so.
texts.gen.1.25: And God made the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
texts.gen.1.26: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over the whole earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth on the earth.
texts.gen.1.27: And God created Man in his image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
texts.gen.1.28: And God blessed them; and God said to them, Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over every animal that moveth on the earth.
texts.gen.1.29: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb producing seed that is on the whole earth, and every tree in which is the fruit of a tree producing seed: it shall be food for you;
texts.gen.1.30: and to every animal of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to everything that creepeth on the earth, in which is a living soul, every green herb for food. And it was so.
texts.gen.1.31: And God saw everything that he had made, and behold it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning -- the sixth day.
texts.gen.2.1: And the heavens and the earth and all their host were finished.
texts.gen.2.2: And God had finished on the seventh day his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
texts.gen.2.3: And God blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it, because that on it he rested from all his work which God had created in making it.
texts.gen.2.4: These are the histories of the heavens and the earth, when they were created, in the day that Jehovah Elohim made earth and heavens,
texts.gen.2.5: and every shrub of the field before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field before it grew; for Jehovah Elohim had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no man to till the ground.
texts.gen.2.6: But a mist went up from the earth, and moistened the whole surface of the ground.
texts.gen.2.7: And Jehovah Elohim formed Man, dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and Man became a living soul.
texts.gen.2.8: And Jehovah Elohim planted a garden in Eden eastward, and there put Man whom he had formed.
texts.gen.2.9: And out of the ground Jehovah Elohim made every tree grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; and the tree of life, in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
texts.gen.2.10: And a river went out of Eden, to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became four main streams.
texts.gen.2.11: The name of the one is Pison: that is it which surrounds the whole land of Havilah, where the gold is.
texts.gen.2.12: And the gold of that land is good; bdellium and the onyx stone are there.
texts.gen.2.13: And the name of the second river is Gihon: that is it which surrounds the whole land of Cush.
texts.gen.2.14: And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which flows forward toward Asshur. And the fourth river, that is Euphrates.
texts.gen.2.15: And Jehovah Elohim took Man, and put him into the garden of Eden, to till it and to guard it.
texts.gen.2.16: And Jehovah Elohim commanded Man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou shalt freely eat;
texts.gen.2.17: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it; for in the day that thou eatest of it thou shalt certainly die.
texts.gen.2.18: And Jehovah Elohim said, It is not good that Man should be alone; I will make him a helpmate, his like.
texts.gen.2.19: And out of the ground Jehovah Elohim had formed every animal of the field and all fowl of the heavens, and brought [them] to Man, to see what he would call them; and whatever Man called each living soul, that was its name.
texts.gen.2.20: And Man gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; but as for Adam, he found no helpmate, his like.
texts.gen.2.21: And Jehovah Elohim caused a deep sleep to fall upon Man; and he slept. And he took one of his ribs and closed up flesh in its stead.
texts.gen.2.22: And Jehovah Elohim built the rib that he had taken from Man into a woman; and brought her to Man.
texts.gen.2.23: And Man said, This time it is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh: this shall be called Woman, because this was taken out of a man.
texts.gen.2.24: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and cleave to his wife; and they shall become one flesh.
texts.gen.2.25: And they were both naked, Man and his wife, and were not ashamed.
texts.gen.3.1: And the serpent was more crafty than any animal of the field which Jehovah Elohim had made. And it said to the woman, Is it even so, that God has said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
texts.gen.3.2: And the woman said to the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden;
texts.gen.3.3: but of the fruit of the tree that is in the midst of the garden, God has said, Ye shall not eat of it, and ye shall not touch it, lest ye die.
texts.gen.3.4: And the serpent said to the woman, Ye will not certainly die;
texts.gen.3.5: but God knows that in the day ye eat of it, your eyes will be opened, and ye will be as God, knowing good and evil.
texts.gen.3.6: And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a pleasure for the eyes, and the tree was to be desired to give intelligence; and she took of its fruit, and ate, and gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.
texts.gen.3.7: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked. And they sewed fig-leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
texts.gen.3.8: And they heard the voice of Jehovah Elohim, walking in the garden in the cool of the day. And Man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Jehovah Elohim, in the midst of the trees of the garden.
texts.gen.3.9: And Jehovah Elohim called to Man, and said to him, Where art thou?
texts.gen.3.10: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I feared, because I am naked; and I hid myself.
texts.gen.3.11: And he said, Who told thee that thou art naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree of which I commanded thee not to eat?
texts.gen.3.12: And Man said, The woman, whom thou hast given [to be] with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.
texts.gen.3.13: And Jehovah Elohim said to the woman, What is this thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent deceived me, and I ate.
texts.gen.3.14: And Jehovah Elohim said to the serpent, Because thou hast done this, be thou cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field. On thy belly shalt thou go, and eat dust all the days of thy life.
texts.gen.3.15: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; he shall crush thy head, and thou shalt crush his heel.
texts.gen.3.16: To the woman he said, I will greatly increase thy travail and thy pregnancy; with pain thou shalt bear children; and to thy husband shall be thy desire, and he shall rule over thee.
texts.gen.3.17: And to Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and eaten of the tree of which I commanded thee saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed be the ground on thy account; with toil shalt thou eat [of] it all the days of thy life;
texts.gen.3.18: and thorns and thistles shall it yield thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field.
texts.gen.3.19: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, until thou return to the ground: for out of it wast thou taken. For dust thou art; and unto dust shalt thou return.
texts.gen.3.20: And Man called his wife's name Eve; because she is the mother of all living.
texts.gen.3.21: And Jehovah Elohim made Adam and his wife coats of skin, and clothed them.
texts.gen.3.22: And Jehovah Elohim said, Behold, Man is become as one of us, to know good and evil. And now, lest he stretch out his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever ...!
texts.gen.3.23: Therefore Jehovah Elohim sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.
texts.gen.3.24: And he drove out Man; and he set the Cherubim, and the flame of the flashing sword, toward the east of the garden of Eden, to guard the way to the tree of life.
texts.gen.4.1: And Man knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bore Cain, and said, I have acquired a man with Jehovah.
texts.gen.4.2: And she further bore his brother Abel. And Abel was a shepherd, but Cain was a husbandman.
texts.gen.4.3: And in process of time it came to pass that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering to Jehovah.
texts.gen.4.4: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat. And Jehovah looked upon Abel, and on his offering;
texts.gen.4.5: and upon Cain, and on his offering, he did not look. And Cain was very angry, and his countenance fell.
texts.gen.4.6: And Jehovah said to Cain, Why art thou angry, and why is thy countenance fallen?
texts.gen.4.7: If thou doest well, will not [thy countenance] look up [with confidence]? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door; and unto thee [shall be] his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
texts.gen.4.8: And Cain spoke to Abel his brother, and it came to pass when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
texts.gen.4.9: And Jehovah said to Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: am I my brother's keeper?
texts.gen.4.10: And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood is crying to me from the ground.
texts.gen.4.11: And now be thou cursed from the ground, which hath opened its mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand.
texts.gen.4.12: When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield thee its strength; a wanderer and fugitive shalt thou be on the earth.
texts.gen.4.13: And Cain said to Jehovah, My punishment is too great to be borne.
texts.gen.4.14: Behold, thou hast driven me this day from the face of the ground, and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a wanderer and fugitive on the earth; and it will come to pass, [that] every one who finds me will slay me.
texts.gen.4.15: And Jehovah said to him, Therefore, whoever slayeth Cain, it shall be revenged sevenfold. And Jehovah set a mark on Cain, lest any finding him should smite him.
texts.gen.4.16: And Cain went out from the presence of Jehovah, and dwelt in the land of Nod, toward the east of Eden.
texts.gen.4.17: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he built a city; and he called the name of the city after the name of his son Enoch.
texts.gen.4.18: And to Enoch was born Irad; and Irad begot Mehujael; and Mehujael begot Methushael; and Methushael begot Lemech.
texts.gen.4.19: And Lemech took two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the second, Zillah.
texts.gen.4.20: And Adah bore Jabal: he was the father of those who dwell in tents, and [breed] cattle.
texts.gen.4.21: And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of those who handle the harp and pipe.
texts.gen.4.22: And Zillah, she also bore Tubal-Cain, the forger of every kind of tool of brass and iron. And the sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.
texts.gen.4.23: And Lemech said to his wives: Adah and Zillah, hear my voice, Ye wives of Lemech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for my wound, and a youth for my bruise.
texts.gen.4.24: If Cain shall be avenged seven-fold; Lemech seventy and seven fold.
texts.gen.4.25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son, and called his name Seth: ... For God has appointed me another seed instead of Abel, because Cain has slain him.
texts.gen.4.26: And to Seth, to him also was born a son; and he called his name Enosh. Then people began to call on the name of Jehovah.
texts.gen.5.1: This is the book of Adam's generations. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.
texts.gen.5.2: Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
texts.gen.5.3: And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot [a son] in his likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth.
texts.gen.5.4: And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight hundred years; and he begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.5: And all the days of Adam that he lived were nine hundred and thirty years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.6: And Seth lived a hundred and five years, and begot Enosh.
texts.gen.5.7: And Seth lived after he had begotten Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.8: And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.9: And Enosh lived ninety years, and begot Cainan.
texts.gen.5.10: And Enosh lived after he had begotten Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.11: And all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.12: And Cainan lived seventy years, and begot Mahalaleel.
texts.gen.5.13: And Cainan lived after he had begotten Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.14: And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.15: And Mahalaleel lived sixty-five years, and begot Jared.
texts.gen.5.16: And Mahalaleel lived after he had begotten Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.17: And all the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred and ninety-five years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.18: And Jared lived a hundred and sixty-two years, and begot Enoch.
texts.gen.5.19: And Jared lived after he had begotten Enoch eight hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.20: And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.21: And Enoch lived sixty-five years, and begot Methushelah.
texts.gen.5.22: And Enoch walked with God after he had begotten Methushelah three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.23: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
texts.gen.5.24: And Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him.
texts.gen.5.25: And Methushelah lived a hundred and eighty-seven years, and begot Lemech.
texts.gen.5.26: And Methushelah lived after he had begotten Lemech seven hundred and eighty-two years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.27: And all the days of Methushelah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.28: And Lemech lived a hundred and eighty-two years, and begot a son.
texts.gen.5.29: And he called his name Noah, saying, This [one] shall comfort us concerning our work and concerning the toil of our hands, because of the ground which Jehovah has cursed.
texts.gen.5.30: And Lemech lived after he had begotten Noah five hundred and ninety-five years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.31: And all the days of Lemech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years; and he died.
texts.gen.5.32: And Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah begot Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
texts.gen.6.1: And it came to pass when mankind began to multiply on the earth, and daughters were born to them,
texts.gen.6.2: that the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair, and took themselves wives of all that they chose.
texts.gen.6.3: And Jehovah said, My Spirit shall not always plead with Man; for he indeed is flesh; but his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.
texts.gen.6.4: In those days were the giants on the earth, and also afterwards, when the sons of God had come in to the daughters of men, and they had borne [children] to them; these were the heroes, who of old were men of renown.
texts.gen.6.5: And Jehovah saw that the wickedness of Man was great on the earth, and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart only evil continually.
texts.gen.6.6: And Jehovah repented that he had made Man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
texts.gen.6.7: And Jehovah said, I will destroy Man, whom I have created, from the earth -- from man to cattle, to creeping things, and to fowl of the heavens; for I repent that I have made them.
texts.gen.6.8: But Noah found favour in the eyes of Jehovah.
texts.gen.6.9: This is the history of Noah. Noah was a just man, perfect amongst his generations: Noah walked with God.
texts.gen.6.10: And Noah begot three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
texts.gen.6.11: And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was full of violence.
texts.gen.6.12: And God looked upon the earth, and behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
texts.gen.6.13: And God said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me, for the earth is full of violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
texts.gen.6.14: Make thyself an ark of gopher wood: [with] cells shalt thou make the ark; and pitch it inside and outside with pitch.
texts.gen.6.15: And thus shalt thou make it: let the length of the ark be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
texts.gen.6.16: A light shalt thou make to the ark; and to a cubit high shalt thou finish it above. And the door of the ark shalt thou set in its side: [with] a lower, second, and third [story] shalt thou make it.
texts.gen.6.17: For I, behold, I bring a flood of waters on the earth, to destroy all flesh under the heavens in which is the breath of life: everything that is on the earth shall expire.
texts.gen.6.18: But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt go into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee.
texts.gen.6.19: And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every [sort] shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep [them] alive with thee: they shall be male and female.
texts.gen.6.20: Of fowl after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of each shall go in to thee, to keep [them] alive.
texts.gen.6.21: And take thou of all food that is eaten, and gather [it] to thee, that it may be for food for thee and for them.
texts.gen.6.22: And Noah did it; according to all that God had commanded him, so did he.
texts.gen.7.1: And Jehovah said to Noah, Go into the ark, thou and all thy house; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
texts.gen.7.2: Of all clean beasts thou shalt take to thee by sevens, a male and its female; but of the beasts that are not clean two, a male and its female.
texts.gen.7.3: Also of the fowl of the heavens by sevens, male and female; to keep seed alive on the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.7.4: For in yet seven days I will cause it to rain on the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living being which I have made will I destroy from the ground.
texts.gen.7.5: And Noah did according to all that Jehovah had commanded him.
texts.gen.7.6: And Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was on the earth.
texts.gen.7.7: And Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
texts.gen.7.8: Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean, and of fowl, and of everything that creeps on the ground,
texts.gen.7.9: there came two and two unto Noah into the ark, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
texts.gen.7.10: And it came to pass after seven days that the waters of the flood were on the earth.
texts.gen.7.11: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that same day all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
texts.gen.7.12: And the pour of rain was on the earth forty days and forty nights.
texts.gen.7.13: On the same day went Noah, and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark;
texts.gen.7.14: they, and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and all fowl after its kind -- every bird of every wing.
texts.gen.7.15: And they went to Noah, into the ark, two and two of all flesh, in which was the breath of life.
texts.gen.7.16: And they that came, came male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him. And Jehovah shut him in.
texts.gen.7.17: And the flood was forty days on the earth. And the waters increased, and bore up the ark; and it was lifted up above the earth.
texts.gen.7.18: And the waters prevailed and increased greatly on the earth; and the ark went on the face of the waters.
texts.gen.7.19: And the waters prevailed exceedingly on the earth; and all the high mountains that are under all the heavens were covered.
texts.gen.7.20: Fifteen cubits upward the waters prevailed; and the mountains were covered.
texts.gen.7.21: And all flesh that moved on the earth expired, fowl as well as cattle, and beasts, and all crawling things which crawl on the earth, and all mankind:
texts.gen.7.22: everything which had in its nostrils the breath of life, of all that was on the dry [land], died.
texts.gen.7.23: And every living being was destroyed that was on the ground, both man, and cattle, and creeping things, and fowl of the heavens; and they were destroyed from the earth. And Noah alone remained, and what was with him in the ark.
texts.gen.7.24: And the waters prevailed on the earth a hundred and fifty days.
texts.gen.8.1: And God remembered Noah, and all the animals, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark; and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
texts.gen.8.2: And the fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven were closed, and the pour of rain from heaven was stopped.
texts.gen.8.3: And the waters retired from the earth, continually retiring; and in the course of a hundred and fifty days the waters abated.
texts.gen.8.4: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat.
texts.gen.8.5: And the waters abated continually until the tenth month: in the tenth [month], on the first of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
texts.gen.8.6: And it came to pass at the end of forty days that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made.
texts.gen.8.7: And he sent out the raven, which went forth going to and fro, until the waters were dried from the earth.
texts.gen.8.8: And he sent out the dove from him, to see if the waters had become low on the ground.
texts.gen.8.9: But the dove found no resting-place for the sole of her foot, and returned to him into the ark; for the waters were on the whole earth; and he put forth his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ark.
texts.gen.8.10: And he waited yet other seven days, and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark.
texts.gen.8.11: And the dove came to him at eventide; and behold, in her beak was an olive-leaf plucked off; and Noah knew that the waters had become low on the earth.
texts.gen.8.12: And he waited yet other seven days, and sent forth the dove; but she returned no more to him.
texts.gen.8.13: And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first [month], on the first of the month, that the waters were dried up from the earth. And Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold, the surface of the ground was dried.
texts.gen.8.14: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
texts.gen.8.15: And God spoke to Noah, saying,
texts.gen.8.16: Go out of the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons' wives with thee.
texts.gen.8.17: Bring forth with thee every animal which is with thee, of all flesh, fowl as well as cattle, and all the creeping things which creep on the earth, that they may swarm on the earth, and may be fruitful and multiply on the earth.
texts.gen.8.18: And Noah went out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him.
texts.gen.8.19: All the animals, all the creeping things, and all the fowl -- everything that moves on the earth, after their kinds, went out of the ark.
texts.gen.8.20: And Noah built an altar to Jehovah; and took of every clean animal, and of all clean fowl, and offered up burnt-offerings on the altar.
texts.gen.8.21: And Jehovah smelled the sweet odour. And Jehovah said in his heart, I will no more henceforth curse the ground on account of Man, for the thought of Man's heart is evil from his youth; and I will no more smite every living thing, as I have done.
texts.gen.8.22: Henceforth, all the days of the earth, seed [time] and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, shall not cease.
texts.gen.9.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
texts.gen.9.2: And let the fear of you and the dread of you be upon every animal of the earth, and upon all fowl of the heavens: upon all that moveth [on] the ground; and upon all the fishes of the sea: into your hand are they delivered.
texts.gen.9.3: Every moving thing that liveth shall be food for you: as the green herb I give you everything.
texts.gen.9.4: Only, the flesh with its life, its blood, ye shall not eat.
texts.gen.9.5: And indeed your blood, [the blood] of your lives, will I require: at the hand of every animal will I require it, and at the hand of Man, at the hand of each [the blood] of his brother, will I require the life of Man.
texts.gen.9.6: Whoso sheddeth Man's blood, by Man shall his blood be shed; for in the image of God he hath made Man.
texts.gen.9.7: And ye, be fruitful and multiply: swarm on the earth, and multiply on it.
texts.gen.9.8: And God spoke to Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,
texts.gen.9.9: And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you;
texts.gen.9.10: and with every living soul which is with you, fowl as well as cattle, and all the animals of the earth with you, of all that has gone out of the ark -- every animal of the earth.
texts.gen.9.11: And I establish my covenant with you, neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood, and henceforth there shall be no flood to destroy the earth.
texts.gen.9.12: And God said, This is the sign of the covenant that I set between me and you and every living soul that is with you, for everlasting generations:
texts.gen.9.13: I set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
texts.gen.9.14: And it shall come to pass when I bring clouds over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud,
texts.gen.9.15: and I will remember my covenant which is between me and you and every living soul of all flesh; and the waters shall not henceforth become a flood to destroy all flesh.
texts.gen.9.16: And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living soul of all flesh that is upon the earth.
texts.gen.9.17: And God said to Noah, This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.
texts.gen.9.18: And the sons of Noah who went out of the ark were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth. And Ham is the father of Canaan.
texts.gen.9.19: These three are the sons of Noah; and from these was [the population of] the whole earth spread abroad.
texts.gen.9.20: And Noah began [to be] a husbandman, and planted a vineyard.
texts.gen.9.21: And he drank of the wine, and was drunken, and he uncovered himself in his tent.
texts.gen.9.22: And Ham the father of Canaan saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren outside.
texts.gen.9.23: And Shem and Japheth took the upper garment and both laid [it] upon their shoulders, and went backwards, and covered the nakedness of their father. And their faces were turned away, that they saw not their father's nakedness.
texts.gen.9.24: And Noah awoke from his wine, and learned what his youngest son had done to him.
texts.gen.9.25: And he said, Cursed be Canaan; Let him be a bondman of bondmen to his brethren.
texts.gen.9.26: And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Shem, And let Canaan be his bondman.
texts.gen.9.27: Let God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem, And let Canaan be his bondman.
texts.gen.9.28: And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
texts.gen.9.29: And all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years; and he died.
texts.gen.10.1: And these are the generations of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and to them were sons born after the flood.
texts.gen.10.2: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
texts.gen.10.3: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
texts.gen.10.4: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
texts.gen.10.5: From these came the distribution of the isles of the nations, according to their lands, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
texts.gen.10.6: And the sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
texts.gen.10.7: And the sons of Cush: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
texts.gen.10.8: And Cush begot Nimrod: he began to be mighty on the earth.
texts.gen.10.9: He was a mighty hunter before Jehovah; therefore it is said, As Nimrod, the mighty hunter before Jehovah!
texts.gen.10.10: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
texts.gen.10.11: From that land went out Asshur, and built Nineveh, and Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,
texts.gen.10.12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah: this is the great city.
texts.gen.10.13: -- And Mizraim begot the Ludim, and the Anamim, and the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim,
texts.gen.10.14: and the Pathrusim, and the Casluhim, out of whom came the Philistines, and the Caphtorim.
texts.gen.10.15: -- And Canaan begot Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth,
texts.gen.10.16: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
texts.gen.10.17: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
texts.gen.10.18: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. And afterwards the families of the Canaanites spread themselves abroad.
texts.gen.10.19: And the border of the Canaanite was from Sidon, as one goes to Gerar, up to Gazah; as one goes to Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, up to Lesha.
texts.gen.10.20: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
texts.gen.10.21: And to Shem -- to him also were [sons] born; he is the father of all the sons of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder.
texts.gen.10.22: The sons of Shem: Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
texts.gen.10.23: And the sons of Aram: Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
texts.gen.10.24: -- And Arphaxad begot Shelah; and Shelah begot Eber.
texts.gen.10.25: And to Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother's name was Joktan.
texts.gen.10.26: And Joktan begot Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
texts.gen.10.27: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
texts.gen.10.28: and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
texts.gen.10.29: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab: all these were sons of Joktan.
texts.gen.10.30: And their dwelling was from Mesha, as one goes to Sephar, the eastern mountain.
texts.gen.10.31: These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.
texts.gen.10.32: These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations. And from these came the distribution of the nations on the earth after the flood.
texts.gen.11.1: And the whole earth had one language, and the same words.
texts.gen.11.2: And it came to pass as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and dwelt there.
texts.gen.11.3: And they said one to another, Come on, let us make bricks, and burn [them] thoroughly. And they had brick for stone, and they had asphalt for mortar.
texts.gen.11.4: And they said, Come on, let us build ourselves a city and a tower, the top of which [may reach] to the heavens; and let us make ourselves a name, lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth.
texts.gen.11.5: And Jehovah came down to see the city and the tower which the children of men built.
texts.gen.11.6: And Jehovah said, Behold, the people is one, and have all one language; and this have they begun to do. And now will they be hindered in nothing that they meditate doing.
texts.gen.11.7: Come, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech.
texts.gen.11.8: And Jehovah scattered them thence over the face of the whole earth. And they left off building the city.
texts.gen.11.9: Therefore was its name called Babel; because Jehovah there confounded the language of the whole earth. And Jehovah scattered them thence over the face of the whole earth.
texts.gen.11.10: These are the generations of Shem. Shem was a hundred years old, and begot Arphaxad two years after the flood.
texts.gen.11.11: And Shem lived after he had begotten Arphaxad five hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.12: And Arphaxad lived thirty-five years, and begot Shelah.
texts.gen.11.13: And Arphaxad lived after he had begotten Shelah four hundred and three years, and begot sons and daughters.
