texts.gen.29.34: And she again conceived, and bore a son, and said, Now this time will my husband be united to me, for I have borne him three sons; therefore was his name called Levi.
texts.gen.29.35: And she again conceived, and bore a son, and said, This time will I praise Jehovah; therefore she called his name Judah. And she ceased to bear.
texts.gen.30.1: And when Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister, and said to Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
texts.gen.30.2: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel, and he said, Am I in God's stead, who has withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?
texts.gen.30.3: And she said, Behold, there is my maid, Bilhah: go in to her, in order that she may bear on my knees, and I may also be built up by her.
texts.gen.30.4: And she gave him Bilhah her maidservant as wife, and Jacob went in to her.
texts.gen.30.5: And Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.
texts.gen.30.6: And Rachel said, God has done me justice, and has also heard my voice, and given me a son; therefore she called his name Dan.
texts.gen.30.7: And Bilhah Rachel's maidservant again conceived, and bore Jacob a second son.
texts.gen.30.8: And Rachel said, Wrestlings of God have I wrestled with my sister, and have prevailed; and she called his name Naphtali.
texts.gen.30.9: And when Leah saw that she had ceased to bear, she took Zilpah her maidservant and gave her to Jacob as wife.
texts.gen.30.10: And Zilpah Leah's maidservant bore Jacob a son.
texts.gen.30.11: And Leah said, Fortunately! and she called his name Gad.
texts.gen.30.12: And Zilpah Leah's maidservant bore Jacob a second son.
texts.gen.30.13: And Leah said, Happy am I; for the daughters will call me blessed! and she called his name Asher.
texts.gen.30.14: And Reuben went out in the days of wheat-harvest, and found mandrakes in the fields; and he brought them to his mother Leah. And Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.
texts.gen.30.15: And she said to her, Is it [too] little that thou hast taken my husband, that thou wilt take my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to-night for thy son's mandrakes.
texts.gen.30.16: And when Jacob came from the fields in the evening, Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in to me, for indeed I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.
texts.gen.30.17: And God hearkened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.
texts.gen.30.18: And Leah said, God has given me my hire, because I have given my maidservant to my husband; and she called his name Issachar.
texts.gen.30.19: And Leah again conceived, and bore Jacob a sixth son;
texts.gen.30.20: and Leah said, God has endowed me with a good dowry; this time will my husband dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons. And she called his name Zebulun.
texts.gen.30.21: And afterwards she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
texts.gen.30.22: And God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her, and opened her womb.
texts.gen.30.23: And she conceived, and bore a son, and said, God has taken away my reproach.
texts.gen.30.24: And she called his name Joseph; and said, Jehovah will add to me another son.
texts.gen.30.25: And it came to pass when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my country.
texts.gen.30.26: Give [me] my wives for whom I have served thee, and my children; that I may go away, for thou knowest my service which I have served thee.
texts.gen.30.27: And Laban said to him, I pray thee, if I have found favour in thine eyes -- I have discovered that Jehovah has blessed me for thy sake.
texts.gen.30.28: And he said, Appoint to me thy wages, and I will give it.
texts.gen.30.29: And he said to him, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and what thy cattle has become with me.
texts.gen.30.30: For it was little that thou hadst before me, and it is increased to a multitude, and Jehovah has blessed thee from the time I came; and now, when shall I also provide for my house?
texts.gen.30.31: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me anything. If thou doest this for me, I will again feed [and] keep thy flock:
texts.gen.30.32: I will pass through all thy flock to-day, to remove thence all the speckled and spotted sheep, and all the brown lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and [that] shall be my hire.
texts.gen.30.33: And my righteousness shall answer for me hereafter, when thou comest about my hire, before thy face: all that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the lambs, let that be stolen with me.
texts.gen.30.34: And Laban said, Well, let it be according to thy word.
texts.gen.30.35: And he removed that day the he-goats that were ringstraked and spotted, and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the brown among the lambs, and gave [them] into the hand of his sons.
texts.gen.30.36: And he put three days' journey between himself and Jacob. And Jacob fed the rest of Laban's flock.
texts.gen.30.37: And Jacob took fresh rods of white poplar, almond-tree, and maple; and peeled off white stripes in them, uncovering the white which was on the rods.
texts.gen.30.38: And he set the rods which he had peeled before the flock, in the troughs at the watering-places where the flock came to drink, and they were ardent when they came to drink.
texts.gen.30.39: And the flock was ardent before the rods; and the flock brought forth ringstraked, speckled, and spotted.
texts.gen.30.40: And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flock toward the ringstraked, and all the brown in the flock of Laban; and he made himself separate flocks, and did not put them with Laban's flock.
texts.gen.30.41: And it came to pass whensoever the strong cattle were ardent, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, that they might become ardent among the rods;
texts.gen.30.42: but when the sheep were feeble, he put [them] not in; so the feeble were Laban's, and the strong Jacob's.
texts.gen.30.43: And the man increased very, very much, and had much cattle, and bondwomen, and bondmen, and camels, and asses.
texts.gen.31.1: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob has taken away all that was our father's, and of what was our father's he has acquired all this glory.
texts.gen.31.2: And Jacob saw the countenance of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as previously.
texts.gen.31.3: And Jehovah said to Jacob, Return into the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.
texts.gen.31.4: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the fields to his flock,
texts.gen.31.5: and said to them, I see your father's countenance, that it is not toward me as previously; but the God of my father has been with me.
texts.gen.31.6: And you know that with all my power I have served your father.
texts.gen.31.7: And your father has mocked me, and has changed my wages ten times; but God suffered him not to hurt me.
texts.gen.31.8: If he said thus; The speckled shall be thy hire, then all the flocks bore speckled; and if he said thus: The ringstraked shall be thy hire, then all the flocks bore ringstraked.
texts.gen.31.9: And God has taken away the cattle of your father, and given [them] to me.
texts.gen.31.10: And it came to pass at the time of the ardour of the flocks, that I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the rams that leaped upon the flocks were ringstraked, speckled, and spotted.
texts.gen.31.11: And the Angel of God said to me in a dream, Jacob! And I said, Here am I.
texts.gen.31.12: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see: all the rams that leap upon the flock are ringstraked, speckled, and spotted; for I have seen all that Laban does to thee.
texts.gen.31.13: I am the ùGod of Bethel, where thou anointedst the pillar, where thou vowedst a vow to me. Now arise, depart out of this land, and return to the land of thy kindred.
texts.gen.31.14: And Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?
texts.gen.31.15: Are we not reckoned of him strangers? for he has sold us, and has even constantly devoured our money.
texts.gen.31.16: For all the wealth that God has taken from our father is ours and our children's; and now whatever God has said to thee do.
texts.gen.31.17: And Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels,
texts.gen.31.18: and carried away all his cattle, and all his property that he had acquired -- the cattle of his possessions that he had acquired in Padan-Aram, to go to Isaac his father, into the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.31.19: And Laban had gone to shear his sheep. And Rachel stole the teraphim that [belonged] to her father.
texts.gen.31.20: And Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he did not tell him that he fled.
texts.gen.31.21: And he fled with all that he had; and he rose up and passed over the river, and set his face [toward] mount Gilead.
texts.gen.31.22: And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.
texts.gen.31.23: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey, and overtook him on mount Gilead.
texts.gen.31.24: And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said to him, Take care thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
texts.gen.31.25: And Laban came up with Jacob; and Jacob had pitched his tent on the mountain; Laban also with his brethren pitched on mount Gilead.
texts.gen.31.26: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast deceived me, and hast carried away my daughters as captives of war?
texts.gen.31.27: Why didst thou flee away covertly, and steal away from me, and didst not tell me, that I might have conducted thee with mirth and with songs, with tambour and with harp;
texts.gen.31.28: and hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now thou hast acted foolishly.
texts.gen.31.29: It would be in the power of my hand to do you hurt; but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, Take care that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
texts.gen.31.30: And now that thou must needs be gone, because thou greatly longedst after thy father's house, why hast thou stolen my gods?
texts.gen.31.31: And Jacob answered and said to Laban, I was afraid; for I said, Lest thou shouldest take by force thy daughters from me.
texts.gen.31.32: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, he shall not live. Before our brethren discern what is thine with me, and take [it] to thee. But Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.
texts.gen.31.33: And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the two handmaids' tents, and found nothing; and he went out of Leah's tent, and entered into Rachel's tent.
texts.gen.31.34: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim and put them under the camel's saddle; and she sat upon them. And Laban explored all the tent, but found nothing.
texts.gen.31.35: And she said to her father, Let it not be an occasion of anger in the eyes of my lord that I cannot rise up before thee, for it is with me after the manner of women. And he searched carefully, but did not find the teraphim.
texts.gen.31.36: And Jacob was angry, and he disputed with Laban. And Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my fault, what my sin, that thou hast so hotly pursued after me?
texts.gen.31.37: Whereas thou hast explored all my baggage, what hast thou found of all thy household stuff? Set [it] here before my brethren and thy brethren, and let them decide between us both.
texts.gen.31.38: These twenty years have I been with thee: thy ewes and thy she-goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock I have not eaten.
texts.gen.31.39: What was torn I have not brought to thee; I had to bear the loss of it: of my hand hast thou required it, [whether] stolen by day or stolen by night.
texts.gen.31.40: Thus it was with me: in the day the heat consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from mine eyes.
texts.gen.31.41: I have been these twenty years in thy house: I have served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy flock; and thou hast changed my wages ten times.
texts.gen.31.42: Had not the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, been with me, it is certain thou wouldest have sent me away now empty. God has looked upon my affliction and the labour of my hands, and has judged last night.
texts.gen.31.43: And Laban answered and said to Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, and the sons are my sons, and the flock is my flock, and all that thou seest is mine; but as for my daughters, what can I do this day to them, or to their sons whom they have brought forth?
texts.gen.31.44: And now, come, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be a witness between me and thee.
texts.gen.31.45: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up [for] a pillar.
texts.gen.31.46: And Jacob said to his brethren, Gather stones. And they took stones, and made a heap, and ate there upon the heap.
texts.gen.31.47: And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
texts.gen.31.48: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed,
texts.gen.31.49: -- and Mizpah; for he said, Let Jehovah watch between me and thee, when we shall be hidden one from another:
texts.gen.31.50: if thou shouldest afflict my daughters, or if thou shouldest take wives besides my daughters, -- no man is with us; see, God is witness between me and thee!
texts.gen.31.51: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold the pillar which I have set up between me and thee:
texts.gen.31.52: [let] this heap be witness, and the pillar a witness, that neither I pass this heap [to go] to thee, nor thou pass this heap and this pillar [to come] to me, for harm.
texts.gen.31.53: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us! And Jacob swore by the fear of his father Isaac.
texts.gen.31.54: And Jacob offered a sacrifice upon the mountain, and invited his brethren to eat bread: and they ate bread, and lodged on the mountain.
texts.gen.31.55: And Laban rose early in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them; and Laban went and returned to his place.
texts.gen.32.1: And Jacob went on his way; and the angels of God met him.
texts.gen.32.2: And when Jacob saw them he said, This is the camp of God. And he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
texts.gen.32.3: And Jacob sent messengers before his face to Esau his brother, into the land of Seir, the fields of Edom.
texts.gen.32.4: And he commanded them, saying, Thus shall ye speak to my lord, to Esau: Thy servant Jacob speaks thus -- With Laban have I sojourned and tarried until now;
texts.gen.32.5: and I have oxen, and asses, sheep, and bondmen, and bondwomen; and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favour in thine eyes.
texts.gen.32.6: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother, to Esau; and he also is coming to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.
texts.gen.32.7: Then Jacob was greatly afraid, and was distressed; and he divided the people that were with him, and the sheep and the cattle and the camels, into two troops.
texts.gen.32.8: And he said, If Esau come to the one troop and smite it, then the other troop which is left shall escape.
texts.gen.32.9: And Jacob said, God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Jehovah, who saidst unto me: Return into thy country and to thy kindred, and I will do thee good,
texts.gen.32.10: -- I am too small for all the loving-kindness and all the faithfulness that thou hast shewn unto thy servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I am become two troops.
texts.gen.32.11: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and smite me, [and] the mother with the children.
texts.gen.32.12: And thou saidst, I will certainly deal well with thee, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.
texts.gen.32.13: And he lodged there that night; and took of what came to his hand a gift for Esau his brother --
texts.gen.32.14: two hundred she-goats, and twenty he-goats; two hundred ewes, and twenty rams;
texts.gen.32.15: thirty milch camels with their colts; forty kine, and ten bulls; twenty she-asses, and ten young asses.
texts.gen.32.16: And he delivered [them] into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself; and he said to his servants, Go on before me, and put a space between drove and drove.
texts.gen.32.17: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meets thee, and asks thee, saying, Whose art thou, and where goest thou, and whose are these before thee?
texts.gen.32.18: -- then thou shalt say, Thy servant Jacob's: it is a gift sent to my lord, to Esau. And behold, he also is behind us.
texts.gen.32.19: And so commanded he the second, and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying, According to this word shall ye speak to Esau when ye find him.
texts.gen.32.20: And, moreover, ye shall say, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will propitiate him with the gift that goes before me, and afterwards I will see his face: perhaps he will accept me.
texts.gen.32.21: And the gift went over before him; and he himself lodged that night in the camp.
texts.gen.32.22: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford of the Jabbok;
texts.gen.32.23: and he took them and led them over the river, and led over what he had.
texts.gen.32.24: And Jacob remained alone; and a man wrestled with him until the rising of the dawn.
texts.gen.32.25: And when he saw that he did not prevail against him, he touched the joint of his thigh; and the joint of Jacob's thigh was dislocated as he wrestled with him.
texts.gen.32.26: And he said, Let me go, for the dawn ariseth. And he said, I will not let thee go except thou bless me.
texts.gen.32.27: And he said to him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.
texts.gen.32.28: And he said, Thy name shall not henceforth be called Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast wrestled with God, and with men, and hast prevailed.
texts.gen.32.29: And Jacob asked and said, Tell [me], I pray thee, thy name. And he said, How is it that thou askest after my name? And he blessed him there.
texts.gen.32.30: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel -- For I have seen God face to face, and my life has been preserved.
texts.gen.32.31: And as he passed over Peniel, the sun rose upon him; and he limped upon his hip.
texts.gen.32.32: Therefore the children of Israel do not eat of the sinew that is over the joint of the thigh, to this day; because he touched the joint of Jacob's thigh -- the sinew.
texts.gen.33.1: And Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. And he distributed the children to Leah, and to Rachel, and to the two maidservants:
texts.gen.33.2: and he put the maidservants and their children foremost, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph hindmost.
texts.gen.33.3: And he passed on before them, and bowed to the earth seven times, until he came near to his brother.
texts.gen.33.4: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him; and they wept.
texts.gen.33.5: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, Who are these with thee? And he said, The children that God has graciously given thy servant.
texts.gen.33.6: And the maidservants drew near, they and their children, and they bowed.
texts.gen.33.7: And Leah also, with her children, drew near, and they bowed. And lastly Joseph drew near, and Rachel, and they bowed.
texts.gen.33.8: And he said, What [meanest] thou by all the drove which I met? And he said, To find favour in the eyes of my lord.
texts.gen.33.9: And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; let what thou hast be thine.
texts.gen.33.10: And Jacob said, No, I pray thee; if now I have found favour in thine eyes, then receive my gift from my hand; for therefore have I seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of God, and thou hast received me with pleasure.
texts.gen.33.11: Take, I pray thee, my blessing which has been brought to thee; because God has been gracious to me, and because I have everything. And he urged him, and he took [it].
texts.gen.33.12: And he said, Let us take our journey, and go on, and I will go before thee.
texts.gen.33.13: And he said to him, My lord knows that the children are tender, and the suckling sheep and kine are with me; and if they should overdrive them only one day, all the flock would die.
texts.gen.33.14: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass on before his servant, and I will drive on at my ease according to the pace of the cattle that is before me, and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord, to Seir.
texts.gen.33.15: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee [some] of the people that are with me. And he said, What need? Let me find favour in the eyes of my lord.
texts.gen.33.16: And Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
texts.gen.33.17: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built himself a house, and for his cattle he made booths. Therefore the name of the place was called Succoth.
texts.gen.33.18: And Jacob came safely [to the] city Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan-Aram; and he encamped before the city.
texts.gen.33.19: And he bought the portion of the field where he had spread his tent, of the hand of the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for a hundred kesitahs.
texts.gen.33.20: And there he set up an altar, and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
texts.gen.34.1: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
texts.gen.34.2: And when Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and humbled her.
texts.gen.34.3: And his soul fastened on Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the maiden, and spoke consolingly to the maiden.
texts.gen.34.4: And Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, Take me this girl as wife.
texts.gen.34.5: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter; but his sons were with his cattle in the fields, and Jacob said nothing until they came.
texts.gen.34.6: And Hamor the father of Shechem came out to Jacob, to speak to him.
texts.gen.34.7: And the sons of Jacob came from the fields when they heard [it]; and the men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had wrought what was disgraceful in Israel, in lying with Jacob's daughter, which thing ought not to be done.
texts.gen.34.8: And Hamor spoke to them, saying, My son Shechem's soul cleaves to your daughter: I pray you, give her to him as wife.
texts.gen.34.9: And make marriages with us: give your daughters to us, and take our daughters to you.
texts.gen.34.10: And dwell with us, and the land shall be before you: dwell and trade in it, and get yourselves possessions in it.
texts.gen.34.11: And Shechem said to her father and to her brethren, Let me find favour in your eyes; and what ye shall say to me I will give.
texts.gen.34.12: Impose on me very much as dowry and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say to me; but give me the maiden as wife.
texts.gen.34.13: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and spoke -- because he had defiled Dinah their sister --
texts.gen.34.14: and said to them, We cannot do this, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that [were] a reproach to us.
texts.gen.34.15: But only in this will we consent to you, if ye will be as we, that every male of you be circumcised;
texts.gen.34.16: then will we give our daughters to you, and take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and be one people.
texts.gen.34.17: But if ye do not hearken to us, to be circumcised, then will we take our daughter and go away.
texts.gen.34.18: And their words were good in the eyes of Hamor and Shechem, Hamor's son.
texts.gen.34.19: And the youth did not delay to do this, because he had delight in Jacob's daughter. And he was honourable above all in the house of his father.
texts.gen.34.20: And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke to the men of their city, saying,
texts.gen.34.21: These men are peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade in it. And the land -- behold, it is of wide extent before them. We will take their daughters as wives, and give them our daughters.
texts.gen.34.22: But only in this will the men consent to us to dwell with us, to be one people -- if every male among us be circumcised, just as they are circumcised.
texts.gen.34.23: Their cattle, and their possessions, and every beast of theirs, shall they not be ours? only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.
texts.gen.34.24: And all that went out at the gate of his city hearkened to Hamor and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised -- all that went out at the gate of his city.
texts.gen.34.25: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.
texts.gen.34.26: And Hamor and Shechem his son they slew with the edge of the sword; and took Dinah out of Shechem's house; and went out.
texts.gen.34.27: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
texts.gen.34.28: Their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and what [was] in the city, and what [was] in the field they took;
texts.gen.34.29: and all their goods, and all their little ones, and their wives took they captive, and plundered them, and all that was in the houses.
texts.gen.34.30: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me, in that ye make me odious among the inhabitants of the land -- among the Canaanites and the Perizzites; and I am few men in number, and they will gather themselves against me and smite me, and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
texts.gen.34.31: And they said, Should people deal with our sister as with a harlot?
texts.gen.35.1: And God said to Jacob, Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there, and make there an altar unto the ùGod that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
texts.gen.35.2: And Jacob said to his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments;
texts.gen.35.3: and we will arise, and go up to Bethel; and I will make there an altar to the ùGod that answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way that I went.
texts.gen.35.4: And they gave to Jacob all the strange gods that were in their hand, and the rings that were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the terebinth that [is] by Shechem.
texts.gen.35.5: And they journeyed; and the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
texts.gen.35.6: And Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Bethel, he and all the people that were with him.
texts.gen.35.7: And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el; because there God had appeared to him when he fled from the face of his brother.
texts.gen.35.8: And Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, died; and she was buried beneath Bethel, under the oak; and the name of it was called Allon-bachuth.
texts.gen.35.9: And God appeared to Jacob again after he had come from Padan-Aram, and blessed him.
texts.gen.35.10: And God said to him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not henceforth be called Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name. And he called his name Israel.
texts.gen.35.11: And God said to him, I am the Almighty ùGod: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee; and kings shall come out of thy loins.
texts.gen.35.12: And the land that I gave Abraham and Isaac, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.
texts.gen.35.13: And God went up from him in the place where he had talked with him.
texts.gen.35.14: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he had talked with him, a pillar of stone, and poured on it a drink-offering, and poured oil on it.
texts.gen.35.15: And Jacob called the name of the place where God had talked with him, Beth-el.
texts.gen.35.16: And they journeyed from Bethel. And there was yet a certain distance to come to Ephrath, when Rachel travailed in childbirth; and it went hard with her in her childbearing.
texts.gen.35.17: And it came to pass when it went hard with her in her childbearing, that the midwife said to her, Fear not; for this also is a son for thee.
texts.gen.35.18: And it came to pass as her soul was departing -- for she died -- that she called his name Benoni; but his father called him Benjamin.
texts.gen.35.19: And Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath, which [is] Bethlehem.
texts.gen.35.20: And Jacob erected a pillar upon her grave: that is the pillar of Rachel's grave to [this] day.
texts.gen.35.21: And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent on the other side of Migdal-Eder.
texts.gen.35.22: And it came to pass when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine; and Israel heard of it. And the sons of Jacob were twelve.
texts.gen.35.23: The sons of Leah: Reuben -- Jacob's firstborn -- and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun.
texts.gen.35.24: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
texts.gen.35.25: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant: Dan and Naphtali.
texts.gen.35.26: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob that were born to him in Padan-Aram.
texts.gen.35.27: And Jacob came to Isaac his father to Mamre -- to Kirjath-Arba, which is Hebron; where Abraham had sojourned, and Isaac.
texts.gen.35.28: And the days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years.
texts.gen.35.29: And Isaac expired and died, and was gathered to his peoples, old and full of days. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
texts.gen.36.1: And these are the generations of Esau, that is Edom.
texts.gen.36.2: Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
texts.gen.36.3: and Basmath Ishmael's daughter, the sister of Nebaioth.
texts.gen.36.4: And Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz; and Basmath bore Reuel.
texts.gen.36.5: And Oholibamah bore Jeush and Jaalam and Korah. These are the sons of Esau that were born to him in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.36.6: And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the souls of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his possessions, that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went into a country away from his brother Jacob.
texts.gen.36.7: For their property was too great for them to dwell together, and the land where they were sojourners could not bear them, because of their cattle.
texts.gen.36.8: Thus Esau dwelt in mount Seir; Esau is Edom.
texts.gen.36.9: And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in mount Seir.
texts.gen.36.10: These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah the wife of Esau; Reuel, the son of Basmath the wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.11: -- And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
texts.gen.36.12: And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau's son, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These are the sons of Adah Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.13: -- And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These are the sons of Basmath Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.14: -- And these are the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, Esau's wife: and she bore to Esau Jeush and Jaalam and Korah.
texts.gen.36.15: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
texts.gen.36.16: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.
texts.gen.36.17: And these are the sons of Reuel Esau's son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah: these are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basmath Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.18: -- And these are the sons of Oholibamah Esau's wife: chief Jeush, chief Jaalam, chief Korah; these are the chiefs of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau's wife.
texts.gen.36.19: These are the sons of Esau, and these their chiefs: he is Edom.
texts.gen.36.20: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitant of the land: Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
texts.gen.36.21: and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom.
texts.gen.36.22: -- And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.
texts.gen.36.23: -- And these are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
texts.gen.36.24: -- And these are the sons of Zibeon: both Ajah and Anah. This is the Anah that found the warm springs in the wilderness as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father.
texts.gen.36.25: -- And these are the sons of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah.
texts.gen.36.26: -- And these are the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
texts.gen.36.27: -- These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
texts.gen.36.28: -- These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
texts.gen.36.29: These are the chiefs of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
texts.gen.36.30: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
texts.gen.36.31: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom before there reigned a king over the children of Israel.
texts.gen.36.32: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom; and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
texts.gen.36.33: And Bela died; and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.34: And Jobab died; and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.35: And Husham died; and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the fields of Moab, reigned in his stead. And the name of his city was Avith.
texts.gen.36.36: And Hadad died; and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.37: And Samlah died; and Saul of Rehoboth on the river reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.38: And Saul died; and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.
texts.gen.36.39: And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died; and Hadar reigned in his stead; and the name of his city was Pau; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred daughter of Mezahab.
texts.gen.36.40: And these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their families, after their places, with their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
texts.gen.36.41: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
texts.gen.36.42: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
texts.gen.36.43: chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their dwelling-places in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of Edom.
texts.gen.37.1: And Jacob dwelt in the land where his father sojourned -- in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.37.2: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, fed the flock with his brethren; and he was doing service with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought to his father an evil report of them.
texts.gen.37.3: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was son of his old age; and he made him a vest of many colours.
texts.gen.37.4: And his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, and they hated him, and could not greet him with friendliness.
texts.gen.37.5: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and told [it] to his brethren, and they hated him yet the more.
texts.gen.37.6: And he said to them, Hear, I pray you, this dream, which I have dreamt:
texts.gen.37.7: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the fields, and lo, my sheaf rose up, and remained standing; and behold, your sheaves came round about and bowed down to my sheaf.
texts.gen.37.8: And his brethren said to him, Wilt thou indeed be a king over us? wilt thou indeed rule over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.
texts.gen.37.9: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamt another dream, and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.
texts.gen.37.10: And he told [it] to his father and to his brethren. And his father rebuked him, and said to him, What is this dream which thou hast dreamt? Shall we indeed come, I and thy mother and thy brethren, to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?
texts.gen.37.11: And his brethren envied him; but his father kept the saying.
texts.gen.37.12: And his brethren went to feed their father's flock at Shechem.
texts.gen.37.13: And Israel said to Joseph, Do not thy brethren feed [the flock] at Shechem? Come, that I may send thee to them. And he said to him, Here am I.
texts.gen.37.14: And he said to him, Go, I pray thee, see after the welfare of thy brethren, and after the welfare of the flock; and bring me word again. And he sent him out of the vale of Hebron; and he came towards Shechem.
texts.gen.37.15: And a man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the country; and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
texts.gen.37.16: And he said, I am seeking my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, where they feed [their flocks].
texts.gen.37.17: And the man said, They have removed from this; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them at Dothan.
texts.gen.37.18: And when they saw him from afar, and before he came near to them, they conspired against him to put him to death.
texts.gen.37.19: And they said one to another, Behold, there comes that dreamer!
texts.gen.37.20: And now come and let us kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say, An evil beast has devoured him; and we will see what becomes of his dreams.
texts.gen.37.21: And Reuben heard [it], and delivered him out of their hand, and said, Let us not take his life.
texts.gen.37.22: And Reuben said to them, Shed no blood: cast him into this pit which is in the wilderness; but lay no hand upon him -- in order that he might deliver him out of their hand, to bring him to his father again.
texts.gen.37.23: And it came to pass when Joseph came to his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his vest, the vest of many colours, which he had on;
texts.gen.37.24: and they took him and cast him into the pit; now the pit was empty -- there was no water in it.
texts.gen.37.25: And they sat down to eat bread; and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites came from Gilead; and their camels bore tragacanth, and balsam, and ladanum -- going to carry [it] down to Egypt.
texts.gen.37.26: And Judah said to his brethren, What profit is it that we kill our brother and secrete his blood?
texts.gen.37.27: Come and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites; but let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brethren hearkened [to him].
texts.gen.37.28: And Midianitish men, merchants, passed by; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty silver-pieces; and they brought Joseph to Egypt.
texts.gen.37.29: And Reuben returned to the pit, and behold, Joseph [was] not in the pit; and he rent his garments,
texts.gen.37.30: and returned to his brethren, and said, The child is not; and I, where shall I go?
texts.gen.37.31: And they took Joseph's vest, and slaughtered a buck of the goats, and dipped the vest in the blood;
texts.gen.37.32: and they sent the vest of many colours and had it carried to their father, and said, This have we found: discern now whether it is thy son's vest or not.
texts.gen.37.33: And he discerned it, and said, [It is] my son's vest! an evil beast has devoured him: Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces!
texts.gen.37.34: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
texts.gen.37.35: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted, and said, For I will go down to my son into Sheol mourning. Thus his father wept for him.
texts.gen.37.36: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt, to Potiphar, a chamberlain of Pharaoh, the captain of the life-guard.
texts.gen.38.1: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a man of Adullam whose name was Hirah.
texts.gen.38.2: And Judah saw there the daughter of a Canaanitish man whose name was Shua; and he took her, and went in to her.
texts.gen.38.3: And she conceived and bore a son; and he called his name Er.
texts.gen.38.4: And she again conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
texts.gen.38.5: And again she bore a son, and she called his name Shelah; and he was at Chezib when she bore him.
texts.gen.38.6: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
texts.gen.38.7: And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of Jehovah, and Jehovah slew him.
texts.gen.38.8: Then Judah said to Onan, Go in to thy brother's wife, and fulfil to her the brother-in-law's duty, and raise up seed to thy brother.
texts.gen.38.9: But when Onan knew that the seed should not be his own, it came to pass when he went in to his brother's wife, that he spilled [it] on the ground, in order to give no seed to his brother.
texts.gen.38.10: And the thing which he did was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and he slew him also.
texts.gen.38.11: And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, Remain a widow in thy father's house, until Shelah my son is grown; for he said, Lest he die also, as his brethren. And Tamar went and remained in her father's house.
texts.gen.38.12: And as the days were multiplied, Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, died. And Judah was comforted, and he went up to his sheep-shearers, to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
texts.gen.38.13: And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold thy father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.
texts.gen.38.14: And she put the garments of her widowhood off from her, and covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the entry of Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given to him as wife.
texts.gen.38.15: And Judah saw her, and took her for a harlot; because she had covered her face.
texts.gen.38.16: And he turned aside to her by the way, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me go in to thee; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in to me?
texts.gen.38.17: And he said, I will send [thee] a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give [me] a pledge, until thou send it?
texts.gen.38.18: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy lace, and thy staff which is in thy hand. And he gave [it] her, and went in to her; and she conceived by him.
texts.gen.38.19: And she arose and went away; and she laid by her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
texts.gen.38.20: And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman's hand; but he found her not.
texts.gen.38.21: And he asked the men of her place, saying, Where is the prostitute that was at Enaim, by the way-side? And they said, There was no prostitute here.
texts.gen.38.22: And he returned to Judah, and said, I have not found her; and also the men of the place said, No prostitute has been here.
texts.gen.38.23: Then Judah said, Let her take [it] for herself, lest we be put to shame. Behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
texts.gen.38.24: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-law has committed fornication, and behold, she is also with child by fornication. And Judah said, Bring her forth, that she may be burned.
texts.gen.38.25: When she was brought forth, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, By the man to whom these [belong] am I with child; and she said, Acknowledge, I pray thee, whose are this signet, and this lace, and this staff.
texts.gen.38.26: And Judah acknowledged [them], and said, She is more righteous than I, because I have not given her to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.
texts.gen.38.27: And it came to pass at the time of her delivery, that behold, twins were in her womb.
texts.gen.38.28: And it came to pass when she brought forth, that one stretched out [his] hand, and the midwife took it and bound round his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.
texts.gen.38.29: And it came to pass as he drew back his hand, that behold, his brother came out; and she said, How hast thou broken forth! on thee be the breach! And they called his name Pherez.
texts.gen.38.30: And afterwards came out his brother, round whose hand was the scarlet thread; and they called his name Zerah.
texts.gen.39.1: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, a chamberlain of Pharaoh, the captain of the life-guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down thither.
texts.gen.39.2: And Jehovah was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
texts.gen.39.3: And his master saw that Jehovah was with him, and that Jehovah made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
texts.gen.39.4: And Joseph found favour in his eyes, and attended on him; and he set him over his house, and all that he had he gave into his hand.
texts.gen.39.5: And it came to pass from the time he had set him over his house and all that he had, that Jehovah blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of Jehovah was on all that he had in the house and in the field.
texts.gen.39.6: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand, and took cognizance of nothing with him, save the bread that he ate. And Joseph was of a beautiful form and of a beautiful countenance.
texts.gen.39.7: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes on Joseph, and said, Lie with me!
texts.gen.39.8: But he refused, and said to his master's wife, Behold, my master takes cognizance of nothing with me: what is in the house, and all that he has, he has given into my hand.
texts.gen.39.9: There is none greater in this house than I; neither has he withheld anything from me but thee, because thou art his wife; and how should I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
texts.gen.39.10: And it came to pass as she spoke to Joseph day by day and he hearkened not to her, to lie with her [and] to be with her,
texts.gen.39.11: that on a certain day he went into the house to do his business, and there was none of the men of the house there in the house.
texts.gen.39.12: Then she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me! But he left his garment in her hand, and fled and ran out.
texts.gen.39.13: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled forth,
texts.gen.39.14: that she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying, See, he has brought in a Hebrew man to us, to mock us: he came in to me, to lie with me; and I cried with a loud voice;
texts.gen.39.15: and it came to pass when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled and went out.
texts.gen.39.16: And she laid his garment by her until his lord came home.
texts.gen.39.17: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew bondman that thou hast brought to us came in to me to mock me;
texts.gen.39.18: and it came to pass as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled forth.
texts.gen.39.19: And it came to pass when his lord heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, After this manner did thy bondman to me, that his wrath was kindled.
texts.gen.39.20: And Joseph's lord took him and put him into the tower-house, [the] place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the tower-house.
texts.gen.39.21: And Jehovah was with Joseph, and extended mercy to him, and gave him favour in the eyes of the chief of the tower-house.
texts.gen.39.22: And the chief of the tower-house committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners that were in the tower-house; and whatever they had to do there he did.
texts.gen.39.23: The chief of the tower-house looked not to anything under his hand, because Jehovah was with him; and what he did, Jehovah made it prosper.
texts.gen.40.1: And it came to pass after these things, [that] the cup-bearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their lord the king of Egypt.
texts.gen.40.2: And Pharaoh was wroth with his two chamberlains -- with the chief of the cup-bearers and with the chief of the bakers;
texts.gen.40.3: and he put them in custody into the house of the captain of the life-guard, into the tower-house, into the place where Joseph was imprisoned.
texts.gen.40.4: And the captain of the life-guard appointed Joseph to them, that he should attend on them. And they were [several] days in custody.
texts.gen.40.5: And they dreamed a dream, both of them in one night, each his dream, each according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup-bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were imprisoned in the tower-house.
texts.gen.40.6: And Joseph came in to them in the morning, and looked on them, and behold, they were sad.
texts.gen.40.7: And he asked Pharaoh's chamberlains that were with him in custody in his lord's house, saying, Why are your faces [so] sad to-day?
texts.gen.40.8: And they said to him, We have dreamt a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said to them, [Do] not interpretations [belong] to God? tell me [your dreams], I pray you.
texts.gen.40.9: Then the chief of the cup-bearers told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;
texts.gen.40.10: and in the vine were three branches; and it was as though it budded: its blossoms shot forth, its clusters ripened into grapes.
texts.gen.40.11: And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
texts.gen.40.12: And Joseph said to him, This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days.
texts.gen.40.13: In yet three days will Pharaoh lift up thy head and restore thee to thy place, and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his cup-bearer.
texts.gen.40.14: Only bear a remembrance with thee of me when it goes well with thee, and deal kindly, I pray thee, with me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house;
texts.gen.40.15: for indeed I was stolen out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
texts.gen.40.16: And when the chief of the bakers saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
texts.gen.40.17: And in the uppermost basket there were all manner of victuals for Pharaoh that the baker makes, and the birds ate them out of the basket upon my head.
texts.gen.40.18: And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation of it: the three baskets are three days.
texts.gen.40.19: In yet three days will Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and hang thee on a tree; and the birds will eat thy flesh from off thee.
texts.gen.40.20: And it came to pass the third day -- Pharaoh's birthday -- that he made a feast to all his bondmen. And he lifted up the head of the chief of the cup-bearers, and the head of the chief of the bakers among his bondmen.
texts.gen.40.21: And he restored the chief of the cup-bearers to his office of cup-bearer again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
texts.gen.40.22: And he hanged the chief of the bakers, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
texts.gen.40.23: But the chief of the cup-bearers did not remember Joseph, and forgot him.
texts.gen.41.1: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.
texts.gen.41.2: And behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fine-looking and fat-fleshed, and they fed in the reed-grass.
texts.gen.41.3: And behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, bad-looking and lean-fleshed, and stood by the kine on the bank of the river.
texts.gen.41.4: And the kine that were bad-looking and lean-fleshed ate up the seven kine that were fine-looking and fat. And Pharaoh awoke.
texts.gen.41.5: And he slept and dreamed the second time; and behold, seven ears of corn grew up on one stalk, fat and good.
texts.gen.41.6: And behold, seven ears, thin and parched with the east wind, sprung up after them.
texts.gen.41.7: And the thin ears devoured the seven fat and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke; and behold, it was a dream.
texts.gen.41.8: And it came to pass in the morning, that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the scribes of Egypt, and all the sages who were therein, and Pharaoh told them his dream; but [there was] none to interpret them to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.9: Then spoke the chief of the cup-bearers to Pharaoh, saying, I remember mine offences this day.
texts.gen.41.10: Pharaoh was wroth with his bondmen, and put me in custody into the captain of the life-guard's house, me and the chief of the bakers.
texts.gen.41.11: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each according to the interpretation of his dream.
texts.gen.41.12: And there was there with us a Hebrew youth, a bondman of the captain of the life-guard, to whom we told [them], and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each he interpreted according to his dream.
texts.gen.41.13: And it came to pass, just as he interpreted to us, so it came about: me has he restored to my office, and him he hanged.
texts.gen.41.14: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph; and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. And he shaved [himself], and changed his clothes, and came in to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I have dreamt a dream, and there is none to interpret it. And I have heard say of thee, thou understandest a dream to interpret it.
texts.gen.41.16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
texts.gen.41.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood on the bank of the river.
texts.gen.41.18: And behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fat-fleshed and of fine form, and they fed in the reed-grass.
texts.gen.41.19: And behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor, and very ill-formed, and lean-fleshed -- such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness.
texts.gen.41.20: And the lean and bad kine ate up the seven first fat kine;
texts.gen.41.21: and they came into their belly, and it could not be known that they had come into their belly; and their look was bad, as at the beginning. And I awoke.
texts.gen.41.22: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, full and good.
texts.gen.41.23: And behold, seven ears, withered, thin, parched with the east wind, sprung up after them;
texts.gen.41.24: and the thin ears devoured the seven good ears. And I told it to the scribes; but there was none to make it known to me.
texts.gen.41.25: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God will do he has made known to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.26: The seven fine kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.
texts.gen.41.27: And the seven lean and bad kine that came up after them are seven years; and the seven empty ears, parched with the east wind, will be seven years of famine.
texts.gen.41.28: This is the word which I have spoken to Pharaoh: what God is about to do he has let Pharaoh see.
texts.gen.41.29: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.30: And there will arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine will waste away the land.
texts.gen.41.31: And the plenty will not be known afterwards in the land by reason of that famine; for it will be very grievous.
texts.gen.41.32: And as regards the double repetition of the dream to Pharaoh, it is that the thing is established by God, and God will hasten to do it.
texts.gen.41.33: And now let Pharaoh look himself out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.34: Let Pharaoh do [this]: let him appoint overseers over the land, and take the fifth part of the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty,
texts.gen.41.35: and let them gather all the food of these coming good years, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, for food in the cities, and keep [it].
texts.gen.41.36: And let the food be as store for the land for the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt, that the land perish not through the famine.
texts.gen.41.37: And the word was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his bondmen.
texts.gen.41.38: And Pharaoh said to his bondmen, Shall we find [one] as this, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?
texts.gen.41.39: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Since God has made all this known to thee, there is none [so] discreet and wise as thou.
texts.gen.41.40: Thou shalt be over my house, and according to thy commandment shall all my people regulate themselves; only concerning the throne will I be greater than thou.
texts.gen.41.41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.42: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in clothes of byssus, and put a gold chain on his neck.
texts.gen.41.43: And he caused him to ride in the second chariot that he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee! and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I am Pharaoh; and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.45: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnath-paaneah, and gave him as wife Asnath the daughter of Potipherah the priest in On. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.46: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh, and passed through the whole land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.47: And in the seven years of plenty the land brought forth by handfuls.
texts.gen.41.48: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years that was in the land of Egypt, and put the food in the cities; the food of the fields of the city, which were round about it, he laid up in it.
texts.gen.41.49: And Joseph laid up corn as sand of the sea exceeding much, until they left off numbering; for it was without number.
texts.gen.41.50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asnath the daughter of Potipherah the priest in On bore to him.
texts.gen.41.51: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh -- For God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house.
texts.gen.41.52: And the name of the second he called Ephraim -- For God has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.
texts.gen.41.53: And the seven years of plenty that were in the land of Egypt were ended;
texts.gen.41.54: and the seven years of the dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said. And there was dearth in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
texts.gen.41.55: And all the land of Egypt suffered from the dearth. And the people cried to Pharaoh for bread; and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, Go to Joseph: what he says to you, that do.
texts.gen.41.56: And the famine was on all the earth. And Joseph opened every place in which there was [provision], and sold grain to the Egyptians; and the famine was grievous in the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.57: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph, to buy [grain], because the famine was grievous on the whole earth.
texts.gen.42.1: And Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?
texts.gen.42.2: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt; go down thither and buy [grain] for us from thence, in order that we may live, and not die.
texts.gen.42.3: And Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy [grain] out of Egypt.
texts.gen.42.4: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest mischief may befall him.
texts.gen.42.5: So the sons of Israel came to buy [grain] among those that came; for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.6: And Joseph, he was the governor over the land -- he it was that sold [the corn] to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brethren came and bowed down to him, the face to the earth.
texts.gen.42.7: And Joseph saw his brethren, and knew them; but he made himself strange to them, and spoke roughly to them, and said to them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan, to buy food.
texts.gen.42.8: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they did not know him.
texts.gen.42.9: And Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamt of them; and he said to them, Ye are spies: to see the exposed places of the land ye are come.
texts.gen.42.10: And they said to him, No, my lord; but to buy food are thy servants come.
texts.gen.42.11: We are all one man's sons; we are honest: thy servants are not spies.
texts.gen.42.12: And he said to them, No; but to see the exposed places of the land are ye come.
texts.gen.42.13: And they said, Thy servants were twelve brethren, sons of one man, in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is not.
texts.gen.42.14: And Joseph said to them, That is it that I have spoken to you, saying, Ye are spies.
texts.gen.42.15: By this ye shall be put to the proof: as Pharaoh lives, ye shall not go forth hence, unless your youngest brother come hither!
texts.gen.42.16: Send one of you, that he may fetch your brother, but ye shall be imprisoned, and your words shall be put to the proof, whether the truth is in you; and if not, as Pharaoh lives, ye are spies.
texts.gen.42.17: And he put them in custody three days.
texts.gen.42.18: And Joseph said to them the third day, This do, that ye may live: I fear God.
texts.gen.42.19: If ye are honest, let one of your brethren remain bound in the house of your prison, but go ye, carry grain for the hunger of your households;
texts.gen.42.20: and bring your youngest brother to me, in order that your words be verified, and that ye may not die. And they did so.
texts.gen.42.21: Then they said one to another, We are indeed guilty concerning our brother, whose anguish of soul we saw when he besought us, and we did not hearken; therefore this distress is come upon us.
texts.gen.42.22: And Reuben answered them, saying, Did I not speak to you, saying, Do not sin against the lad? But ye did not hearken; and now behold, his blood also is required.
texts.gen.42.23: And they did not know that Joseph understood, for the interpreter was between them.
texts.gen.42.24: And he turned away from them, and wept. And he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
texts.gen.42.25: And Joseph gave orders to fill their vessels with corn, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way. And thus did they to them.
texts.gen.42.26: And they loaded their asses with their grain, and departed thence.
texts.gen.42.27: And one of them opened his sack to give his ass food in the inn, and saw his money, and behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
texts.gen.42.28: And he said to his brethren, My money is returned [to me], and behold, it is even in my sack. And their heart failed [them], and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this [that] God has done to us?
texts.gen.42.29: And they came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father, and told him all that had befallen them, saying,
texts.gen.42.30: The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly to us, and treated us as spies of the land.
texts.gen.42.31: And we said to him, We are honest; we are not spies:
texts.gen.42.32: we are twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.33: And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, Hereby shall I know that ye are honest: leave one of your brethren with me, and take [for] the hunger of your households, and go,
texts.gen.42.34: and bring your youngest brother to me, and I shall know that ye are not spies, but are honest. Your brother will I give up to you; and ye may trade in the land.
texts.gen.42.35: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man had his bundle of money in his sack; and they saw their bundles of money, they and their father, and were afraid.
texts.gen.42.36: And Jacob their father said to them, Ye have bereaved me of children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin! All these things are against me.
texts.gen.42.37: And Reuben spoke to his father, saying, Slay my two sons if I bring him not back to thee: give him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.
texts.gen.42.38: But he said, My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left; and if mischief should befall him by the way in which ye go, then would ye bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to Sheol.
texts.gen.43.1: And the famine was grievous in the land.
texts.gen.43.2: And it came to pass, when they had finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, Go again, buy us a little food.
texts.gen.43.3: And Judah spoke to him, saying, The man did positively testify to us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, unless your brother be with you.
texts.gen.43.4: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food;
texts.gen.43.5: but if thou do not send [him], we will not go down, for the man said to us, Ye shall not see my face, unless your brother be with you.
texts.gen.43.6: And Israel said, Why did ye deal [so] ill with me [as] to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?
texts.gen.43.7: And they said, The man asked very closely after us, and after our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye a brother? And we told him according to the tenor of these words. Could we at all know that he would say, Bring your brother down?
texts.gen.43.8: And Judah said to Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live, and not die, both we and thou and our little ones.
texts.gen.43.9: I will be surety for him: of my hand shalt thou require him; if I bring him not to thee, and set him before thy face, then shall I be guilty toward thee for ever.
texts.gen.43.10: For had we not lingered, we should now certainly have returned already twice.
texts.gen.43.11: And their father Israel said to them, If it is then so, do this: take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a gift: a little balsam and a little honey, tragacanth and ladanum, pistacia-nuts and almonds.
texts.gen.43.12: And take other money in your hand, and the money that was returned to you in the mouth of your sacks, carry back in your hand: perhaps it is an oversight.
texts.gen.43.13: And take your brother, and arise, go again to the man.
texts.gen.43.14: And the Almighty ùGod give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother and Benjamin! And I, if I be bereaved of children, am bereaved.
texts.gen.43.15: And the men took that gift, and took double money in their hand, and Benjamin, and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and came before Joseph.
texts.gen.43.16: And Joseph saw Benjamin with them, and said to the [man] who was over his house, Bring the men into the house, and slaughter cattle, and make ready; for the men shall eat with me at noon.
texts.gen.43.17: And the man did as Joseph had said; and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
texts.gen.43.18: And the men were afraid because they were brought into Joseph's house, and said, Because of the money that was returned to us in our sacks at the beginning are we brought in, that he may turn against us, and fall upon us and take us for bondmen, and our asses.
texts.gen.43.19: And they came up to the man that was over Joseph's house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,
texts.gen.43.20: and said, Ah! my lord, we came indeed down at the first to buy food.
texts.gen.43.21: And it came to pass when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and behold, [every] man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money according to its weight; and we have brought it again in our hand.
texts.gen.43.22: And other money have we brought down in our hand to buy food. We do not know who put our money in our sacks.
texts.gen.43.23: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks; your money came to me. And he brought Simeon out to them.
texts.gen.43.24: And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses food.
texts.gen.43.25: And they made ready the gift for Joseph's coming at noon; for they had heard that they should eat bread there.
texts.gen.43.26: When Joseph came home, they brought him the gift that was in their hand, into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.
texts.gen.43.27: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well -- the old man of whom ye spoke? Is he yet alive?
texts.gen.43.28: And they said, Thy servant our father is well; he is yet alive. And they bowed, and made obeisance.
texts.gen.43.29: And he lifted up his eyes and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, Is this your younger brother of whom ye spoke to me? And he said, God be gracious to thee, my son!
texts.gen.43.30: And Joseph made haste, for his bowels burned for his brother; and he sought [a place] to weep, and he went into the chamber, and wept there.
texts.gen.43.31: And he washed his face, and came out, and controlled himself, and said, Set on bread.
texts.gen.43.32: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves; because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.
texts.gen.43.33: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth; and the men marvelled one at another.
texts.gen.43.34: And he had portions carried to them from before him. And Benjamin's portion was five times greater than the portions of them all. And they drank, and made merry with him.
texts.gen.44.1: And he commanded him who was over his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry; and put every man's money in the mouth of his sack.
texts.gen.44.2: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and his grain-money. And he did according to the word of Joseph which he had spoken.
texts.gen.44.3: In the morning, when it was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.
texts.gen.44.4: They were gone out of the city, [and] not [yet] far off, when Joseph said to him who was over his house, Up! follow after the men; and when thou overtakest them, thou shalt say to them, Why have ye rewarded evil for good?
texts.gen.44.5: Is not this [it] in which my lord drinks, and in which indeed he divines? Ye have done evil [in] what ye have done.
texts.gen.44.6: And he overtook them, and he spoke to them these words.
texts.gen.44.7: And they said to him, Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from thy servants to do such a thing!
texts.gen.44.8: Behold, the money that we found in our sacks' mouths we have brought again to thee from the land of Canaan; and how should we steal out of thy lord's house silver or gold?
texts.gen.44.9: With whomsoever of thy servants it is found, let him die; and we also will be my lord's bondmen.
texts.gen.44.10: And he said, Now also [let] it [be] according to your words: let him with whom it is found be my bondman, but ye shall be blameless.
texts.gen.44.11: And they hasted and laid down every man his sack on the ground, and opened every man his sack.
texts.gen.44.12: And he searched carefully: he began at the eldest, and ended at the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
texts.gen.44.13: Then they rent their clothes, and loaded every man his ass, and they returned to the city.
texts.gen.44.14: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph's house; and he was still there; and they fell down before him to the ground.
texts.gen.44.15: And Joseph said to them, What deed is this which ye have done? Did ye not know that such a man as I can certainly divine?
texts.gen.44.16: And Judah said, What shall we say to my lord? what shall we speak, and how justify ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of thy servants; behold, we are my lord's bondmen, both we, and he in whose hand the cup has been found.
texts.gen.44.17: And he said, Far be it from me to do so! The man in whose hand the cup has been found, he shall be my bondman; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.
texts.gen.44.18: Then Judah came near to him, and said, Ah! my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant; for thou art even as Pharaoh.
texts.gen.44.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?
texts.gen.44.20: And we said to my lord, We have an aged father, and a child born to him in his old age, [yet] young; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.
texts.gen.44.21: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down to me, that I may set mine eye on him.
texts.gen.44.22: And we said to my lord, The youth cannot leave his father: if he should leave his father, [his father] would die.
texts.gen.44.23: And thou saidst to thy servants, Unless your youngest brother come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.
texts.gen.44.24: And it came to pass when we came up to thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
texts.gen.44.25: And our father said, Go again, buy us a little food.
texts.gen.44.26: But we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down; for we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.
texts.gen.44.27: And thy servant my father said to us, Ye know that my wife bore me two [sons];
texts.gen.44.28: and the one went out from me, and I said, He must certainly have been torn in pieces; and I have not seen him [again] hitherto.
texts.gen.44.29: And if ye take this one also from me, and mischief should befall him, ye will bring down my grey hairs with misery to Sheol.
texts.gen.44.30: And now, when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not with us, -- seeing that his life is bound up with his life,
texts.gen.44.31: it will come to pass when he sees that the lad is not [there], that he will die; and thy servants will bring down the grey hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.
texts.gen.44.32: For thy servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, If I bring him not to thee, then I shall be guilty toward my father all my days.
texts.gen.44.33: And now, let thy servant stay, I pray thee, instead of the lad a bondman to my lord, and let the lad go up with his brethren;
texts.gen.44.34: for how should I go up to my father if the lad were not with me? -- lest I see the evil that would come on my father.
texts.gen.45.1: And Joseph could not control himself before all them that stood by him, and he cried, Put every man out from me! And no man stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brethren.
texts.gen.45.2: And he raised his voice in weeping; and the Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
texts.gen.45.3: And Joseph said to his brethren, I am Joseph. Does my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled at his presence.
texts.gen.45.4: And Joseph said to his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
texts.gen.45.5: And now, be not grieved, and be not angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
texts.gen.45.6: For the famine has been these two years in the land; and yet there are five years in which there will be neither ploughing nor harvest.
texts.gen.45.7: So God sent me before you to preserve you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
texts.gen.45.8: And now it was not you [that] sent me here, but God; and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and governor over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.45.9: Haste and go up to my father, and say to him, Thus says thy son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, tarry not.
texts.gen.45.10: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near to me, thou, and thy sons, and thy sons' sons, and thy sheep, and thy cattle, and all that thou hast.
texts.gen.45.11: And there will I maintain thee; for yet there are five years of famine; in order that thou be not impoverished, thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast.
texts.gen.45.12: And behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth which speaks to you.
texts.gen.45.13: And tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen, and haste and bring down my father hither.
texts.gen.45.14: And he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept on his neck.
texts.gen.45.15: And he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them; and after that his brethren talked with him.
texts.gen.45.16: And the report was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, Joseph's brethren are come. And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his bondmen.
texts.gen.45.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Say to thy brethren, Do this: load your beasts and depart, go into the land of Canaan,
texts.gen.45.18: and take your father and your households, and come to me; and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.
texts.gen.45.19: And thou art commanded -- this do: take waggons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and take up your father, and come.
texts.gen.45.20: And let not your eye regret your stuff; for the good of all the land of Egypt shall be yours.
