texts.gen.45.21: And the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them waggons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
texts.gen.45.22: To each one of them all he gave changes of clothing; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred [pieces] of silver and five changes of clothing.
texts.gen.45.23: And to his father he sent this: ten asses laden with the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses laden with corn and bread, and food for his father by the way.
texts.gen.45.24: And he sent his brethren away, and they departed. And he said to them, Do not quarrel on the way.
texts.gen.45.25: And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan to Jacob their father.
texts.gen.45.26: And they told him, saying, Joseph is still alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And his heart fainted, for he did not believe them.
texts.gen.45.27: And they spoke to him all the words of Joseph, which he had spoken to them. And he saw the waggons that Joseph had sent to carry him. And the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
texts.gen.45.28: And Israel said, It is enough: Joseph my son is yet alive; I will go and see him before I die.
texts.gen.46.1: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba; and he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
texts.gen.46.2: And God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night and said, Jacob, Jacob! And he said, Here am I.
texts.gen.46.3: And he said, I am ùGod, the God of thy father: fear not to go down to Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation.
texts.gen.46.4: I will go down with thee to Egypt, and I will also certainly bring thee up; and Joseph shall put his hand on thine eyes.
texts.gen.46.5: And Jacob rose up from Beer-sheba; and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, on the waggons that Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
texts.gen.46.6: And they took their cattle, and their goods which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and came to Egypt, Jacob and all his seed with him;
texts.gen.46.7: his sons and his sons' sons with him, his daughters and his sons' daughters and all his seed he brought with him to Egypt.
texts.gen.46.8: And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt: Jacob and his sons. Jacob's firstborn, Reuben.
texts.gen.46.9: And the sons of Reuben: Enoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
texts.gen.46.10: -- And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Saul the son of a Canaanitish woman.
texts.gen.46.11: -- And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
texts.gen.46.12: -- And the sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pherez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pherez were Hezron and Hamul.
texts.gen.46.13: -- And the sons of Issachar: Tola, and Puah, and Job, and Shimron.
texts.gen.46.14: -- And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
texts.gen.46.15: -- These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Padan-Aram; and his daughter, Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
texts.gen.46.16: And the sons of Gad: Ziphion and Haggi, Shuni and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
texts.gen.46.17: -- And the sons of Asher: Jimnah, and Jishvah, and Jishvi, and Beriah; and Serah their sister; and the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
texts.gen.46.18: -- These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob: sixteen souls.
texts.gen.46.19: The sons of Rachel Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
texts.gen.46.20: And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asnath bore to him, the daughter of Potipherah the priest in On.
texts.gen.46.21: -- And the sons of Benjamin: Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera and Naaman, Ehi and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
texts.gen.46.22: -- These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
texts.gen.46.23: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
texts.gen.46.24: -- And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
texts.gen.46.25: -- These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
texts.gen.46.26: All the souls that came with Jacob to Egypt, that had come out of his loins, besides Jacob's sons' wives: all the souls were sixty-six.
texts.gen.46.27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob that came to Egypt were seventy.
texts.gen.46.28: And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to give notice before he came to Goshen. And they came into the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.46.29: Then Joseph yoked his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and he presented himself to him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
texts.gen.46.30: And Israel said to Joseph, Now let me die, after I have seen thy face, since thou still livest.
texts.gen.46.31: And Joseph said to his brethren and to his father's house, I will go up, and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, My brethren and my father's house, who were in the land of Canaan, are come to me;
texts.gen.46.32: and the men are shepherds, for they have been occupied with cattle; and they have brought their sheep, and their cattle, and all that they have.
texts.gen.46.33: And it shall come to pass that when Pharaoh shall call you and say, What is your occupation?
texts.gen.46.34: then ye shall say, Thy servants are men that have been occupied with cattle from our youth even until now, both we and our fathers; in order that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.
texts.gen.47.1: And Joseph came and told Pharaoh and said, My father and my brethren, and their sheep and their cattle, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.47.2: And he took from the whole number of his brethren, five men, and set them before Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.3: And Pharaoh said to his brethren, What is your occupation? And they said to Pharaoh, Thy servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers.
texts.gen.47.4: And they said to Pharaoh, To sojourn in the land are we come; for there is no pasture for the sheep that thy servants have, for the famine is grievous in the land of Canaan; and now, we pray thee, let thy servants dwell in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.47.5: And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren are come to thee.
texts.gen.47.6: The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land settle thy father and thy brethren: let them dwell in the land of Goshen. And if thou knowest men of activity among them, then set them as overseers of cattle over what I have.
texts.gen.47.7: And Joseph brought Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh. And Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, How many are the days of the years of thy life?
texts.gen.47.9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, The days of the years of my sojourning are a hundred and thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they do not attain to the days of the years of the life of my fathers, in the days of their sojourning.
texts.gen.47.10: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.11: And Joseph settled his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
texts.gen.47.12: And Joseph maintained his father, and his brethren, and all his father's household, with bread, according to the number of the little ones.
texts.gen.47.13: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very grievous; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan were exhausted through the famine.
texts.gen.47.14: And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought; and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.
texts.gen.47.15: And when money came to an end in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, Give us bread! for why should we die before thee? for [our] money is all gone.
texts.gen.47.16: And Joseph said, Give your cattle, and I will give you for your cattle, if [your] money be all gone.
texts.gen.47.17: And they brought their cattle to Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread for horses, and for flocks of sheep, and for herds of cattle, and for asses; and he fed them with bread for all their cattle that year.
texts.gen.47.18: And that year ended; and they came to him the second year, and said to him, We will not hide [it] from my lord that since [our] money is come to an end, and the herds of cattle are in the possession of my lord, nothing is left before my lord but our bodies and our land.
texts.gen.47.19: Why should we die before thine eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be bondmen to Pharaoh; and give seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land be not desolate.
texts.gen.47.20: And Joseph bought all the soil of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them; and the land became Pharaoh's.
texts.gen.47.21: And as for the people, he removed them into the cities, from [one] end of the borders of Egypt even to the [other] end of it.
texts.gen.47.22: Only the land of the priests he did not buy; for the priests had an assigned portion from Pharaoh, and ate their assigned portion which Pharaoh had given them; so they did not sell their land.
texts.gen.47.23: And Joseph said to the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is seed for you, and sow the land.
texts.gen.47.24: And it shall come to pass in the increase that ye shall give the fifth to Pharaoh, and the four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.
texts.gen.47.25: And they said, Thou hast saved us alive. Let us find favour in the eyes of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's bondmen.
texts.gen.47.26: And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt to this day, [that] the fifth should be for Pharaoh, except the land of the priests: theirs alone did not become Pharaoh's.
texts.gen.47.27: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they had possessions in it, and were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly.
texts.gen.47.28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years.
texts.gen.47.29: And the days of Israel approached that he should die. And he called his son Joseph, and said to him, If now I have found favour in thine eyes, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me: bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt;
texts.gen.47.30: but when I shall lie with my fathers, thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their sepulchre. And he said, I will do according to thy word.
texts.gen.47.31: And he said, Swear to me; and he swore to him. And Israel worshipped on the bed's head.
texts.gen.48.1: And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick. And he took with him his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim.
texts.gen.48.2: And one told Jacob and said, Behold, thy son Joseph is coming to thee. And Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
texts.gen.48.3: And Jacob said to Joseph, The Almighty ùGod appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
texts.gen.48.4: and he said to me, Behold, I will make thee fruitful and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a company of peoples; and will give this land to thy seed after thee [for] an everlasting possession.
texts.gen.48.5: And now thy two sons, who were born to thee in the land of Egypt before I came to thee into Egypt, shall be mine: Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon.
texts.gen.48.6: And thy family which thou hast begotten after them shall be thine: they shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.
texts.gen.48.7: And as for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was yet a certain distance to come to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.
texts.gen.48.8: And Israel beheld Joseph's sons, and said, Who are these?
texts.gen.48.9: And Joseph said to his father, They are my sons, whom God has given me here. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, to me, that I may bless them.
texts.gen.48.10: But the eyes of Israel were heavy from age: he could not see. And he brought them nearer to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
texts.gen.48.11: And Israel said to Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face; and behold, God has let me see also thy seed.
texts.gen.48.12: And Joseph brought them out from his knees, and bowed down with his face to the earth.
texts.gen.48.13: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought [them] near to him.
texts.gen.48.14: But Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid [it] on Ephraim's head -- now he was the younger -- and his left hand on Manasseh's head; guiding his hands intelligently, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
texts.gen.48.15: And he blessed Joseph, and said, The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God that shepherded me all my life long to this day,
texts.gen.48.16: the Angel that redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the land!
texts.gen.48.17: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it was evil in his eyes; and he took hold of his father's hand to remove it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.
texts.gen.48.18: And Joseph said to his father, Not so, my father, for this is the firstborn: put thy right hand on his head.
texts.gen.48.19: But his father refused and said, I know, my son, I know: he also will become a people, and he also will be great; but truly his younger brother will be greater than he; and his seed will become the fulness of nations.
texts.gen.48.20: And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee will Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and Manasseh! And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
texts.gen.48.21: And Israel said to Joseph, Behold, I die; and God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
texts.gen.48.22: And *I* have given to thee one tract [of land] above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.
texts.gen.49.1: And Jacob called his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, and I will tell you what will befall you at the end of days.
texts.gen.49.2: Assemble yourselves, and hear, ye sons of Jacob, And listen to Israel your father.
texts.gen.49.3: Reuben, thou art my firstborn, My might, and the firstfruits of my vigour: Excellency of dignity, and excellency of strength.
texts.gen.49.4: Impetuous as the waters, thou shalt have no pre-eminence; Because thou wentest up to thy father's couch: Then defiledst thou [it]: he went up to my bed.
texts.gen.49.5: Simeon and Levi are brethren: Instruments of violence their swords.
texts.gen.49.6: My soul, come not into their council; Mine honour, be not united with their assembly; For in their anger they slew men, And in their wantonness houghed oxen.
texts.gen.49.7: Cursed be their anger, for it [was] violent; And their rage, for it [was] cruel! I will divide them in Jacob, And scatter them in Israel.
texts.gen.49.8: Judah -- [as to] thee, thy brethren will praise thee; Thy hand will be upon the neck of thine enemies; Thy father's children will bow down to thee.
texts.gen.49.9: Judah is a young lion; From the prey, my son, thou art gone up. He stoopeth, he layeth himself down as a lion, And as a lioness: who will rouse him up?
texts.gen.49.10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, Nor the lawgiver from between his feet, Until Shiloh come, And to him will be the obedience of peoples.
texts.gen.49.11: He bindeth his foal to the vine, And his ass's colt to the choice vine; He washeth his dress in wine, And his garment in the blood of grapes.
texts.gen.49.12: The eyes are red with wine, And the teeth [are] white with milk.
texts.gen.49.13: Zebulun will dwell at the shore of the seas; Yea, he will be at the shore of the ships, And his side [toucheth] upon Sidon.
texts.gen.49.14: Issachar is a bony ass, Crouching down between two hurdles.
texts.gen.49.15: And he saw the rest that it was good, And the land that it was pleasant; And he bowed his shoulder to bear, And was a tributary servant.
texts.gen.49.16: Dan will judge his people, As another of the tribes of Israel.
texts.gen.49.17: Dan will be a serpent on the way, A horned snake on the path, Which biteth the horse's heels, So that the rider falleth backwards.
texts.gen.49.18: I wait for thy salvation, O Jehovah.
texts.gen.49.19: Gad -- troops will rush upon him; But he will rush upon the heel.
texts.gen.49.20: Out of Asher, his bread shall be fat, And he will give royal dainties.
texts.gen.49.21: Naphtali is a hind let loose; He giveth goodly words.
texts.gen.49.22: Joseph is a fruitful bough; A fruitful bough by a well; [His] branches shoot over the wall.
texts.gen.49.23: The archers have provoked him, And shot at, and hated him;
texts.gen.49.24: But his bow abideth firm, And the arms of his hands are supple By the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob. From thence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel:
texts.gen.49.25: From the ùGod of thy father, and he will help thee; And from the Almighty, and he will bless thee -- With blessings of heaven from above, With blessings of the deep that lieth under, With blessings of the breast and of the womb.
texts.gen.49.26: The blessings of thy father surpass the blessings of my ancestors, Unto the bounds of the everlasting hills: They shall be on the head of Joseph, And on the crown of the head of him that was separated from his brethren.
texts.gen.49.27: Benjamin -- [as] a wolf will he tear to pieces; In the morning he will devour the prey, And in the evening he will divide the booty.
texts.gen.49.28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them; and he blessed them: every one according to his blessing he blessed them.
texts.gen.49.29: And he charged them, and said to them, I am gathered to my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
texts.gen.49.30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is opposite to Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought of Ephron the Hittite along with the field for a possession of a sepulchre.
texts.gen.49.31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebecca his wife; and there I buried Leah.
texts.gen.49.32: The purchase of the field, and of the cave that is in it, was from the children of Heth.
texts.gen.49.33: And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered his feet into the bed, and expired, and was gathered to his peoples.
texts.gen.50.1: And Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.
texts.gen.50.2: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father. And the physicians embalmed Israel.
texts.gen.50.3: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those who are embalmed. And the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.
texts.gen.50.4: And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found favour in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
texts.gen.50.5: My father made me swear, saying, Behold, I die; in my grave which I have dug myself in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. And now, let me go up, I pray thee, that I may bury my father; and I will come again.
texts.gen.50.6: And Pharaoh said, Go up and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.
texts.gen.50.7: And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the bondmen of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
texts.gen.50.8: and all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father's house; only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.50.9: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen; and the camp was very great.
texts.gen.50.10: And they came to the threshing-floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan; and there they lamented with a great and very grievous lamentation; and he made a mourning for his father of seven days.
texts.gen.50.11: And the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing-floor of Atad, and they said, This is a grievous mourning of the Egyptians. Therefore the name of it was called Abel-Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
texts.gen.50.12: And his sons did to him according as he had commanded them;
texts.gen.50.13: and his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah which Abraham had bought along with the field, for a possession of a sepulchre, of Ephron the Hittite, opposite to Mamre.
texts.gen.50.14: And, after he had buried his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brethren, and all that had gone up with him to bury his father.
texts.gen.50.15: And when Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, If now Joseph should be hostile to us, and should indeed requite us all the evil that we did to him!
texts.gen.50.16: And they sent a messenger to Joseph, saying, Thy father commanded before he died, saying,
texts.gen.50.17: Thus shall ye speak to Joseph: Oh forgive, I pray thee, the transgression of thy brethren, and their sin! for they did evil to thee. And now, we pray thee, forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
texts.gen.50.18: And his brethren also went and fell down before his face, and said, Behold, we are thy bondmen.
texts.gen.50.19: And Joseph said to them, Fear not: am I then in the place of God?
texts.gen.50.20: Ye indeed meant evil against me: God meant it for good, in order that he might do as [it is] this day, to save a great people alive.
texts.gen.50.21: And now, fear not: I will maintain you and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spoke consolingly to them.
texts.gen.50.22: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he and his father's house; and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
texts.gen.50.23: And Joseph saw Ephraim's children of the third [generation]; the sons also of Machir the son of Manasseh were born on Joseph's knees.
texts.gen.50.24: And Joseph said to his brethren, I die; and God will certainly visit you, and bring you up out of this land, into the land that he swore unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
texts.gen.50.25: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will certainly visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones hence.
texts.gen.50.26: And Joseph died, a hundred and ten years old; and they embalmed him; and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

texts.gen.1.1: In the beginning of God's preparing the heavens and the earth --
texts.gen.1.2: the earth hath existed waste and void, and darkness [is] on the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God fluttering on the face of the waters,
texts.gen.1.3: and God saith, `Let light be;' and light is.
texts.gen.1.4: And God seeth the light that [it is] good, and God separateth between the light and the darkness,
texts.gen.1.5: and God calleth to the light `Day,' and to the darkness He hath called `Night;' and there is an evening, and there is a morning -- day one.
texts.gen.1.6: And God saith, `Let an expanse be in the midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters and waters.'
texts.gen.1.7: And God maketh the expanse, and it separateth between the waters which [are] under the expanse, and the waters which [are] above the expanse: and it is so.
texts.gen.1.8: And God calleth to the expanse `Heavens;' and there is an evening, and there is a morning -- day second.
texts.gen.1.9: And God saith, `Let the waters under the heavens be collected unto one place, and let the dry land be seen:' and it is so.
texts.gen.1.10: And God calleth to the dry land `Earth,' and to the collection of the waters He hath called `Seas;' and God seeth that [it is] good.
texts.gen.1.11: And God saith, `Let the earth yield tender grass, herb sowing seed, fruit-tree (whose seed [is] in itself) making fruit after its kind, on the earth:' and it is so.
texts.gen.1.12: And the earth bringeth forth tender grass, herb sowing seed after its kind, and tree making fruit (whose seed [is] in itself) after its kind; and God seeth that [it is] good;
texts.gen.1.13: and there is an evening, and there is a morning -- day third.
texts.gen.1.14: And God saith, `Let luminaries be in the expanse of the heavens, to make a separation between the day and the night, then they have been for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years,
texts.gen.1.15: and they have been for luminaries in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth:' and it is so.
texts.gen.1.16: And God maketh the two great luminaries, the great luminary for the rule of the day, and the small luminary -- and the stars -- for the rule of the night;
texts.gen.1.17: and God giveth them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
texts.gen.1.18: and to rule over day and over night, and to make a separation between the light and the darkness; and God seeth that [it is] good;
texts.gen.1.19: and there is an evening, and there is a morning -- day fourth.
texts.gen.1.20: And God saith, `Let the waters teem with the teeming living creature, and fowl let fly on the earth on the face of the expanse of the heavens.'
texts.gen.1.21: And God prepareth the great monsters, and every living creature that is creeping, which the waters have teemed with, after their kind, and every fowl with wing, after its kind, and God seeth that [it is] good.
texts.gen.1.22: And God blesseth them, saying, `Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and the fowl let multiply in the earth:'
texts.gen.1.23: and there is an evening, and there is a morning -- day fifth.
texts.gen.1.24: And God saith, `Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind, cattle and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after its kind:' and it is so.
texts.gen.1.25: And God maketh the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, and God seeth that [it is] good.
texts.gen.1.26: And God saith, `Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness, and let them rule over fish of the sea, and over fowl of the heavens, and over cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth.'
texts.gen.1.27: And God prepareth the man in His image; in the image of God He prepared him, a male and a female He prepared them.
texts.gen.1.28: And God blesseth them, and God saith to them, `Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over fish of the sea, and over fowl of the heavens, and over every living thing that is creeping upon the earth.'
texts.gen.1.29: And God saith, `Lo, I have given to you every herb sowing seed, which [is] upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which [is] the fruit of a tree sowing seed, to you it is for food;
texts.gen.1.30: and to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to every creeping thing on the earth, in which [is] breath of life, every green herb [is] for food:' and it is so.
texts.gen.1.31: And God seeth all that He hath done, and lo, very good; and there is an evening, and there is a morning -- day the sixth.
texts.gen.2.1: And the heavens and the earth are completed, and all their host;
texts.gen.2.2: and God completeth by the seventh day His work which He hath made, and ceaseth by the seventh day from all His work which He hath made.
texts.gen.2.3: And God blesseth the seventh day, and sanctifieth it, for in it He hath ceased from all His work which God had prepared for making.
texts.gen.2.4: These [are] births of the heavens and of the earth in their being prepared, in the day of Jehovah God's making earth and heavens;
texts.gen.2.5: and no shrub of the field is yet in the earth, and no herb of the field yet sprouteth, for Jehovah God hath not rained upon the earth, and a man there is not to serve the ground,
texts.gen.2.6: and a mist goeth up from the earth, and hath watered the whole face of the ground.
texts.gen.2.7: And Jehovah God formeth the man -- dust from the ground, and breatheth into his nostrils breath of life, and the man becometh a living creature.
texts.gen.2.8: And Jehovah God planteth a garden in Eden, at the east, and He setteth there the man whom He hath formed;
texts.gen.2.9: and Jehovah God causeth to sprout from the ground every tree desirable for appearance, and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
texts.gen.2.10: And a river is going out from Eden to water the garden, and from thence it is parted, and hath become four chief [rivers];
texts.gen.2.11: the name of the one [is] Pison, it [is] that which is surrounding the whole land of the Havilah where the gold [is],
texts.gen.2.12: and the gold of that land [is] good, there [is] the bdolach and the shoham stone;
texts.gen.2.13: and the name of the second river [is] Gibon, it [is] that which is surrounding the whole land of Cush;
texts.gen.2.14: and the name of the third river [is] Hiddekel, it [is] that which is going east of Asshur; and the fourth river is Phrat.
texts.gen.2.15: And Jehovah God taketh the man, and causeth him to rest in the garden of Eden, to serve it, and to keep it.
texts.gen.2.16: And Jehovah God layeth a charge on the man, saying, `Of every tree of the garden eating thou dost eat;
texts.gen.2.17: and of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou dost not eat of it, for in the day of thine eating of it -- dying thou dost die.'
texts.gen.2.18: And Jehovah God saith, `Not good for the man to be alone, I do make to him an helper -- as his counterpart.'
texts.gen.2.19: And Jehovah God formeth from the ground every beast of the field, and every fowl of the heavens, and bringeth in unto the man, to see what he doth call it; and whatever the man calleth a living creature, that [is] its name.
texts.gen.2.20: And the man calleth names to all the cattle, and to fowl of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; and to man hath not been found an helper -- as his counterpart.
texts.gen.2.21: And Jehovah God causeth a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he sleepeth, and He taketh one of his ribs, and closeth up flesh in its stead.
texts.gen.2.22: And Jehovah God buildeth up the rib which He hath taken out of the man into a woman, and bringeth her in unto the man;
texts.gen.2.23: and the man saith, `This [is] the [proper] step! bone of my bone, and flesh of my flesh!' for this it is called Woman, for from a man hath this been taken;
texts.gen.2.24: therefore doth a man leave his father and his mother, and hath cleaved unto his wife, and they have become one flesh.
texts.gen.2.25: And they are both of them naked, the man and his wife, and they are not ashamed of themselves.
texts.gen.3.1: And the serpent hath been subtile above every beast of the field which Jehovah God hath made, and he saith unto the woman, `Is it true that God hath said, Ye do not eat of every tree of the garden?'
texts.gen.3.2: And the woman saith unto the serpent, `Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we do eat,
texts.gen.3.3: and of the fruit of the tree which [is] in the midst of the garden God hath said, Ye do not eat of it, nor touch it, lest ye die.'
texts.gen.3.4: And the serpent saith unto the woman, `Dying, ye do not die,
texts.gen.3.5: for God doth know that in the day of your eating of it -- your eyes have been opened, and ye have been as God, knowing good and evil.'
texts.gen.3.6: And the woman seeth that the tree [is] good for food, and that it [is] pleasant to the eyes, and the tree is desirable to make [one] wise, and she taketh of its fruit and eateth, and giveth also to her husband with her, and he doth eat;
texts.gen.3.7: and the eyes of them both are opened, and they know that they [are] naked, and they sew fig-leaves, and make to themselves girdles.
texts.gen.3.8: And they hear the sound of Jehovah God walking up and down in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hide themselves from the face of Jehovah God in the midst of the trees of the garden.
texts.gen.3.9: And Jehovah God calleth unto the man, and saith to him, `Where [art] thou?'
texts.gen.3.10: and he saith, `Thy sound I have heard in the garden, and I am afraid, for I am naked, and I hide myself.'
texts.gen.3.11: And He saith, `Who hath declared to thee that thou [art] naked? of the tree of which I have commanded thee not to eat, hast thou eaten?'
texts.gen.3.12: and the man saith, `The woman whom Thou didst place with me -- she hath given to me of the tree -- and I do eat.'
texts.gen.3.13: And Jehovah God saith to the woman, `What [is] this thou hast done?' and the woman saith, `The serpent hath caused me to forget -- and I do eat.'
texts.gen.3.14: And Jehovah God saith unto the serpent, `Because thou hast done this, cursed [art] thou above all the cattle, and above every beast of the field: on thy belly dost thou go, and dust thou dost eat, all days of thy life;
texts.gen.3.15: and enmity I put between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; he doth bruise thee -- the head, and thou dost bruise him -- the heel.'
texts.gen.3.16: Unto the woman He said, `Multiplying I multiply thy sorrow and thy conception, in sorrow dost thou bear children, and toward thy husband [is] thy desire, and he doth rule over thee.'
texts.gen.3.17: And to the man He said, `Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and dost eat of the tree concerning which I have charged thee, saying, Thou dost not eat of it, cursed [is] the ground on thine account; in sorrow thou dost eat of it all days of thy life,
texts.gen.3.18: and thorn and bramble it doth bring forth to thee, and thou hast eaten the herb of the field;
texts.gen.3.19: by the sweat of thy face thou dost eat bread till thy return unto the ground, for out of it hast thou been taken, for dust thou [art], and unto dust thou turnest back.'
texts.gen.3.20: And the man calleth his wife's name Eve: for she hath been mother of all living.
texts.gen.3.21: And Jehovah God doth make to the man and to his wife coats of skin, and doth clothe them.
texts.gen.3.22: And Jehovah God saith, `Lo, the man was as one of Us, as to the knowledge of good and evil; and now, lest he send forth his hand, and have taken also of the tree of life, and eaten, and lived to the age,' --
texts.gen.3.23: Jehovah God sendeth him forth from the garden of Eden to serve the ground from which he hath been taken;
texts.gen.3.24: yea, he casteth out the man, and causeth to dwell at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubs and the flame of the sword which is turning itself round to guard the way of the tree of life.
texts.gen.4.1: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceiveth and beareth Cain, and saith, `I have gotten a man by Jehovah;'
texts.gen.4.2: and she addeth to bear his brother, even Abel. And Abel is feeding a flock, and Cain hath been servant of the ground.
texts.gen.4.3: And it cometh to pass at the end of days that Cain bringeth from the fruit of the ground a present to Jehovah;
texts.gen.4.4: and Abel, he hath brought, he also, from the female firstlings of his flock, even from their fat ones; and Jehovah looketh unto Abel and unto his present,
texts.gen.4.5: and unto Cain and unto his present He hath not looked; and it is very displeasing to Cain, and his countenance is fallen.
texts.gen.4.6: And Jehovah saith unto Cain, `Why hast thou displeasure? and why hath thy countenance fallen?
texts.gen.4.7: Is there not, if thou dost well, acceptance? and if thou dost not well, at the opening a sin-offering is crouching, and unto thee its desire, and thou rulest over it.'
texts.gen.4.8: And Cain saith unto Abel his brother, [`Let us go into the field;'] and it cometh to pass in their being in the field, that Cain riseth up against Abel his brother, and slayeth him.
texts.gen.4.9: And Jehovah saith unto Cain, `Where [is] Abel thy brother?' and he saith, `I have not known; my brother's keeper -- I?'
texts.gen.4.10: And He saith, `What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood is crying unto Me from the ground;
texts.gen.4.11: and now, cursed [art] thou from the ground, which hath opened her mouth to receive the blood of thy brother from thy hand;
texts.gen.4.12: when thou tillest the ground, it doth not add to give its strength to thee -- a wanderer, even a trembling one, thou art in the earth.'
texts.gen.4.13: And Cain saith unto Jehovah, `Greater is my punishment than to be borne;
texts.gen.4.14: lo, Thou hast driven me to-day from off the face of the ground, and from Thy face I am hid; and I have been a wanderer, even a trembling one, in the earth, and it hath been -- every one finding me doth slay me.'
texts.gen.4.15: And Jehovah saith to him, `Therefore -- of any slayer of Cain sevenfold it is required;' and Jehovah setteth to Cain a token that none finding him doth slay him.
texts.gen.4.16: And Cain goeth out from before Jehovah, and dwelleth in the land, moving about east of Eden;
texts.gen.4.17: and Cain knoweth his wife, and she conceiveth, and beareth Enoch; and he is building a city, and he calleth the name of the city, according to the name of his son -- Enoch.
texts.gen.4.18: And born to Enoch is Irad; and Irad hath begotten Mehujael; and Mehujael hath begotten Methusael; and Methusael hath begotten Lamech.
texts.gen.4.19: And Lamech taketh to himself two wives, the name of the one Adah, and the name of the second Zillah.
texts.gen.4.20: And Adah beareth Jabal, he hath been father of those inhabiting tents and purchased possessions;
texts.gen.4.21: and the name of his brother [is] Jubal, he hath been father of every one handling harp and organ.
texts.gen.4.22: And Zillah she also bare Tubal-Cain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron; and a sister of Tubal-Cain [is] Naamah.
texts.gen.4.23: And Lamech saith to his wives: -- `Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Wives of Lamech, give ear [to] my saying: For a man I have slain for my wound, Even a young man for my hurt;
texts.gen.4.24: For sevenfold is required for Cain, And for Lamech seventy and sevenfold.'
texts.gen.4.25: And Adam again knoweth his wife, and she beareth a son, and calleth his name Seth, `for God hath appointed for me another seed instead of Abel:' for Cain had slain him.
texts.gen.4.26: And to Seth, to him also a son hath been born, and he calleth his name Enos; then a beginning was made of preaching in the name of Jehovah.
texts.gen.5.1: This [is] an account of the births of Adam: In the day of God's preparing man, in the likeness of God He hath made him;
texts.gen.5.2: a male and a female He hath prepared them, and He blesseth them, and calleth their name Man, in the day of their being prepared.
texts.gen.5.3: And Adam liveth an hundred and thirty years, and begetteth [a son] in his likeness, according to his image, and calleth his name Seth.
texts.gen.5.4: And the days of Adam after his begetting Seth are eight hundred years, and he begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.5: And all the days of Adam which he lived are nine hundred and thirty years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.6: And Seth liveth an hundred and five years, and begetteth Enos.
texts.gen.5.7: And Seth liveth after his begetting Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.8: And all the days of Seth are nine hundred and twelve years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.9: And Enos liveth ninety years, and begetteth Cainan.
texts.gen.5.10: And Enos liveth after his begetting Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.11: And all the days of Enos are nine hundred and five years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.12: And Cainan liveth seventy years, and begetteth Mahalaleel.
texts.gen.5.13: And Cainan liveth after his begetting Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.14: And all the days of Cainan are nine hundred and ten years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.15: And Mahalaleel liveth five and sixty years, and begetteth Jared.
texts.gen.5.16: And Mahalaleel liveth after his begetting Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.17: And all the days of Mahalaleel are eight hundred and ninety and five years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.18: And Jared liveth an hundred and sixty and two years, and begetteth Enoch.
texts.gen.5.19: And Jared liveth after his begetting Enoch eight hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.20: And all the days of Jared are nine hundred and sixty and two years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.21: And Enoch liveth five and sixty years, and begetteth Methuselah.
texts.gen.5.22: And Enoch walketh habitually with God after his begetting Methuselah three hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.23: And all the days of Enoch are three hundred and sixty and five years.
texts.gen.5.24: And Enoch walketh habitually with God, and he is not, for God hath taken him.
texts.gen.5.25: And Methuselah liveth an hundred and eighty and seven years, and begetteth Lamech.
texts.gen.5.26: And Methuselah liveth after his begetting Lamech seven hundred and eighty and two years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.27: And all the days of Methuselah are nine hundred and sixty and nine years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.28: And Lamech liveth an hundred and eighty and two years, and begetteth a son,
texts.gen.5.29: and calleth his name Noah, saying, `This [one] doth comfort us concerning our work, and concerning the labour of our hands, because of the ground which Jehovah hath cursed.'
texts.gen.5.30: And Lamech liveth after his begetting Noah five hundred and ninety and five years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.5.31: And all the days of Lamech are seven hundred and seventy and seven years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.5.32: And Noah is a son of five hundred years, and Noah begetteth Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
texts.gen.6.1: And it cometh to pass that mankind have begun to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters have been born to them,
texts.gen.6.2: and sons of God see the daughters of men that they [are] fair, and they take to themselves women of all whom they have chosen.
texts.gen.6.3: And Jehovah saith, `My Spirit doth not strive in man -- to the age; in their erring they [are] flesh:' and his days have been an hundred and twenty years.
texts.gen.6.4: The fallen ones were in the earth in those days, and even afterwards when sons of God come in unto daughters of men, and they have borne to them -- they [are] the heroes, who, from of old, [are] the men of name.
texts.gen.6.5: And Jehovah seeth that abundant [is] the wickedness of man in the earth, and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart only evil all the day;
texts.gen.6.6: and Jehovah repenteth that He hath made man in the earth, and He grieveth Himself -- unto His heart.
texts.gen.6.7: And Jehovah saith, `I wipe away man whom I have prepared from off the face of the ground, from man unto beast, unto creeping thing, and unto fowl of the heavens, for I have repented that I have made them.'
texts.gen.6.8: And Noah found grace in the eyes of Jehovah.
texts.gen.6.9: These [are] births of Noah: Noah [is] a righteous man; perfect he hath been among his generations; with God hath Noah walked habitually.
texts.gen.6.10: And Noah begetteth three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
texts.gen.6.11: And the earth is corrupt before God, and the earth is filled [with] violence.
texts.gen.6.12: And God seeth the earth, and lo, it hath been corrupted, for all flesh hath corrupted its way on the earth.
texts.gen.6.13: And God said to Noah, `An end of all flesh hath come before Me, for the earth hath been full of violence from their presence; and lo, I am destroying them with the earth.
texts.gen.6.14: `Make for thyself an ark of gopher-wood; rooms dost thou make with the ark, and thou hast covered it within and without with cypress;
texts.gen.6.15: and this [is] that which thou dost with it: three hundred cubits [is] the length of the ark, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height;
texts.gen.6.16: a window dost thou make for the ark, and unto a cubit thou dost restrain it from above; and the opening of the ark thou dost put in its side, -- lower, second, and third [stories] dost thou make it.
texts.gen.6.17: `And I, lo, I am bringing in the deluge of waters on the earth to destroy all flesh, in which [is] a living spirit, from under the heavens; all that [is] in the earth doth expire.
texts.gen.6.18: `And I have established My covenant with thee, and thou hast come in unto the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy son's wives with thee;
texts.gen.6.19: and of all that liveth, of all flesh, two of every [sort] thou dost bring in unto the ark, to keep alive with thee; male and female are they.
texts.gen.6.20: Of the fowl after its kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every [sort] they come in unto thee, to keep alive.
texts.gen.6.21: `And thou, take to thyself of all food that is eaten; and thou hast gathered unto thyself, and it hath been to thee and to them for food.'
texts.gen.6.22: And Noah doth according to all that God hath commanded him; so hath he done.
texts.gen.7.1: And Jehovah saith to Noah, `Come in, thou and all thy house, unto the ark, for thee I have seen righteous before Me in this generation;
texts.gen.7.2: of all the clean beasts thou dost take to thee seven pairs, a male and its female; and of the beasts which are not clean two, a male and its female;
texts.gen.7.3: also, of fowl of the heavens seven pairs, a male and a female, to keep alive seed on the face of all the earth;
texts.gen.7.4: for after other seven days I am sending rain on the earth forty days and forty nights, and have wiped away all the substance that I have made from off the face of the ground.'
texts.gen.7.5: And Noah doth according to all that Jehovah hath commanded him:
texts.gen.7.6: and Noah [is] a son of six hundred years, and the deluge of waters hath been upon the earth.
texts.gen.7.7: And Noah goeth in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, unto the ark, from the presence of the waters of the deluge;
texts.gen.7.8: of the clean beasts and of the beasts that [are] not clean, and of the fowl, and of every thing that is creeping upon the ground,
texts.gen.7.9: two by two they have come in unto Noah, unto the ark, a male and a female, as God hath commanded Noah.
texts.gen.7.10: And it cometh to pass, after the seventh of the days, that waters of the deluge have been on the earth.
texts.gen.7.11: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, in this day have been broken up all fountains of the great deep, and the net-work of the heavens hath been opened,
texts.gen.7.12: and the shower is on the earth forty days and forty nights.
texts.gen.7.13: In this self-same day went in Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, sons of Noah, and Noah's wife and the three wives of his sons with them, unto the ark;
texts.gen.7.14: they, and every living creature after its kind, and every beast after its kind, and every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth after its kind, and every fowl after its kind, every bird -- every wing.
texts.gen.7.15: And they come in unto Noah, unto the ark, two by two of all the flesh in which [is] a living spirit;
texts.gen.7.16: and they that are coming in, male and female of all flesh, have come in as God hath commanded him, and Jehovah doth close [it] for him.
texts.gen.7.17: And the deluge is forty days on the earth, and the waters multiply, and lift up the ark, and it is raised up from off the earth;
texts.gen.7.18: and the waters are mighty, and multiply exceedingly upon the earth; and the ark goeth on the face of the waters.
texts.gen.7.19: And the waters have been very very mighty on the earth, and covered are all the high mountains which [are] under the whole heavens;
texts.gen.7.20: fifteen cubits upwards have the waters become mighty, and the mountains are covered;
texts.gen.7.21: and expire doth all flesh that is moving on the earth, among fowl, and among cattle, and among beasts, and among all the teeming things which are teeming on the earth, and all mankind;
texts.gen.7.22: all in whose nostrils [is] breath of a living spirit -- of all that [is] in the dry land -- have died.
texts.gen.7.23: And wiped away is all the substance that is on the face of the ground, from man unto beast, unto creeping thing, and unto fowl of the heavens; yea, they are wiped away from the earth, and only Noah is left, and those who [are] with him in the ark;
texts.gen.7.24: and the waters are mighty on the earth a hundred and fifty days.
texts.gen.8.1: And God remembereth Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle which [are] with him in the ark, and God causeth a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subside,
texts.gen.8.2: and closed are the fountains of the deep and the net-work of the heavens, and restrained is the shower from the heavens.
texts.gen.8.3: And turn back do the waters from off the earth, going on and returning; and the waters are lacking at the end of a hundred and fifty days.
texts.gen.8.4: And the ark resteth, in the seventh month, in the seventeenth day of the month, on mountains of Ararat;
texts.gen.8.5: and the waters have been going and becoming lacking till the tenth month; in the tenth [month], on the first of the month, appeared the heads of the mountains.
texts.gen.8.6: And it cometh to pass, at the end of forty days, that Noah openeth the window of the ark which he made,
texts.gen.8.7: and he sendeth forth the raven, and it goeth out, going out and turning back till the drying of the waters from off the earth.
texts.gen.8.8: And he sendeth forth the dove from him to see whether the waters have been lightened from off the face of the ground,
texts.gen.8.9: and the dove hath not found rest for the sole of her foot, and she turneth back unto him, unto the ark, for waters [are] on the face of all the earth, and he putteth out his hand, and taketh her, and bringeth her in unto him, unto the ark.
texts.gen.8.10: And he stayeth yet other seven days, and addeth to send forth the dove from the ark;
texts.gen.8.11: and the dove cometh in unto him at even-time, and lo, an olive leaf torn off in her mouth; and Noah knoweth that the waters have been lightened from off the earth.
texts.gen.8.12: And he stayeth yet other seven days, and sendeth forth the dove, and it added not to turn back unto him any more.
texts.gen.8.13: And it cometh to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first [month], in the first of the month, the waters have been dried from off the earth; and Noah turneth aside the covering of the ark, and looketh, and lo, the face of the ground hath been dried.
texts.gen.8.14: And in the second month, in the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth hath become dry.
texts.gen.8.15: And God speaketh unto Noah, saying, `Go out from the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons' wives with thee;
texts.gen.8.16: every living thing that [is] with thee, of all flesh, among fowl, and among cattle, and among every creeping thing which is creeping on the earth, bring out with thee;
texts.gen.8.17: and they have teemed in the earth, and been fruitful, and have multiplied on the earth.'
texts.gen.8.18: And Noah goeth out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him;
texts.gen.8.19: every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl; every creeping thing on the earth, after their families, have gone out from the ark.
texts.gen.8.20: And Noah buildeth an altar to Jehovah, and taketh of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and causeth burnt-offerings to ascend on the altar;
texts.gen.8.21: and Jehovah smelleth the sweet fragrance, and Jehovah saith unto His heart, `I continue not to disesteem any more the ground because of man, though the imagination of the heart of man [is] evil from his youth; and I continue not to smite any more all living, as I have done;
texts.gen.8.22: during all days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, do not cease.'
texts.gen.9.1: And God blesseth Noah, and his sons, and saith to them, `Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth;
texts.gen.9.2: and your fear and your dread is on every beast of the earth, and on every fowl of the heavens, on all that creepeth on the ground, and on all fishes of the sea -- into your hand they have been given.
texts.gen.9.3: Every creeping thing that is alive, to you it is for food; as the green herb I have given to you the whole;
texts.gen.9.4: only flesh in its life -- its blood -- ye do not eat.
texts.gen.9.5: `And only your blood for your lives do I require; from the hand of every living thing I require it, and from the hand of man, from the hand of every man's brother I require the life of man;
texts.gen.9.6: whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man is his blood shed: for in the image of God hath He made man.
texts.gen.9.7: And ye, be fruitful and multiply, teem in the earth, and multiply in it.'
texts.gen.9.8: And God speaketh unto Noah, and unto his sons with him, saying,
texts.gen.9.9: `And I, lo, I am establishing My covenant with you, and with your seed after you,
texts.gen.9.10: and with every living creature which [is] with you, among fowl, among cattle, and among every beast of the earth with you, from all who are going out of the ark -- to every beast of the earth.
texts.gen.9.11: And I have established My covenant with you, and all flesh is not any more cut off by waters of a deluge, and there is not any more a deluge to destroy the earth.'
texts.gen.9.12: And God saith, `This is a token of the covenant which I am giving between Me and you, and every living creature that [is] with you, to generations age-during;
texts.gen.9.13: My bow I have given in the cloud, and it hath been for a token of a covenant between Me and the earth;
texts.gen.9.14: and it hath come to pass (in My sending a cloud over the earth) that the bow hath been seen in the cloud,
texts.gen.9.15: and I have remembered My covenant which is between Me and you, and every living creature among all flesh, and the waters become no more a deluge to destroy all flesh;
texts.gen.9.16: and the bow hath been in the cloud, and I have seen it -- to remember the covenant age-during between God and every living creature among all flesh which [is] on the earth.'
texts.gen.9.17: And God saith unto Noah, `This [is] a token of the covenant which I have established between Me and all flesh that [is] upon the earth.'
texts.gen.9.18: And the sons of Noah who are going out of the ark are Shem, and Ham, and Japheth; and Ham is father of Canaan.
texts.gen.9.19: These three [are] sons of Noah, and from these hath all the earth been overspread.
texts.gen.9.20: And Noah remaineth a man of the ground, and planteth a vineyard,
texts.gen.9.21: and drinketh of the wine, and is drunken, and uncovereth himself in the midst of the tent.
texts.gen.9.22: And Ham, father of Canaan, seeth the nakedness of his father, and declareth to his two brethren without.
texts.gen.9.23: And Shem taketh -- Japheth also -- the garment, and they place on the shoulder of them both, and go backward, and cover the nakedness of their father; and their faces [are] backward, and their father's nakedness they have not seen.
texts.gen.9.24: And Noah awaketh from his wine, and knoweth that which his young son hath done to him,
texts.gen.9.25: and saith: `Cursed [is] Canaan, Servant of servants he is to his brethren.'
texts.gen.9.26: And he saith: `Blessed of Jehovah my God [is] Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.
texts.gen.9.27: God doth give beauty to Japheth, And he dwelleth in tents of Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.'
texts.gen.9.28: And Noah liveth after the deluge three hundred and fifty years;
texts.gen.9.29: and all the days of Noah are nine hundred and fifty years, and he dieth.
texts.gen.10.1: And these [are] births of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and born to them are sons after the deluge.
texts.gen.10.2: `Sons of Japheth [are] Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
texts.gen.10.3: And sons of Gomer [are] Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
texts.gen.10.4: And sons of Javan [are] Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
texts.gen.10.5: By these have the isles of the nations been parted in their lands, each by his tongue, by their families, in their nations.
texts.gen.10.6: And sons of Ham [are] Cush, and Mitzraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
texts.gen.10.7: And sons of Cush [are] Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtechah; and sons of Raamah [are] Sheba and Dedan.
texts.gen.10.9: he hath begun to be a hero in the land; he hath been a hero in hunting before Jehovah; therefore it is said, `As Nimrod the hero [in] hunting before Jehovah.'
texts.gen.10.10: And the first part of his kingdom is Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar;
texts.gen.10.11: from that land he hath gone out to Asshur, and buildeth Nineveh, even the broad places of the city, and Calah,
texts.gen.10.12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; it [is] the great city.
texts.gen.10.13: And Mitzraim hath begotten the Ludim, and the Anamim, and the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim,
texts.gen.10.14: and the Pathrusim, and the Casluhim, (whence have come out Philistim,) and the Caphtorim.
texts.gen.10.15: And Canaan hath begotten Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
texts.gen.10.16: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
texts.gen.10.17: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
texts.gen.10.18: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite; and afterwards have the families of the Canaanite been scattered.
texts.gen.10.19: And the border of the Canaanite is from Sidon, [in] thy coming towards Gerar, unto Gaza; [in] thy coming towards Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, unto Lasha.
texts.gen.10.20: These [are] sons of Ham, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
texts.gen.10.21: As to Shem, father of all sons of Eber, brother of Japheth the elder, he hath also begotten:
texts.gen.10.22: Sons of Shem [are] Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
texts.gen.10.23: And sons of Aram [are] Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
texts.gen.10.24: And Arphaxad hath begotten Salah, and Salah hath begotten Eber.
texts.gen.10.25: And to Eber have two sons been born; the name of the one [is] Peleg (for in his days hath the earth been divided,) and his brother's name [is] Joktan.
texts.gen.10.26: And Joktan hath begotten Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
texts.gen.10.27: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
texts.gen.10.28: and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
texts.gen.10.29: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab; all these [are] sons of Joktan;
texts.gen.10.30: and their dwelling is from Mesha, [in] thy coming towards Sephar, a mount of the east.
texts.gen.10.31: These [are] sons of Shem, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, by their nations.
texts.gen.10.32: These [are] families of the sons of Noah, by their births, in their nations, and by these have the nations been parted in the earth after the deluge.
texts.gen.11.1: And the whole earth is of one pronunciation, and of the same words,
texts.gen.11.2: and it cometh to pass, in their journeying from the east, that they find a valley in the land of Shinar, and dwell there;
texts.gen.11.3: and they say each one to his neighbour, `Give help, let us make bricks, and burn [them] thoroughly:' and the brick is to them for stone, and the bitumen hath been to them for mortar.
texts.gen.11.4: And they say, `Give help, let us build for ourselves a city and tower, and its head in the heavens, and make for ourselves a name, lest we be scattered over the face of all the earth.'
texts.gen.11.5: And Jehovah cometh down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men have builded;
texts.gen.11.6: and Jehovah saith, `Lo, the people [is] one, and one pronunciation [is] to them all, and this it hath dreamed of doing; and now, nothing is restrained from them of that which they have purposed to do.
texts.gen.11.7: Give help, let us go down, and mingle there their pronunciation, so that a man doth not understand the pronunciation of his companion.'
texts.gen.11.8: And Jehovah doth scatter them from thence over the face of all the earth, and they cease to build the city;
texts.gen.11.9: therefore hath [one] called its name Babel, for there hath Jehovah mingled the pronunciation of all the earth, and from thence hath Jehovah scattered them over the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.11.10: These [are] births of Shem: Shem [is] a son of an hundred years, and begetteth Arphaxad two years after the deluge.
texts.gen.11.11: And Shem liveth after his begetting Arphaxad five hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.12: And Arphaxad hath lived five and thirty years, and begetteth Salah.
texts.gen.11.13: And Arphaxad liveth after his begetting Salah four hundred and three years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.14: And Salah hath lived thirty years, and begetteth Eber.
texts.gen.11.15: And Salah liveth after his begetting Eber four hundred and three years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.16: And Eber liveth four and thirty years, and begetteth Peleg.
texts.gen.11.17: And Eber liveth after his begetting Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.18: And Peleg liveth thirty years, and begetteth Reu.
texts.gen.11.19: And Peleg liveth after his begetting Reu two hundred and nine years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.20: And Reu liveth two and thirty years, and begetteth Serug.
texts.gen.11.21: And Reu liveth after his begetting Serug two hundred and seven years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.22: And Serug liveth thirty years, and begetteth Nahor.
texts.gen.11.23: And Serug liveth after his begetting Nahor two hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.24: And Nahor liveth nine and twenty years, and begetteth Terah.
texts.gen.11.25: And Nahor liveth after his begetting Terah an hundred and nineteen years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.26: And Terah liveth seventy years, and begetteth Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
texts.gen.11.27: And these [are] births of Terah: Terah hath begotten Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran hath begotten Lot;
texts.gen.11.28: and Haran dieth in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees.
texts.gen.11.29: And Abram and Nahor take to themselves wives; the name of Abram's wife [is] Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife [is] Milcah, daughter of Haran, father of Milcah, and father of Iscah.
texts.gen.11.30: And Sarai is barren -- she hath no child.
texts.gen.11.31: And Terah taketh Abram his son, and Lot, son of Haran, his son's son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, wife of Abram his son, and they go out with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go towards the land of Canaan; and they come unto Charan, and dwell there.
texts.gen.11.32: And the days of Terah are two hundred and five years, and Terah dieth in Charan.
texts.gen.12.1: And Jehovah saith unto Abram, `Go for thyself, from thy land, and from thy kindred, and from the house of thy father, unto the land which I shew thee.
texts.gen.12.2: And I make thee become a great nation, and bless thee, and make thy name great; and be thou a blessing.
texts.gen.12.3: And I bless those blessing thee, and him who is disesteeming thee I curse, and blessed in thee have been all families of the ground.'
texts.gen.12.4: And Abram goeth on, as Jehovah hath spoken unto him, and Lot goeth with him, and Abram [is] a son of five and seventy years in his going out from Charan.
texts.gen.12.5: And Abram taketh Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they have gained, and the persons that they have obtained in Charan; and they go out to go towards the land of Canaan; and they come in to the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.12.6: And Abram passeth over into the land, unto the place Shechem, unto the oak of Moreh; and the Canaanite [is] then in the land.
texts.gen.12.7: And Jehovah appeareth unto Abram, and saith, `To thy seed I give this land;' and he buildeth there an altar to Jehovah, who hath appeared unto him.
texts.gen.12.8: And he removeth from thence towards a mountain at the east of Beth-El, and stretcheth out the tent (Beth-El at the west, and Hai at the east), and he buildeth there an altar to Jehovah, and preacheth in the name of Jehovah.
texts.gen.12.9: And Abram journeyeth, going on and journeying towards the south.
texts.gen.12.10: And there is a famine in the land, and Abram goeth down towards Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine [is] grievous in the land;
texts.gen.12.11: and it cometh to pass as he hath drawn near to enter Egypt, that he saith unto Sarai his wife, `Lo, I pray thee, I have known that thou [art] a woman of beautiful appearance;
texts.gen.12.12: and it hath come to pass that the Egyptians see thee, and they have said, `This [is] his wife,' and they have slain me, and thee they keep alive:
texts.gen.12.13: say, I pray thee, thou [art] my sister, so that it is well with me because of thee, and my soul hath lived for thy sake.'
texts.gen.12.14: And it cometh to pass, at the entering of Abram into Egypt, that the Egyptians see the woman that she [is] exceeding fair;
texts.gen.12.15: and princes of Pharaoh see her, and praise her unto Pharaoh, and the woman is taken [to] Pharaoh's house;
texts.gen.12.16: and to Abram he hath done good because of her, and he hath sheep and oxen, and he-asses, and men-servants, and handmaids, and she-asses, and camels.
texts.gen.12.17: And Jehovah plagueth Pharaoh and his house -- great plagues -- for the matter of Sarai, Abram's wife.
texts.gen.12.18: And Pharaoh calleth for Abram, and saith, `What [is] this thou hast done to me? why hast thou not declared to me that she [is] thy wife?
texts.gen.12.19: Why hast thou said, She [is] my sister, and I take her to myself for a wife? and now, lo, thy wife, take and go.'
texts.gen.12.20: And Pharaoh chargeth men concerning him, and they send him away, and his wife, an all that he hath.
texts.gen.13.1: And Abram goeth up from Egypt (he and his wife, and all that he hath, and Lot with him) towards the south;
texts.gen.13.2: and Abram [is] exceedingly wealthy in cattle, in silver, and in gold.
texts.gen.13.3: And he goeth on his journeyings from the south, even unto Bethel, unto the place where his tent had been at the commencement, between Bethel and Hai --
texts.gen.13.4: unto the place of the altar which he made there at the first, and there doth Abram preach in the name of Jehovah.
texts.gen.13.5: And also to Lot, who is going with Abram, there hath been sheep and oxen and tents;
texts.gen.13.6: and the land hath not suffered them to dwell together, for their substance hath been much, and they have not been able to dwell together;
texts.gen.13.7: and there is a strife between those feeding Abram's cattle and those feeding Lot's cattle; and the Canaanite and the Perizzite [are] then dwelling in the land.
texts.gen.13.8: And Abram saith unto Lot, `Let there not, I pray thee, be strife between me and thee, and between my shepherds and thy shepherds, for we [are] men -- brethren.
texts.gen.13.9: Is not all the land before thee? be parted, I pray thee, from me; if to the left, then I to the right; and if to the right, then I to the left.'
texts.gen.13.10: And Lot lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the whole circuit of the Jordan that it [is] all a watered country (before Jehovah's destroying Sodom and Gomorrah, as Jehovah's garden, as the land of Egypt,) in thy coming toward Zoar,
texts.gen.13.11: and Lot chooseth for himself the whole circuit of the Jordan; and Lot journeyeth from the east, and they are parted -- a man from his companion;
texts.gen.13.12: Abram hath dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot hath dwelt in the cities of the circuit, and tenteth unto Sodom;
texts.gen.13.13: and the men of Sodom [are] evil, and sinners before Jehovah exceedingly.
texts.gen.13.14: And Jehovah said unto Abram, after Lot's being parted from him, `Lift up, I pray thee, thine eyes, and look from the place where thou [art], northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward;
texts.gen.13.15: for the whole of the land which thou are seeing, to thee I give it, and to thy seed -- to the age.
texts.gen.13.16: And I have set thy seed as dust of the earth, so that, if one is able to number the dust of the earth, even thy seed is numbered;
texts.gen.13.17: rise, go up and down through the land, to its length, and to its breadth, for to thee I give it.'
texts.gen.13.18: And Abram tenteth, and cometh, and dwelleth among the oaks of Mamre, which [are] in Hebron, and buildeth there an altar to Jehovah.
texts.gen.14.1: And it cometh to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim,
texts.gen.14.2: they have made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, which [is] Zoar.
texts.gen.14.3: All these have been joined together unto the valley of Siddim, which [is] the Salt Sea;
texts.gen.14.4: twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and the thirteenth year they rebelled.
texts.gen.14.5: And in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings who [are] with him, and they smite the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
texts.gen.14.6: and the Horites in their mount Seir, unto El-Paran, which [is] by the wilderness;
texts.gen.14.7: and they turn back and come in unto En-Mishpat, which [is] Kadesh, and smite the whole field of the Amalekite, and also the Amorite who is dwelling in Hazezon-Tamar.
texts.gen.14.8: And the king of Sodom goeth out, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela, which [is] Zoar; and they set the battle in array with them in the valley of Siddim,
texts.gen.14.9: with Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings with the five.
texts.gen.14.10: And the valley of Siddim [is] full of bitumen-pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee, and fall there, and those left have fled to the mountain.
texts.gen.14.11: And they take the whole substance of Sodom and Gomorrah, and the whole of their food, and go away;
texts.gen.14.12: and they take Lot, Abram's brother's son (seeing he is dwelling in Sodom), and his substance, and go away.
texts.gen.14.13: And one who is escaping cometh and declareth to Abram the Hebrew, and he is dwelling among the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner, and they [are] Abram's allies.
texts.gen.14.14: And Abram heareth that his brother hath been taken captive, and he draweth out his trained domestics, three hundred and eighteen, and pursueth unto Dan.
texts.gen.14.15: And he divideth himself against them by night, he and his servants, and smiteth them, and pursueth them unto Hobah, which [is] at the left of Damascus;
texts.gen.14.16: and he bringeth back the whole of the substance, and also Lot his brother and his substance hath he brought back, and also the women and the people.
texts.gen.14.17: And the king of Sodom goeth out to meet him (after his turning back from the smiting of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings who [are] with him), unto the valley of Shaveh, which [is] the king's valley.
texts.gen.14.18: And Melchizedek king of Salem hath brought out bread and wine, and he [is] priest of God Most High;
texts.gen.14.19: and he blesseth him, and saith, `Blessed [is] Abram to God Most High, possessing heaven and earth;
texts.gen.14.20: and blessed [is] God Most High, who hath delivered thine adversaries into thy hand;' and he giveth to him a tenth of all.
texts.gen.14.21: And the king of Sodom saith unto Abram, `Give to me the persons, and the substance take to thyself,'
texts.gen.14.22: and Abram saith unto the king of Sodom, `I have lifted up my hand unto Jehovah, God Most High, possessing heaven and earth --
texts.gen.14.23: from a thread even unto a shoe-latchet I take not of anything which thou hast, that thou say not, I -- I have made Abram rich;
texts.gen.14.24: save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who have gone with me -- Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre -- they take their portion.'
texts.gen.15.1: After these things hath the word of Jehovah been unto Abram in a vision, saying, `Fear not, Abram, I [am] a shield to thee, thy reward [is] exceeding great.'
texts.gen.15.2: And Abram saith, `Lord Jehovah, what dost Thou give to me, and I am going childless? and an acquired son in my house is Demmesek Eliezer.'
texts.gen.15.3: And Abram saith, `Lo, to me Thou hast not given seed, and lo, a domestic doth heir me.'
texts.gen.15.4: And lo, the word of Jehovah [is] unto him, saying, `This [one] doth not heir thee; but he who cometh out from thy bowels, he doth heir thee;'
texts.gen.15.5: and He bringeth him out without, and saith, `Look attentively, I pray thee, towards the heavens, and count the stars, if thou art able to count them;' and He saith to him, `Thus is thy seed.'
texts.gen.15.6: And he hath believed in Jehovah, and He reckoneth it to him -- righteousness.
texts.gen.15.7: And He saith unto him, `I [am] Jehovah who brought thee out from Ur of the Chaldees, to give to thee this land to possess it;'
texts.gen.15.8: and he saith, `Lord Jehovah, whereby do I know that I possess it?'
texts.gen.15.9: And He saith unto him, `Take for Me a heifer of three years, and a she-goat of three years, and a ram of three years, and a turtle-dove, and a young bird;'
texts.gen.15.10: and he taketh to him all these, and separateth them in the midst, and putteth each piece over against its fellow, but the bird he hath not divided;
texts.gen.15.11: and the ravenous birds come down upon the carcases, and Abram causeth them to turn back.
texts.gen.15.12: And the sun is about to go in, and deep sleep hath fallen upon Abram, and lo, a terror of great darkness is falling upon him;
texts.gen.15.13: and He saith to Abram, `knowing -- know that thy seed is a sojourner in a land not theirs, and they have served them, and they have afflicted them four hundred years,
texts.gen.15.14: and the nation also whom they serve I judge, and after this they go out with great substance;
texts.gen.15.15: and thou -- thou comest in unto thy fathers in peace; thou art buried in a good old age;
texts.gen.15.16: and the fourth generation doth turn back hither, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet complete.'
texts.gen.15.17: And it cometh to pass -- the sun hath gone in, and thick darkness hath been -- and lo, a furnace of smoke, and a lamp of fire, which hath passed over between those pieces.
texts.gen.15.18: In that day hath Jehovah made with Abram a covenant, saying, `To thy seed I have given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Phrat,
texts.gen.15.19: with the Kenite, and the Kenizzite, and the Kadmonite,
texts.gen.15.20: and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,
texts.gen.15.21: and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.'
texts.gen.16.1: And Sarai, Abram's wife, hath not borne to him, and she hath an handmaid, an Egyptian, and her name [is] Hagar;
texts.gen.16.2: and Sarai saith unto Abram, `Lo, I pray thee, Jehovah hath restrained me from bearing, go in, I pray thee, unto my handmaid; perhaps I am built up from her;' and Abram hearkeneth to the voice of Sarai.
texts.gen.16.3: And Sarai, Abram's wife, taketh Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid, at the end of the tenth year of Abram's dwelling in the land of Canaan, and giveth her to Abram her husband, to him for a wife,
texts.gen.16.4: and he goeth in unto Hagar, and she conceiveth, and she seeth that she hath conceived, and her mistress is lightly esteemed in her eyes.
texts.gen.16.5: And Sarai saith unto Abram, `My violence [is] for thee; I -- I have given mine handmaid into thy bosom, and she seeth that she hath conceived, and I am lightly esteemed in her eyes; Jehovah doth judge between me and thee.'
texts.gen.16.6: And Abram saith unto Sarai, `Lo, thine handmaid [is] in thine hand, do to her that which is good in thine eyes;' and Sarai afflicted her, and she fleeth from her presence.
texts.gen.16.7: And a messenger of Jehovah findeth her by the fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way [to] Shur,
texts.gen.16.8: and he saith, `Hagar, Sarai's handmaid, whence hast thou come, and whither dost thou go?' and she saith, `From the presence of Sarai, my mistress, I am fleeing.'
texts.gen.16.9: And the messenger of Jehovah saith to her, `Turn back unto thy mistress, and humble thyself under her hands;'
texts.gen.16.10: and the messenger of Jehovah saith to her, `Multiplying I multiply thy seed, and it is not numbered from multitude;'
texts.gen.16.11: and the messenger of Jehovah saith to her, `Behold thou [art] conceiving, and bearing a son, and hast called his name Ishmael, for Jehovah hath hearkened unto thine affliction;
texts.gen.16.12: and he is a wild-ass man, his hand against every one, and every one's hand against him -- and before the face of all his brethren he dwelleth.'
texts.gen.16.13: And she calleth the name of Jehovah who is speaking unto her, `Thou [art], O God, my beholder;' for she said, `Even here have I looked behind my beholder?'
texts.gen.16.14: therefore hath one called the well, `The well of the Living One, my beholder;' lo, between Kadesh and Bered.
texts.gen.16.15: And Hagar beareth to Abram a son; and Abram calleth the name of his son, whom Hagar hath borne, Ishmael;
texts.gen.16.16: and Abram [is] a son of eighty and six years in Hagar's bearing Ishmael to Abram.
texts.gen.17.1: And Abram is a son of ninety and nine years, and Jehovah appeareth unto Abram, and saith unto him, `I [am] God Almighty, walk habitually before Me, and be thou perfect;
texts.gen.17.2: and I give My covenant between Me and thee, and multiply thee very exceedingly.'
texts.gen.17.3: And Abram falleth upon his face, and God speaketh with him, saying,
texts.gen.17.4: `I -- lo, My covenant [is] with thee, and thou hast become father of a multitude of nations;
