texts.gen.17.5: and thy name is no more called Abram, but thy name hath been Abraham, for father of a multitude of nations have I made thee;
texts.gen.17.6: and I have made thee exceeding fruitful, and made thee become nations, and kings go out from thee.
texts.gen.17.7: `And I have established My covenant between Me and thee, and thy seed after thee, to their generations, for a covenant age-during, to become God to thee, and to thy seed after thee;
texts.gen.17.8: and I have given to thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land of thy sojournings, the whole land of Canaan, for a possession age-during, and I have become their God.'
texts.gen.17.9: And God saith unto Abraham, `And thou dost keep My covenant, thou and thy seed after thee, to their generations;
texts.gen.17.10: this [is] My covenant which ye keep between Me and you, and thy seed after thee: Every male of you [is] to be circumcised;
texts.gen.17.11: and ye have circumcised the flesh of your foreskin, and it hath become a token of a covenant between Me and you.
texts.gen.17.12: `And a son of eight days is circumcised by you; every male to your generations, born in the house, or bought with money from any son of a stranger, who is not of thy seed;
texts.gen.17.13: he is certainly circumcised who [is] born in thine house, or bought with thy money; and My covenant hath become in your flesh a covenant age-during;
texts.gen.17.14: and an uncircumcised one, a male, the flesh of whose foreskin is not circumcised, even that person hath been cut off from his people; My covenant he hath broken.'
texts.gen.17.15: And God saith unto Abraham, `Sarai thy wife -- thou dost not call her name Sarai, for Sarah [is] her name;
texts.gen.17.16: and I have blessed her, and have also given to thee a son from her; and I have blessed her, and she hath become nations -- kings of peoples are from her.'
texts.gen.17.17: And Abraham falleth upon his face, and laugheth, and saith in his heart, `To the son of an hundred years is one born? or doth Sarah -- daughter of ninety years -- bear?'
texts.gen.17.18: And Abraham saith unto God, `O that Ishmael may live before Thee;'
texts.gen.17.19: and God saith, `Sarah thy wife is certainly bearing a son to thee, and thou hast called his name Isaac, and I have established My covenant with him, for a covenant age-during, to his seed after him.
texts.gen.17.20: As to Ishmael, I have heard thee; lo, I have blessed him, and made him fruitful, and multiplied him, very exceedingly; twelve princes doth he beget, and I have made him become a great nation;
texts.gen.17.21: and My covenant I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah doth bear to thee at this appointed time in the next year;'
texts.gen.17.22: and He finisheth speaking with him, and God goeth up from Abraham.
texts.gen.17.23: And Abraham taketh Ishmael his son, and all those born in his house, and all those bought with his money -- every male among the men of Abraham's house -- and circumciseth the flesh of their foreskin, in this self-same day, as God hath spoken with him.
texts.gen.17.24: And Abraham [is] a son of ninety and nine years in the flesh of his foreskin being circumcised;
texts.gen.17.25: and Ishmael his son [is] a son of thirteen years in the flesh of his foreskin being circumcised;
texts.gen.17.26: in this self-same day hath Abraham been circumcised, and Ishmael his son;
texts.gen.17.27: and all the men of his house -- born in the house, and bought with money from the son of a stranger -- have been circumcised with him.
texts.gen.18.1: And Jehovah appeareth unto him among the oaks of Mamre, and he is sitting at the opening of the tent, about the heat of the day;
texts.gen.18.2: and he lifteth up his eyes and looketh, and lo, three men standing by him, and he seeth, and runneth to meet them from the opening of the tent, and boweth himself towards the earth,
texts.gen.18.3: And he saith, `My Lord, if, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, do not, I pray thee, pass on from thy servant;
texts.gen.18.4: let, I pray thee, a little water be accepted, and wash your feet, and recline under the tree;
texts.gen.18.5: and I bring a piece of bread, and support ye your heart; afterwards pass on, for therefore have ye passed over unto your servant;' and they say, `So mayest thou do as thou has spoken.'
texts.gen.18.6: And Abraham hasteth towards the tent, unto Sarah, and saith, `Hasten three measures of flour-meal, knead, and make cakes;'
texts.gen.18.7: and Abraham ran unto the herd, and taketh a son of the herd, tender and good, and giveth unto the young man, and he hasteth to prepare it;
texts.gen.18.8: and he taketh butter and milk, and the son of the herd which he hath prepared, and setteth before them; and he is standing by them under the tree, and they do eat.
texts.gen.18.9: And they say unto him, `Where [is] Sarah thy wife?' and he saith, `Lo -- in the tent;'
texts.gen.18.10: and he saith, `returning I return unto thee, about the time of life, and lo, to Sarah thy wife a son.'
texts.gen.18.11: And Sarah is hearkening at the opening of the tent, which is behind him;
texts.gen.18.12: and Abraham and Sarah [are] aged, entering into days -- the way of women hath ceased to be to Sarah;
texts.gen.18.13: and Sarah laugheth in her heart, saying, `After I have waxed old I have had pleasure! -- my lord also [is] old!'
texts.gen.18.14: And Jehovah saith unto Abraham, `Why [is] this? Sarah hath laughed, saying, Is it true really -- I bear -- and I am aged? Is any thing too wonderful for Jehovah? at the appointed time I return unto thee, about the time of life, and Sarah hath a son.'
texts.gen.18.15: And Sarah denieth, saying, `I did not laugh;' for she hath been afraid; and He saith, `Nay, but thou didst laugh.'
texts.gen.18.16: And the men rise from thence, and look on the face of Sodom, and Abraham is going with them to send them away;
texts.gen.18.17: and Jehovah said, `Am I concealing from Abraham that which I am doing,
texts.gen.18.18: and Abraham certainly becometh a nation great and mighty, and blessed in him have been all nations of the earth?
texts.gen.18.19: for I have known him, that he commandeth his children, and his house after him (and they have kept the way of Jehovah), to do righteousness and judgment, that Jehovah may bring on Abraham that which He hath spoken concerning him.'
texts.gen.18.20: And Jehovah saith, `The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah -- because great; and their sin -- because exceeding grievous:
texts.gen.18.21: I go down now, and see whether according to its cry which is coming unto Me they have done completely -- and if not -- I know;'
texts.gen.18.22: and the men turn from thence, and go towards Sodom; and Abraham is yet standing before Jehovah.
texts.gen.18.23: And Abraham draweth nigh and saith, `Dost Thou also consume righteous with wicked?
texts.gen.18.24: peradventure there are fifty righteous in the midst of the city; dost Thou also consume, and not bear with the place for the sake of the fifty -- the righteous who [are] in its midst?
texts.gen.18.25: Far be it from Thee to do according to this thing, to put to death the righteous with the wicked; that it hath been -- as the righteous so the wicked -- far be it from Thee; doth the Judge of all the earth not do justice?'
texts.gen.18.26: And Jehovah saith, `If I find in Sodom fifty righteous in the midst of the city, then have I borne with all the place for their sake.'
texts.gen.18.27: And Abraham answereth and saith, `Lo, I pray thee, I have willed to speak unto the Lord, and I -- dust and ashes;
texts.gen.18.28: peradventure there are lacking five of the fifty righteous -- dost Thou destroy for five the whole of the city?' and He saith, `I destroy [it] not, if I find there forty and five.'
texts.gen.18.29: And he addeth again to speak unto Him and saith, `Peradventure there are found there forty?' and He saith, `I do [it] not, because of the forty.'
texts.gen.18.30: And he saith, `Let it not be, I Pray thee, displeasing to the Lord, and I speak: peradventure there are found there thirty?' and He saith, `I do [it] not, if I find there thirty.'
texts.gen.18.31: And he saith, `Lo, I pray thee, I have willed to speak unto the Lord: peradventure there are found there twenty?' and He saith, `I do not destroy [it], because of the twenty.'
texts.gen.18.32: And he saith, `Let it not be, I pray Thee, displeasing to the Lord, and I speak only this time: peradventure there are found there ten?' and He saith, `I do not destroy [it], because of the ten.'
texts.gen.18.33: And Jehovah goeth on, when He hath finished speaking unto Abraham, and Abraham hath turned back to his place.
texts.gen.19.1: And two of the messengers come towards Sodom at even, and Lot is sitting at the gate of Sodom, and Lot seeth, and riseth to meet them, and boweth himself -- face to the earth,
texts.gen.19.2: and he saith, `Lo, I pray you, my lords, turn aside, I pray you, unto the house of your servant, and lodge, and wash your feet -- then ye have risen early and gone on your way;' and they say, `Nay, but in the broad place we do lodge.'
texts.gen.19.3: And he presseth on them greatly, and they turn aside unto him, and come in unto his house; and he maketh for them a banquet, and hath baked unleavened things; and they do eat.
texts.gen.19.4: Before they lie down, the men of the city -- men of Sodom -- have come round about against the house, from young even unto aged, all the people from the extremity;
texts.gen.19.5: and they call unto Lot and say to him, `Where [are] the men who have come in unto thee to-night? bring them out unto us, and we know them.'
texts.gen.19.6: And Lot goeth out unto them, to the opening, and the door hath shut behind him,
texts.gen.19.7: and saith, `Do not, I pray you, my brethren, do evil;
texts.gen.19.8: lo, I pray you, I have two daughters, who have not known any one; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do to them as [is] good in your eyes; only to these men do not anything, for therefore have they come in within the shadow of my roof.'
texts.gen.19.9: And they say, `Come nigh hither;' they say also, `This one hath come in to sojourn, and he certainly judgeth! now, we do evil to thee more than [to] them;' and they press against the man, against Lot greatly, and come nigh to break the door.
texts.gen.19.10: And the men put forth their hand, and bring in Lot unto them, into the house, and have shut the door;
texts.gen.19.11: and the men who [are] at the opening of the house they have smitten with blindness, from small even unto great, and they weary themselves to find the opening.
texts.gen.19.12: And the men say unto Lot, `Whom hast thou here still? son-in-law, thy sons also, and thy daughters, and all whom thou hast in the city, bring out from this place;
texts.gen.19.13: for we are destroying this place, for their cry hath been great [before] the face of Jehovah, and Jehovah doth send us to destroy it.'
texts.gen.19.14: And Lot goeth out, and speaketh unto his sons-in-law, those taking his daughters, and saith, `Rise, go out from this place, for Jehovah is destroying the city;' and he is as [one] mocking in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
texts.gen.19.15: And when the dawn hath ascended, then the messengers press upon Lot, saying, `Rise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters who are found present, lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.'
texts.gen.19.16: And he lingereth, and the men lay hold on his hand, and on the hand of his wife, and on the hand of his two daughters, through the mercy of Jehovah unto him, and they bring him out, and cause him to rest without the city.
texts.gen.19.17: And it cometh to pass when he hath brought them out without, that he saith, `Escape for thy life; look not expectingly behind thee, nor stand thou in all the circuit; to the mountain escape, lest thou be consumed.'
texts.gen.19.18: And Lot saith unto them, `Not [so], I pray thee, my lord;
texts.gen.19.19: lo, I pray thee, thy servant hath found grace in thine eyes, and thou dost make great thy kindness which thou hast done with me by saving my life, and I am unable to escape to the mountain, lest the evil cleave [to] me, and I have died;
texts.gen.19.20: lo, I pray thee, this city [is] near to flee thither, and it [is] little; let me escape, I pray thee, thither, (is it not little?) and my soul doth live.'
texts.gen.19.21: And he saith unto him, `Lo, I have accepted thy face also for this thing, without overthrowing the city [for] which thou hast spoken;
texts.gen.19.22: haste, escape thither, for I am not able to do anything till thine entering thither;' therefore hath he calleth the name of the city Zoar.
texts.gen.19.23: The sun hath gone out on the earth, and Lot hath entered into Zoar,
texts.gen.19.24: and Jehovah hath rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Jehovah, from the heavens;
texts.gen.19.25: and He overthroweth these cities, and all the circuit, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which is shooting up from the ground.
texts.gen.19.26: And his wife looketh expectingly from behind him, and she is -- a pillar of salt!
texts.gen.19.27: And Abraham riseth early in the morning, unto the place where he hath stood [before] the face of Jehovah;
texts.gen.19.28: and he looketh on the face of Sodom and Gomorrah, and on all the face of the land of the circuit, and seeth, and lo, the smoke of the land went up as smoke of the furnace.
texts.gen.19.29: And it cometh to pass, in God's destroying the cities of the circuit, that God remembereth Abraham, and sendeth Lot out of the midst of the overthrow in the overthrowing of the cities in which Lot dwelt.
texts.gen.19.30: And Lot goeth up out of Zoar, and dwelleth in the mountain, and his two daughters with him, for he hath been afraid of dwelling in Zoar, and he dwelleth in a cave, he and his two daughters.
texts.gen.19.31: And the first-born saith unto the younger, `Our father [is] old, and a man there is not in the earth to come in unto us, as [is] the way of all the earth;
texts.gen.19.32: come, we cause our father to drink wine, and lie with him, and preserve from our father -- a seed.'
texts.gen.19.33: And they cause their father to drink wine on that night; and the first-born goeth in, and lieth with her father, and he hath not known in her lying down, or in her rising up.
texts.gen.19.34: And it cometh to pass, on the morrow, that the first-born saith unto the younger, `Lo, I have lain yesterday-night with my father: we cause him to drink wine also to-night, and go thou in, lie with him, and we preserve from our father -- a seed.'
texts.gen.19.35: And they cause their father to drink wine on that night also, and the younger riseth and lieth with him, and he hath not known in her lying down, or in her rising up.
texts.gen.19.36: And the two daughters of Lot conceive from their father,
texts.gen.19.37: and the first-born beareth a son, and calleth his name Moab; he [is] father of Moab unto this day;
texts.gen.19.38: as to the younger, she also hath born a son, and calleth his name Ben-Ammi: he [is] father of the Beni-Ammon unto this day.
texts.gen.20.1: And Abraham journeyeth from thence toward the land of the south, and dwelleth between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourneth in Gerar;
texts.gen.20.2: and Abraham saith concerning Sarah his wife, `She is my sister;' and Abimelech king of Gerar sendeth and taketh Sarah.
texts.gen.20.3: And God cometh in unto Abimelech in a dream of the night, and saith to him, `Lo, thou [art] a dead man, because of the woman whom thou hast taken -- and she married to a husband.'
texts.gen.20.4: And Abimelech hath not drawn near unto her, and he saith, `Lord, also a righteous nation dost thou slay?
texts.gen.20.5: hath not he himself said to me, She [is] my sister! and she, even she herself, said, He [is] my brother; in the integrity of my heart, and in the innocency of my hands, I have done this.'
texts.gen.20.6: And God saith unto him in the dream, `Yea, I -- I have known that in the integrity of thy heart thou hast done this, and I withhold thee, even I, from sinning against Me, therefore I have not suffered thee to come against her;
texts.gen.20.7: and now send back the man's wife, for he [is] inspired, and he doth pray for thee, and live thou; and if thou do not send back, know that dying thou dost die, thou, and all that thou hast.'
texts.gen.20.8: And Abimelech riseth early in the morning, and calleth for all his servants, and speaketh all these words in their ears; and the men fear exceedingly;
texts.gen.20.9: and Abimelech calleth for Abraham, and saith to him, `What hast thou done to us? and what have I sinned against thee, that thou hast brought upon me, and upon my kingdom, a great sin? works which are not done thou hast done with me.'
texts.gen.20.10: Abimelech also saith unto Abraham, `What hast thou seen that thou hast done this thing?'
texts.gen.20.11: And Abraham saith, `Because I said, `Surely the fear of God is not in this place, and they have slain me for the sake of my wife;
texts.gen.20.12: and also, truly she is my sister, daughter of my father, only not daughter of my mother, and she becometh my wife;
texts.gen.20.13: and it cometh to pass, when God hath caused me to wander from my father's house, that I say to her, This [is] thy kindness which thou dost with me: at every place whither we come, say of me, He [is] my brother.'
texts.gen.20.14: And Abimelech taketh sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and giveth to Abraham, and sendeth back to him Sarah his wife;
texts.gen.20.15: and Abimelech saith, `Lo, my land [is] before thee, where it is good in thine eyes, dwell;'
texts.gen.20.16: and to Sarah he hath said, `Lo, I have given a thousand silverlings to thy brother; lo, it is to thee a covering of eyes, to all who are with thee;' and by all this she is reasoned with.
texts.gen.20.17: And Abraham prayeth unto God, and God healeth Abimelech and his wife, and his handmaids, and they bear:
texts.gen.20.18: for Jehovah restraining had restrained every womb of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
texts.gen.21.1: And Jehovah hath looked after Sarah as He hath said, and Jehovah doth to Sarah as He hath spoken;
texts.gen.21.2: and Sarah conceiveth, and beareth a son to Abraham, to his old age, at the appointed time that God hath spoken of with him;
texts.gen.21.3: and Abraham calleth the name of his son who is born to him, whom Sarah hath born to him -- Isaac;
texts.gen.21.4: and Abraham circumciseth Isaac his son, [being] a son of eight days, as God hath commanded him.
texts.gen.21.5: And Abraham [is] a son of a hundred years in Isaac his son being born to him,
texts.gen.21.6: and Sarah saith, `God hath made laughter for me; every one who is hearing laugheth for me.'
texts.gen.21.7: She saith also, `Who hath said to Abraham, Sarah hath suckled sons, that I have born a son for his old age?'
texts.gen.21.8: And the lad groweth, and is weaned, and Abraham maketh a great banquet in the day of Isaac's being weaned;
texts.gen.21.9: and Sarah seeth the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she hath borne to Abraham, mocking,
texts.gen.21.10: and she saith to Abraham, `Cast out this handmaid and her son; for the son of this handmaid hath no possession with my son -- with Isaac.'
texts.gen.21.11: And the thing is very wrong in the eyes of Abraham, for his son's sake;
texts.gen.21.12: and God saith unto Abraham, `Let it not be wrong in thine eyes because of the youth, and because of thy handmaid: all that Sarah saith unto thee -- hearken to her voice, for in Isaac is a seed called to thee.
texts.gen.21.13: As to the son of the handmaid also, for a nation I set him, because he [is] thy seed.'
texts.gen.21.14: And Abraham riseth early in the morning, and taketh bread, and a bottle of water, and giveth unto Hagar (placing [it] on her shoulder), also the lad, and sendeth her out; and she goeth on, and goeth astray in the wilderness of Beer-Sheba;
texts.gen.21.15: and the water is consumed from the bottle, and she placeth the lad under one of the shrubs.
texts.gen.21.16: And she goeth and sitteth by herself over-against, afar off, about a bow-shot, for she said, `Let me not look on the death of the lad;' and she sitteth over-against, and lifteth up her voice, and weepeth.
texts.gen.21.17: And God heareth the voice of the youth; and the messenger of God calleth unto Hagar from the heavens, and saith to her, `What to thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath hearkened unto the voice of the youth where he [is];
texts.gen.21.18: rise, lift up the youth, and lay hold on him with thy hand, for for a great nation I set him.'
texts.gen.21.19: And God openeth her eyes, and she seeth a well of water, and she goeth and filleth the bottle [with] water, and causeth the youth to drink;
texts.gen.21.20: and God is with the youth, and he groweth, and dwelleth in the wilderness, and is an archer;
texts.gen.21.21: and he dwelleth in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother taketh for him a wife from the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.21.22: And it cometh to pass at that time that Abimelech speaketh -- Phichol also, head of his host -- unto Abraham, saying, `God [is] with thee in all that thou art doing;
texts.gen.21.23: and now, swear to me by God here: thou dost not lie to me, or to my continuator, or to my successor; according to the kindness which I have done with thee thou dost with me, and with the land in which thou hast sojourned.'
texts.gen.21.24: And Abraham saith, `I -- I do swear.'
texts.gen.21.25: And Abraham reasoned with Abimelech concerning the matter of a well of water which Abimelech's servants have taken violently away,
texts.gen.21.26: and Abimelech saith, `I have not known who hath done this thing, and even thou didst not declare to me, and I also, I have not heard save to-day.'
texts.gen.21.27: And Abraham taketh sheep and oxen, and giveth to Abimelech, and they make, both of them, a covenant;
texts.gen.21.28: and Abraham setteth seven Lambs of the flock by themselves.
texts.gen.21.29: And Abimelech saith unto Abraham, `What [are] they -- these seven lambs which thou hast set by themselves?'
texts.gen.21.30: And he saith, `For -- the seven lambs thou dost accept from my hand, so that it becometh a witness for me that I have digged this well;'
texts.gen.21.31: therefore hath he called that place `Beer-Sheba,' for there have both of them sworn.
texts.gen.21.32: And they make a covenant in Beer-Sheba, and Abimelech riseth -- Phichol also, head of his host -- and they turn back unto the land of the Philistines;
texts.gen.21.33: and [Abraham] planteth a tamarask in Beer-Sheba, and preacheth there in the name of Jehovah, God age-during;
texts.gen.21.34: and Abraham sojourneth in the land of the Philistines many days.
texts.gen.22.1: And it cometh to pass after these things that God hath tried Abraham, and saith unto him, `Abraham;' and he saith, `Here [am] I.'
texts.gen.22.2: And He saith, `Take, I pray thee, thy son, thine only one, whom thou hast loved, even Isaac, and go for thyself unto the land of Moriah, and cause him to ascend there for a burnt-offering on one of the mountains of which I speak unto thee.'
texts.gen.22.3: And Abraham riseth early in the morning, and saddleth his ass, and taketh two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and he cleaveth the wood of the burnt-offering, and riseth and goeth unto the place of which God hath spoken to him.
texts.gen.22.4: On the third day -- Abraham lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the place from afar;
texts.gen.22.5: and Abraham saith unto his young men, `Remain by yourselves here with the ass, and I and the youth go yonder and worship, and turn back unto you.'
texts.gen.22.6: And Abraham taketh the wood of the burnt-offering, and placeth on Isaac his son, and he taketh in his hand the fire, and the knife; and they go on both of them together.
texts.gen.22.7: And Isaac speaketh unto Abraham his father, and saith, `My father,' and he saith, `Here [am] I, my son.' And he saith, `Lo, the fire and the wood, and where the lamb for a burnt-offering?'
texts.gen.22.8: and Abraham saith, `God doth provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son;' and they go on both of them together.
texts.gen.22.9: And they come in unto the place of which God hath spoken to him, and there Abraham buildeth the altar, and arrangeth the wood, and bindeth Isaac his son, and placeth him upon the altar above the wood;
texts.gen.22.10: and Abraham putteth forth his hand, and taketh the knife -- to slaughter his son.
texts.gen.22.11: And the messenger of Jehovah calleth unto him from the heavens, and saith, `Abraham, Abraham;' and he saith, `Here [am] I;'
texts.gen.22.12: and He saith, `Put not forth thine hand unto the youth, nor do anything to him, for now I have known that thou art fearing God, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only one, from Me.'
texts.gen.22.13: And Abraham lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, a ram behind, seized in a thicket by its horns; and Abraham goeth, and taketh the ram, and causeth it to ascend for a burnt-offering instead of his son;
texts.gen.22.14: and Abraham calleth the name of that place `Jehovah-Jireh,' because it is said this day in the mount, `Jehovah doth provide.'
texts.gen.22.15: And the messenger of Jehovah calleth unto Abraham a second time from the heavens,
texts.gen.22.16: and saith, `By Myself I have sworn -- the affirmation of Jehovah -- that because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only one --
texts.gen.22.17: that blessing I bless thee, and multiplying I multiply thy seed as stars of the heavens, and as sand which [is] on the sea-shore; and thy seed doth possess the gate of his enemies;
texts.gen.22.18: and blessed themselves in thy seed have all nations of the earth, because that thou hast hearkened to My voice.'
texts.gen.22.19: And Abraham turneth back unto his young men, and they rise and go together unto Beer-Sheba; and Abraham dwelleth in Beer-Sheba.
texts.gen.22.20: And it cometh to pass after these things that it is declared to Abraham, saying, `Lo, Milcah hath borne, even she, sons to Nahor thy brother:
texts.gen.22.21: Huz his first-born, and Buz his brother; and Kemuel father of Aram,
texts.gen.22.22: and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel;
texts.gen.22.23: and Bethuel hath begotten Rebekah;' these eight hath Milcah borne to Nahor, Abraham's brother;
texts.gen.22.24: and his concubine, whose name [is] Reumah, she also hath borne Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maachah.
texts.gen.23.1: And the life of Sarah is a hundred and twenty and seven years -- years of the life of Sarah;
texts.gen.23.2: and Sarah dieth in Kirjath-Arba, which [is] Hebron, in the land of Caanan, and Abraham goeth in to mourn for Sarah, and to bewail her.
texts.gen.23.3: And Abraham riseth up from the presence of his dead, and speaketh unto the sons of Heth, saying,
texts.gen.23.4: `A sojourner and a settler I [am] with you; give to me a possession of a burying-place with you, and I bury my dead from before me.'
texts.gen.23.5: And the sons of Heth answer Abraham, saying to him,
texts.gen.23.6: `Hear us, my lord; a prince of God [art] thou in our midst; in the choice of our burying-places bury thy dead: none of us his burying-place doth withhold from thee, from burying thy dead.'
texts.gen.23.7: And Abraham riseth and boweth himself to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth,
texts.gen.23.8: and he speaketh with them, saying, `If it is your desire to bury my dead from before me, hear me, and meet for me with Ephron, son of Zoar;
texts.gen.23.9: and he giveth to me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which [is] in the extremity of his field; for full money doth he give it to me, in your midst, for a possession of a burying-place.'
texts.gen.23.10: And Ephron is sitting in the midst of the sons of Heth, and Ephron the Hittite answereth Abraham in the ears of the sons of Heth, of all those entering the gate of his city, saying,
texts.gen.23.11: `Nay, my lord, hear me: the field I have given to thee, and the cave that [is] in it, to thee I have given it; before the eyes of the sons of my people I have given it to thee -- bury thy dead.'
texts.gen.23.12: And Abraham boweth himself before the people of the land,
texts.gen.23.13: and speaketh unto Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, saying, `Only -- if thou wouldst hear me -- I have given the money of the field -- accept from me, and I bury my dead there.'
texts.gen.23.14: And Ephron answereth Abraham, saying to him,
texts.gen.23.15: `My lord, hear me: the land -- four hundred shekels of silver; between me and thee, what [is] it? -- thy dead bury.'
texts.gen.23.16: And Abraham hearkeneth unto Ephron, and Abraham weigheth to Ephron the silver which he hath spoken of in the ears of the sons of Heth, four hundred silver shekels, passing with the merchant.
texts.gen.23.17: And established are the field of Ephron, which [is] in Machpelah, which [is] before Mamre, the field and the cave which [is] in it, and all the trees which [are] in the field, which [are] in all its border round about,
texts.gen.23.18: to Abraham by purchase, before the eyes of the sons of Heth, among all entering the gate of his city.
texts.gen.23.19: And after this hath Abraham buried Sarah his wife at the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (which [is] Hebron), in the land of Canaan;
texts.gen.23.20: and established are the field, and the cave which [is] in it, to Abraham for a possession of a burying-place, from the sons of Heth.
texts.gen.24.1: And Abraham [is] old, he hath entered into days, and Jehovah hath blessed Abraham in all [things];
texts.gen.24.2: and Abraham saith unto his servant, the eldest of his house, who is ruling over all that he hath, `Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh,
texts.gen.24.3: and I cause thee to swear by Jehovah, God of the heavens, and God of the earth, that thou dost not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in the midst of whom I am dwelling;
texts.gen.24.4: but unto my land and unto my kindred dost thou go, and hast taken a wife for my son, for Isaac.'
texts.gen.24.5: And the servant saith unto him, `It may be the woman is not willing to come after me unto this land; do I at all cause thy son to turn back unto the land from whence thou camest out?'
texts.gen.24.6: And Abraham saith unto him, `Take heed to thyself, lest thou cause my son to turn back thither;
texts.gen.24.7: Jehovah, God of the heavens, who hath taken me from the house of my father, and from the land of my birth, and who hath spoken to me, and who hath sworn to me, saying, To thy seed I give this land, He doth send His messenger before thee, and thou hast taken a wife for my son from thence;
texts.gen.24.8: and if the woman be not willing to come after thee, then thou hast been acquitted from this mine oath: only my son thou dost not cause to turn back thither.'
texts.gen.24.9: And the servant putteth his hand under the thigh of Abraham his lord, and sweareth to him concerning this matter.
texts.gen.24.10: And the servant taketh ten camels of the camels of his lord and goeth, also of all the goods of his lord in his hand, and he riseth, and goeth unto Aram-Naharaim, unto the city of Nahor;
texts.gen.24.11: and he causeth the camels to kneel at the outside of the city, at the well of water, at even-time, at the time of the coming out of the women who draw water.
texts.gen.24.12: And he saith, `Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, cause to meet, I pray Thee, before me this day -- (and do kindness with my lord Abraham;
texts.gen.24.13: lo, I am standing by the fountain of water, and daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water;
texts.gen.24.14: and it hath been, the young person unto whom I say, Incline, I pray thee, thy pitcher, and I drink, and she hath said, Drink, and I water also thy camels) -- her Thou hast decided for Thy servant, for Isaac; and by it I know that Thou hast done kindness with my lord.'
texts.gen.24.15: And it cometh to pass, before he hath finished speaking, that lo, Rebekah (who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, brother of Abraham) is coming out, and her pitcher on her shoulder,
texts.gen.24.16: and the young person [is] of very good appearance, a virgin, and a man hath not known her; and she goeth down to the fountain, and filleth her pitcher, and cometh up.
texts.gen.24.17: And the servant runneth to meet her, and saith, `Let me swallow, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher;'
texts.gen.24.18: and she saith, `Drink, my lord;' and she hasteth, and letteth down her pitcher upon her hand, and giveth him drink.
texts.gen.24.19: And she finisheth giving him drink, and saith, `Also for thy camels I draw till they have finished drinking;'
texts.gen.24.20: and she hasteth, and emptieth her pitcher into the drinking-trough, and runneth again unto the well to draw, and draweth for all his camels.
texts.gen.24.21: And the man, wondering at her, remaineth silent, to know whether Jehovah hath made his way prosperous or not.
texts.gen.24.22: And it cometh to pass when the camels have finished drinking, that the man taketh a golden ring (whose weight [is] a bekah), and two bracelets for her hands (whose weight [is] ten [bekahs] of gold),
texts.gen.24.23: and saith, `Whose daughter [art] thou? declare to me, I pray thee, is the house of thy father a place for us to lodge in?'
texts.gen.24.24: And she saith unto him, `I [am] daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she hath borne to Nahor.'
texts.gen.24.25: She saith also unto him, `Both straw and provender [are] abundant with us, also a place to lodge in.'
texts.gen.24.26: And the man boweth, and doth obeisance to Jehovah,
texts.gen.24.27: and saith, `Blessed [is] Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, who hath not left off His kindness and His truth with my lord; -- I [being] in the way, Jehovah hath led me to the house of my lord's brethren.'
texts.gen.24.28: And the young person runneth, and declareth to the house of her mother according to these words.
texts.gen.24.29: And Rebekah hath a brother, and his name [is] Laban, and Laban runneth unto the man who [is] without, unto the fountain;
texts.gen.24.30: yea, it cometh to pass, when he seeth the ring, and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and when he heareth the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, `Thus hath the man spoken unto me,' that he cometh in unto the man, and lo, he is standing by the camels by the fountain.
texts.gen.24.31: And he saith, `Come in, O blessed one of Jehovah, why standest thou without, and I -- I have prepared the house and place for the camels!'
texts.gen.24.32: And he bringeth in the man into the house, and looseth the camels, and giveth straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who [are] with him:
texts.gen.24.33: and setteth before him to eat; but he saith, `I do not eat till I have spoken my word;' and he saith, `Speak.'
texts.gen.24.35: and Jehovah hath blessed my lord exceedingly, and he is great; and He giveth to him flock, and herd, and silver, and gold, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and camels, and asses;
texts.gen.24.36: and Sarah, my lord's wife, beareth a son to my lord, after she hath been aged, and he giveth to him all that he hath.
texts.gen.24.37: `And my lord causeth me to swear, saying, Thou dost not take a wife to my son from the daughters of the Canaanite, in whose land I am dwelling.
texts.gen.24.38: If not -- unto the house of my father thou dost go, and unto my family, and thou hast taken a wife for my son.
texts.gen.24.39: `And I say unto my lord, It may be the woman doth not come after me;
texts.gen.24.40: and he saith unto me, Jehovah, before whom I have walked habitually, doth send His messenger with thee, and hath prospered thy way, and thou hast taken a wife for my son from my family, and from the house of my father;
texts.gen.24.41: then art thou acquitted from my oath, when thou comest unto my family, and if they give not [one] to thee; then thou hast been acquitted from my oath.
texts.gen.24.42: `And I come to-day unto the fountain, and I say, Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, if Thou art, I pray Thee, making prosperous my way in which I am going --
texts.gen.24.43: (lo, I am standing by the fountain of water), then the virgin who is coming out to draw, and I have said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher,
texts.gen.24.44: and she hath said unto me, Both drink thou, and also for thy camels I draw -- she is the woman whom Jehovah hath decided for my lord's son.
texts.gen.24.45: `Before I finish speaking unto my heart, then lo, Rebekah is coming out, and her pitcher on her shoulder, and she goeth down to the fountain, and draweth; and I say unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee,
texts.gen.24.46: and she hasteth and letteth down her pitcher from off her and saith, Drink, and thy camels also I water; and I drink, and the camels also she hath watered.
texts.gen.24.47: `And I ask her, and say, Whose daughter [art] thou? and she saith, Daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom Milcah hath borne to him, and I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands,
texts.gen.24.48: and I bow, and do obeisance before Jehovah, and I bless Jehovah, God of my lord Abraham, who hath led me in the true way to receive the daughter of my lord's brother for his son.
texts.gen.24.49: `And now, if ye are dealing kindly and truly with my lord, declare to me; and if not, declare to me; and I turn unto the right or unto the left.'
texts.gen.24.50: And Laban answereth -- Bethuel also -- and they say, `The thing hath gone out from Jehovah; we are not able to speak unto thee bad or good;
texts.gen.24.51: lo, Rebekah [is] before thee, take and go, and she is a wife to thy lord's son, as Jehovah hath spoken.'
texts.gen.24.52: And it cometh to pass, when the servant of Abraham hath heard their words, that he boweth himself towards the earth before Jehovah;
texts.gen.24.53: and the servant taketh out vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and giveth to Rebekah; precious things also he hath given to her brother and to her mother.
texts.gen.24.54: And they eat and drink, he and the men who [are] with him, and lodge all night; and they rise in the morning, and he saith, `Send me to my lord;'
texts.gen.24.55: and her brother saith -- her mother also -- `Let the young person abide with us a week or ten days, afterwards doth she go.'
texts.gen.24.56: And he saith unto them, `Do not delay me, seeing Jehovah hath prospered my way; send me away, and I go to my lord;'
texts.gen.24.57: and they say, `Let us call for the young person, and ask at her mouth;'
texts.gen.24.58: and they call for Rebekah, and say unto her, `Dost thou go with this man?' and she saith, `I go.'
texts.gen.24.59: And they send away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men;
texts.gen.24.60: and they bless Rebekah, and say to her, `Thou [art] our sister; become thou thousands of myriads, and thy seed doth possess the gate of those hating it.'
texts.gen.24.61: And Rebekah and her young women arise, and ride on the camels, and go after the man; and the servant taketh Rebekah and goeth.
texts.gen.24.62: And Isaac hath come in from the entrance of the Well of the Living One, my Beholder; and he is dwelling in the land of the south,
texts.gen.24.63: and Isaac goeth out to meditate in the field, at the turning of the evening, and he lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, camels are coming.
texts.gen.24.64: And Rebekah lifteth up her eyes, and seeth Isaac, and alighteth from off the camel;
texts.gen.24.65: and she saith unto the servant, `Who [is] this man who is walking in the field to meet us?' and the servant saith, `It [is] my lord;' and she taketh the veil, and covereth herself.
texts.gen.24.66: And the servant recounteth to Isaac all the things that he hath done,
texts.gen.24.67: and Isaac bringeth her in unto the tent of Sarah his mother, and he taketh Rebekah, and she becometh his wife, and he loveth her, and Isaac is comforted after [the death of] his mother.
texts.gen.25.1: And Abraham addeth and taketh a wife, and her name [is] Keturah;
texts.gen.25.2: and she beareth to him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
texts.gen.25.3: And Jokshan hath begotten Sheba and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim;
texts.gen.25.4: and the sons of Midian [are] Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah: all these [are] sons of Keturah.
texts.gen.25.5: And Abraham giveth all that he hath to Isaac;
texts.gen.25.6: and to the sons of the concubines whom Abraham hath, Abraham hath given gifts, and sendeth them away from Isaac his son (in his being yet alive) eastward, unto the east country.
texts.gen.25.7: And these [are] the days of the years of the life of Abraham, which he lived, a hundred and seventy and five years;
texts.gen.25.8: and Abraham expireth, and dieth in a good old age, aged and satisfied, and is gathered unto his people.
texts.gen.25.9: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons bury him at the cave of Machpelah, at the field of Ephron, son of Zoar the Hittite, which [is] before Mamre --
texts.gen.25.10: the field which Abraham bought from the sons of Heth -- there hath Abraham been buried, and Sarah his wife.
texts.gen.25.11: And it cometh to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blesseth Isaac his son; and Isaac dwelleth by the Well of the Living One, my Beholder.
texts.gen.25.12: And these [are] births of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, hath borne to Abraham;
texts.gen.25.13: and these [are] the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their births: first-born of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
texts.gen.25.14: and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
texts.gen.25.15: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
texts.gen.25.16: these are sons of Ishmael, and these their names, by their villages, and by their towers; twelve princes according to their peoples.
texts.gen.25.17: And these [are] the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty and seven years; and he expireth, and dieth, and is gathered unto his people;
texts.gen.25.18: and they tabernacle from Havilah unto Shur, which [is] before Egypt, in [thy] going towards Asshur; in the presence of all his brethren hath he fallen.
texts.gen.25.19: And these [are] births of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham hath begotten Isaac;
texts.gen.25.20: and Isaac is a son of forty years in his taking Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramaean, from Padan-Aram, sister of Laban the Aramaean, to him for a wife.
texts.gen.25.21: And Isaac maketh entreaty to Jehovah before his wife, for she [is] barren: and Jehovah is entreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceiveth,
texts.gen.25.22: and the children struggle together within her, and she saith, `If [it is] right -- why [am] I thus?' and she goeth to seek Jehovah.
texts.gen.25.23: And Jehovah saith to her, `Two nations [are] in thy womb, and two peoples from thy bowels are parted; and the [one] people than the [other] people is stronger; and the elder doth serve the younger.'
texts.gen.25.24: And her days to bear are fulfilled, and lo, twins [are] in her womb;
texts.gen.25.25: and the first cometh out all red as a hairy robe, and they call his name Esau;
texts.gen.25.26: and afterwards hath his brother come out, and his hand is taking hold on Esau's heel, and one calleth his name Jacob; and Isaac [is] a son of sixty years in her bearing them.
texts.gen.25.27: And the youths grew, and Esau is a man acquainted [with] hunting, a man of the field; and Jacob [is] a plain man, inhabiting tents;
texts.gen.25.28: and Isaac loveth Esau, for [his] hunting [is] in his mouth; and Rebekah is loving Jacob.
texts.gen.25.29: And Jacob boileth pottage, and Esau cometh in from the field, and he [is] weary;
texts.gen.25.30: and Esau saith unto Jacob, `Let me eat, I pray thee, some of this red red thing, for I [am] weary;' therefore hath [one] called his name Edom [Red];
texts.gen.25.31: and Jacob saith, `Sell to-day thy birthright to me.'
texts.gen.25.32: And Esau saith, `Lo, I am going to die, and what is this to me -- birthright?'
texts.gen.25.33: and Jacob saith, `Swear to me to-day:' and he sweareth to him, and selleth his birthright to Jacob;
texts.gen.25.34: and Jacob hath given to Esau bread and pottage of lentiles, and he eateth, and drinketh, and riseth, and goeth; and Esau despiseth the birthright.
texts.gen.26.1: And there is a famine in the land, besides the first famine which was in the days of Abraham, and Isaac goeth unto Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
texts.gen.26.2: And Jehovah appeareth unto him, and saith, `Go not down towards Egypt, tabernacle in the land concerning which I speak unto thee,
texts.gen.26.3: sojourn in this land, and I am with thee, and bless thee, for to thee and to thy seed I give all these lands, and I have established the oath which I have sworn to Abraham thy father;
texts.gen.26.4: and I have multiplied thy seed as stars of the heavens, and I have given to thy seed all these lands; and blessed themselves in thy seed have all nations of the earth;
texts.gen.26.5: because that Abraham hath hearkened to My voice, and keepeth My charge, My commands, My statutes, and My laws.'
texts.gen.26.7: and men of the place ask him of his wife, and he saith, `She [is] my sister:' for he hath been afraid to say, `My wife -- lest the men of the place kill me for Rebekah, for she [is] of good appearance.'
texts.gen.26.8: And it cometh to pass, when the days have been prolonged to him there, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looketh through the window, and seeth, and lo, Isaac is playing with Rebekah his wife.
texts.gen.26.9: And Abimelech calleth for Isaac, and saith, `Lo, she [is] surely thy wife; and how hast thou said, She [is] my sister?' and Isaac saith unto him, `Because I said, Lest I die for her.'
texts.gen.26.10: And Abimelech saith, `What [is] this thou hast done to us? as a little thing one of the people had lain with thy wife, and thou hadst brought upon us guilt;'
texts.gen.26.11: and Abimelech commandeth all the people, saying, `He who cometh against this man or against his wife, dying doth die.'
texts.gen.26.12: And Isaac soweth in that land, and findeth in that year a hundredfold, and Jehovah blesseth him;
texts.gen.26.13: and the man is great, and goeth on, going on and becoming great, till that he hath been very great,
texts.gen.26.14: and he hath possession of a flock, and possession of a herd, and an abundant service; and the Philistines envy him,
texts.gen.26.15: and all the wells which his father's servants digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines have stopped them, and fill them with dust.
texts.gen.26.16: And Abimelech saith unto Isaac, `Go from us; for thou hast become much mightier than we;'
texts.gen.26.17: and Isaac goeth from thence, and encampeth in the valley of Gerar, and dwelleth there;
texts.gen.26.18: and Isaac turneth back, and diggeth the wells of water which they digged in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines do stop after the death of Abraham, and he calleth to them names according to the names which his father called them.
texts.gen.26.19: And Isaac's servants dig in the valley, and find there a well of living water,
texts.gen.26.20: and shepherds of Gerar strive with shepherds of Isaac, saying, `The water [is] ours;' and he calleth the name of the well `Strife,' because they have striven habitually with him;
texts.gen.26.21: and they dig another well, and they strive also for it, and he calleth its name `Hatred.'
texts.gen.26.22: And he removeth from thence, and diggeth another well, and they have not striven for it, and he calleth its name Enlargements, and saith, `For -- now hath Jehovah given enlargement to us, and we have been fruitful in the land.'
texts.gen.26.23: And he goeth up from thence [to] Beer-Sheba,
texts.gen.26.24: and Jehovah appeareth unto him during that night, and saith, `I [am] the God of Abraham thy father, fear not, for I [am] with thee, and have blessed thee, and have multiplied thy seed, because of Abraham My servant;'
texts.gen.26.25: and he buildeth there an altar, and preacheth in the name of Jehovah, and stretcheth out there his tent, and there Isaac's servants dig a well.
texts.gen.26.26: And Abimelech hath gone unto him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phichol head of his host;
texts.gen.26.27: and Isaac saith unto them, `Wherefore have ye come unto me, and ye have hated me, and ye send me away from you?'
texts.gen.26.28: And they say, `We have certainly seen that Jehovah hath been with thee, and we say, `Let there be, we pray thee, an oath between us, between us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;
texts.gen.26.29: do not evil with us, as we have not touched thee, and as we have only done good with thee, and send thee away in peace; thou [art] now blessed of Jehovah.'
texts.gen.26.30: And he maketh for them a banquet, and they eat and drink,
texts.gen.26.31: and rise early in the morning, and swear one to another, and Isaac sendeth them away, and they go from him in peace.
texts.gen.26.32: And it cometh to pass during that day that Isaac's servants come and declare to him concerning the circumstances of the well which they have digged, and say to him, `We have found water;'
texts.gen.26.33: and he calleth it Shebah, [oath,] therefore the name of the city [is] Beer-Sheba, [well of the oath,] unto this day.
texts.gen.26.34: And Esau is a son of forty years, and he taketh a wife, Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite,
texts.gen.26.35: and they are a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.
texts.gen.27.1: And it cometh to pass that Isaac [is] aged, and his eyes are too dim for seeing, and he calleth Esau his elder son, and saith unto him, `My son;' and he saith unto him, `Here [am] I.'
texts.gen.27.2: And he saith, `Lo, I pray thee, I have become aged, I have not known the day of my death;
texts.gen.27.3: and now, take up, I pray thee, thy instruments, thy quiver, and thy bow, and go out to the field, and hunt for me provision,
texts.gen.27.4: and make for me tasteful things, [such] as I have loved, and bring in to me, and I do eat, so that my soul doth bless thee before I die.'
texts.gen.27.5: And Rebekah is hearkening while Isaac is speaking unto Esau his son; and Esau goeth to the field to hunt provision -- to bring in;
texts.gen.27.6: and Rebekah hath spoken unto Jacob her son, saying, `Lo, I have heard thy father speaking unto Esau thy brother, saying,
texts.gen.27.7: Bring for me provision, and make for me tasteful things, and I do eat, and bless thee before Jehovah before my death.
texts.gen.27.8: `And now, my son, hearken to my voice, to that which I am commanding thee:
texts.gen.27.9: Go, I pray thee, unto the flock, and take for me from thence two good kids of the goats, and I make them tasteful things for thy father, [such] as he hath loved;
texts.gen.27.10: and thou hast taken in to thy father, and he hath eaten, so that his soul doth bless thee before his death.
texts.gen.27.11: And Jacob saith unto Rebekah his mother, `Lo, Esau my brother [is] a hairy man, and I a smooth man,
texts.gen.27.12: it may be my father doth feel me, and I have been in his eyes as a deceiver, and have brought upon me disesteem, and not a blessing;'
texts.gen.27.13: and his mother saith to him, `On me thy disesteem, my son; only hearken to my voice, and go, take for me.'
texts.gen.27.14: And he goeth, and taketh, and bringeth to his mother, and his mother maketh tasteful things, [such] as his father hath loved;
texts.gen.27.15: and Rebekah taketh the desirable garments of Esau her elder son, which [are] with her in the house, and doth put on Jacob her younger son;
texts.gen.27.16: and the skins of the kids of the goats she hath put on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck,
texts.gen.27.17: and she giveth the tasteful things, and the bread which she hath made, into the hand of Jacob her son.
texts.gen.27.18: And he cometh in unto his father, and saith, `My father;' and he saith, `Here [am] I; who [art] thou, my son?'
texts.gen.27.19: And Jacob saith unto his father, `I [am] Esau thy first-born; I have done as thou hast spoken unto me; rise, I pray thee, sit, and eat of my provision, so that thy soul doth bless me.'
texts.gen.27.20: And Isaac saith unto his son, `What [is] this thou hast hasted to find, my son?' and he saith, `That which Jehovah thy God hath caused to come before me.'
texts.gen.27.21: And Isaac saith unto Jacob, `Come nigh, I pray thee, and I feel thee, my son, whether thou [art] he, my son Esau, or not.'
texts.gen.27.22: And Jacob cometh nigh unto Isaac his father, and he feeleth him, and saith, `The voice [is] the voice of Jacob, and the hands hands of Esau.'
texts.gen.27.23: And he hath not discerned him, for his hands have been hairy, as the hands of Esau his brother, and he blesseth him,
texts.gen.27.24: and saith, `Thou art he -- my son Esau?' and he saith, `I [am].'
texts.gen.27.25: And he saith, `Bring nigh to me, and I do eat of my son's provision, so that my soul doth bless thee;' and he bringeth nigh to him, and he eateth; and he bringeth to him wine, and he drinketh.
texts.gen.27.26: And Isaac his father saith to him, `Come nigh, I pray thee, and kiss me, my son;'
texts.gen.27.27: and he cometh nigh, and kisseth him, and he smelleth the fragrance of his garments, and blesseth him, and saith, `See, the fragrance of my son [is] as the fragrance of a field which Jehovah hath blessed;
texts.gen.27.28: and God doth give to thee of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of corn and wine;
texts.gen.27.29: peoples serve thee, and nations bow themselves to thee, be thou mighty over thy brethren, and the sons of thy mother bow themselves to thee; those who curse thee [are] cursed, and those who bless thee [are] blessed.'
texts.gen.27.30: And it cometh to pass, as Isaac hath finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob is only just going out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother hath come in from his hunting;
texts.gen.27.31: and he also maketh tasteful things, and bringeth to his father, and saith to his father, `Let my father arise, and eat of his son's provision, so that thy soul doth bless me.'
texts.gen.27.32: And Isaac his father saith to him, `Who [art] thou?' and he saith, `I [am] thy son, thy first-born, Esau;'
texts.gen.27.33: and Isaac trembleth a very great trembling, and saith, `Who, now, [is] he who hath provided provision, and bringeth in to me, and I eat of all before thou comest in, and I bless him? -- yea, blessed is he.'
texts.gen.27.34: When Esau heareth the words of his father, then he crieth a very great and bitter cry, and saith to his father, `Bless me, me also, O my father;'
texts.gen.27.35: and he saith, `Thy brother hath come with subtilty, and taketh thy blessing.'
texts.gen.27.36: And he saith, `Is it because [one] called his name Jacob that he doth take me by the heel these two times? my birthright he hath taken; and lo, now, he hath taken my blessing;' he saith also, `Hast thou not kept back a blessing for me?'
texts.gen.27.37: And Isaac answereth and saith to Esau, `Lo, a mighty one have I set him over thee, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants, and [with] corn and wine have I sustained him; and for thee now, what shall I do, my son?'
texts.gen.27.38: And Esau saith unto his father, `One blessing hast thou my father? bless me, me also, O my father;' and Esau lifteth up his voice, and weepeth.
texts.gen.27.39: And Isaac his father answereth and saith unto him, `Lo, of the fatness of the earth is thy dwelling, and of the dew of the heavens from above;
texts.gen.27.40: and by thy sword dost thou live, and thy brother dost thou serve; and it hath come to pass when thou rulest, that thou hast broken his yoke from off thy neck.'
texts.gen.27.41: And Esau hateth Jacob, because of the blessing with which his father blessed him, and Esau saith in his heart, `The days of mourning [for] my father draw near, and I slay Jacob my brother.'
texts.gen.27.42: And the words of Esau her elder son are declared to Rebekah, and she sendeth and calleth for Jacob her younger son, and saith unto him, `Lo, Esau thy brother is comforting himself in regard to thee -- to slay thee;
texts.gen.27.43: and now, my son, hearken to my voice, and rise, flee for thyself unto Laban my brother, to Haran,
texts.gen.27.44: and thou hast dwelt with him some days, till thy brother's fury turn back,
texts.gen.27.45: till thy brother's anger turn back from thee, and he hath forgotten that which thou hast done to him, and I have sent and taken thee from thence; why am I bereaved even of you both the same day?'
texts.gen.27.46: And Rebekah saith unto Isaac, `I have been disgusted with my life because of the presence of the daughters of Heth; if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, like these -- from the daughters of the land -- why do I live?'
texts.gen.28.1: And Isaac calleth unto Jacob, and blesseth him, and commandeth him, and saith to him, `Thou dost not take a wife of the daughters of Caanan;
texts.gen.28.2: rise, go to Padan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel, thy mother's father, and take for thyself from thence a wife, of the daughters of Laban, thy mother's brother;
texts.gen.28.3: and God Almighty doth bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and thou hast become an assembly of peoples;
texts.gen.28.4: and He doth give to thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee and to thy seed with thee, to cause thee to possess the land of thy sojournings, which God gave to Abraham.'
texts.gen.28.5: And Isaac sendeth away Jacob, and he goeth to Padan-Aram, unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramaean, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.
texts.gen.28.6: And Esau seeth that Isaac hath blessed Jacob, and hath sent him to Padan-Aram to take to himself from thence a wife -- in his blessing him that he layeth a charge upon him, saying, Thou dost not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan --
texts.gen.28.7: that Jacob hearkeneth unto his father and unto his mother, and goeth to Padan-Aram --
texts.gen.28.8: and Esau seeth that the daughters of Canaan are evil in the eyes of Isaac his father,
texts.gen.28.9: and Esau goeth unto Ishmael, and taketh Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, sister of Nebajoth, unto his wives, to himself, for a wife.
texts.gen.28.10: And Jacob goeth out from Beer-Sheba, and goeth toward Haran,
texts.gen.28.11: and he toucheth at a [certain] place, and lodgeth there, for the sun hath gone in, and he taketh of the stones of the place, and maketh [them] his pillows, and lieth down in that place.
texts.gen.28.12: And he dreameth, and lo, a ladder set up on the earth, and its head is touching the heavens; and lo, messengers of God are going up and coming down by it;
texts.gen.28.13: and lo, Jehovah is standing upon it, and He saith, `I [am] Jehovah, God of Abraham thy father, and God of Isaac; the land on which thou art lying, to thee I give it, and to thy seed;
texts.gen.28.14: and thy seed hath been as the dust of the land, and thou hast broken forth westward, and eastward, and northward, and southward, and all families of the ground have been blessed in thee and in thy seed.
texts.gen.28.15: `And lo, I [am] with thee, and have kept thee whithersoever thou goest, and have caused thee to turn back unto this ground; for I leave thee not till that I have surely done that which I have spoken to thee.'
texts.gen.28.16: And Jacob awaketh out of his sleep, and saith, `Surely Jehovah is in this place, and I knew not;'
texts.gen.28.17: and he feareth, and saith, `How fearful [is] this place; this is nothing but a house of God, and this a gate of the heavens.'
texts.gen.28.18: And Jacob riseth early in the morning, and taketh the stone which he hath made his pillows, and maketh it a standing pillar, and poureth oil upon its top,
texts.gen.28.19: and he calleth the name of that place Bethel, [house of God,] and yet, Luz [is] the name of the city at the first.
texts.gen.28.20: And Jacob voweth a vow, saying, `Seeing God is with me, and hath kept me in this way which I am going, and hath given to me bread to eat, and a garment to put on --
texts.gen.28.21: when I have turned back in peace unto the house of my father, and Jehovah hath become my God,
texts.gen.28.22: then this stone which I have made a standing pillar is a house of God, and all that Thou dost give to me -- tithing I tithe to Thee.'
texts.gen.29.1: And Jacob lifteth up his feet, and goeth towards the land of the sons of the east;
texts.gen.29.2: and he looketh, and lo, a well in the field, and lo, there three droves of a flock crouching by it, for from that well they water the droves, and the great stone [is] on the mouth of the well.
texts.gen.29.3: (When thither have all the droves been gathered, and they have rolled the stone from off the mouth of the well, and have watered the flock, then they have turned back the stone on the mouth of the well to its place.)
texts.gen.29.4: And Jacob saith to them, `My brethren, from whence [are] ye?' and they say, `We [are] from Haran.'
texts.gen.29.5: And he saith to them, `Have ye known Laban, son of Nahor?' and they say, `We have known.'
texts.gen.29.6: And he saith to them, `Hath he peace?' and they say, `Peace; and lo, Rachel his daughter is coming with the flock.'
texts.gen.29.7: And he saith, `Lo, the day [is] still great, [it is] not time for the cattle to be gathered; water ye the flock, and go, delight yourselves.'
texts.gen.29.8: And they say, `We are not able, till that all the droves be gathered together, and they have rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well, and we have watered the flock.'
texts.gen.29.9: He is yet speaking with them, and Rachel hath come with the flock which her father hath, for she [is] shepherdess;
texts.gen.29.10: and it cometh to pass when Jacob hath seen Rachel, daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the flock of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob cometh nigh and rolleth the stone from off the mouth of the well, and watereth the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
texts.gen.29.11: And Jacob kisseth Rachel, and lifteth up his voice, and weepeth,
texts.gen.29.12: and Jacob declareth to Rachel that he [is] her father's brother, and that he [is] Rebekah's son, and she runneth and declareth to her father.
texts.gen.29.13: And it cometh to pass, when Laban heareth the report of Jacob his sister's son, that he runneth to meet him, and embraceth him, and kisseth him, and bringeth him in unto his house; and he recounteth to Laban all these things,
texts.gen.29.14: and Laban saith to him, `Only my bone and my flesh [art] thou;' and he dwelleth with him a month of days.
texts.gen.29.15: And Laban saith to Jacob, `Is it because thou [art] my brother that thou hast served me for nought? declare to me what [is] thy hire.'
texts.gen.29.16: And Laban hath two daughters, the name of the elder [is] Leah, and the name of the younger Rachel,
texts.gen.29.17: and the eyes of Leah [are] tender, and Rachel hath been fair of form and fair of appearance.
texts.gen.29.18: And Jacob loveth Rachel, and saith, `I serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter:'
texts.gen.29.19: and Laban saith, `It is better for me to give her to thee than to give her to another man; dwell with me;'
texts.gen.29.20: and Jacob serveth for Rachel seven years; and they are in his eyes as some days, because of his loving her.
texts.gen.29.21: And Jacob saith unto Laban, `Give up my wife, for my days have been fulfilled, and I go in unto her;'
texts.gen.29.22: and Laban gathereth all the men of the place, and maketh a banquet.
texts.gen.29.23: And it cometh to pass in the evening, that he taketh Leah, his daughter, and bringeth her in unto him, and he goeth in unto her;
texts.gen.29.24: and Laban giveth to her Zilpah, his maid-servant, to Leah his daughter, a maid-servant.
texts.gen.29.25: And it cometh to pass in the morning, that lo, it [is] Leah; and he saith unto Laban, `What [is] this thou hast done to me? for Rachel have I not served with thee? and why hast thou deceived me?'
texts.gen.29.26: And Laban saith, `It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the first-born;
texts.gen.29.27: fulfil the week of this one, and we give to thee also this one, for the service which thou dost serve with me yet seven other years.'
texts.gen.29.28: And Jacob doth so, and fulfilleth the week of this one, and he giveth to him Rachel his daughter, to him for a wife;
texts.gen.29.29: and Laban giveth to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his maid-servant, for a maid-servant to her.
texts.gen.29.30: And he goeth in also unto Rachel, and he also loveth Rachel more than Leah; and he serveth with him yet seven other years.
texts.gen.29.31: And Jehovah seeth that Leah [is] the hated one, and He openeth her womb, and Rachel [is] barren;
texts.gen.29.32: and Leah conceiveth, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Reuben, for she said, `Because Jehovah hath looked on mine affliction; because now doth my husband love me.'
texts.gen.29.33: And she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and saith, `Because Jehovah hath heard that I [am] the hated one, He also giveth to me even this [one];' and she calleth his name Simeon.
texts.gen.29.34: And she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and saith, `Now [is] the time, my husband is joined unto me, because I have born to him three sons,' therefore hath [one] called his name Levi.
texts.gen.29.35: And she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and saith this time, `I praise Jehovah;' therefore hath she called his name Judah; and she ceaseth from bearing.
texts.gen.30.1: And Rachel seeth that she hath not borne to Jacob, and Rachel is envious of her sister, and saith unto Jacob, `Give me sons, and if there is none -- I die.'
texts.gen.30.2: And Jacob's anger burneth against Rachel, and he saith, `Am I in stead of God who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?'
texts.gen.30.3: And she saith, `Lo, my handmaid Bilhah, go in unto her, and she doth bear on my knees, and I am built up, even I, from her;'
texts.gen.30.4: and she giveth to him Bilhah her maid-servant for a wife, and Jacob goeth in unto her;
texts.gen.30.5: and Bilhah conceiveth, and beareth to Jacob a son,
texts.gen.30.6: and Rachel saith, `God hath decided for me, and also hath hearkened to my voice, and giveth to me a son;' therefore hath she called his name Dan.
texts.gen.30.7: And Bilhah, Rachel's maid-servant, conceiveth again, and beareth a second son to Jacob,
texts.gen.30.8: and Rachel saith, `With wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, yea, I have prevailed;' and she calleth his name Napthali.
texts.gen.30.9: And Leah seeth that she hath ceased from bearing, and she taketh Zilpah her maid-servant, and giveth her to Jacob for a wife;
texts.gen.30.10: and Zilpah, Leah's maid-servant, beareth to Jacob a son,
texts.gen.30.11: and Leah saith, `A troop is coming;' and she calleth his name Gad.
texts.gen.30.12: And Zilpah, Leah's maid-servant, beareth a second son to Jacob,
texts.gen.30.13: and Leah saith, `Because of my happiness, for daughters have pronounced me happy;' and she calleth his name Asher.
texts.gen.30.14: And Reuben goeth in the days of wheat-harvest, and findeth love-apples in the field, and bringeth them in unto Leah, his mother, and Rachel saith unto Leah, `Give to me, I pray thee, of the love-apples of thy son.'
texts.gen.30.15: And she saith to her, `Is thy taking my husband a little thing, that thou hast taken also the love-apples of my son?' and Rachel saith, `Therefore doth he lie with thee to-night, for thy son's love-apples.'
texts.gen.30.16: And Jacob cometh in from the field at evening; and Leah goeth to meet him, and saith, `Unto me dost thou come in, for hiring I have hired thee with my son's love-apples;' and he lieth with her during that night.
texts.gen.30.17: And God hearkeneth unto Leah, and she conceiveth, and beareth to Jacob a son, a fifth,
texts.gen.30.18: and Leah saith, `God hath given my hire, because I have given my maid-servant to my husband;' and she calleth his name Issachar.
texts.gen.30.19: And conceive again doth Leah, and she beareth a sixth son to Jacob,
texts.gen.30.20: and Leah saith, `God hath endowed me -- a good dowry; this time doth my husband dwell with me, for I have borne to him six sons;' and she calleth his name Zebulun;
texts.gen.30.21: and afterwards hath she born a daughter, and calleth her name Dinah.
texts.gen.30.22: And God remembereth Rachel, and God hearkeneth unto her, and openeth her womb,
texts.gen.30.23: and she conceiveth and beareth a son, and saith, `God hath gathered up my reproach;'
texts.gen.30.24: and she calleth his name Joseph, saying, `Jehovah is adding to me another son.'
texts.gen.30.25: And it cometh to pass, when Rachel hath borne Joseph, that Jacob saith unto Laban, `Send me away, and I go unto my place, and to my land;
texts.gen.30.26: give up my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and I go; for thou -- thou hast known my service which I have served thee.'
texts.gen.30.27: And Laban saith unto him, `If, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes -- I have observed diligently that Jehovah doth bless me for thy sake.'
texts.gen.30.28: He saith also, `Define thy hire to me, and I give.'
texts.gen.30.29: And he saith unto him, `Thou -- thou hast known that which I have served thee [in], and that which thy substance was with me;
texts.gen.30.30: for [it is] little which thou hast had at my appearance, and it breaketh forth into a multitude, and Jehovah blesseth thee at my coming; and now, when do I make, I also, for mine own house?'
texts.gen.30.31: And he saith, `What do I give to thee?' And Jacob saith, `Thou dost not give me anything; if thou do for me this thing, I turn back; I have delight; thy flock I watch;
texts.gen.30.32: I pass through all thy flock to-day to turn aside from thence every sheep speckled and spotted, and every brown sheep among the lambs, and speckled and spotted among the goats -- and it hath been my hire;
texts.gen.30.33: and my righteousness hath answered for me in the day to come, when it cometh in for my hire before thy face; -- every one which is not speckled and spotted among [my] goats, and brown among [my] lambs -- it is stolen with me.'
texts.gen.30.34: And Laban saith, `Lo, O that it were according to thy word;'
texts.gen.30.35: and he turneth aside during that day the ring-straked and the spotted he-goats, and all the speckled and the spotted she-goats, every one that [hath] white in it, and every brown one among the lambs, and he giveth into the hand of his sons,
texts.gen.30.36: and setteth a journey of three days between himself and Jacob; and Jacob is feeding the rest of the flock of Laban.
texts.gen.30.37: And Jacob taketh to himself a rod of fresh poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut, and doth peel in them white peelings, making bare the white that [is] on the rods,
texts.gen.30.38: and setteth up the rods which he hath peeled in the gutters in the watering troughs (when the flock cometh in to drink), over-against the flock, that they may conceive in their coming in to drink;
texts.gen.30.39: and the flocks conceive at the rods, and the flock beareth ring-straked, speckled, and spotted ones.
texts.gen.30.40: And the lambs hath Jacob parted, and he putteth the face of the flock towards the ring-straked, also all the brown in the flock of Laban, and he setteth his own droves by themselves, and hath not set them near Laban's flock.
texts.gen.30.41: And it hath come to pass whenever the strong ones of the flock conceive, that Jacob set the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, to cause them to conceive by the rods,
texts.gen.30.42: and when the flock is feeble, he doth not set [them]; and the feeble ones have been Laban's, and the strong ones Jacob's.
texts.gen.30.43: And the man increaseth very exceedingly, and hath many flocks, and maid-servants, and men-servants, and camels, and asses.
texts.gen.31.1: And he heareth the words of Laban's sons, saying, `Jacob hath taken all that our father hath; yea, from that which our father hath, he hath made all this honour;'
texts.gen.31.2: and Jacob seeth the face of Laban, and lo, it is not with him as heretofore.
texts.gen.31.3: And Jehovah saith unto Jacob, `Turn back unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred, and I am with thee.'
texts.gen.31.4: And Jacob sendeth and calleth for Rachel and for Leah to the field unto his flock;
texts.gen.31.5: and saith to them, `I am beholding your father's face -- that it is not towards me as heretofore, and the God of my father hath been with me,
texts.gen.31.6: and ye -- ye have known that with all my power I have served your father,
texts.gen.31.7: and your father hath played upon me, and hath changed my hire ten times; and God hath not suffered him to do evil with me.
texts.gen.31.8: `If he say thus: The speckled are thy hire, then bare all the flock speckled ones; and if he say thus: The ring-straked are thy hire, then bare all the flock ring-straked;
texts.gen.31.9: and God taketh away the substance of your father, and doth give to me.
texts.gen.31.10: `And it cometh to pass at the time of the flock conceiving, that I lift up mine eyes and see in a dream, and lo, the he-goats, which are going up on the flock, [are] ring-straked, speckled, and grisled;
texts.gen.31.11: and the messenger of God saith unto me in the dream, Jacob, and I say, Here [am] I.
texts.gen.31.12: `And He saith, Lift up, I pray thee, thine eyes, and see -- all the he-goats which are going up on the flock [are] ring-straked, speckled, and grisled, for I have seen all that Laban is doing to thee;
texts.gen.31.13: I [am] the God of Bethel where thou hast anointed a standing pillar, where thou hast vowed a vow to me; now, arise, go out from this land, and turn back unto the land of thy birth.'
texts.gen.31.14: And Rachel answereth -- Leah also -- and saith to him, `Have we yet a portion and inheritance in the house of our father?
texts.gen.31.15: have we not been reckoned strangers to him? for he hath sold us, and he also utterly consumeth our money;
texts.gen.31.16: for all the wealth which God hath taken away from our father, it [is] ours, and our children's; and now, all that God hath said unto thee -- do.'
texts.gen.31.17: And Jacob riseth, and lifteth up his sons and his wives on the camels,
texts.gen.31.18: and leadeth all his cattle, and all his substance which he hath acquired, the cattle of his getting, which he hath acquired in Padan-Aram, to go unto Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.31.19: And Laban hath gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stealeth the teraphim which her father hath;
texts.gen.31.20: and Jacob deceiveth the heart of Laban the Aramaean, because he hath not declared to him that he is fleeing;
texts.gen.31.21: and he fleeth, he and all that he hath, and riseth, and passeth over the River, and setteth his face [toward] the mount of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.22: And it is told to Laban on the third day that Jacob hath fled,
texts.gen.31.23: and he taketh his brethren with him, and pursueth after him a journey of seven days, and overtaketh him in the mount of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.24: And God cometh in unto Laban the Aramaean in a dream of the night, and saith to him, `Take heed to thyself lest thou speak with Jacob from good unto evil.'
texts.gen.31.25: And Laban overtaketh Jacob; and Jacob hath fixed his tent in the mount; and Laban with his brethren have fixed [theirs] in the mount of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.26: And Laban saith to Jacob, `What hast thou done that thou dost deceive my heart, and lead away my daughters as captives of the sword?
texts.gen.31.27: Why hast thou hidden thyself to flee, and deceivest me, and hast not declared to me, and I send thee away with joy and with songs, with tabret and with harp,
texts.gen.31.28: and hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters? -- now thou hast acted foolishly in doing [so];
texts.gen.31.29: my hand is to God to do evil with you, but the God of your father yesternight hath spoken unto me, saying, Take heed to thyself from speaking with Jacob from good unto evil.
texts.gen.31.30: `And now, thou hast certainly gone, because thou hast been very desirous for the house of thy father; why hast thou stolen my gods?'
texts.gen.31.31: And Jacob answereth and saith to Laban, `Because I was afraid, for I said, Lest thou take violently away thy daughters from me;
texts.gen.31.32: with whomsoever thou findest thy gods -- he doth not live; before our brethren discern for thyself what [is] with me, and take to thyself:' and Jacob hath not known that Rachel hath stolen them.
texts.gen.31.33: And Laban goeth into the tent of Jacob, and into the tent of Leah, and into the tent of the two handmaidens, and hath not found; and he goeth out from the tent of Leah, and goeth into the tent of Rachel.
texts.gen.31.34: And Rachel hath taken the teraphim, and putteth them in the furniture of the camel, and sitteth upon them; and Laban feeleth all the tent, and hath not found;
texts.gen.31.35: and she saith unto her father, `Let it not be displeasing in the eyes of my lord that I am not able to rise at thy presence, for the way of women [is] on me;' and he searcheth, and hath not found the teraphim.
texts.gen.31.36: And it is displeasing to Jacob, and he striveth with Laban; and Jacob answereth and saith to Laban, `What [is] my transgression? what my sin, that thou hast burned after me?
texts.gen.31.37: for thou hast felt all my vessels: what hast thou found of all the vessels of thy house? set here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and they decide between us both.
texts.gen.31.38: `These twenty years I [am] with thee: thy ewes and thy she-goats have not miscarried, and the rams of thy flock I have not eaten;
texts.gen.31.39: the torn I have not brought in unto thee -- I, I repay it -- from my hand thou dost seek it; I have been deceived by day, and I have been deceived by night;
texts.gen.31.40: I have been [thus]: in the day consumed me hath drought, and frost by night, and wander doth my sleep from mine eyes.
texts.gen.31.41: `This [is] to me twenty years in thy house: I have served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy flock; and thou changest my hire ten times;
texts.gen.31.42: unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac, had been for me, surely now empty thou hadst sent me away; mine affliction and the labour of my hands hath God seen, and reproveth yesternight.'
texts.gen.31.43: And Laban answereth and saith unto Jacob, `The daughters [are] my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the flock my flock, and all that thou art seeing [is] mine; and to my daughters -- what do I to these to-day, or to their sons whom they have born?
texts.gen.31.44: and now, come, let us make a covenant, I and thou, and it hath been for a witness between me and thee.'
texts.gen.31.45: And Jacob taketh a stone, and lifteth it up [for] a standing pillar;
texts.gen.31.46: and Jacob saith to his brethren, `Gather stones,' and they take stones, and make a heap; and they eat there on the heap;
texts.gen.31.47: and Laban calleth it Jegar-Sahadutha; and Jacob hath called it Galeed.
texts.gen.31.48: And Laban saith, `This heap [is] witness between me and thee to-day;' therefore hath he called its name Galeed;
texts.gen.31.49: Mizpah also, for he said, `Jehovah doth watch between me and thee, for we are hidden one from another;
