texts.gen.31.50: if thou afflict my daughters, or take wives beside my daughters -- there is no man with us -- see, God [is] witness between me and thee.'
texts.gen.31.51: And Laban saith to Jacob, `Lo, this heap, and lo, the standing pillar which I have cast between me and thee;
texts.gen.31.52: this heap [is] witness, and the standing pillar [is] witness, that I do not pass over this heap unto thee, and that thou dost not pass over this heap and this standing pillar unto me -- for evil;
texts.gen.31.53: the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, doth judge between us -- the God of their father,' and Jacob sweareth by the Fear of his father Isaac.
texts.gen.31.54: And Jacob sacrificeth a sacrifice in the mount, and calleth to his brethren to eat bread, and they eat bread, and lodge in the mount;
texts.gen.31.55: and Laban riseth early in the morning, and kisseth his sons and his daughters, and blesseth them; and Laban goeth on, and turneth back to his place.
texts.gen.32.1: And Jacob hath gone on his way, and messengers of God come upon him;
texts.gen.32.2: and Jacob saith, when he hath seen them, `This [is] the camp of God;' and he calleth the name of that place `Two Camps.'
texts.gen.32.3: And Jacob sendeth messengers before him unto Esau his brother, towards the land of Seir, the field of Edom,
texts.gen.32.4: and commandeth them, saying, `Thus do ye say to my lord, to Esau: Thus said thy servant Jacob, With Laban I have sojourned, and I tarry until now;
texts.gen.32.5: and I have ox, and ass, flock, and man-servant, and maid-servant, and I send to declare to my lord, to find grace in his eyes.'
texts.gen.32.6: And the messengers turn back unto Jacob, saying, `We came in unto thy brother, unto Esau, and he also is coming to meet thee, and four hundred men with him;'
texts.gen.32.7: and Jacob feareth exceedingly, and is distressed, and he divideth the people who [are] with him, and the flock, and the herd, and the camels, into two camps,
texts.gen.32.8: and saith, `If Esau come in unto the one camp, and have smitten it -- then the camp which is left hath been for an escape.'
texts.gen.32.9: And Jacob saith, `God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Jehovah who saith unto me, Turn back to thy land, and to thy kindred, and I do good with thee:
texts.gen.32.10: I have been unworthy of all the kind acts, and of all the truth which Thou hast done with thy servant -- for, with my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
texts.gen.32.11: `Deliver me, I pray Thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I am fearing him, less he come and have smitten me -- mother beside sons;
texts.gen.32.12: and Thou -- Thou hast said, I certainly do good with thee, and have set thy seed as the sand of the sea, which is not numbered because of the multitude.'
texts.gen.32.13: And he lodgeth there during that night, and taketh from that which is coming into his hand, a present for Esau his brother:
texts.gen.32.14: she-goats two hundred, and he-goats twenty, ewes two hundred, and rams twenty,
texts.gen.32.15: suckling camels and their young ones thirty, cows forty, and bullocks ten, she-asses twenty, and foals ten;
texts.gen.32.16: and he giveth into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and saith unto his servants, `Pass over before me, and a space ye do put between drove and drove.'
texts.gen.32.17: And he commandeth the first, saying, `When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and hath asked thee, saying, Whose [art] thou? and whither goest thou? and whose [are] these before thee?
texts.gen.32.18: then thou hast said, Thy servant Jacob's: it [is] a present sent to my lord, to Esau; and lo, he also [is] behind us.'
texts.gen.32.19: And he commandeth also the second, also the third, also all who are going after the droves, saying, `According to this manner do ye speak unto Esau in your finding him,
texts.gen.32.20: and ye have said also, Lo, thy servant Jacob [is] behind us;' for he said, `I pacify his face with the present which is going before me, and afterwards I see his face; it may be he lifteth up my face;'
texts.gen.32.21: and the present passeth over before his face, and he hath lodged during that night in the camp.
texts.gen.32.22: And he riseth in that night, and taketh his two wives, and his two maid-servants, and his eleven children, and passeth over the passage of Jabbok;
texts.gen.32.23: and he taketh them, and causeth them to pass over the brook, and he causeth that which he hath to pass over.
texts.gen.32.24: And Jacob is left alone, and one wrestleth with him till the ascending of the dawn;
texts.gen.32.25: and he seeth that he is not able for him, and he cometh against the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob's thigh is disjointed in his wrestling with him;
texts.gen.32.26: and he saith, `Send me away, for the dawn hath ascended:' and he saith, `I send thee not away, except thou hast blessed me.'
texts.gen.32.27: And he saith unto him, `What [is] thy name?' and he saith, `Jacob.'
texts.gen.32.28: And he saith, `Thy name is no more called Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast been a prince with God and with men, and dost prevail.'
texts.gen.32.29: And Jacob asketh, and saith, `Declare, I pray thee, thy name;' and he saith, `Why [is] this, thou askest for My name?' and He blesseth him there.
texts.gen.32.30: And Jacob calleth the name of the place Peniel: for `I have seen God face unto face, and my life is delivered;'
texts.gen.32.31: and the sun riseth on him when he hath passed over Penuel, and he is halting on his thigh;
texts.gen.32.32: therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew which shrank, which [is] on the hollow of the thigh, unto this day, because He came against the hollow of Jacob's thigh, against the sinew which shrank.
texts.gen.33.1: And Jacob lifteth up his eyes, and looketh, and lo, Esau is coming, and with him four hundred men; and he divideth the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two maid-servants;
texts.gen.33.2: and he setteth the maid-servants and their children first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.
texts.gen.33.3: And he himself passed over before them, and boweth himself to the earth seven times, until his drawing nigh unto his brother,
texts.gen.33.4: and Esau runneth to meet him, and embraceth him, and falleth on his neck, and kisseth him, and they weep;
texts.gen.33.5: and he lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the women and the children, and saith, `What [are] these to thee?' And he saith, `The children with whom God hath favoured thy servant.'
texts.gen.33.6: And the maid-servants draw nigh, they and their children, and bow themselves;
texts.gen.33.7: and Leah also draweth nigh, and her children, and they bow themselves; and afterwards Joseph hath drawn nigh with Rachel, and they bow themselves.
texts.gen.33.8: And he saith, `What to thee [is] all this camp which I have met?' and he saith, `To find grace in the eyes of my lord.'
texts.gen.33.9: And Esau saith, `I have abundance, my brother, let it be to thyself that which thou hast.'
texts.gen.33.10: And Jacob saith, `Nay, I pray thee, if, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, then thou hast received my present from my hand, because that I have seen thy face, as the seeing of the face of God, and thou art pleased with me;
texts.gen.33.11: receive, I pray thee, my blessing, which is brought to thee, because God hath favoured me, and because I have all [things];' and he presseth on him, and he receiveth,
texts.gen.33.12: and saith, `Let us journey and go on, and I go on before thee.'
texts.gen.33.13: And he saith unto him, `My lord knoweth that the children [are] tender, and the suckling flock and the herd [are] with me; when they have beaten them one day, then hath all the flock died.
texts.gen.33.14: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant, and I -- I lead on gently, according to the foot of the work which [is] before me, and to the foot of the children, until that I come unto my lord, to Seir.'
texts.gen.33.15: And Esau saith, `Let me, I pray thee, place with thee some of the people who [are] with me;' and he said, `Why [is] this? I find grace in the eyes of my lord.'
texts.gen.33.16: And turn back on that day doth Esau on his way to Seir;
texts.gen.33.17: and Jacob hath journeyed to Succoth, and buildeth to himself a house, and for his cattle hath made booths, therefore hath he called the name of the place Succoth.
texts.gen.33.18: And Jacob cometh in to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which [is] in the land of Canaan, in his coming from Padan-Aram, and encampeth before the city,
texts.gen.33.19: and he buyeth the portion of the field where he hath stretched out his tent, from the hand of the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem, for a hundred kesitah;
texts.gen.33.20: and he setteth up there an altar, and proclaimeth at it God -- the God of Israel.
texts.gen.34.1: And Dinah, daughter of Leah, whom she hath borne to Jacob, goeth out to look on the daughters of the land,
texts.gen.34.2: and Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, a prince of the land, seeth her, and taketh her, and lieth with her, and humbleth her;
texts.gen.34.3: and his soul cleaveth to Dinah, daughter of Jacob, and he loveth the young person, and speaketh unto the heart of the young person.
texts.gen.34.4: And Shechem speaketh unto Hamor his father, saying, `Take for me this damsel for a wife.'
texts.gen.34.5: And Jacob hath heard that he hath defiled Dinah his daughter, and his sons were with his cattle in the field, and Jacob kept silent till their coming.
texts.gen.34.6: And Hamor, father of Shechem, goeth out unto Jacob to speak with him;
texts.gen.34.7: and the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard, and the men grieve themselves, and it [is] very displeasing to them, for folly he hath done against Israel, to lie with the daughter of Jacob -- and so it is not done.
texts.gen.34.8: And Hamor speaketh with them, saying, `Shechem, my son, his soul hath cleaved to your daughter; give her, I pray you, to him for a wife,
texts.gen.34.9: and join ye in marriage with us; your daughters ye give to us, and our daughters ye take to yourselves,
texts.gen.34.10: and with us ye dwell, and the land is before you; dwell ye and trade [in] it, and have possessions in it.'
texts.gen.34.11: And Shechem saith unto her father, and unto her brethren, `Let me find grace in your eyes, and that which ye say unto me, I give;
texts.gen.34.12: multiply on me exceedingly dowry and gift, and I give as ye say unto me, and give to me the young person for a wife.'
texts.gen.34.13: And the sons of Jacob answer Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and they speak (because he defiled Dinah their sister),
texts.gen.34.14: and say unto them, `We are not able to do this thing, to give our sister to one who hath a foreskin: for it [is] a reproach to us.
texts.gen.34.15: `Only for this we consent to you; if ye be as we, to have every male of you circumcised,
texts.gen.34.16: then we have given our daughters to you, and your daughters we take to ourselves, and we have dwelt with you, and have become one people;
texts.gen.34.17: and if ye hearken not unto us to be circumcised, then we have taken our daughter, and have gone.'
texts.gen.34.18: And their words are good in the eyes of Hamor, and in the eyes of Shechem, Hamor's son;
texts.gen.34.19: and the young man delayed not to do the thing, for he had delight in Jacob's daughter, and he is honourable above all the house of his father.
texts.gen.34.20: And Hamor cometh -- Shechem his son also -- unto the gate of their city, and they speak unto the men of their city, saying,
texts.gen.34.21: `These men are peaceable with us; then let them dwell in the land, and trade [in] it; and the land, lo, [is] wide before them; their daughters let us take to ourselves for wives, and our daughters give to them.
texts.gen.34.22: `Only for this do the men consent to us, to dwell with us, to become one people, in every male of us being circumcised, as they are circumcised;
texts.gen.34.23: their cattle, and their substance, and all their beasts -- are they not ours? only let us consent to them, and they dwell with us.'
texts.gen.34.24: And unto Hamor, and unto Shechem his son, hearken do all those going out of the gate of his city, and every male is circumcised, all those going out of the gate of his city.
texts.gen.34.25: And it cometh to pass, on the third day, in their being pained, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, take each his sword, and come in against the city confidently, and slay every male;
texts.gen.34.26: and Hamor, and Shechem his son, they have slain by the mouth of the sword, and they take Dinah out of Shechem's house, and go out.
texts.gen.34.27: Jacob's sons have come in upon the wounded, and they spoil the city, because they had defiled their sister;
texts.gen.34.28: their flock and their herd, and their asses, and that which [is] in the city, and that which [is] in the field, have they taken;
texts.gen.34.29: and all their wealth, and all their infants, and their wives they have taken captive, and they spoil also all that [is] in the house.
texts.gen.34.30: And Jacob saith unto Simeon and unto Levi, `Ye have troubled me, by causing me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanite, and among the Perizzite: and I [am] few in number, and they have been gathered against me, and have smitten me, and I have been destroyed, I and my house.'
texts.gen.34.31: And they say, `As a harlot doth he make our sister?'
texts.gen.35.1: And God saith unto Jacob, `Rise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there, and make there an altar to God, who appeared unto thee in thy fleeing from the face of Esau thy brother.'
texts.gen.35.2: And Jacob saith unto his household, and unto all who [are] with him, `Turn aside the gods of the stranger which [are] in your midst, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments;
texts.gen.35.3: and we rise, and go up to Bethel, and I make there an altar to God, who is answering me in the day of my distress, and is with me in the way that I have gone.'
texts.gen.35.4: And they give unto Jacob all the gods of the stranger that [are] in their hand, and the rings that [are] in their ears, and Jacob hideth them under the oak which [is] by Shechem;
texts.gen.35.5: and they journey, and the terror of God is on the cities which [are] round about them, and they have not pursued after the sons of Jacob.
texts.gen.35.6: And Jacob cometh in to Luz which [is] in the land of Canaan (it [is] Bethel), he and all the people who [are] with him,
texts.gen.35.7: and he buildeth there an altar, and proclaimeth at the place the God of Bethel: for there had God been revealed unto him, in his fleeing from the face of his brother.
texts.gen.35.8: And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, dieth, and she is buried at the lower part of Bethel, under the oak, and he calleth its name `Oak of weeping.'
texts.gen.35.9: And God appeareth unto Jacob again, in his coming from Padan-Aram, and blesseth him;
texts.gen.35.10: and God saith to him, `Thy name [is] Jacob: thy name is no more called Jacob, but Israel is thy name;' and He calleth his name Israel.
texts.gen.35.11: And God saith to him, `I [am] God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply, a nation and an assembly of nations is from thee, and kings from thy loins go out;
texts.gen.35.12: and the land which I have given to Abraham and to Isaac -- to thee I give it, yea to thy seed after thee I give the land.'
texts.gen.35.13: And God goeth up from him, in the place where He hath spoken with him.
texts.gen.35.14: And Jacob setteth up a standing pillar in the place where He hath spoken with him, a standing pillar of stone, and he poureth on it an oblation, and he poureth on it oil;
texts.gen.35.15: and Jacob calleth the name of the place where God spake with him Bethel.
texts.gen.35.16: And they journey from Bethel, and there is yet a kibrath of land before entering Ephratha, and Rachel beareth, and is sharply pained in her bearing;
texts.gen.35.17: and it cometh to pass, in her being sharply pained in her bearing, that the midwife saith to her, `Fear not, for this also [is] a son for thee.'
texts.gen.35.18: And it cometh to pass in the going out of her soul (for she died), that she calleth his name Ben-Oni; and his father called him Benjamin;
texts.gen.35.19: and Rachel dieth, and is buried in the way to Ephratha, which [is] Bethlehem,
texts.gen.35.20: and Jacob setteth up a standing pillar over her grave; which [is] the standing pillar of Rachel's grave unto this day.
texts.gen.35.21: And Israel journeyeth, and stretcheth out his tent beyond the tower of Edar;
texts.gen.35.22: and it cometh to pass in Israel's dwelling in that land, that Reuben goeth, and lieth with Bilhah his father's concubine; and Israel heareth.
texts.gen.35.23: And the sons of Jacob are twelve. Sons of Leah: Jacob's first-born Reuben, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun.
texts.gen.35.24: Sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
texts.gen.35.25: And sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maid-servant: Dan and Naphtali.
texts.gen.35.26: And sons of Zilpah, Leah's maid-servant: Gad and Asher. These [are] sons of Jacob, who have been born to him in Padan-Aram.
texts.gen.35.27: And Jacob cometh unto Isaac his father, at Mamre, the city of Arba (which [is] Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac have sojourned.
texts.gen.35.28: And the days of Isaac are a hundred and eighty years,
texts.gen.35.29: and Isaac expireth, and dieth, and is gathered unto his people, aged and satisfied with days; and bury him do Esau and Jacob his sons.
texts.gen.36.1: And these [are] births of Esau, who [is] Edom.
texts.gen.36.2: Esau hath taken his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
texts.gen.36.3: and Bashemath daughter of Ishmael, sister of Nebajoth.
texts.gen.36.4: And Adah beareth to Esau, Eliphaz; and Bashemath hath born Reuel;
texts.gen.36.5: and Aholibamah hath born Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. These [are] sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.36.6: And Esau taketh his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance which he hath acquired in the land of Canaan, and goeth into the country from the face of Jacob his brother;
texts.gen.36.7: for their substance was more abundant than to dwell together, and the land of their sojournings was not able to bear them because of their cattle;
texts.gen.36.8: and Esau dwelleth in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
texts.gen.36.9: And these [are] births of Esau, father of Edom, in mount Seir.
texts.gen.36.10: These [are] the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz son of Adah, wife of Esau; Reuel son of Bashemath, wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.11: And the sons of Eliphaz are Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz;
texts.gen.36.12: and Timnath hath been concubine to Eliphaz son of Esau, and she beareth to Eliphaz, Amalek; these [are] sons of Adah wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.13: And these [are] sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah; these were sons of Bashemath wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.14: And these have been the sons of Aholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, wife of Esau; and she beareth to Esau, Jeush and Jaalam and Korah.
texts.gen.36.15: These [are] chiefs of the sons of Esau: sons of Eliphaz, first-born of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
texts.gen.36.16: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek; these [are] chiefs of Eliphaz, in the land of Edom; these [are] sons of Adah.
texts.gen.36.17: And these [are] sons of Reuel son of Esau: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah; these [are] chiefs of Reuel, in the land of Edom; these [are] sons of Bashemath wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.18: And these [are] sons of Aholibamah wife of Esau: chief Jeush, chief Jaalam, chief Korah; these [are] chiefs of Aholibamah daughter of Anah, wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.19: These [are] sons of Esau (who [is] Edom), and these their chiefs.
texts.gen.36.20: These [are] sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
texts.gen.36.21: and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan; these [are] chiefs of the Horites, sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
texts.gen.36.22: And the sons of Lotan are Hori and Heman; and a sister of Lotan [is] Timna.
texts.gen.36.23: And these [are] sons of Shobal: Alvan and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
texts.gen.36.24: And these [are] sons of Zibeon, both Ajah and Anah: it [is] Anah that hath found the Imim in the wilderness, in his feeding the asses of Zibeon his father.
texts.gen.36.25: And these [are] sons of Anah: Dishon, and Aholibamah daughter of Anah.
texts.gen.36.26: And these [are] sons of Dishon: Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
texts.gen.36.27: These [are] sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
texts.gen.36.28: These [are] sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
texts.gen.36.29: These [are] chiefs of the Horite: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
texts.gen.36.30: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan: these [are] chiefs of the Horite in reference to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
texts.gen.36.31: And these [are] the kings who have reigned in the land of Edom before the reigning of a king over the sons of Israel.
texts.gen.36.32: And Bela son of Beor reigneth in Edom, and the name of his city [is] Dinhabah;
texts.gen.36.33: and Bela dieth, and reign in his stead doth Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah;
texts.gen.36.34: and Jobab dieth, and reign in his stead doth Husham from the land of the Temanite.
texts.gen.36.35: And Husham dieth, and reign in his stead doth Hadad son of Bedad (who smiteth Midian in the field of Moab), and the name of his city [is] Avith;
texts.gen.36.36: and Hadad dieth, and reign in his stead doth Samlah of Masrekah;
texts.gen.36.37: and Samlah dieth, and reign in his stead doth Saul from Rehoboth of the River;
texts.gen.36.38: and Saul dieth, and reign in his stead doth Baal-hanan son of Achbor;
texts.gen.36.39: and Baal-hanan son of Achbor dieth, and reign in his stead doth Hadar, and the name of his city [is] Pau; and his wife's name [is] Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
texts.gen.36.40: And these [are] the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their families, according to their places, by their names: chief Timnah, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
texts.gen.36.41: chief Aholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
texts.gen.36.42: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
texts.gen.36.43: chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these [are] chiefs of Edom, in reference to their dwellings, in the land of their possession; he [is] Esau father of Edom.
texts.gen.37.1: And Jacob dwelleth in the land of his father's sojournings -- in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.37.2: These [are] births of Jacob: Joseph, a son of seventeen years, hath been enjoying himself with his brethren among the flock, (and he [is] a youth,) with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives, and Joseph bringeth in an account of their evil unto their father.
texts.gen.37.3: And Israel hath loved Joseph more than any of his sons, for he [is] a son of his old age, and hath made for him a long coat;
texts.gen.37.4: and his brethren see that their father hath loved him more than any of his brethren, and they hate him, and have not been able to speak [to] him peaceably.
texts.gen.37.5: And Joseph dreameth a dream, and declareth to his brethren, and they add still more to hate him.
texts.gen.37.6: And he saith unto them, `Hear ye, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:
texts.gen.37.7: that, lo, we are binding bundles in the midst of the field, and lo, my bundle hath arisen, and hath also stood up, and lo, your bundles are round about, and bow themselves to my bundle.'
texts.gen.37.8: And his brethren say to him, `Dost thou certainly reign over us? dost thou certainly rule over us?' and they add still more to hate him, for his dreams, and for his words.
texts.gen.37.9: And he dreameth yet another dream, and recounteth it to his brethren, and saith, `Lo, I have dreamed a dream again, and lo, the sun and the moon, and eleven stars, are bowing themselves to me.'
texts.gen.37.10: And he recounteth unto his father, and unto his brethren; and his father pusheth against him, and saith to him, `What [is] this dream which thou hast dreamt? do we certainly come -- I, and thy mother, and thy brethren -- to bow ourselves to thee, to the earth?'
texts.gen.37.11: and his brethren are zealous against him, and his father hath watched the matter.
texts.gen.37.12: And his brethren go to feed the flock of their father in Shechem,
texts.gen.37.13: and Israel saith unto Joseph, `Are not thy brethren feeding in Shechem? come, and I send thee unto them;' and he saith to him, `Here [am] I;'
texts.gen.37.14: and he saith to him, `Go, I pray thee, see the peace of thy brethren, and the peace of the flock, and bring me back word;' and he sendeth him from the valley of Hebron, and he cometh to Shechem.
texts.gen.37.15: And a man findeth him, and lo, he is wandering in the field, and the man asketh him, saying, `What seekest thou?'
texts.gen.37.16: and he saith, `My brethren I am seeking, declare to me, I pray thee, where they are feeding?'
texts.gen.37.17: And the man saith, `They have journeyed from this, for I have heard some saying, Let us go to Dothan,' and Joseph goeth after his brethren, and findeth them in Dothan.
texts.gen.37.18: And they see him from afar, even before he draweth near unto them, and they conspire against him to put him to death.
texts.gen.37.19: And they say one unto another, `Lo, this man of the dreams cometh;
texts.gen.37.20: and now, come, and we slay him, and cast him into one of the pits, and have said, An evil beast hath devoured him; and we see what his dreams are.'
texts.gen.37.21: And Reuben heareth, and delivereth him out of their hand, and saith, `Let us not smite the life;'
texts.gen.37.22: and Reuben saith unto them, `Shed no blood; cast him into this pit which [is] in the wilderness, and put not forth a hand upon him,' -- in order to deliver him out of their hand, to bring him back unto his father.
texts.gen.37.23: And it cometh to pass, when Joseph hath come unto his brethren, that they strip Joseph of his coat, the long coat which [is] upon him,
texts.gen.37.24: and take him and cast him into the pit, and the pit [is] empty, there is no water in it.
texts.gen.37.25: And they sit down to eat bread, and they lift up their eyes, and look, and lo, a company of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, and their camels bearing spices, and balm, and myrrh, going to take [them] down to Egypt.
texts.gen.37.26: And Judah saith unto his brethren, `What gain when we slay our brother, and have concealed his blood?
texts.gen.37.27: Come, and we sell him to the Ishmaelites, and our hands are not on him, for he [is] our brother -- our flesh;' and his brethren hearken.
texts.gen.37.28: And Midianite merchantmen pass by and they draw out and bring up Joseph out of the pit, and sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty silverlings, and they bring Joseph into Egypt.
texts.gen.37.29: And Reuben returneth unto the pit, and lo, Joseph is not in the pit, and he rendeth his garments,
texts.gen.37.30: and he returneth unto his brethren, and saith, `The lad is not, and I -- whither am I going?'
texts.gen.37.31: And they take the coat of Joseph, and slaughter a kid of the goats, and dip the coat in the blood,
texts.gen.37.32: and send the long coat, and they bring [it] in unto their father, and say, `This have we found; discern, we pray thee, whether it [is] thy son's coat or not?'
texts.gen.37.33: And he discerneth it, and saith, `My son's coat! an evil beast hath devoured him; torn -- torn is Joseph!'
texts.gen.37.34: And Jacob rendeth his raiment, and putteth sackcloth on his loins, and becometh a mourner for his son many days,
texts.gen.37.35: and all his sons and all his daughters rise to comfort him, and he refuseth to comfort himself, and saith, `For -- I go down mourning unto my son, to Sheol,' and his father weepeth for him.
texts.gen.37.36: And the Medanites have sold him unto Egypt, to Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, head of the executioners.
texts.gen.38.1: And it cometh to pass, at that time, that Judah goeth down from his brethren, and turneth aside unto a man, an Adullamite, whose name [is] Hirah;
texts.gen.38.2: and Judah seeth there the daughter of a man, a Canaanite, whose name [is] Shuah, and taketh her, and goeth in unto her.
texts.gen.38.3: And she conceiveth, and beareth a son, and he calleth his name Er;
texts.gen.38.4: and she conceiveth again, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Onan;
texts.gen.38.5: and she addeth again, and beareth a son, and calleth his name Shelah; and he was in Chezib in her bearing him.
texts.gen.38.6: And Judah taketh a wife for Er, his first-born, and her name [is] Tamar;
texts.gen.38.7: and Er, Judah's first-born, is evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah doth put him to death.
texts.gen.38.8: And Judah saith to Onan, `Go in unto the wife of thy brother, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother;'
texts.gen.38.9: and Onan knoweth that the seed is not [reckoned] his; and it hath come to pass, if he hath gone in unto his brother's wife, that he hath destroyed [it] to the earth, so as not to give seed to his brother;
texts.gen.38.10: and that which he hath done is evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and He putteth him also to death.
texts.gen.38.11: And Judah saith to Tamar his daughter-in-law, `Abide a widow at thy father's house, till Shelah my son groweth up;' for he said, `Lest he die -- even he -- like his brethren;' and Tamar goeth and dwelleth at her father's house.
texts.gen.38.12: And the days are multiplied, and the daughter of Shuah, Judah's wife, dieth; and Judah is comforted, and goeth up unto his sheep-shearers, he and Hirah his friend the Adullamite, to Timnath.
texts.gen.38.13: And it is declared to Tamar, saying, `Lo, thy husband's father is going up to Timnath to shear his flock;'
texts.gen.38.14: and she turneth aside the garments of her widowhood from off her, and covereth herself with a vail, and wrappeth herself up, and sitteth in the opening of Enayim, which [is] by the way to Timnath, for she hath seen that Shelah hath grown up, and she hath not been given to him for a wife.
texts.gen.38.15: And Judah seeth her, and reckoneth her for a harlot, for she hath covered her face,
texts.gen.38.16: and he turneth aside unto her by the way, and saith, `Come, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee,' (for he hath not known that she [is] his daughter-in-law); and she saith, `What dost thou give to me, that thou mayest come in unto me?'
texts.gen.38.17: and he saith, `I -- I send a kid of the goats from the flock.' And she saith, `Dost thou give a pledge till thou send [it]?'
texts.gen.38.18: and he saith, `What [is] the pledge that I give to thee?' and she saith, `Thy seal, and thy ribbon, and thy staff which [is] in thy hand;' and he giveth to her, and goeth in unto her, and she conceiveth to him;
texts.gen.38.19: and she riseth, and goeth, and turneth aside her vail from off her, and putteth on the garments of her widowhood.
texts.gen.38.20: And Judah sendeth the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the hand of the woman, and he hath not found her.
texts.gen.38.21: And he asketh the men of her place, saying, `Where [is] the separated one -- she in Enayim, by the way?' and they say, `There hath not been in this [place] a separated one.'
texts.gen.38.22: And he turneth back unto Judah, and saith, `I have not found her; and the men of the place also have said, There hath not been in this [place] a separated one,'
texts.gen.38.23: and Judah saith, `Let her take to herself, lest we become despised; lo, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.'
texts.gen.38.24: And it cometh to pass about three months [after], that it is declared to Judah, saying, `Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath committed fornication; and also, lo, she hath conceived by fornication:' and Judah saith, `Bring her out -- and she is burnt.'
texts.gen.38.25: She is brought out, and she hath sent unto her husband's father, saying, `To a man whose these [are], I [am] pregnant;' and she saith, `Discern, I pray thee, whose [are] these -- the seal, and the ribbons, and the staff.'
texts.gen.38.26: And Judah discerneth and saith, `She hath been more righteous than I, because that I did not give her to Shelah my son;' and he hath not added to know her again.
texts.gen.38.27: And it cometh to pass in the time of her bearing, that lo, twins [are] in her womb;
texts.gen.38.28: and it cometh to pass in her bearing, that [one] giveth out a hand, and the midwife taketh and bindeth on his hand a scarlet thread, saying, `This hath come out first.'
texts.gen.38.29: And it cometh to pass as he draweth back his hand, that lo, his brother hath come out, and she saith, `What! thou hast broken forth -- on thee [is] the breach;' and he calleth his name Pharez;
texts.gen.38.30: and afterwards hath his brother come out, on whose hand [is] the scarlet thread, and he calleth his name Zarah.
texts.gen.39.1: And Joseph hath been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, head of the executioners, an Egyptian man, buyeth him out of the hands of the Ishmaelites who have brought him thither.
texts.gen.39.2: And Jehovah is with Joseph, and he is a prosperous man, and he is in the house of his lord the Egyptian,
texts.gen.39.3: and his lord seeth that Jehovah is with him, and all that he is doing Jehovah is causing to prosper in his hand,
texts.gen.39.4: and Joseph findeth grace in his eyes and serveth him, and he appointeth him over his house, and all that he hath he hath given into his hand.
texts.gen.39.5: And it cometh to pass from the time that he hath appointed him over his house, and over all that he hath, that Jehovah blesseth the house of the Egyptian for Joseph's sake, and the blessing of Jehovah is on all that he hath, in the house, and in the field;
texts.gen.39.6: and he leaveth all that he hath in the hand of Joseph, and he hath not known anything that he hath, except the bread which he is eating. And Joseph is of a fair form, and of a fair appearance.
texts.gen.39.7: And it cometh to pass after these things, that his lord's wife lifteth up her eyes unto Joseph, and saith, `Lie with me;'
texts.gen.39.8: and he refuseth, and saith unto his lord's wife, `Lo, my lord hath not known what [is] with me in the house, and all that he hath he hath given into my hand;
texts.gen.39.9: none is greater in this house than I, and he hath not withheld from me anything, except thee, because thou [art] his wife; and how shall I do this great evil? -- then have I sinned against God.'
texts.gen.39.10: And it cometh to pass at her speaking unto Joseph day [by] day, that he hath not hearkened unto her, to lie near her, to be with her;
texts.gen.39.11: and it cometh to pass about this day, that he goeth into the house to do his work, and there is none of the men of the house there in the house,
texts.gen.39.12: and she catcheth him by his garment, saying, `Lie with me;' and he leaveth his garment in her hand, and fleeth, and goeth without.
texts.gen.39.13: And it cometh to pass when she seeth that he hath left his garment in her hand, and fleeth without,
texts.gen.39.14: that she calleth for the men of her house, and speaketh to them, saying, `See, he hath brought in to us a man, a Hebrew, to play with us; he hath come in unto me, to lie with me, and I call with a loud voice,
texts.gen.39.15: and it cometh to pass, when he heareth that I have lifted up my voice and call, that he leaveth his garment near me, and fleeth, and goeth without.'
texts.gen.39.16: And she placeth his garment near her, until the coming in of his lord unto his house.
texts.gen.39.17: And she speaketh unto him according to these words, saying, `The Hebrew servant whom thou hast brought unto us, hath come in unto me to play with me;
texts.gen.39.18: and it cometh to pass, when I lift my voice and call, that he leaveth his garment near me, and fleeth without.'
texts.gen.39.19: And it cometh to pass when his lord heareth the words of his wife, which she hath spoken unto him, saying, `According to these things hath thy servant done to me,' that his anger burneth;
texts.gen.39.20: and Joseph's lord taketh him, and putteth him unto the round-house, a place where the king's prisoners [are] bound; and he is there in the round-house.
texts.gen.39.21: And Jehovah is with Joseph, and stretcheth out kindness unto him, and putteth his grace in the eyes of the chief of the round-house;
texts.gen.39.22: and the chief of the round-house giveth into the hand of Joseph all the prisoners who [are] in the round-house, and of all that they are doing there, he hath been doer;
texts.gen.39.23: the chief of the round-house seeth not anything under his hand, because Jehovah [is] with him, and that which he is doing Jehovah is causing to prosper.
texts.gen.40.1: And it cometh to pass, after these things -- the butler of the king of Egypt and the baker have sinned against their lord, against the king of Egypt;
texts.gen.40.2: and Pharaoh is wroth against his two eunuchs, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers,
texts.gen.40.3: and giveth them in charge in the house of the chief of the executioners, unto the round-house, the place where Joseph [is] a prisoner,
texts.gen.40.4: and the chief of the executioners chargeth Joseph with them, and he serveth them; and they are days in charge.
texts.gen.40.5: And they dream a dream both of them, each his dream in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker whom the king of Egypt hath, who [are] prisoners in the round-house.
texts.gen.40.6: And Joseph cometh in unto them in the morning, and seeth them, and lo, they [are] morose;
texts.gen.40.7: and he asketh Pharaoh's eunuchs who [are] with him in charge in the house of his lord, saying, `Wherefore [are] your faces sad to-day?'
texts.gen.40.8: And they say unto him, `A dream we have dreamed, and there is no interpreter of it;' and Joseph saith unto them, `Are not interpretations with God? recount, I pray you, to me.'
texts.gen.40.9: And the chief of the butlers recounteth his dream to Joseph, and saith to him, `In my dream, then lo, a vine [is] before me!
texts.gen.40.10: and in the vine [are] three branches, and it [is] as it were flourishing; gone up hath its blossom, its clusters have ripened grapes;
texts.gen.40.11: and Pharaoh's cup [is] in my hand, and I take the grapes and press them into the cup of Pharaoh, and I give the cup into the hand of Pharaoh.'
texts.gen.40.12: And Joseph saith to him, `This [is] its interpretation: the three branches are three days;
texts.gen.40.13: yet, within three days doth Pharaoh lift up thy head, and hath put thee back on thy station, and thou hast given the cup of Pharaoh into his hand, according to the former custom when thou wast his butler.
texts.gen.40.14: `Surely if thou hast remembered me with thee, when it is well with thee, and hast done (I pray thee) kindness with me, and hast made mention of me unto Pharaoh, then hast thou brought me out from this house,
texts.gen.40.15: for I was really stolen from the land of the Hebrews; and here also have I done nothing that they have put me in the pit.'
texts.gen.40.16: And the chief of the bakers seeth that he hath interpreted good, and he saith unto Joseph, `I also [am] in a dream, and lo, three baskets of white bread [are] on my head,
texts.gen.40.17: and in the uppermost basket [are] of all [kinds] of Pharaoh's food, work of a baker; and the birds are eating them out of the basket, from off my head.'
texts.gen.40.18: And Joseph answereth and saith, `This [is] its interpretation: the three baskets are three days;
texts.gen.40.19: yet, within three days doth Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and hath hanged thee on a tree, and the birds have eaten thy flesh from off thee.'
texts.gen.40.20: And it cometh to pass, on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, that he maketh a banquet to all his servants, and lifteth up the head of the chief of the butlers, and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants,
texts.gen.40.21: and he putteth back the chief of the butlers to his butlership, and he giveth the cup into the hand of Pharaoh;
texts.gen.40.22: and the chief of the bakers he hath hanged, as Joseph hath interpreted to them;
texts.gen.40.23: and the chief of the butlers hath not remembered Joseph, but forgetteth him.
texts.gen.41.1: And it cometh to pass, at the end of two years of days that Pharaoh is dreaming, and lo, he is standing by the River,
texts.gen.41.2: and lo, from the River coming up are seven kine, of fair appearance, and fat [in] flesh, and they feed among the reeds;
texts.gen.41.3: and lo, seven other kine are coming up after them out of the River, of bad appearance, and lean [in] flesh, and they stand near the kine on the edge of the River,
texts.gen.41.4: and the kine of bad appearance and lean [in] flesh eat up the seven kine of fair appearance, and fat -- and Pharaoh awaketh.
texts.gen.41.5: And he sleepeth, and dreameth a second time, and lo, seven ears are coming up on one stalk, fat and good,
texts.gen.41.6: and lo, seven ears, thin, and blasted with an east wind, are springing up after them;
texts.gen.41.7: and the thin ears swallow the seven fat and full ears -- and Pharaoh awaketh, and lo, a dream.
texts.gen.41.8: And it cometh to pass in the morning, that his spirit is moved, and he sendeth and calleth all the scribes of Egypt, and all its wise men, and Pharaoh recounteth to them his dream, and there is no interpreter of them to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.9: And the chief of the butlers speaketh with Pharaoh, saying, `My sin I mention this day:
texts.gen.41.10: Pharaoh hath been wroth against his servants, and giveth me into charge in the house of the chief of the executioners, me and the chief of the bakers;
texts.gen.41.11: and we dream a dream in one night, I and he, each according to the interpretation of his dream we have dreamed.
texts.gen.41.12: And there [is] with us a youth, a Hebrew, servant to the chief of the executioners, and we recount to him, and he interpreteth to us our dreams, [to] each according to his dream hath he interpreted,
texts.gen.41.13: and it cometh to pass, as he hath interpreted to us so it hath been, me he put back on my station, and him he hanged.'
texts.gen.41.14: And Pharaoh sendeth and calleth Joseph, and they cause him to run out of the pit, and he shaveth, and changeth his garments, and cometh in unto Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.15: And Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, `A dream I have dreamed, and there is no interpreter of it, and I -- I have heard concerning thee, saying, Thou understandest a dream to interpret it,'
texts.gen.41.16: and Joseph answereth Pharaoh, saying, `Without me -- God doth answer Pharaoh with peace.'
texts.gen.41.17: And Pharaoh speaketh unto Joseph: `In my dream, lo, I am standing by the edge of the River,
texts.gen.41.18: and lo, out of the River coming up are seven kine, fat [in] flesh, and of fair form, and they feed among the reeds;
texts.gen.41.19: and lo, seven other kine are coming up after them, thin, and of very bad form, and lean [in] flesh; I have not seen like these in all the land of Egypt for badness.
texts.gen.41.20: `And the lean and the bad kine eat up the first seven fat kine,
texts.gen.41.21: and they come in unto their midst, and it hath not been known that they have come in unto their midst, and their appearance [is] bad as at the commencement; and I awake.
texts.gen.41.22: `And I see in my dream, and lo, seven ears are coming up on one stalk, full and good;
texts.gen.41.23: and lo, seven ears, withered, thin, blasted with an east wind, are springing up after them;
texts.gen.41.24: and the thin ears swallow the seven good ears; and I tell unto the scribes, and there is none declaring to me.'
texts.gen.41.25: And Joseph saith unto Pharaoh, `The dream of Pharaoh is one: that which God is doing he hath declared to Pharaoh;
texts.gen.41.26: the seven good kine are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years, the dream is one;
texts.gen.41.27: and the seven thin and bad kine which are coming up after them are seven years, and the seven empty ears, blasted with an east wind, are seven years of famine;
texts.gen.41.28: this [is] the thing which I have spoken unto Pharaoh: That which God is doing, he hath shewn Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.29: `Lo, seven years are coming of great abundance in all the land of Egypt,
texts.gen.41.30: and seven years of famine have arisen after them, and all the plenty is forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine hath finished the land,
texts.gen.41.31: and the plenty is not known in the land because of that famine afterwards, for it [is] very grievous.
texts.gen.41.32: `And because of the repeating of the dream unto Pharaoh twice, surely the thing is established by God, and God is hastening to do it.
texts.gen.41.33: `And now, let Pharaoh provide a man, intelligent and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt;
texts.gen.41.34: let Pharaoh make and appoint overseers over the land, and receive a fifth of the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty,
texts.gen.41.35: and they gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and heap up corn under the hand of Pharaoh -- food in the cities; and they have kept [it],
texts.gen.41.36: and the food hath been for a store for the land, for the seven years of famine which are in the land of Egypt; and the land is cut off by the famine.'
texts.gen.41.37: And the thing is good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants,
texts.gen.41.38: and Pharaoh saith unto his servants, `Do we find like this, a man in whom the spirit of God [is]?'
texts.gen.41.39: and Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, `After God's causing thee to know all this, there is none intelligent and wise as thou;
texts.gen.41.40: thou -- thou art over my house, and at thy mouth do all my people kiss; only in the throne I am greater than thou.'
texts.gen.41.41: And Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, `See, I have put thee over all the land of Egypt.'
texts.gen.41.42: And Pharaoh turneth aside his seal-ring from off his hand, and putteth it on the hand of Joseph, and clotheth him [with] garments of fine linen, and placeth a chain of gold on his neck,
texts.gen.41.43: and causeth him to ride in the second chariot which he hath, and they proclaim before him, `Bow the knee!' and -- to put him over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.44: And Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, `I [am] Pharaoh, and without thee a man doth not lift up his hand and his foot in all the land of Egypt;'
texts.gen.41.45: and Pharaoh calleth Joseph's name Zaphnath-Paaneah, and he giveth to him Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, for a wife, and Joseph goeth out over the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.46: And Joseph [is] a son of thirty years in his standing before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and Joseph goeth out from the presence of Pharaoh, and passeth over through all the land of Egypt;
texts.gen.41.47: and the land maketh in the seven years of plenty by handfuls.
texts.gen.41.48: And he gathereth all the food of the seven years which have been in the land of Egypt, and putteth food in the cities; the food of the field which [is] round about [each] city hath he put in its midst;
texts.gen.41.49: and Joseph gathereth corn as sand of the sea, multiplying exceedingly, until that he hath ceased to number, for there is no number.
texts.gen.41.50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine cometh, whom Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, hath borne to him,
texts.gen.41.51: and Joseph calleth the name of the first-born Manasseh: `for, God hath made me to forget all my labour, and all the house of my father;'
texts.gen.41.52: and the name of the second he hath called Ephraim: `for, God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of mine affliction.'
texts.gen.41.53: And the seven years of plenty are completed which have been in the land of Egypt,
texts.gen.41.54: and the seven years of famine begin to come, as Joseph said, and famine is in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt hath been bread;
texts.gen.41.55: and all the land of Egypt is famished, and the people crieth unto Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh saith to all the Egyptians, `Go unto Joseph; that which he saith to you -- do.'
texts.gen.41.56: And the famine has been over all the face of the land, and Joseph openeth all [places] which have [corn] in them, and selleth to the Egyptians; and the famine is severe in the land of Egypt,
texts.gen.41.57: and all the earth hath come to Egypt, to buy, unto Joseph, for the famine was severe in all the earth.
texts.gen.42.1: And Jacob seeth that there is corn in Egypt, and Jacob saith to his sons, `Why do you look at each other?'
texts.gen.42.2: he saith also, `Lo, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt, go down thither, and buy for us from thence, and we live and do not die;'
texts.gen.42.3: and the ten brethren of Joseph go down to buy corn in Egypt,
texts.gen.42.4: and Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob hath not sent with his brethren, for he said, `Lest mischief meet him.'
texts.gen.42.5: And the sons of Israel come to buy in the midst of those coming, for the famine hath been in the land of Canaan,
texts.gen.42.6: and Joseph is the ruler over the land, he who is selling to all the people of the land, and Joseph's brethren come and bow themselves to him -- face to the earth.
texts.gen.42.7: And Joseph seeth his brethren, and discerneth them, and maketh himself strange unto them, and speaketh with them sharp things, and saith unto them, `From whence have ye come?' and they say, `From the land of Canaan -- to buy food.'
texts.gen.42.8: And Joseph discerneth his brethren, but they have not discerned him,
texts.gen.42.9: and Joseph remembereth the dreams which he dreamed of them, and saith unto them, `Ye [are] spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye have come.'
texts.gen.42.10: And they say unto him, `No, my lord, but thy servants have come to buy food;
texts.gen.42.11: we [are] all of us sons of one man, we [are] right men; thy servants have not been spies;'
texts.gen.42.12: and he saith unto them, `No, but the nakedness of the land ye have come to see;'
texts.gen.42.13: and they say, `Thy servants [are] twelve brethren; we [are] sons of one man in the land of Canaan, and lo, the young one [is] with our father to-day, and the one is not.'
texts.gen.42.14: And Joseph saith unto them, `This [is] that which I have spoken unto you, saying, Ye [are] spies,
texts.gen.42.15: by this ye are proved: Pharaoh liveth! if ye go out from this -- except by your young brother coming hither;
texts.gen.42.16: send one of you, and let him bring your brother, and ye, remain ye bound, and let your words be proved, whether truth be with you: and if not -- Pharaoh liveth! surely ye [are] spies;'
texts.gen.42.17: and he removeth them unto charge three days.
texts.gen.42.18: And Joseph saith unto them on the third day, `This do and live; God I fear!
texts.gen.42.19: if ye [are] right men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your ward, and ye, go, carry in corn [for] the famine of your houses,
texts.gen.42.20: and your young brother ye bring unto me, and your words are established, and ye die not;' and they do so.
texts.gen.42.21: And they say one unto another, `Verily we [are] guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul, in his making supplication unto us, and we did not hearken: therefore hath this distress come upon us.'
texts.gen.42.22: And Reuben answereth them, saying, `Spake I not unto you, saying, Sin not against the lad? and ye hearkened not; and his blood also, lo, it is required.'
texts.gen.42.23: And they have not known that Joseph understandeth, for the interpreter [is] between them;
texts.gen.42.24: and he turneth round from them, and weepeth, and turneth back unto them, and speaketh unto them, and taketh from them Simeon, and bindeth him before their eyes.
texts.gen.42.25: And Joseph commandeth, and they fill their vessels [with] corn, also to put back the money of each unto his sack, and to give to them provision for the way; and one doth to them so.
texts.gen.42.26: And they lift up their corn upon their asses, and go from thence,
texts.gen.42.27: and the one openeth his sack to give provender to his ass at a lodging-place, and he seeth his money, and lo, it [is] in the mouth of his bag,
texts.gen.42.28: and he saith unto his brethren, `My money hath been put back, and also, lo, in my bag:' and their heart goeth out, and they tremble, one to another saying, `What [is] this God hath done to us!'
texts.gen.42.29: And they come in unto Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and they declare to him all the things meeting them, saying,
texts.gen.42.30: `The man, the lord of the land, hath spoken with us sharp things, and maketh us as spies of the land;
texts.gen.42.31: and we say unto him, We [are] right men, we have not been spies,
texts.gen.42.32: we [are] twelve brethren, sons of our father, the one is not, and the young one [is] to-day with our father in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.33: `And the man, the lord of the land, saith unto us, By this I know that ye [are] right men -- one of your brethren leave with me, and [for] the famine of your houses take ye and go,
texts.gen.42.34: and bring your young brother unto me, and I know that ye [are] not spies, but ye [are] right men; your brother I give to you, and ye trade with the land.'
texts.gen.42.35: And it cometh to pass, they are emptying their sacks, and lo, the bundle of each man's silver [is] in his sack, and they see their bundles of silver, they and their father, and are afraid;
texts.gen.42.36: and Jacob their father saith unto them, `Me ye have bereaved; Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin ye take -- against me have been all these.'
texts.gen.42.37: And Reuben speaketh unto his father, saying, `My two sons thou dost put to death, if I bring him not in unto thee; give him into my hand, and I -- I bring him back unto thee;'
texts.gen.42.38: and he saith, `My son doth not go down with you, for his brother [is] dead, and he by himself is left; when mischief hath met him in the way in which ye go, then ye have brought down my grey hairs in sorrow to sheol.'
texts.gen.43.1: And the famine [is] severe in the land;
texts.gen.43.2: and it cometh to pass, when they have finished eating the corn which they brought from Egypt, that their father saith unto them, `Turn back, buy for us a little food.'
texts.gen.43.3: And Judah speaketh unto him, saying, `The man protesting protested to us, saying, Ye do not see my face without your brother [being] with you;
texts.gen.43.4: if thou art sending our brother with us, we go down, and buy for thee food,
texts.gen.43.5: and if thou art not sending -- we do not go down, for the man said unto us, Ye do not see my face without your brother [being] with you.'
texts.gen.43.6: And Israel saith, `Why did ye evil to me, by declaring to the man that ye had yet a brother?'
texts.gen.43.7: and they say, `The man asked diligently concerning us, and concerning our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye a brother? and we declare to him according to the tenor of these things; do we certainly know that he will say, Bring down your brother?'
texts.gen.43.8: And Judah saith unto Israel his father, `Send the youth with me, and we arise, and go, and live, and do not die, both we, and thou, and our infants.
texts.gen.43.9: I -- I am surety [for] him, from my hand thou dost require him; if I have not brought him in unto thee, and set him before thee -- then I have sinned against thee all the days;
texts.gen.43.10: for if we had not lingered, surely now we had returned these two times.'
texts.gen.43.11: And Israel their father saith unto them, `If so, now, this do: take of the praised thing of the land in your vessels, and take down to the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts and almonds;
texts.gen.43.12: and double money take in your hand, even the money which is brought back in the mouth of your bags, ye take back in your hand, it may be it [is] an oversight.
texts.gen.43.13: `And take your brother, and rise, turn back unto the man;
texts.gen.43.14: and God Almighty give to you mercies before the man, so that he hath sent to you your other brother and Benjamin; and I, when I am bereaved -- I am bereaved.'
texts.gen.43.15: And the men take this present, double money also they have taken in their hand, and Benjamin; and they rise, and go down to Egypt, and stand before Joseph;
texts.gen.43.16: and Joseph seeth Benjamin with them, and saith to him who [is] over his house, `Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal, and make ready, for with me do the men eat at noon.'
texts.gen.43.17: And the man doth as Joseph hath said, and the man bringeth in the men into the house of Joseph,
texts.gen.43.18: and the men are afraid because they have been brought into the house of Joseph, and they say, `For the matter of the money which was put back in our bags at the commencement are we brought in -- to roll himself upon us, and to throw himself on us, and to take us for servants -- our asses also.'
texts.gen.43.19: And they come nigh unto the man who [is] over the house of Joseph, and speak unto him at the opening of the house,
texts.gen.43.20: and say, `O, my lord, we really come down at the commencement to buy food;
texts.gen.43.21: and it cometh to pass, when we have come in unto the lodging-place, and open our bags, that lo, each one's money [is] in the mouth of his bag, our money in its weight, and we bring it back in our hand;
texts.gen.43.22: and other money have we brought down in our hand to buy food; we have not known who put our money in our bags.'
texts.gen.43.23: And he saith, `Peace to you, fear not: your God and the God of your father hath given to you hidden treasure in your bags, your money came unto me;' and he bringeth out Simeon unto them.
texts.gen.43.24: And the man bringeth in the men into Joseph's house, and giveth water, and they wash their feet; and he giveth provender for their asses,
texts.gen.43.25: and they prepare the present until the coming of Joseph at noon, for they have heard that there they do eat bread.
texts.gen.43.26: And Joseph cometh into the house, and they bring to him the present which [is] in their hand, into the house, and bow themselves to him, to the earth;
texts.gen.43.27: and he asketh of them of peace, and saith, `Is your father well? the aged man of whom ye have spoken, is he yet alive?'
texts.gen.43.28: and they say, `Thy servant our father [is] well, he is yet alive;' and they bow, and do obeisance.
texts.gen.43.29: And he lifteth up his eyes, and seeth Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and saith, `Is this your young brother, of whom ye have spoken unto me?' and he saith, `God favour thee, my son.'
texts.gen.43.30: And Joseph hasteth, for his bowels have been moved for his brother, and he seeketh to weep, and entereth the inner chamber, and weepeth there;
texts.gen.43.31: and he washeth his face, and goeth out, and refraineth himself, and saith, `Place bread.'
texts.gen.43.32: And they place for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who are eating with him by themselves: for the Egyptians are unable to eat bread with the Hebrews, for it [is] an abomination to the Egyptians.
texts.gen.43.33: And they sit before him, the first-born according to his birthright, and the young one according to his youth, and the men wonder one at another;
texts.gen.43.34: and he lifteth up gifts from before him unto them, and the gift of Benjamin is five hands more than the gifts of all of them; and they drink, yea, they drink abundantly with him.
texts.gen.44.1: And he commandeth him who [is] over his house, saying, `Fill the bags of the men [with] food, as they are able to bear, and put the money of each in the mouth of his bag;
texts.gen.44.2: and my cup, the silver cup, thou dost put in the mouth of the bag of the young one, and his corn-money;' and he doth according to the word of Joseph which he hath spoken.
texts.gen.44.3: The morning is bright, and the men have been sent away, they and their asses --
texts.gen.44.4: they have gone out of the city -- they have not gone far off -- and Joseph hath said to him who [is] over his house, `Rise, pursue after the men; and thou hast overtaken them, and thou hast said unto them, Why have ye recompensed evil for good?
texts.gen.44.5: Is not this that with which my lord drinketh? and he observeth diligently with it; ye have done evil [in] that which ye have done.'
texts.gen.44.6: And he overtaketh them, and speaketh unto them these words,
texts.gen.44.7: and they say unto him, `Why doth my lord speak according to these words? far be it from thy servants to do according to this word;
texts.gen.44.8: lo, the money which we found in the mouth of our bags we brought back unto thee from the land of Canaan, and how do we steal from the house of thy lord silver or gold?
texts.gen.44.9: with whomsoever of thy servants it is found, he hath died, and we also are to my lord for servants.'
texts.gen.44.10: And he saith, `Now, also, according to your words, so it [is]; he with whom it is found becometh my servant, and ye are acquitted;'
texts.gen.44.11: and they hasten and take down each his bag to the earth, and each openeth his bag;
texts.gen.44.12: and he searcheth -- at the eldest he hath begun, and at the youngest he hath completed -- and the cup is found in the bag of Benjamin;
texts.gen.44.13: and they rend their garments, and each ladeth his ass, and they turn back to the city.
texts.gen.44.14: And Judah -- his brethren also -- cometh in unto the house of Joseph, and he is yet there, and they fall before him to the earth;
texts.gen.44.15: and Joseph saith to them, `What [is] this deed that ye have done? have ye not known that a man like me doth diligently observe?'
texts.gen.44.16: And Judah saith, `What do we say to my lord? what do we speak? and what -- do we justify ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants; lo, we [are] servants to my lord, both we, and he in whose hand the cup hath been found;'
texts.gen.44.17: and he saith, `Far be it from me to do this; the man in whose hand the cup hath been found, he becometh my servant; and ye, go ye up in peace unto your father.'
texts.gen.44.18: And Judah cometh nigh unto him, and saith, `O, my lord, let thy servant speak, I pray thee, a word in the ears of my lord, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant -- for thou art as Pharaoh.
texts.gen.44.19: My lord hath asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father or brother?
texts.gen.44.20: and we say unto my lord, We have a father, an aged one, and a child of old age, a little one; and his brother died, and he is left alone of his mother, and his father hath loved him.
texts.gen.44.21: `And thou sayest unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me, and I set mine eye upon him;
texts.gen.44.22: and we say unto my lord, The youth is not able to leave his father, when he hath left his father, then he hath died;
texts.gen.44.23: and thou sayest unto thy servants, If your young brother come not down with you, ye add not to see my face.
texts.gen.44.24: `And it cometh to pass, that we have come up unto thy servant my father, that we declare to him the words of my lord;
texts.gen.44.25: and our father saith, Turn back, buy for us a little food,
texts.gen.44.26: and we say, We are not able to go down; if our young brother is with us, then we have gone down; for we are not able to see the man's face, and our young brother not with us.
texts.gen.44.27: `And thy servant my father saith unto us, Ye -- ye have known that two did my wife bare to me,
texts.gen.44.28: and the one goeth out from me, and I say, Surely he is torn -- torn! and I have not seen him since;
texts.gen.44.29: when ye have taken also this from my presence, and mischief hath met him, then ye have brought down my grey hairs with evil to sheol.
texts.gen.44.30: `And now, at my coming in unto thy servant my father, and the youth not with us (and his soul is bound up in his soul),
texts.gen.44.31: then it hath come to pass when he seeth that the youth is not, that he hath died, and thy servants have brought down the grey hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to sheol;
texts.gen.44.32: for thy servant obtained the youth by surety from my father, saying, If I bring him not in unto thee -- then I have sinned against my father all the days.
texts.gen.44.33: `And now, let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the youth a servant to my lord, and the youth goeth up with his brethren,
texts.gen.44.34: for how do I go up unto my father, and the youth not with me? lest I look on the evil which doth find my father.'
texts.gen.45.1: And Joseph hath not been able to refrain himself before all those standing by him, and he calleth, `Put out every man from me;' and no man hath stood with him when Joseph maketh himself known unto his brethren,
texts.gen.45.2: and he giveth forth his voice in weeping, and the Egyptians hear, and the house of Pharaoh heareth.
texts.gen.45.3: And Joseph saith unto his brethren, `I [am] Joseph, is my father yet alive?' and his brethren have not been able to answer him, for they have been troubled at his presence.
texts.gen.45.4: And Joseph saith unto his brethren, `Come nigh unto me, I pray you,' and they come nigh; and he saith, `I [am] Joseph, your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt;
texts.gen.45.5: and now, be not grieved, nor let it be displeasing in your eyes that ye sold me hither, for to preserve life hath God sent me before you.
texts.gen.45.6: `Because these two years the famine [is] in the heart of the land, and yet [are] five years, [in] which there is neither ploughing nor harvest;
texts.gen.45.7: and God sendeth me before you, to place of you a remnant in the land, and to give life to you by a great escape;
texts.gen.45.8: and now, ye -- ye have not sent me hither, but God, and He doth set me for a father to Pharaoh, and for lord to all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.45.9: `Haste, and go up unto my father, then ye have said to him, Thus said Joseph thy son, God hath set me for lord to all Egypt; come down unto me, stay not,
texts.gen.45.10: and thou hast dwelt in the land of Goshen, and been near unto me, thou and thy sons, and thy son's sons, and thy flock, and thy herd, and all that thou hast,
texts.gen.45.11: and I have nourished thee there -- for yet [are] five years of famine -- lest thou become poor, thou and thy household, and all that thou hast.
texts.gen.45.12: `And lo, your eyes are seeing, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that [it is] my mouth which is speaking unto you;
texts.gen.45.13: and ye have declared to my father all my honour in Egypt, and all that ye have seen, and ye have hasted, and have brought down my father hither.'
texts.gen.45.14: And he falleth on the neck of Benjamin his brother, and weepeth, and Benjamin hath wept on his neck;
texts.gen.45.15: and he kisseth all his brethren, and weepeth over them; and afterwards have his brethren spoken with him.
texts.gen.45.16: And the sound hath been heard in the house of Pharaoh, saying, `Come have the brethren of Joseph;' and it is good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants,
texts.gen.45.17: and Pharaoh saith unto Joseph, `Say unto thy brethren, This do ye: lade your beasts, and go, enter ye the land of Canaan,
texts.gen.45.18: and take your father, and your households, and come unto me, and I give to you the good of the land of Egypt, and eat ye the fat of the land.
texts.gen.45.19: `Yea, thou -- thou hast been commanded: this do ye, take for yourselves out of the land of Egypt, waggons for your infants, and for your wives, and ye have brought your father, and come;
texts.gen.45.20: and your eye hath no pity on your vessels, for the good of all the land of Egypt [is] yours.'
texts.gen.45.21: And the sons of Israel do so, and Joseph giveth waggons to them by the command of Pharaoh, and he giveth to them provision for the way;
texts.gen.45.22: to all of them hath he given -- to each changes of garments, and to Benjamin he hath given three hundred silverlings, and five changes of garments;
texts.gen.45.23: and to his father he hath sent thus: ten asses bearing of the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses bearing corn and bread, even food for his father for the way.
texts.gen.45.24: And he sendeth his brethren away, and they go; and he saith unto them, `Be not angry in the way.'
texts.gen.45.25: And they go up out of Egypt, and come in to the land of Canaan, unto Jacob their father,
texts.gen.45.26: and they declare to him, saying, `Joseph [is] yet alive,' and that he [is] ruler over all the land of Egypt; and his heart ceaseth, for he hath not given credence to them.
texts.gen.45.27: And they speak unto him all the words of Joseph, which he hath spoken unto them, and he seeth the waggons which Joseph hath sent to bear him away, and live doth the spirit of Jacob their father;
texts.gen.45.28: and Israel saith, `Enough! Joseph my son [is] yet alive; I go and see him before I die.'
texts.gen.46.1: And Israel journeyeth, and all that he hath, and cometh in to Beer-Sheba, and sacrificeth sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac;
texts.gen.46.2: and God speaketh to Israel in visions of the night, and saith, `Jacob, Jacob;' and he saith, `Here [am] I.'
texts.gen.46.3: And He saith, `I [am] God, God of thy father, be not afraid of going down to Egypt, for for a great nation I set thee there;
texts.gen.46.4: I -- I go down with thee to Egypt, and I -- I also certainly bring thee up, and Joseph doth put his hand on thine eyes.'
texts.gen.46.5: And Jacob riseth from Beer-Sheba, and the sons of Israel bear away Jacob their father, And their infants, and their wives, in the waggons which Pharaoh hath sent to bear him,
texts.gen.46.6: and they take their cattle, and their goods which they have acquired in the land of Canaan, and come into Egypt -- Jacob, and all his seed with him,
texts.gen.46.7: his sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, yea, all his seed he brought with him into Egypt.
texts.gen.46.8: And these [are] the names of the sons of Israel who are coming into Egypt: Jacob and his sons, Jacob's first-born, Reuben.
texts.gen.46.9: And sons of Reuben: Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
texts.gen.46.10: And sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul son of the Canaanitess.
texts.gen.46.11: And sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
texts.gen.46.12: And sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zarah, (and Er and Onan die in the land of Canaan.) And sons of Pharez are Hezron and Hamul.
texts.gen.46.13: And sons of Issachar: Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
texts.gen.46.14: And sons of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
texts.gen.46.15: These [are] sons of Leah whom she bare to Jacob in Padan-Aram, and Dinah his daughter; all the persons of his sons and his daughters [are] thirty and three.
texts.gen.46.16: And sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
texts.gen.46.17: And sons of Asher: Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
texts.gen.46.18: These [are] sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and she beareth these to Jacob -- sixteen persons.
texts.gen.46.19: Sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
texts.gen.46.20: And born to Joseph in the land of Egypt (whom Asenath daughter of Poti-Pherah, priest of On, hath borne to him) [are] Manasseh and Ephraim.
texts.gen.46.21: And sons of Benjamin: Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
texts.gen.46.22: These [are] sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob; all the persons [are] fourteen.
texts.gen.46.24: And sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
texts.gen.46.25: These [are] sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; and she beareth these to Jacob -- all the persons [are] seven.
texts.gen.46.26: All the persons who are coming to Jacob to Egypt, coming out of his thigh, apart from the wives of Jacob's sons, all the persons [are] sixty and six.
texts.gen.46.27: And the sons of Joseph who have been born to him in Egypt [are] two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who are coming into Egypt [are] seventy.
texts.gen.46.28: And Judah he hath sent before him unto Joseph, to direct before him to Goshen, and they come into the land of Goshen;
texts.gen.46.29: and Joseph harnesseth his chariot, and goeth up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and appeareth unto him, and falleth on his neck, and weepeth on his neck again;
texts.gen.46.30: and Israel saith unto Joseph, `Let me die this time, after my seeing thy face, for thou [art] yet alive.'
texts.gen.46.31: And Joseph saith unto his brethren, and unto the house of his father, `I go up, and declare to Pharaoh, and say unto him, My brethren, and the house of my father who [are] in the land of Canaan have come in unto me;
texts.gen.46.32: and the men [are] feeders of a flock, for they have been men of cattle; and their flock, and their herd, and all that they have, they have brought.'
texts.gen.46.33: `And it hath come to pass when Pharaoh calleth for you, and hath said, What [are] your works?
texts.gen.46.34: that ye have said, Thy servants have been men of cattle from our youth, even until now, both we and our fathers, -- in order that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen, for the abomination of the Egyptians is every one feeding a flock.'
texts.gen.47.1: And Joseph cometh, and declareth to Pharaoh, and saith, `My father, and my brethren, and their flock, and their herd, and all they have, have come from the land of Canaan, and lo, they [are] in the land of Goshen.'
texts.gen.47.2: And out of his brethren he hath taken five men, and setteth them before Pharaoh;
texts.gen.47.3: and Pharaoh saith unto his brethren, `What [are] your works?' and they say unto Pharaoh, `Thy servants [are] feeders of a flock, both we and our fathers;'
texts.gen.47.4: and they say unto Pharaoh, `To sojourn in the land we have come, for there is no pasture for the flock which thy servants have, for grievous [is] the famine in the land of Canaan; and now, let thy servants, we pray thee, dwell in the land of Goshen.'
texts.gen.47.5: And Pharaoh speaketh unto Joseph, saying, `Thy father and thy brethren have come unto thee:
texts.gen.47.6: the land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land cause thy father and thy brethren to dwell -- they dwell in the land of Goshen, and if thou hast known, and there are among them men of ability, then thou hast set them heads over the cattle I have.'
texts.gen.47.7: And Joseph bringeth in Jacob his father, and causeth him to stand before Pharaoh; and Jacob blesseth Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.8: And Pharaoh saith unto Jacob, `How many [are] the days of the years of thy life?'
texts.gen.47.9: And Jacob saith unto Pharaoh, `The days of the years of my sojournings [are] an hundred and thirty years; few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, in the days of their sojournings.'
texts.gen.47.10: And Jacob blesseth Pharaoh, and goeth out from before Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.11: And Joseph settleth his father and his brethren, and giveth to them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh commanded;
texts.gen.47.12: and Joseph nourisheth his father, and his brethren, and all the house of his father [with] bread, according to the mouth of the infants.
texts.gen.47.13: And there is no bread in all the land, for the famine [is] very grievous, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan are feeble because of the famine;
texts.gen.47.14: and Joseph gathereth all the silver that is found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn that they are buying, and Joseph bringeth the silver into the house of Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.15: And the silver is consumed out of the land of Egypt, and out of the land of Canaan, and all the Egyptians come in unto Joseph, saying, `Give to us bread -- why do we die before thee, though the money hath ceased?'
texts.gen.47.16: and Joseph saith, `Give your cattle; and I give to you for your cattle, if the money hath ceased.'
texts.gen.47.17: And they bring in their cattle unto Joseph, and Joseph giveth to them bread, for the horses, and for the cattle of the flock, and for the cattle of the herd, and for the asses; and he tendeth them with bread, for all their cattle, during that year.
texts.gen.47.18: And that year is finished, and they come in unto him on the second year, and say to him, `We do not hide from my lord, that since the money hath been finished, and possession of the cattle [is] unto my lord, there hath not been left before my lord save our bodies, and our ground;
texts.gen.47.19: why do we die before thine eyes, both we and our ground? buy us and our ground for bread, and we and our ground are servants to Pharaoh; and give seed, and we live, and die not, and the ground is not desolate.'
texts.gen.47.20: And Joseph buyeth all the ground of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians have sold each his field, for the famine hath been severe upon them, and the land becometh Pharaoh's;
texts.gen.47.21: as to the people he hath removed them to cities from the [one] end of the border of Egypt even unto its [other] end.
texts.gen.47.22: Only the ground of the priests he hath not bought, for the priests have a portion from Pharaoh, and they have eaten their portion which Pharaoh hath given to them, therefore they have not sold their ground.
texts.gen.47.23: And Joseph saith unto the people, `Lo, I have bought you to-day and your ground for Pharaoh; lo, seed for you, and ye have sown the ground,
texts.gen.47.24: and it hath come to pass in the increases, that ye have given a fifth to Pharaoh, and four of the parts are for yourselves, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for those who [are] in your houses, and for food for your infants.'
texts.gen.47.25: And they say, `Thou hast revived us; we find grace in the eyes of my lord, and have been servants to Pharaoh;'
texts.gen.47.26: and Joseph setteth it for a statute unto this day, concerning the ground of Egypt, [that] Pharaoh hath a fifth; only the ground of the priests alone hath not become Pharaoh's.
texts.gen.47.27: And Israel dwelleth in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, and they have possession in it, and are fruitful, and multiply exceedingly;
texts.gen.47.28: and Jacob liveth in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, are an hundred and forty and seven years.
texts.gen.47.29: And the days of Israel are near to die, and he calleth for his son, for Joseph, and saith to him, `If, I pray thee, I have found grace in thine eyes, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and thou hast done with me kindness and truth; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt,
