texts.gen.6.19: Moreover of all the living creatures of all flesh—two of each, shalt thou bring into the ark to keep alive with thee,—male and female, shall they be.
texts.gen.6.20: Of the bird after its kind and of the beast after its kind, [and] of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of each, shall come in unto thee. for keeping alive.
texts.gen.6.21: But thou, take to thee of all food that is eaten, and gather it unto thee,—and it shall be for thee and for them for food.
texts.gen.6.22: And Noah did [so],—according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
texts.gen.7.1: And Yahweh said to Noah, Enter thou and all thy house, into the ark,—for, thee, have I seen righteous before me, in this generation.
texts.gen.7.2: Of all the clean beasts, shalt thou take to thee by sevens, a male and his female,—and, of the beasts that are not clean, shall be two a male and his female.
texts.gen.7.3: Also of the bird of the heavens, by sevens, male and female,—to keep alive a seed on the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.7.4: For in seven days more, I, am sending rain on the earth, forty days and forty nights,—so will I wipe out all the living things which I have made, from off the face of the ground.
texts.gen.7.5: And Noah did,—according to all that Yahweh commanded him.
texts.gen.7.6: Now, Noah, was six hundred years old,—when, the flood, came, even waters on the earth.
texts.gen.7.7: So Noah entered, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him into the ark,—from before the waters of the flood,
texts.gen.7.8: Of the beasts that were clean, and of the beasts that were not clean,—and of the birds, and everything that creepeth on the ground,
texts.gen.7.9: two and two, went they in unto Noah, into the ark male and female,—as God commanded Noah.
texts.gen.7.10: And it came to pass, in the seven days,—that the waters of the flood, came on the earth.
texts.gen.7.11: In the six hundredth year, the year of the life of Noah. in the second month on the seventeenth day of the month on this day, were burst open all the fountains of the great roaring deep, and the windows of the heavens, were set open.
texts.gen.7.12: (And it came to pass that the heavy rain was on the earth,—forty days and forty nights.)
texts.gen.7.13: On this selfsame day, entered Noah, and Shem and Ham and Japheth. Noah’s sons,—and Noah’s wife, and his sons’ three wives with them into the ark:
texts.gen.7.14: they, and all the wild-beasts after their kind and all the tame-beasts after their kind, and all the creeping things that creep on the earth after their kind,—and all the birds after their kind, every bird of every wing.
texts.gen.7.15: So they entered in unto Noah, into the ark,—two and two of all flesh, wherein was the spirit of life.
texts.gen.7.16: And, they that entered, male and female of all flesh, entered, as God commanded him,—and Yahweh shut him in round about.
texts.gen.7.17: And it came to pass, that the flood was forty days on the earth,—and the waters increased and bare up the ark, and it was lifted high above the earth,
texts.gen.7.18: And the waters prevailed and increased greatly, on the earth,—and the ark went its way on the face of the waters.
texts.gen.7.19: Yea the waters, prevailed very greatly, on the earth,—so that all the high mountains became covered, that were under all the heavens:
texts.gen.7.20: fifteen cubits upwards, prevailed the waters, so that the mountains became covered.
texts.gen.7.21: And all flesh ceased to breathe that moved on the earth, of birds and of tame-beasts and of wild-beasts, and of all the swarming things that swarm on the earth,—and all mankind.
texts.gen.7.22: All in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life of all that were on the dry ground died.
texts.gen.7.23: Thus was wiped out all that existed on the face of the ground, from man unto beast unto creeping thing, and unto the bird of the heavens, thus were they wiped out from the earth,—so that there was left—only Noah and they that were with him in the ark.
texts.gen.7.24: Thus prevailed the waters on the earth,—a hundred and fifty days.
texts.gen.8.1: And God remembered Noah, and all the wild—beasts and all the tame-beasts that were with him in the ark,—and God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided;
texts.gen.8.2: and the fountains of the roaring-deep were shut, and the windows of the heavens,—and the heavy rain was restrained from the heavens;
texts.gen.8.3: and the waters returned from off the earth they went on returning,—and so the waters decreased at the end of a hundred and fifty days.
texts.gen.8.4: And the ark rested, in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month,—on the mountains of Ararat.
texts.gen.8.5: But, the waters went on decreasing, until the tenth month,—in the tenth [month], on the first of the month, were seen the tops of the mountains.
texts.gen.8.6: And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made;
texts.gen.8.7: and sent forth a raven,—and it kept going forth and returning, until the drying up of the waters from off the earth.
texts.gen.8.8: And he sent forth a dove from him,—to see whether the waters had abated, from off the face of the ground;
texts.gen.8.9: but the dove found no resting-place for the sole of her foot so she returned unto him into the ark, for, waters, were on the face of all the earth; and he put forth his hand and took her, and brought her in unto him, into the ark.
texts.gen.8.10: Then stayed he yet seven days more,—and, again sent forth the dove out of the ark.
texts.gen.8.11: And the dove came in unto him at eventide, and lo! a newly sprouted olive-leaf, in her mouth,—so Noah knew that the waters had abated from off the earth.
texts.gen.8.12: And he stayed yet seven days more,—and sent forth the dove, but she returned not again unto him any more.
texts.gen.8.13: So it came to pass in the six hundred and first year at the beginning, on the first of the month, that the waters had dried up from off the earth,—and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked and lo! the face of the ground was dried.
texts.gen.8.14: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, was the earth dry.
texts.gen.8.15: So then, God spake to Noah, saying:
texts.gen.8.16: Come forth out of the ark,—thou and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ wives with thee.
texts.gen.8.17: All the living creatures that are with thee of all flesh among birds, and among beasts, and among all the creeping things that creep on the earth, bring forth with thee,—and they shall swarm in the earth, and be fruitful and multiply, on the earth.
texts.gen.8.18: So Noah came forth,—and his sons and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him:
texts.gen.8.19: All the living creatures, all that move along, and all birds, and all that moveth along over the earth—by their families, came forth out of the ark.
texts.gen.8.20: And Noah builded an altar to Yahweh,—and took of all the clean beasts and of all the clean birds, and caused ascending Sacrifices to go up on the altar.
texts.gen.8.21: And Yahweh smelled a satisfying odour, so Yahweh said to himself. I will not, again, curse any more the ground for man’s sake, although the device of the heart of man, be wicked from his youth,—neither will I again, any more smite every living thing, as I have done.
texts.gen.8.22: During all the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat and summer and winter, and day and night, shall not cease.
texts.gen.9.1: So God blessed Noah and his sons,—and said to them Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth;
texts.gen.9.2: and let the fear of you and the dread of you be upon every living creature of the earth, and upon every bird of the heavens,—over everything that moveth along on the ground, and over all the fishes of the sea,—into your hand, have they been given.
texts.gen.9.3: As for every moving thing that hath life, yours, shall it be, for food,—Like the green herb, have I given you all things.
texts.gen.9.4: Yet flesh with the life thereof, the blood thereof, shall ye not eat;
texts.gen.9.5: And surely your blood, of your lives, will I require, From the hand of every living creature, will I require it,—and from the hand of man From the hand of each one’s brother, will I require the life of man:
texts.gen.9.6: He that sheddeth man’s blood, by man, shall his blood be shed,—For, in the image of God, made he man.
texts.gen.9.7: Ye, therefore, be fruitful and multiply, swarm in the earth and multiply therein.
texts.gen.9.8: And God spake unto Noah, and unto his sons with him saying:
texts.gen.9.9: I, therefore, behold me! establishing my covenant with you,—and with your seed after you;
texts.gen.9.10: and with every living soul that is with you, of birds, of tame-beasts and of all wild-beasts of the earth that are with you,—of all coming forth out of the ark, even to all wild-beasts of the earth;
texts.gen.9.11: yea, I will establish my covenant with you, so that all flesh shall not be cut off any more, by reason of the waters of a flood,—neither shall there be any more a flood to destroy the earth.
texts.gen.9.12: And God said, This, is the sign of the covenant which I am granting betwixt me and you, and every living soul that is with you,—to age-abiding generations:—
texts.gen.9.13: My bow, have I set in the cloud,—and it shall be for a sign of a covenant, betwixt me and the earth;
texts.gen.9.14: and it shall be when I draw a veil of cloud over the earth,—and the bow in the cloud appeareth,
texts.gen.9.15: then will I remember my covenant which is betwixt me and you, and every living soul among all flesh,—that the waters may no more become a flood, to destroy all flesh:
texts.gen.9.16: so the bow shall be in the cloud,—and I will behold it, to remember an age-abiding covenant, between God, and every living soul among all flesh that is on the earth.
texts.gen.9.17: And God said unto Noah, This is the sign of the covenant which have established, between me and all flesh that is on the earth.
texts.gen.9.18: And the sons of Noah who came forth out of the ark, were—Shem and Ham and Japheth,—now, Ham, was the father of Canaan.
texts.gen.9.19: These three, were the sons of Noah,—and from these, was all the earth overspread.
texts.gen.9.20: And Noah began to be a husbandman,—so he planted a vineyard:
texts.gen.9.21: and dank of the wine and became drunk, and uncovered himself in the midst of his tent.
texts.gen.9.22: And Ham the father of Canaan saw his father’s shame,—and told his two brethren outside.
texts.gen.9.23: And Shem and Japheth took a mantle, and put it on the shoulder of them both and went backwards, and covered the shame of their father, but their faces were backwards, and the shame of their father, saw they not.
texts.gen.9.24: And Noah awoke from his wine,—and came to know what his youngest son had done to him.
texts.gen.9.25: And he said, Accursed be Canaan,—a servant of servants, shall he be to his brethren!
texts.gen.9.26: And he said, Blessed be Yahweh, God of Shem,—And let Canaan be their servant:
texts.gen.9.27: God give extension to Japheth, But make his habitation in the tents of Shem, And let Canaan be their servant.
texts.gen.9.28: And Noah lived after the flood,—three hundred and fifty years:
texts.gen.9.29: so, all the days of Noah, were—nine hundred and fifty years,—and he died.
texts.gen.10.1: Now, these are the generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and there were born to them sons after the flood.
texts.gen.10.2: The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog, and Madai, and Javan and Tubal,—and Meshech, and Tiras.
texts.gen.10.3: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz and Riphath, and Togarmah.
texts.gen.10.4: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish. Kittim, and Rodanim,—
texts.gen.10.5: From these, were dispersed [the inhabitants] of the coastlands of the nations, in their lands, each man by his tongue, by their families in their nations.
texts.gen.10.6: And, the sons of Ham: Cush and Mizraim and Phut and Canaan.
texts.gen.10.7: And, the sons of Cush: Seba and Havilah, and Sabtah and Raamah, and Sabtechah,—And the sons of Raamah, Sheba and Dedan.
texts.gen.10.8: And, Cush begat Nimrod.—he, became a hero in the earth;
texts.gen.10.9: he, became a hero of hunting before Yahweh, for this cause, it is said. Like Nimrod, a hero of hunting before Yahweh.
texts.gen.10.10: So the beginning of his kingdom came to be Babel, and Erech, and Accad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
texts.gen.10.11: From that land, went forth Asshur,—and he built Nineveh, and Rehoboth-ir, and Calah:
texts.gen.10.12: and Resen, between Niveveh and Calah,—the same is the great city.
texts.gen.10.13: And, Mizraim, begat Ludim and Anamim and Lehabim, and Naphtuchim;
texts.gen.10.14: and Pathrusim and Casluhim whence came forth Philistim and Caphtorim.
texts.gen.10.15: And Canaan begat Zidon his firstborn, and Heth:
texts.gen.10.16: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite;
texts.gen.10.17: and the Hivite and the Arkite, and the Sinite:
texts.gen.10.18: and the Arvadite and the Zemarite and the Hamathite,—and after-wards, were spread abroad the families of the Canaanite.
texts.gen.10.19: And it came to pass that the boundary of the Canaanite was from Zidon, as thou enterest in towards Gerar unto Gaza,—as thou enterest in towards Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboim, as far as Lasha.
texts.gen.10.20: These, are the sons of Ham, by their families by their tongues, in their lands in their nations.
texts.gen.10.21: Now, to Shem, father of all the sons of Eber, elder brother of Japheth, to him also, were children born.
texts.gen.10.22: The sons of Shem, Elam and Asshur,—and Arpachshad and Lud and Aram.
texts.gen.10.23: And, the sons of Aram: Uz and Hul, and Gether and Mash.
texts.gen.10.24: Now Arpachshad, begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber.
texts.gen.10.25: And to Eber, were born two sons,—the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days, was the earth divided, and the name of his brother was Joktan.
texts.gen.10.26: Now, Joktan, begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah;
texts.gen.10.27: and Hadoram and Uzal, and Diklah:
texts.gen.10.28: and Obal and Abimael, and Sheba:
texts.gen.10.29: and Ophir and Havilah, and Jobab—all these were sons of Joktan.
texts.gen.10.30: And it came to pass that their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou enterest in towards Sephar, the mountain of the east.
texts.gen.10.31: These are the sons of Shem, by their families by their tongues, in their lands by their nations.
texts.gen.10.32: These, are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations in their nations, and from these, were dispersed the nations in the earth after the flood.
texts.gen.11.1: So it came to pass that, all the earth, was of one manner of speech,—and of one stock of words.
texts.gen.11.2: And it came to pass as they brake away onwards, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and dwelt there.
texts.gen.11.3: Then said they, each man to his friend, Come on! let us make bricks, and burn them thoroughly,—So the bricks, served them for stone, and bitumen, served them for mortar,
texts.gen.11.4: And they said Come on! let us build for ourselves a city, and a tower with its head in the heavens, so let us make for ourselves a name,—lest we be scattered abroad over the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.11.5: And Yahweh came down, to behold the city, and the tower,—which the sons of men had built.
texts.gen.11.6: Then said Yahweh: Lo! one people and one manner of speech, have they all, this, then is what they have begun to do,—now, therefore, nothing will be withholden from them which they may plan to do.
texts.gen.11.7: Come on! let us go down, and there confuse their speech,—that they may not understand, each man the speech of his friend.
texts.gen.11.8: So Yahweh scattered them from thence over the face of all the earth,—and so they left off building the city.
texts.gen.11.9: For this cause, was the name thereof called Babel [="Confusion"]; because there, did Yahweh confuse the speech of all the earth,—and, from thence, did Yahweh scatter them abroad, over the face of all the earth.
texts.gen.11.10: These, are the genealogies of Shem, Shem was a hundred years old when he begat Arpachshad, two years after the flood
texts.gen.11.11: and Shem lived after he begat Arpachshad, five hundred years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.12: And, Arpachshad, lived thirty-five years,—and begat Shelah;
texts.gen.11.13: and Arpachshad lived after he begat Shelah, four hundred and three years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.14: And, Shelah, lived thirty years,—and begat Eber;
texts.gen.11.15: and Shelah lived, after he begat Eber, four hundred and three years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.16: And Eber lived thirty-four years,—and begat Peleg;
texts.gen.11.17: and Eber lived after he begat Peleg, four hundred and thirty years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.18: And Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu:
texts.gen.11.19: and Peleg lived after he begat Reu, two hundred and nine years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.20: And Reu lived thirty-two years—and begat Serug;
texts.gen.11.21: and Reu lived after he begat Serug, two hundred and seven years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.22: And Serug lived thirty years,—and begat Nahor;
texts.gen.11.23: and Serug lived after he begat Nahor, two hundred years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.24: And Nahor lived twenty-nine years,—and begat Terah;
texts.gen.11.25: and Nahor lived, after he begat Terah, a hundred and nineteen years,—and begat sons and daughters.
texts.gen.11.26: And Terah lived seventy years,—and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
texts.gen.11.27: These, then are the generations of Terah, Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran,—and, Haran, begat Lot;
texts.gen.11.28: and Haran died, in the presence of Terah his father,—in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees.
texts.gen.11.29: And Abram and Nahor took to themselves wives; the name of Abram’s wife, was Sarai; and, the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, daughter of Haran father of Milcah, and father of Iscah.
texts.gen.11.30: And, Sarai, remained barren,—she had no child,
texts.gen.11.31: And Terah took Abram his son and Lot son of Haran his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, wife of Abram his son,—and came forth with them out of Ur of the Chaldees, that they might go their way towards the land of Canaan, and they came in as far as Haran and dwelt there.
texts.gen.11.32: And the days of Terah were two hundred and five years,—and Terah died in Haran.
texts.gen.12.1: And Yahweh said unto Abram: Come thou on thy way, Out of thy land and out of the place of thy birth and out of the house of thy father,—Unto the land that I will show thee;
texts.gen.12.2: That I may make thee into a great nation, And bless thee and make great thy name, And become thou a blessing;
texts.gen.12.3: That I may bless them who bless thee, But him who maketh light of thee, will I curse,—So shall be, blessed in thee, all the families of the ground.
texts.gen.12.4: And Abram came on his way, according to that which Yahweh had spoken unto him, and Lot came with him,—now, Abram, was seventy-five years old, when he came forth out of Haran.
texts.gen.12.5: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, with all the goods that they had gathered and the souls that they had gained in Haran,—and they came forth to go towards the land of Canaan, and came in to the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.12.6: And Abram passed along throughout the land, as far as the place of Shechem as far as the Teacher’s Terebinth, the Canaanite being then in the land.
texts.gen.12.7: And Yahweh appeared unto Abram, and said: To thy seed, will I give this land,—And he built there an altar, unto Yahweh who appeared unto him.
texts.gen.12.8: And he moved on from thence towards the hill country, on the east of Bethel and pitched his tent,—with Bethel on the west, and Ai on the east, and built there an altar to Yahweh, and called on the name of Yahweh.
texts.gen.12.9: Thus Abram brake up, again and again, towards the South.
texts.gen.12.10: And it came to pass that there was a famine, in the land,—so Abram went down towards Egypt, to sojourn there, because grievous, was the famine in the land.
texts.gen.12.11: And it came to pass when he had come near to enter into Egypt, that he said unto Sarai his wife: Behold! I beseech thee I know that a woman fair to look on, thou art:
texts.gen.12.12: so will it come to pass when the Egyptians behold thee, that they will say, His wife, this! and will slay me while thee, they preserve alive.
texts.gen.12.13: Say, I beseech thee that my sister, art thou,—to the end it may be well with me for thy sake, so shall my soul be preserved alive because of thee.
texts.gen.12.14: And so it was when Abram entered into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman, that fair, was she exceedingly.
texts.gen.12.15: And the princes of Pharaoh beheld her, and praised her unto Pharaoh,—so the woman was taken to the house of Pharaoh;
texts.gen.12.16: and with Abram, dealt he well for her sake,—so that he came to have flocks and herds and he-asses, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and she-asses and camels.
texts.gen.12.17: And Yahweh plagued Pharaoh with great plagues, also his house,—for the matter of Sarai, wife of Abram.
texts.gen.12.18: And Pharaoh called out to Abram, and said, What is this thou hast done to me? Wherefore didst thou not tell me, that she was, thy wife?
texts.gen.12.19: Wherefore saidst thou My sister, she; and so I was about to take her to me, to wife? But now, lo! thy wife take her and go thy way.
texts.gen.12.20: And Pharaoh gave command concerning him unto certain men,—and sent him away, with his wife and all that he had.
texts.gen.13.1: So Abram came up out of Egypt he and his wife and all that he had and Lot with him, towards the South.
texts.gen.13.2: Now, Abram, was very rich,—in cattle, in silver and in gold.
texts.gen.13.3: And he went his way, by his removals, from the South even as far as to Bethel,—as far as the place where his tent was at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai:
texts.gen.13.4: unto the place of the altar, which he made there at first,—and Abram called there, on the name of Yahweh.
texts.gen.13.5: Now, Lot also, who was going with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents.
texts.gen.13.6: And the land suffered them not to dwell together,—because their substance had become, great, so that they could not dwell together.
texts.gen.13.7: And there arose a strife betwixt the herdmen of Abram, and the herdmen of Lot. Now the Canaanite and the Perizzite, were then dwelling in the land.
texts.gen.13.8: So then Abram said unto Lot Pray let not cause of strife arise betwixt me and thee, or betwixt my herdmen and thy herdmen; for brethren, are we.
texts.gen.13.9: Is not, all the land, before thee? I pray thee, separate thyself from me,—if to the left hand, then I will go to the right, if to the right hand, then I will go to the left.
texts.gen.13.10: So Lot lifted up his eyes and beheld all the circuit of the Jordan, that the whole of it, was well-watered,—before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the Garden of Yahweh, like the land of Egypt, as thou enterest into Zoar.
texts.gen.13.11: And Lot chose for himself all the circuit of the Jordan, so Lot brake up eastwards,—and they separated themselves, each man from his brother:
texts.gen.13.12: Abram, fixed his dwelling in the land of Canaan,—but, Lot, fixed his dwelling among the cities, of the circuit, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
texts.gen.13.13: Now, the men of Sodom were base and sinful,—against Yahweh, exceedingly.
texts.gen.13.14: And, Yahweh, said unto Abram after that Lot had separated himself from him, Lift up, I pray thee thine eyes and look, from the place where thou art,—northward and southward and eastward and westward;
texts.gen.13.15: for all the land which thou art beholding—to thee, will I give it, and to thy seed unto times age-abiding;
texts.gen.13.16: and I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth,—so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, thy seed also, may be numbered.
texts.gen.13.17: Rise! go up and down in the land, to the length thereof and to the breadth thereof, for to thee, will I give it.
texts.gen.13.18: So Abram moved his tent and came in and dwelt among the oaks of Mamre, which were in Hebron,—and built there an altar to Yahweh.
texts.gen.14.1: And it came to pass, in the days of Amraphel, king of Shinar, Arioch, king of Ellasar,—Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goim,
texts.gen.14.2: that they made war, with Bera, king of Sodom, and with Birsha, king of Gomorrah,—Shinab, king of Admah, and Shemeber, king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela—the same, is Zoar.
texts.gen.14.3: All these, joined together in the valley of the open fields, the same, is the Salt Sea.
texts.gen.14.4: Twelve years, had they served Chedorlaomer,—but in the thirteenth year had they rebelled;
texts.gen.14.5: and in the fourteenth year, had Chedorlaomer come in and the kings who were with him, so they smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham,—and the Emim, in Shaveh-kiriathaim;
texts.gen.14.6: and the Horites in their Mount Seir,—as far as El-paran, which is by the desert.
texts.gen.14.7: So they returned and came in unto En-mishpat, the same, is Kadish, and smote all the field of the Amalekites,—and the Amorites also that dwelt in Hazazon-tamar,
texts.gen.14.8: Thus then went forth the King of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah and the king of Zeboim, and the king of Bela the same, is Zoar—and set themselves in array against them for battle, in the valley of the open fields:
texts.gen.14.9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar,—four kings against five.
texts.gen.14.10: Now, the valley of the open fields, had many pits of bitumen, so the king of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and fell there,—while, they who remained, towards a mountain, fled.
texts.gen.14.11: And they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food and went their way.
texts.gen.14.12: And they took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son with his goods, and went their way,—he, being a dweller in Sodom.
texts.gen.14.13: Then came in a fugitive, and told Abram the Hebrew,—he, having his dwelling among the oaks of Mamre the Amorite brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner, they, also having a covenant with Abram.
texts.gen.14.14: So Abram, hearing that his brother had been taken captive, drew forth his trained men born in his house three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.
texts.gen.14.15: And he divided himself against them by night, he, and his servants, and smote them,—and pursued them as far as Hobah, which was on the left of Damascus.
texts.gen.14.16: So he brought back all the goods,—yea Lot also his brother with his goods, did he bring back, and the women also, and the people.
texts.gen.14.17: Then came forth the king of Sodom to meet him, after his return from the smiting of Chedorlaomer, and the kings who were with him,—into the vale of Shaveh the same, was the vale of the king.
texts.gen.14.18: Now Melchizedek king of Salem, had brought forth bread and wine,—he, being priest of GOD Most High.
texts.gen.14.19: So he blessed him and said,—Blessed be Abram of GOD Most High, possessor of [the] heavens and earth;
texts.gen.14.20: And blessed be GOD Most High, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. So he gave unto him a tenth of all.
texts.gen.14.21: Then said the king of Sodom unto Abram,—Give unto me the persons, but the goods, take thou for thyself.
texts.gen.14.22: And Abram said unto the king of Sodom,—I have lifted up my hand unto Yahweh GOD Most High, possessor of [the] heavens and earth:
texts.gen.14.23: That not from a thread even unto a sandal-thong,—will I take, anything, that is thine,—Lest thou shouldst say, I, enriched Abram!
texts.gen.14.24: Save only what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre, they may take their share.
texts.gen.15.1: After these things, came the word of Yahweh unto Abram, in a vision saying,—Do not fear Abram, I am a shield to thee, thine exceeding great reward.
texts.gen.15.2: And Abram said My Lord Yahweh, what canst thou give me, when, I, am going on childless,—and the heir of my house, is Eliezer, of Damascus,
texts.gen.15.3: And Abram said—Lo, to me, hast thou not given seed,—And lo! a son of my household, is mine heir!
texts.gen.15.4: And lo! the word of Yahweh [came] unto him, saying, This one, shall not be thine heir: But one who cometh forth of thy body—he shall be thine heir.
texts.gen.15.5: And he brought him forth abroad and said—Look steadfastly. I pray thee towards the heavens, and number the stars, if thou be able to number, them, And he said to him, Thus, shall be thy seed.
texts.gen.15.6: And he had faith in Yahweh,—so he reckoned it to him as righteousness.
texts.gen.15.7: And he said unto him,—I, am Yahweh, who brought thee forth out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.
texts.gen.15.8: And he said, My Lord Yahweh, whereby, can I know that I shall inherit it?
texts.gen.15.9: And he said unto him, Take for me a heifer three years old, and a she-goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtle-dove and a young pigeon.
texts.gen.15.10: So he took for him all these, and divided them, in the midst, and placed each piece over against its fellow, but the birds, divided he not.
texts.gen.15.11: Then came down the birds of prey upon the carcass, and Abram drove them away.
texts.gen.15.12: And it came to pass when, the sun, was about to go in, and, a deep sleep, had fallen upon Abram, lo! a terror a great darkness, was falling upon him.
texts.gen.15.13: And he said to Abram—Thou must surely know, that, sojourners, will thy seed become in a land not theirs, and shall serve them and they will humble them, four hundred years;
texts.gen.15.14: moreover also, the nation whom they will serve, I, am going to judge, and after that, shall they come forth with great substance.
texts.gen.15.15: But, thou, shalt go in unto thy fathers in peace, thou shalt be buried in a good old age.
texts.gen.15.16: And, in the fourth generation, shall they return hither,—for not complete, is the iniquity of the Amorites, as yet,
texts.gen.15.17: So it came to pass when, the sun, had gone in, and, a thick darkness, had come on, that lo there was a smoking hearth and torch of fire, which passed through between these pieces.
texts.gen.15.18: In that day, did Yahweh solemnise with Abram a covenant, saying,—To thy seed, have I given this land, from the river of Egypt as far as the great river—the river Euphrates:
texts.gen.15.19: the Kenite, and the Kenizzite, and the Kadmonite;
texts.gen.15.20: and the Hittite and the Perizzite, and the Rephaim;
texts.gen.15.21: and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.
texts.gen.16.1: But Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children,—she had, however, an Egyptian handmaid, whose name was Hagar.
texts.gen.16.2: So then Sarai said unto Abram Behold, I pray thee, Yahweh hath restrained me, from bearing, go in I pray thee unto, my handmaid, peradventure I may be built up from, her, And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai.
texts.gen.16.3: So Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian. her handmaid, at the end of ten years of Abram’s dwelling in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband, to be to him as a wife.
texts.gen.16.4: And he went in unto Hagar and she conceived,—and when she saw that she had conceived, lightly esteemed, was her lady, in her eyes.
texts.gen.16.5: Then said Sarai unto Abram: My wrong, is, on thee! I, gave my handmaid into thy bosom, and when she seeth that she hath conceived, then am I lightly esteemed in her eyes Yahweh judge betwixt me and her.
texts.gen.16.6: And Abram said unto Sarai, Lo! thy handmaid, is in thy hand, do to her what is good in thine eyes. So Sarai humbled her, and she fled from her face.
texts.gen.16.7: And the messenger of Yahweh found her by the fountain of water in the desert,—by the fountain in the way to Shur.
texts.gen.16.8: So he said Hagar! handmaid of Sarai! Whence hast thou come, and whither wouldst thou go? And she said, From the face of Sarai, my lady, am, I, fleeing.
texts.gen.16.9: And the messenger of Yahweh said to her, Return unto thy lady,—and humble thyself under her hands.
texts.gen.16.10: And the messenger of Yahweh said to her, I will, greatly multiply, thy seed—so that it shall not be numbered for multitude.
texts.gen.16.11: And the messenger of Yahweh said to her, Behold thee! with child, and about bearing a son—and thou shalt call his name Ishmael [="God hearkeneth"] for Yahweh hath hearkened unto thy humiliation.
texts.gen.16.12: But, he, will be a wild ass of a man, his hand, against every one, and every one’s hand against him—yet, in presence of all his brethren, shall he have his habitation.
texts.gen.16.13: And she called the name of Yahweh, who had spoken unto her, Thou GOD of vision! For she said. Do I even here, retain my vision after a vision?
texts.gen.16.14: On this account, is the well called, the well of the life of vision, lo! it is between Kadesh and Bered.
texts.gen.16.15: So Hagar bare to Abram a son,—and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bare, Ishmael.
texts.gen.16.16: Now, Abram, was eighty—six years old,—when Hagar bare Ishmael to Abram.
texts.gen.17.1: And it came to pass that, when Abram was ninety and nine years old, Yahweh appeared unto Abram, and said unto him, I, am GOD Almighty,—Walk, thou before me and become thou blameless:
texts.gen.17.2: That I may set my covenant betwixt me and thee, And may multiply thee, exceedingly.
texts.gen.17.3: And Abram fell on his face,—and God spake with him, saying:
texts.gen.17.4: As for me, lo! my covenant is with thee,—So shalt thou become—father of a multitude of nations;
texts.gen.17.5: And thy name shall no more be called Abram,—but thy name shall become Abraham, for father of a multitude of nations, have I appointed thee;
texts.gen.17.6: And I will make thee fruitful, exceedingly, and grant thee to be nations,—Yea kings, out of thee, shall come forth;
texts.gen.17.7: And I will confirm my covenant betwixt me and thee and thy seed after thee to their generations for an age-abiding covenant,—to become to thee a God, and to thy seed after thee;
texts.gen.17.8: And I will give to thee and to thy seed after thee the land of thy sojournings—all the land of Canaan, for an age-abiding possession—And I will be to them a God.
texts.gen.17.9: And God said unto Abraham, But, as for thee, my covenant, must thou keep, thou and thy seed after thee, to their generations:—
texts.gen.17.10: This, is my covenant which ye shall keep, betwixt me and you, and thy seed after thee,—To circumcise to you every male:
texts.gen.17.11: So shall ye be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin,—So shall it become a sign of a covenant, betwixt me and you.
texts.gen.17.12: And he that is eight days old, shall be circumcised to you every male to your generations,—he that is born of the house, and he that is bought with silver of any son of a stranger, who is, not of thy seed,
texts.gen.17.13: He must surely be circumcised, born of thy house or bought with thy silver,—So shall my covenant be in your flesh for an age-abiding covenant.
texts.gen.17.14: But, as for the uncircumcised male who shall not be circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin,—that person shall be cut off from among his people,—my covenant, hath he made void.
texts.gen.17.15: And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai,—but, Sarah, is her name;
texts.gen.17.16: and I will bless her, yea moreover will give—from her—to thee, a son,—And I will bless her, and she shall become nations. Kings of peoples, from her, shall arise.
texts.gen.17.17: And Abraham fell on his face and laughed,—and said in his heart To one a hundred years old, shall a child be born? And shall even Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?
texts.gen.17.18: And Abraham said unto God,—Oh that, Ishmael, might live before thee!
texts.gen.17.19: And God said—Truly, Sarah thy wife, is about to bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name, Isaac,—and I will establish my covenant with him as an age-abiding covenant, to his seed after him.
texts.gen.17.20: Yet as for Ishmael, I have heard thee; lo! I have blessed him and will make him fruitful, and multiply him, exceedingly,—twelve princes, shall he beget, and I will grant him to be a great nation;
texts.gen.17.21: But my covenant, will I establish with Isaac,—whom Sarah shall bear, to thee, by this set time, in the next year.
texts.gen.17.22: And he left off speaking with him,—and God went up from Abraham.
texts.gen.17.23: So Abraham took Ishmael his son and all born of his house and all bought with his silver—every male among the men of the house of Abraham,—and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on this selfsame day, according to that which God had spoken with him.
texts.gen.17.24: Now Abraham, was ninety-nine years old,—when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
texts.gen.17.25: And Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
texts.gen.17.26: On this selfsame day, was Abraham circumcised,—and Ishmael his son;
texts.gen.17.27: and, all the men of his house, born of his house, and bought with silver from the son of a stranger, were circumcised with him.
texts.gen.18.1: And Yahweh appeared unto him among the oaks of Mamre,—as, he, was sitting at the opening of the tent in the heat of the day.
texts.gen.18.2: And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and lo! three men, standing over against him,—so he looked and ran to meet them from the opening of the tent, and bowed himself to the earth;
texts.gen.18.3: and said,—O My Lord! if, I pray thee, I have found favour in thine eyes, do not I pray thee pass on from thy servant.
texts.gen.18.4: Let there be fetched, I pray thee a little water, and bathe ye your feet,—and rest yourselves under the tree.
texts.gen.18.5: And let me fetch a morsel of bread, and stay ye your heart, Afterwards, ye may pass on, For on this account, have ye passed by, over against your servant. And they said, Thus, shalt thou do as thou hast spoken.
texts.gen.18.6: So Abraham hastened towards the tent unto Sarah,—and said, Hasten thou three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make hearth-cakes.
texts.gen.18.7: And unto the herd, ran Abraham,—and took a calf tender and good and gave unto the young man, and he hastened to make it ready.
texts.gen.18.8: And he took butter and milk and the calf that he had made ready, and set before them,—while, he, was standing near them under the tree, they did eat.
texts.gen.18.9: And they said unto him, As to Sarah thy wife… And he said Lo! [she is] in the tent.
texts.gen.18.10: And he said, I will, surely return, unto thee at the quickening season,—and lo! a son for Sarah thy wife. Now Sarah, was hearkening at the opening of the tent, it, being behind him.
texts.gen.18.11: But Abraham and Sarah, were old, far gone in days,—it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.
texts.gen.18.12: So then Sarah laughed within herself, saying: After I am past age, hath there come to me pleasure, my lord, also being old?
texts.gen.18.13: And Yahweh said unto Abraham,—Wherefore now did Sarah laugh saying. Can it really and truly be that I should bear, seeing that I have become old?
texts.gen.18.14: Is anything, too wonderful for Yahweh? At the appointed time, I will return unto thee, at the quickening season and Sarah, shall have a son.
texts.gen.18.15: And Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not, For she was afraid. And he said—Nay! but thou didst laugh!
texts.gen.18.16: And the men rose up from thence, and looked out over the face of Sodom,—Abraham also going with them to set them on their way.
texts.gen.18.17: Now, Yahweh, had said,—Am I going to hide from Abraham what I do,
texts.gen.18.18: when, Abraham, shall surely become, a great and mighty nation,—and all the nations of the earth, shall be blessed in him?
texts.gen.18.19: For I have become his intimate friend, To the end that he may command his sons and his house after him, so shall they keep the way of Yahweh, by doing righteousness and justice. To the end that Yahweh may bring in for Abraham, what he hath spoken concerning him.
texts.gen.18.20: So Yahweh said, The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah, because it hath become great,—And their sin, because it hath become exceeding grievous,
texts.gen.18.21: Let me go down, pray, and let me behold, whether according to their outcry which hath come in unto me, they have done altogether, And if not. I must know!
texts.gen.18.22: And the men turned from thence, and went their way, towards Sodom,—but, Yahweh was yet standing before Abraham.
texts.gen.18.23: So then Abraham drew near and said, Wilt thou really sweep away, the righteous with the lawless?
texts.gen.18.24: Peradventure there are fifty righteous, in the midst of the city, Wilt thou really sweep away, and not spare the place, for the sake of the fifty righteous which are therein?
texts.gen.18.25: Far be it from thee! to do after this manner. to put to death the righteous with the lawless! Then should righteous and lawless be alike, Far be it from thee! Shall, the Judge of all the earth not do justice?
texts.gen.18.26: And Yahweh said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous in the midst of the city, then will I spare all the place for their sake.
texts.gen.18.27: And Abraham responded and said,—Behold I pray thee I have ventured to speak unto My Lord, though I am dust and ashes:
texts.gen.18.28: Peradventure there may lack, of the fifty righteous, five, Wilt thou destroy for five all the city? And he said, I will not destroy, if I find there forty and five.
texts.gen.18.29: And he added, yet once more, to speak unto him, and said, Peradventure there may be found there—forty. And he said—I will not do it, for the sake of the forty.
texts.gen.18.30: And he said Let it not, I pray thee, be vexing to My Lord, but let me speak, Peradventure there may be found there—thirty And he said, I will not to it, if I find there—thirty.
texts.gen.18.31: And he said Behold, I pray thee, I have ventured to speak unto My Lord, Peradventure there may be found there—twenty. And he said I will not destroy it, for the sake of the twenty.
texts.gen.18.32: And he said, Let it not, I pray thee, be vexing to My Lord, but let me speak only this once, Peradventure there may be found there—ten. And he said, I will not destroy [it], for the sake of the ten!
texts.gen.18.33: And Yahweh went his way, when he had made an end. of speaking unto Abraham,—Abraham, also returned to his place.
texts.gen.19.1: So the two messengers went in towards Sodom at eventide, Lot, being seated in the gate of Sodom,—so Lot beheld and rose up to meet them, and bowed himself with his face to the earth.
texts.gen.19.2: And he said Behold, I pray you my lords turn aside, I pray you, into the house of your servant,—and tarry the night and bathe your feet, so shall ye rise early, and go on your way. And they said, Nay, but, in the broad way, will we tarry the night.
texts.gen.19.3: But he became exceeding urgent with them, so they turned aside unto him and entered into his house,—and he made for them a banquet, unleavened cakes, also did he bake, and they did eat.
texts.gen.19.4: Ere yet they lay down, the men of the city—the men of Sodom, had come round against the house, from youth even unto age,—all the people from every quarter,
texts.gen.19.5: And they called unto Lot and said to him, Where are the men who have come in unto thee tonight? Bring them forth unto us, and let us know them!
texts.gen.19.6: And Lot went forth unto them to the entrance; but the door, closed he behind him.
texts.gen.19.7: And he said,—Do not I pray you my brethren act wickedly.
texts.gen.19.8: Behold, I pray you, I, have two daughters who have not known man, I must needs now bring, them, forth unto you, and do ye to them, as may be good in your eyes,—Only to these men, ye may do nothing; for on this account, have they come under the shade of my roof.
texts.gen.19.9: And they said, Stand back, And they said, This one, by himself, hath come in to sojourn and must always be acting the judge, Now, will we do more wickedly to thee, than to them. So they pressed sore upon the man—upon Lot—exceedingly, and drew near to break open the door.
texts.gen.19.10: And the men thrust forth their hand, and brought Lot in unto them into the house—and, the door, they closed:
texts.gen.19.11: the men also who were at the entrance of the house, smote they with blindness, from small even unto great, so that they wearied themselves to find the entrance.
texts.gen.19.12: And the men said unto Lot, Whom besides hast thou here? Son-in-law and thy sons and thy daughters, and all that thou hast in the city, bring thou forth out of the place;
texts.gen.19.13: For we are about to destroy this place,—for, great, is the outcry of them unto the face of Yahweh, so that Yahweh hath sent us to destroy it.
texts.gen.19.14: And Lot went forth and spake unto his sons-in-law who were about to take his two daughters and said Arise come forth out of this place, for Yahweh is about to destroy the city. And it came to pass, that he was as one that laughed, in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
texts.gen.19.15: But as soon as, the dawn had sprung up, the messengers hastened Lot saying,—Arise! take thy wife and thy two daughters that are at hand, lest thou be swept away in the punishment of the city.
texts.gen.19.16: And he lingered—so the men laid hold of his hand and of the hand of his wife and of the hand of his two daughters, in the tenderness of Yahweh towards him,—and they brought him out and led him forth outside the city.
texts.gen.19.17: And it came to pass when they had brought them forth outside, that they said, Escape for thy life, Look not behind thee, neither stand still in all the vale,—To the mountain, escape thou lest thou be swept away.
texts.gen.19.18: And Lot said unto them,—No, I pray thee, My Lord!
texts.gen.19.19: Behold, I pray thee thy servant hath found favour in thine eyes, so that thou hast magnified thy lovingkindness which thou hast performed with me in keeping alive my soul.—But, I, cannot escape to the mountain, lest calamity overtake me so shall I die.
texts.gen.19.20: Behold, I pray thee, this city, is near for fleeing thither And, it, is a little one, let me I pray thee, escape thither—is it not a, little, one? That my soul may live!
texts.gen.19.21: And he said unto him, Behold! I have lifted up thy countenance, even as to this thing,—so that I will not overthrow the city, of which thou hast spoken.
texts.gen.19.22: Haste thee escape thither, for I cannot do anything, until thou have come in thither. For this cause: was the name of the city called Zoar.
texts.gen.19.23: When, the sun, had come forth on the earth, Lot had entered into Zoar.
texts.gen.19.24: And, Yahweh, rained, upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah, brimstone and fire,—from Yahweh, out of the heavens:
texts.gen.19.25: so he overthrew these cities, and all the circuit,—and all the inhabitants of the cities, and the produce of the ground.
texts.gen.19.26: But his wife looked from behind him,—and became—a pillar of salt.
texts.gen.19.27: And Abraham gat up early in the morning, unto the place where he had stood before Yahweh;
texts.gen.19.28: and he looked out over the face of Sodom and Gomorrah, and over all the face of the land of the circuit, and beheld and lo! the smoke of the land went up, like the smoke of a furnace.
texts.gen.19.29: And it came to pass when God destroyed the cities of the circuit, that God remembered Abraham, and sent forth Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities wherein Lot had dwelt.
texts.gen.19.30: And Lot went up out of Zoar, and dwelt in the mountain and his two daughters with him. for he feared to dwell in Zoar, so he dwelt in a cave, he, and his two daughters.
texts.gen.19.31: And the firstborn said unto the younger. Our father is old,—and, a man, there is not in the earth to come in unto us, after the way of all the earth.
texts.gen.19.32: Come on! let us cause our father to drink wine and let us lie with him, that we may keep alive from our father, a seed.
texts.gen.19.33: So they caused their father to drink wine that night,—and the firstborn went in. and lay with her father, but he noticed not her lying down nor her rising up.
texts.gen.19.34: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the firstborn said unto the younger, Lo! I lay, last night with my father, let us cause him to drink wine this night also, and go thou in—lie with him, that we may keep alive from our father, a seed.
texts.gen.19.35: So they caused their father, on that night also to drink wine, and the younger arose, and lay with him, but he noticed not her lying down, nor her rising up.
texts.gen.19.36: Thus did, the two daughters of Lot conceive from their father.
texts.gen.19.37: And the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab,—the same, is the father of Moab, unto this day.
texts.gen.19.38: And the younger she also bare a son, and called his name Ben-ammi,—the same, is the father of the sons of Ammon—unto this day.
texts.gen.20.1: And Abraham brake up from thence, towards the land of the South, and fixed his dwelling between Kadesh and Shur, so he sojourned in Gerar.
texts.gen.20.2: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife: My, sister, is she,—So Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
texts.gen.20.3: Then God went in unto Abimelech, in a dream of the night,—and said to him, Behold thee dead! because of the woman whom thou hast taken, seeing that, she, is a married woman.
texts.gen.20.4: Now, Abimelech, had not come near unto her,—so he said, O My Lord! a nation even a righteous one, wilt thou slay?
texts.gen.20.5: Had not, he himself, said to me, My sister, is she? and even she herself, said, My brother, is he? In the integrity of my heart and in the pureness of my hand, have I done this!
texts.gen.20.6: And God said unto him in a dream, I, also, knew, that in the integrity of thy heart, thou didst this, so then, even I myself, withheld thee from sinning against me, for this reason, have I not suffered thee to touch her.
texts.gen.20.7: Now, therefore restore the man’s wife, for a prophet, is he, that he may pray for thee and live thou,—But if thou art not going to restore her, know, that thou shalt die, thou—and all that are thine.
texts.gen.20.8: So Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and spake all these words in their ears, and the men feared greatly.
texts.gen.20.9: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, What hast thou done to us? and wherein had I sinned against thee, that thou shouldst have brought in over me and over my kingdom, a sin so great? Deeds, which should not be done, hast thou done with me.
texts.gen.20.10: And Abimelech said unto Abraham,—What hadst thou seen, that thou shouldst have done this thing?
texts.gen.20.11: And Abraham said, Because I thought, Surely there is no fear of God, in this place,—therefore will they slay me for the sake of my wife.
texts.gen.20.12: Moreover also, in truth, my sister daughter of my father, she is, only not daughter of my mother,—so she became my wife.
texts.gen.20.13: And so it came to pass when the Gods caused me to wander from my father’s house, that I said to her, This, is thy lovingkindness, wherewith thou shalt deal with me,—Into whatsoever place we enter, say of me My brother, is he.
texts.gen.20.14: Then took Abimelech sheep and oxen and men—servants and maid-servants, and gave to Abraham,—and restored to him Sarah his wife.
texts.gen.20.15: And Abimelech, said, Lo! my land is before thee,—wherever it may seem good in thine eyes, dwell.
texts.gen.20.16: And to Sarah, he said, Lo! I have given a thousand of silver unto thy brother: Lo! that is for thee as a covering of eyes, to all who are with thee,—And so in every way, hath right been done.
texts.gen.20.17: And Abraham prayed unto God,—and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maid-servants, so that they bare children,
texts.gen.20.18: For Yahweh, had restrained from bearing, every female of the house of Abimelech,—because of Sarah, wife of Abraham.
texts.gen.21.1: Now, Yahweh, visited Sarah, as he had said,—And Yahweh did for Sarah as he had spoken.
texts.gen.21.2: So, Sarah, conceived and bare, to Abraham, a son, for his old age, at the set time, of which God had spoken with him.
texts.gen.21.3: And Abraham called the name of his son that was born to him, whom, Sarah, bare to him, Isaac.
texts.gen.21.4: And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son, when eight days old,—as God commanded him.
texts.gen.21.5: Now Abraham was a hundred years old,—when Isaac his son was born to him.
texts.gen.21.6: And Sarah said, A laughing, hath God made for me,—Everyone that heareth will laugh with me.
texts.gen.21.7: And she said—Who would have announced to Abraham, Sarah hath suckled children? yet have I borne a son, for his old age!
texts.gen.21.8: And the child grew, and was weaned,—and Abraham made a great banquet, on the day of the weaning of Isaac.
texts.gen.21.9: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian woman whom she had borne to Abraham laughing!
texts.gen.21.10: So she said to Abraham, Cast out this bondwoman and her son,—for the son of this bondwoman must not inherit with my son with Isaac.
texts.gen.21.11: And the word was very grievous in the eyes of Abraham,—on account of his son.
texts.gen.21.12: And God said unto Abraham Let it not be grievous in thine eyes concerning the boy and concerning thy bondwoman, In all that Sarah may say unto thee, hearken to her voice,—For in Isaac, shall there be called to thee—a seed.
texts.gen.21.13: Yet even the son of the bondwoman, will I appoint to become, a nation, because thy seed, he is.
texts.gen.21.14: So Abraham rose up early in the morning—and took bread and a skin of water and gave unto hagar,—putting them on her shoulder and the child, and sent her forth,—so she went her way and wandered, in the desert of Beer-sheba.
texts.gen.21.15: And the water out of the skin was spent,—so she cast the child under one of the shrubs;
texts.gen.21.16: and went and sat her down over against him at a distance like as of such as draw the bow, for she said Let me not look upon the death of the child,—So she sat down over against him, and the boy lifted up his voice, and wept
texts.gen.21.17: And God heard the voice of the boy, and a messenger of God called unto Hagar out of the heavens; and said to her, What aileth thee, Hagar? Do not fear, for God hath hearkened unto the voice of the boy where he is.
texts.gen.21.18: Arise lift up the boy, and hold him up with thy hand,—for, a great nation, will I make him.
texts.gen.21.19: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water,—and went and filled the skin with water, and gave drink unto the boy
texts.gen.21.20: And it came to pass that God was with the boy, and he grew,—and dwelt in the desert, and he became as he grew up, an archer,
texts.gen.21.21: And he dwelt in the desert of Paran,—and his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.21.22: And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech, with Phicol chieftain of his host, spake unto Abraham, saying,—God, is with thee in all that, thou art doing.
texts.gen.21.23: Now, therefore, swear to me by God, here, that thou wilt not deal falsely by me, nor by mine offspring, nor by my descendants,—according to the lovingkindness wherewith I have dealt with thee, shalt thou deal with me, and with the land wherein thou hast sojourned.
texts.gen.21.24: And Abraham said, I, will swear.
texts.gen.21.25: But Abraham reproved Abimelech,—on account of the well of water, which the servants of Abimelech had seized.
texts.gen.21.26: And Abimelech said, I know not, who hath done this thing,—nor hast even thou, ever told me, nor have even I, ever heard, save to-day.
texts.gen.21.27: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave to Abimelech,—and they two solemnised a covenant
texts.gen.21.28: So then Abraham set seven young sheep of the flock by them-selves,
texts.gen.21.29: And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What, then mean these seven young sheep here, which thou hast set by themselves?
texts.gen.21.30: And he said, The seven young sheep, shalt thou take at my hand,—that they may serve as my witness, that I digged this well.
texts.gen.21.31: On this account, was the name of that place called Beer-sheba [="oath well"],—because there, had they two sworn.
texts.gen.21.32: And when they had solemnised a covenant in Beer-sheba,—then arose Abimelech, with Phicol chief of his host, and returned unto the land of the Philistines.
texts.gen.21.33: Then planted he a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba,—and called there on the name of Yahweh the age-abiding GOD.
texts.gen.21.34: So Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
texts.gen.22.1: And it came to pass after these things, that God, did prove Abraham,—and he said unto him, Abraham! And he said Behold me!
texts.gen.22.2: And he said—Take, I pray thee, thy son, thine only one, whom thou lovest, even, Isaac, and get thee into the land of Moriah and cause him to ascend there as an ascending-sacrifice, on one of the mountains which I shall name unto thee.
texts.gen.22.3: So Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took his two young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the pieces of wood for an ascending-sacrifice, and mounted and went his way unto the place which God had named to him.
texts.gen.22.4: It was, on the third day, that Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.
texts.gen.22.5: And Abraham said unto his young men—Tarry by yourselves here with the ass, but I and the young man must go yonder,—that we may bow ourselves down and return unto you.
texts.gen.22.6: So Abraham took the pieces of wood for the ascending-sacrifice, and laid them on Isaac his son, and took in his own hand the fire and the knife, and they went on their way, both of them together.
texts.gen.22.7: Then said Isaac unto Abraham his father, then said he; My father! And he said, Behold me, my son, And he said, Behold the fire, and the pieces of wood,—but where is the lamb, for an ascending-sacrifice?
texts.gen.22.8: And Abraham said, God, will provide for himself the lamb for an ascending-sacrifice, my son! So they went on their way, both of them, together.
texts.gen.22.9: Then came they into the place which God had named to him, and Abraham built there the altar, and laid in order the pieces of wood, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, above the pieces of wood.
texts.gen.22.10: And Abraham put forth his hand, and took the knife,—to slay his son.
texts.gen.22.11: Then called out unto him the messenger of Yahweh out of the heavens, and said. Abraham, Abraham! And he said Behold me!
texts.gen.22.12: Then he said, Do not put forth thy hand unto the young man, neither do to him—anything at all,—for, now, know I that one who reverest God, thou art, when thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only one, from me.
texts.gen.22.13: And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and lo! a ram, behind, caught in a thicket by his horns, and Abraham went, and took the ram, and caused him to ascend as an ascending-sacrifice instead of his son.
texts.gen.22.14: So Abraham called the name of that place Yahweh-yireh,—as to which it is still said to-day, In the mountain of Yahweh, will provision be made.
texts.gen.22.15: Then called out the messenger of Yahweh unto Abraham,—a second time out of the heavens;
texts.gen.22.16: and said, By myself, have I sworn is the oracle of Yahweh,—Because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only one,
texts.gen.22.17: That I will, richly bless, thee, and, abundantly multiply, thy seed, as the stars of the heavens, and as the sand which is on the lip of the sea,—that thy seed may take possession of the gate of his foes:
texts.gen.22.18: So shall all the nations of the earth bless themselves in thy seed,—Because thou didst hearken unto my voice.
texts.gen.22.19: So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they mounted, and went on their way together unto Beer-sheba,—and Abraham dwelt in Beer-sheba.
texts.gen.22.20: And it came to pass after these things, that it was told Abraham, saying,—Behold! Milcah—she also, hath borne sons, to Nahor thy brother:
texts.gen.22.21: Uz his firstborn and Buz his brother,—and Kemuel, father of Aram—
texts.gen.22.22: and Chesed and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph,—and Bethuel;
texts.gen.22.23: And, Bethuel, hath begotten Rebekah,—These eight, hath Milcah borne to Nahor brother of Abraham.
texts.gen.22.24: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, she also, hath borne Tebah and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maacah.
texts.gen.23.1: And the life of Sarah came to be, a hundred and twenty-seven years,—the years of the life of Sarah.
texts.gen.23.2: And Sarah died in Kiriath-arba, the same, is Hebron in the land of Canaan,—and Abraham went in to wail for Sarah and to weep for her.
texts.gen.23.3: And Abraham rose up from over the face of his dead,—and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying;
texts.gen.23.4: A sojourner and settler, am I with you,—Give me a possession of a buryingplace with you, That I may bury my dead, from before me.
texts.gen.23.5: And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him:
texts.gen.23.6: Hear us, my lord! A prince of God, art thou in our midst, In the choice of our buryingplaces, bury thy dead,—Not, a man from among us his, burying-place, will withhold from thee, from burying thy dead.
texts.gen.23.7: And Abraham rose up, and bowed himself down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth;
texts.gen.23.8: and spake with them, saying,—If it is with the consent of your minds that I should bury my dead from before me, hear me, and intercede for me, with Ephron son of Zohar:
texts.gen.23.9: That he would give me, the cave of Machpelah, which pertaineth unto him, which is within the bounds of his field,—For full silver, let him give it me in your midst, For a possession of a buryingplace.
texts.gen.23.10: Now, Ephron, was sitting in the midst of the sons of Heth,—so Ephron the Hittite responded to Abraham, in the ears of the sons of Heth, even all that were entering the gate of his city, saying:
texts.gen.23.11: Nay, my lord, hear me, The field, have I given to thee And, the cave that is therein, to thee, have I given it,—In the eyes of the sons of my people, have I given it thee Bury thy dead.
texts.gen.23.12: So Abraham boweth himself down, before the people of the land:
texts.gen.23.13: and spake unto Ephron in the ears of the people of the land saying, Only if, thou, wouldst, hear me,—I have given the silver of the field Take it of me, That I may bury my dead here.
texts.gen.23.14: And Ephron responded to Abraham, saying to him,
texts.gen.23.15: My lord, hear me,—Land worth four hundred shekels of silver—betwixt me and thee, what is that? And thy dead., bury thou.
texts.gen.23.16: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron, and Abraham weighed out to Ephron the silver of which he had spoken in the ears of the sons of Heth,—four hundred shekels of silver, current with the merchant,
texts.gen.23.17: So was confirmed the field of Ephron, which is in Machpelah, which is before Mamre,—the field and the cave which is therein, and all the timber which was in the field, which was in all the boundary thereof round about,
texts.gen.23.18: to Abraham as a purchase in the eyes of the sons of Heth,—with all who were entering the gate of his city.
texts.gen.23.19: And after this, did Abraham bury Sarah his wife, within the cave of the field of Machpelah, over against Mamre, the same, is Hebron,—in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.23.20: So was confirmed the field with the cave which was therein to Abraham, for a possession of a buryingplace,—from the sons of Heth.
texts.gen.24.1: Now, Abraham, was old, far gone in days,—and, Yahweh, had blessed Abraham, in all things.
texts.gen.24.2: So Abraham said unto his servant, elder of his house, ruler of all that he had,—Place, I pray thee thy hand under my thigh;
texts.gen.24.3: that I may put thee on oath, by Yahweh God of the heavens and God of the earth—That thou wilt not take a wife for my son, from among the daughters of the Canaanites in the midst of whom, I, am dwelling:
texts.gen.24.4: but unto my own land and unto my own kindred, wilt go,—So shalt thou take a wife for my son—for Isaac.
texts.gen.24.5: And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman may not be willing to follow me into this land,—May I take back thy son, into the land from whence thou camest?
texts.gen.24.6: And Abraham said unto him,—Beware that thou do not take back my son thither!
texts.gen.24.7: Yahweh, God of the heavens, and God of the earth, who took me out of the house of my father, and out of the land of my kindred, and, who spake to me, and who sware to me, saying, To thy seed, will I give this land, he, will send his messenger before thee, so shalt thou take a wife for my son from thence.
texts.gen.24.8: But if unwilling be the woman to follow thee, then shalt thou be clear from this mine oath,—Only my son, shalt thou not take back thither
texts.gen.24.9: So the servant placed his hand, under the thigh of Abraham, his lord,—and sware to him, over this thing.
texts.gen.24.10: Then took the servant ten camels, from among the camels of his lord, and went his way,—all the goods of his master being in his hand,—so be mounted, and went his way unto Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
texts.gen.24.11: And he made the camels kneel down outside the city, against the well of water,—at the time of evening, at the time of the coming forth of the women that drew water,
texts.gen.24.12: Then he said, O Yahweh, God of my lord Abraham! I pray thee cause it to fall out before me today, that thou deal in lovingkindness with my lord Abraham.
texts.gen.24.13: Here am, I, stationed by the fountain of water,—and, the daughters of the men of the city, are coming forth to draw water:
texts.gen.24.14: so it shall come to pass that the young woman unto whom I shall say. Let down pray. thy pitcher that I may drink, and she shall say, Drink, and to thy camels also, will I give to drink, that, her! hast thou appointed for thy servant for Isaac, And, hereby, shall I get to know, that thou hast dealt in lovingkindness with my lord!
texts.gen.24.15: And it came to pass, ere yet, he, had done speaking, that lo! Rebekah, was coming forth who had been born to Bethuel son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, brother of Abraham,—with her pitcher upon her shoulder,
texts.gen.24.16: Now the young woman! was of very pleasing appearance, a virgin whom, no man, had known,—and she went down unto the fountain, and filled her pitcher and came up.
texts.gen.24.17: And the servant ran to meet her,—and said, I pray thee let me drink a little water out of thy pitcher.
texts.gen.24.18: And she said, Drink my lord,—And she hastened and lowered her pitcher on her hand and let him drink.
texts.gen.24.19: And when she had done giving him drink,—she said For thy camels also, will I draw, until they have done drinking.
texts.gen.24.20: So she hastened and emptied her pitcher into the drinking-trough, and ran again unto the well, to draw,—and she drew for all his camels.
texts.gen.24.21: Now the man, was eagerly watching her,—keeping silence to see—whether Yahweh had prospered his way., or not.
texts.gen.24.22: And it came to pass when the camels had done drinking, that the man took a ring of gold, half a shekel its weight,—and two bracelets for her hands, ten of gold their weight;
texts.gen.24.23: and said Whose daughter art, thou? I pray thee, tell me. Is there in the house of thy father a place for us to tarry the night?
texts.gen.24.24: And she said unto him, Daughter of Bethuel, am, I,—[Bethuel] son of Milcah whom she bare to Nahor.
texts.gen.24.25: And she said unto him, Both straw and fodder in plenty, have we,—also a place to tarry the night.
texts.gen.24.26: Then the man bowed his head, and bent himself down unto Yahweh;
texts.gen.24.27: and said, Blessed be Yahweh. God of my lord Abraham, who hath not withdrawn his lovingkindness and his faithfulness, from my lord,—I—being in the way, Yahweh led me unto the house of the brethren of my lord!
texts.gen.24.28: And the young woman ran, and told the household of her mother,—according to these words.
texts.gen.24.29: Now, Rebekah, had a brother, whose name, was Laban,—so Laban ran unto the man outside, unto the fountain.
texts.gen.24.30: And it came to pass, when he saw the ring, and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister saying, Thus, did the man speak unto me, that he came unto the man, and lo! he was standing by the camels near the fountain;
texts.gen.24.31: and he said, Come in. thou blessed of Yahweh,—Wherefore shouldst thou stand outside, when I have made ready the house and a place for the camels?
texts.gen.24.32: So the man came in towards the house, and ungirded the camels,—and there was given him straw and fodder for the camels, and water for bathing his own feet and the feet of the men who were with him;
texts.gen.24.33: and [food] was set before him to eat, But he said, I cannot eat, until I have spoken my words. And he said—Speak!
texts.gen.24.34: Then said he,—Servant of Abraham, am I.
texts.gen.24.35: Now, Yahweh, having blessed my lord exceedingly, and made him great,—and given him flocks and herds and silver and gold, and men-servants and maid-servants, and camels, and asses,
texts.gen.24.36: then did Sarah wife of my lord, bear a son to my lord, after she had become old,—so he gave to him all that he had;
texts.gen.24.37: And my lord put me on oath saying,—Thou shalt not take a wife for my son, of the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land, I, am dwelling;
texts.gen.24.38: but, unto the house of my father, shalt thou go, and unto my family,—and take a wife for my son.
texts.gen.24.39: So I said unto my lord,—Peradventure the woman will not follow me.
texts.gen.24.40: And he said unto me,—Yahweh, before whom I have walked to and fro, will send his messenger with thee, so shall he prosper thy way, and thou shalt take a wife for my son out of my kindred and out of the house of my father.
texts.gen.24.41: Then, shalt thou clear thyself from mine oath, for thou shalt go in unto my kindred,—and, if they will not grant her unto thee, then shalt thou be clear from mine oath.
texts.gen.24.42: So I came in to-day, unto the fountain,—and I said O Yahweh God of my lord Abraham! if, I pray thee thou art prospering my way whereon I am going,
texts.gen.24.43: here, am I stationed by the fountain of water,—so then it shall come to pass that, the maiden that is coming forth to draw, and I shall say unto her Let me drink. I pray thee a little water out of thy pitcher;
texts.gen.24.44: and she shall say unto me Both, thou, drink, and for thy camels also, will I draw, the same, shall be the woman whom Yahweh hath appointed for the son of my lord.
texts.gen.24.45: Ere yet, I, could make an end of speaking unto mine own heart, lo! then Rebekah, coming forth, with her pitcher on her shoulder, and she went down to the fountain, and drew,—and I said unto her Let me drink I pray thee!
texts.gen.24.46: So she hastened and lowered her pitcher from off her, and said. Drink! and to thy camels also, will I give to drink,—So I drank and the camels also, she let drink.
texts.gen.24.47: Then I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said Daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom, Milcah, bare to him,—Then put I the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands;
texts.gen.24.48: and bowed my head and bent myself down unto Yahweh,—and I blessed Yahweh God of my lord Abraham, who had led me in a way of faithfulness, to take the daughter of the brother of my lord for his son.
texts.gen.24.49: Now, therefore, if ye are dealing in lovingkindness and faithfulness with my lord, tell me,—and, if not, tell me, that I may turn unto the right hand or unto the left.
texts.gen.24.50: Then answered Laban and Bethuel and said, from Yahweh, hath come forth the word,—we cannot speak unto thee ill or well.
texts.gen.24.51: Lo! Rebekah, is before thee, Take her and go thy way,—And let her become wife unto the son of thy lord, as Yahweh hath spoken.
texts.gen.24.52: And it came to pass when Abraham’s servant heard their words, that he bowed himself down towards the earth unto Yahweh.
texts.gen.24.53: Then the servant brought forth jewels of silver and jewels of gold and raiment, and gave unto Rebekah,—and precious things, gave he to her brother and to her mother.
texts.gen.24.54: And they did eat and drink he, and the men who were with him, and they tarried the night,—and when they arose in the morning, he said Let me go unto my lord!
texts.gen.24.55: Then said her brother and her mother, Let the young woman remain with us some days or rather ten,—After that, she shall go.
texts.gen.24.56: And he said unto them, Do not hinder me, when, Yahweh, hath prospered my journey,—Let me go, that I may take my journey unto my lord!
texts.gen.24.57: Then said they, We must call the young woman and ask at her mouth.
texts.gen.24.58: So they called Rebekah and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
texts.gen.24.59: So they let go Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant and his men.
texts.gen.24.60: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, Our sister! become thou, thousands of ten thousands,—And let thy seed take possession of the gate of them that hate them!
texts.gen.24.61: Then mounted Rebekah and her young woman and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man,—so the servant took Rebekah. and went his way.
texts.gen.24.62: Now, Isaac, had come in at the entrance, of Beer-lahai-roi,—for, he, was dwelling in the land of the South:
texts.gen.24.63: and Isaac came forth to meditate in the field at the approach of evening,—so he lifted up his eyes and looked, and lo! camels, coming in.
texts.gen.24.64: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and saw Isaac,—so she alighted with haste from off the camel;
texts.gen.24.65: and said unto the servant, Who is this man that is walking in the field to meet us? And the servant said, That, is my lord. So she took the veil and covered herself.
texts.gen.24.66: And the servant recounted to Isaac,—all the things which he had done.
texts.gen.24.67: And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother; thus he took Rebekah and she became his wife and he loved her,—and Isaac consoled himself, for the loss of his mother.
texts.gen.25.1: And Abraham took another wife and her name, was Keturah;
texts.gen.25.2: and she bare to him Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midian,—and Ishbak, and Shuah.
texts.gen.25.3: And, Yokshan, begat Sheba and Dedan,—and, the sons of Dedan, were Asshurim and Letushim, and Leummim.
texts.gen.25.4: And the sons of Midian, Ephah and Epher and Hanoch, and Abida. and Eldaah,—all these, were the sons of Keturah.
texts.gen.25.5: And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac;
texts.gen.25.6: but, to the sons of the concubines whom Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts,—and then sent them away from Isaac his son while he himself yet lived, eastward unto the land of the east.
texts.gen.25.7: Now, these, are the days of the years of the life of Abraham which he lived—a hundred and seventy-five years.
texts.gen.25.8: So Abraham breathed his last, and died in a fine old age, old and satisfied,—and was gathered unto his people,
texts.gen.25.9: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him, in the cave of Machpelah,—in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, which is over against Mamre;
texts.gen.25.10: the field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth,—there, was buried Abraham, with Sarah his wife.
texts.gen.25.11: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed Isaac his son,—and Isaac dwelt by Beer-lahai-roi.
texts.gen.25.12: Now, these, are the generations of Ishmael son of Abraham,—whom hagar the Egyptian woman the handmaid of Sarah bare to Abraham;
texts.gen.25.13: and these, are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names after their generations,—the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth, and Kedar and Adbeel and Mibsam;
texts.gen.25.14: and Mishma and Dumah, and Massa;
texts.gen.25.15: Hadad, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
texts.gen.25.16: these, same, are the sons of Ishmael and these, their names, by their villages and by their encampments,—twelve princes, after their tribes.
texts.gen.25.17: And these, are the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty-seven years,—and he breathed his last and died, and was gathered unto his people.
texts.gen.25.18: And they stretched their habitations from Havilah as far as to Shur, which is over against Egypt, as thou goest in towards Assyria,—over against all his brethren, he settled down.
texts.gen.25.19: And, these, are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham,—Abraham, begat Isaac;
texts.gen.25.20: and it came to pass that, Isaac, was forty years old, when he took Rebekah daughter of Bethuel the Syrian, of the Plain of Syria,—sister of Laban the Syrian. to himself to wife.
texts.gen.25.21: So then Isaac made entreaty unto Yahweh in behalf of his wife, for she was, barren,—and Yahweh suffered himself to be entreated by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
texts.gen.25.22: And the sons within her struggled together, so she said—If so, wherefore now am, I, [thus]? And she went to seek Yahweh.
texts.gen.25.23: And Yahweh said to her. Two nations, are in thy womb, And two races, from thy body, shall be parted,—And, one race, shall be stronger, than the other race, And the elder, shall serve the younger.
texts.gen.25.24: Then were fulfilled her days to bring forth,—and lo! twins in her womb.
texts.gen.25.25: And the first came forth red, all over, as a mantle of hair,—so they called his name, Esau,
texts.gen.25.26: And, after that, came forth his brother with his hand fast hold of the heel of Esau, so they called his name Jacob—Now, Isaac, was sixty years old when she bare them,
texts.gen.25.27: And when the youths grew up, it came to pass that Esau was a man skilled in game a man of the field,—but, Jacob, was a ready man, dwelling in tents.
texts.gen.25.28: And, Isaac, loved, Esau, because of the game he put in his mouth,—but, Rebekah, was a lover of Jacob!.
texts.gen.25.29: And Jacob had boiled pottage,—when Esau came in from the field, he, being famished.
texts.gen.25.30: So Esau said unto Jacob. Do let me devour some of the red—this red, for, famished, I am. For this cause, was his name called Edom.
texts.gen.25.31: And Jacob said,—Come sell, just now, thy birthright unto me.
texts.gen.25.32: And Esau said, Here am I, on the point of dying,—wherefore, then, should I, have, a birthright?
texts.gen.25.33: And Jacob said, Come swear to me just now! And he sware to him,—and sold his birthright to Jacob.
texts.gen.25.34: And Jacob, having given to Esau bread and a dish of lentils, he did eat and drink and rose up, and went his way,—thus Esau despised his birthright!
texts.gen.26.1: And there came to be a famine in the land, besides the first famine which happened in the days of Abraham,—so Isaac went his way unto Abimelech, king of the Philistines towards Gerar;
