texts.gen.26.2: and Yahweh appeared unto him, and said, do not go down towards Egypt,—Make thy habitation in the land, which I may name unto thee:
texts.gen.26.3: Sojourn in this land, that I may be with thee and bless thee,—for, to thee, and to thy seed, will I give all these lands, So will I establish the oath which I sware to Abraham thy father;
texts.gen.26.4: and will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heavens, and will give to thy seed, all these lands,—And all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves in thy seed:
texts.gen.26.5: Because that Abraham hearkened unto my voice,—and so kept my charge, my commandments my statutes and my laws.
texts.gen.26.7: Then asked the men of the place as to his wife, and he said, My sister, is she,—For he feared to say My wife, lest [said he] the men of the place should slay me on account of Rebekah, for fair to look on, she is.
texts.gen.26.8: And it came to pass when the days had lengthened out to him there, that Abimelech king of the Philistines, looked out through the lattice of a window,—and he beheld and lo! Isaac—laughing with Rebekah his wife.
texts.gen.26.9: So Abimelech called for Isaac, and said, But lo she is, thy wife! How then, saidst thou, She is, my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because, I said, Lest I die on her account.
texts.gen.26.10: Then, said, Abimelech, What is this thou hast done to us? A little more, and one of the people might have lien with thy wife, so shouldst thou have brought upon us, guilt.
texts.gen.26.11: And Abimelech commanded all the people saying,—He that toucheth this man or his wife, shall surely be put to death
texts.gen.26.12: And Isaac sowed in that land, and found in the same year, a hundredfold,—seeing that Yahweh had blessed him.
texts.gen.26.13: So the man waxed great,—and went on and on waxing great until that he had waxed exceeding great.
texts.gen.26.14: So he came to have possessions of flocks and possessions of herds, and a large body of servants,—and the Philistines envied him.
texts.gen.26.15: And as for all the wells which the servants of his father digged, in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped them up, and filled them with dust.
texts.gen.26.16: And Abimelech said unto Isaac,—Get thee from us, for thou hast become far mightier than we.
texts.gen.26.17: So Isaac went from thence,—and encamped in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
texts.gen.26.18: And Isaac again digged the wells of water which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father, and which the Philistines stopped up after the death of Abraham,—and he called their names, after the names which his father called them.
texts.gen.26.19: And Isaac’s servants digged in the valley,—and found there a well of living water.
texts.gen.26.20: And the herdmen of Gerar disputed with the herdmen of Isaac saying, Ours, is the, water! So he called the name of the well Esek, because they had stirred up a quarrel with him.
texts.gen.26.21: And they digged another well, and they disputed over that also,—so he called the name thereof Sitnah.
texts.gen.26.22: And he moved on from thence and digged another well, and they disputed not for it,—so he called the name thereof. Rehoboth, and said, For, now, hath Yahweh made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
texts.gen.26.23: And he went up from thence, to Beer-sheba.
texts.gen.26.24: And Yahweh appeared unto him the same night, and said, I, am the God of Abraham thy father,—Do not fear for with thee, am, I, And I will bless thee and multiply thy seed, For the sake of Abraham my servant.
texts.gen.26.25: So he builded there all altar and called on the name of Yahweh, and spread out there, his tent,—and the servants of Isaac cut out there a well.
texts.gen.26.26: And, Abimelech, came unto him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol, commander of his host.
texts.gen.26.27: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore have ye come in mite me, seeing that, ye, hated me, and sent me away from you?
texts.gen.26.28: And they said: We, saw plainly, that Yahweh was with thee, so we said, Let there be we pray thee an oath betwixt us both, betwixt us and thee,—and let us solemnise a covenant with thee:—
texts.gen.26.29: That, thou wilt not do wrong by us, according as we touched not thee, and according as we did by thee nothing but good, and then sent thee away in peace, thee who, now, art blessed of Yahweh!
texts.gen.26.30: So he made for them a banquet, and they did eat and drink,—
texts.gen.26.31: and rose up early in the morning, and took an oath each man to his brother, so Isaac let them go, and they departed from him in peace.
texts.gen.26.32: And it came to pass, on the same day, that the servants of Isaac came in, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said to him, We have found water!
texts.gen.26.33: So he called it, Shibah. For this cause, hath the name of the city, been Beer-sheba, unto this day.
texts.gen.26.34: And when Esau was forty years old, he took to wife Judith, daughter of Beeri. the Hittite; and Basemath, daughter of Elon, the Hittite;
texts.gen.26.35: and they became a bitterness of spirit, to Isaac and to Rebekah.
texts.gen.27.1: And it came to pass that Isaac, was old, and his eyes became too dim to see, so he called Esau his elder son and said unto him My son! And he said unto him, Behold me!
texts.gen.27.2: And he said, Behold, I pray thee, I am old,—I know not the day of my death.
texts.gen.27.3: Now, therefore, take I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and catch for me game;
texts.gen.27.4: and make for me dainty meats, such as I love and bring in to me, that I may eat,—To the end my soul may bless thee, ere yet I die!
texts.gen.27.5: Now, Rebekah, was hearkening, when Isaac spake unto Esau his son, and Esau went his way to the field, to catch game, to bring in.
texts.gen.27.6: Rebekah, therefore spake unto Jacob her son saying,—Lo! I heard thy father, speaking unto Esau thy brother, saying,
texts.gen.27.7: Bring in for me game and make for me dainty meats, that I may eat; and let me bless thee in the presence of Yahweh before my death.
texts.gen.27.8: Now, therefore my son, hearken unto my voice,—in that which I am commanding thee:
texts.gen.27.9: Go, I pray thee, unto the flock, and fetch me from thence two kids of the goats, fine ones,—that I may make of them dainty meats for thy father such as he loveth:
texts.gen.27.10: Then shalt thou take them in unto thy father and he shall eat,—To the end he may bless thee before his death.
texts.gen.27.11: And Jacob said unto Rebekah his mother, Lo! Esau my brother, is a hairy man, whereas, I, am a smooth man:
texts.gen.27.12: peradventure my father might feel me, then should I be in his eyes as one that mocketh,—and should bring upon myself a reproach, and not a blessing!
texts.gen.27.13: And his mother said to him, Upon me, be thy reproach my son,—only hearken unto my voice and go fetch [them] for me.
texts.gen.27.14: So he went, and fetched [them], and brought them in to his mother, and his mother made dainty meats, such as his father loved.
texts.gen.27.15: Then took Rebekah the garments of Esau her elder son, the costly ones, which were with her in the house,—and put them on Jacob her younger son:
texts.gen.27.16: and the, skins of the kids of the goats, put she upon his hands,—and on the smooth part of his neck;
texts.gen.27.17: then placed she the dainty meats and the bread, which she had made ready, in the hand of Jacob her son.
texts.gen.27.18: So he went in unto his father, and said My father! And he said Behold me! who art, thou, my son?
texts.gen.27.19: And Jacob said unto his father I, am Esau thy firstborn, I have made ready, as thou didst bid me. Rise, I pray thee, sit up, and eat thou of my game, To the end thy soul may bless me.
texts.gen.27.20: Then said Isaac unto his son. How is it thou hast been so quick in finding, my son? And he said, Because Yahweh thy God caused it so to fall out before me.
texts.gen.27.21: Then said Isaac unto Jacob. Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee my son—whether, thou thyself, art my son Esau, or not.
texts.gen.27.22: So Jacob came near unto Isaac his father, and he felt him; then said he the voice is the voice of Jacob; But, the hands, are the hands of Esau.
texts.gen.27.23: So he did not find him out, because, his hands were like the hands of Esau his brother hairy,—so he blessed him.
texts.gen.27.24: And he said, Thou thyself, art my son Esau? And he said, I am!
texts.gen.27.25: So he said, Bring it near to me., that I may eat of the game of my son, To the end my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat, and he brought in to him wine, and he drank.
texts.gen.27.26: Then Isaac his father said unto him,—Come thou near I pray thee and kiss me my son.
texts.gen.27.27: So he came near, and kissed him, and he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him,—and said. See! the smell of my son, As the smell of a field, which Yahweh hath blessed;
texts.gen.27.28: Then, may God give thee of the dew of the heavens, And of the fatness of the earth,—And abundance of corn and new wine:
texts.gen.27.29: Let peoples serve thee And races bow down to thee, Become thou lord to thy brethren, And let the sons of thy mother bow down to thee,—He that curseth thee, be accursed! And he that blesseth thee, be blessed!
texts.gen.27.30: And it came to pass as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob,—yea it came to pass when Jacob, had only just gone forth, from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother, came in from his hunting.
texts.gen.27.31: Then, he too, made dainty meats, and brought in to his father,—and said to his father, Let my father rise that he may eat of the game of his son, To the end thy soul may bless me!
texts.gen.27.32: And Isaac his father said to him Who art, thou? And he said, I, am thy son thy firstborn, Esau.
texts.gen.27.33: Then did Isaac tremble with an exceeding great trembling, and said Who then was it that caught game and brought in to me and I did eat of all ere yet thou didst come in and I blessed him? Yea blessed, shall he remain!
texts.gen.27.34: When Esau heard the words of his father, then cried he out with an outcry loud and bitter exceedingly,—and said to his father, Bless even me also, O my father!
texts.gen.27.35: Then he said, Thy brother came in with deceit,—and took away thy blessing.
texts.gen.27.36: And he said, Is it because his name, is called, Jacob, that he hath tricked me, now twice? My birthright, he took away, And lo! now, he hath taken away my blessing! And he said, Hast thou not reserved for me a blessing?
texts.gen.27.37: Then answered Isaac and said to Esau,—Lo a lord, have I appointed him unto thee, And, all his brethren, have I given to him as servants, And with corn and new wine, have I sustained him,—And for thee—now, what can I do, my son?
texts.gen.27.38: And Esau said unto his father, But one blessing, hast thou, O my father? Bless, me also, O my father! And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
texts.gen.27.39: Then answered Isaac his father and said unto him,—Lo! of the fat parts of the earth, shall be thy dwelling, And of the dew of the heavens, above;
texts.gen.27.40: And on thy sword, shalt thou live, And thy brother, shalt thou serve: But it shall come to pass when thou shalt rove at large, Then shalt thou break his yoke from off thy neck.
texts.gen.27.41: And Esau lay in wait for Jacob, on account of the blessing wherewith his father had blessed him,—and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father draw near, when I can slay Jacob my brother.
texts.gen.27.42: Then were told to Rebekah, the words of Esau her elder son, so she sent and called for Jacob, her younger son, and said unto him—Lo! Esau, thy brother, is consoling himself as touching thee, to slay thee.
texts.gen.27.43: Now, therefore, my son, hearken to my voice,—and rise flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
texts.gen.27.44: And thou shalt dwell with him a few days,—until that the wrath of thy brother turn away:
texts.gen.27.45: until the turning away of the anger of thy brother from thee, and he forget what thou hast done to him, and I send and fetch thee from thence. Wherefore should I lose, you both, in one day?
texts.gen.27.46: So then Rebekah said unto Isaac, I am disgusted with my life because of the daughters of Heth,—Should Jacob be taking a wife of the daughters of Heth, like these, of the daughters of the land, wherefore could I wish for life?
texts.gen.28.1: Then Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him,—and commanded him and said to him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
texts.gen.28.2: Rise, go thy way to Padan-aram to the house of Bethuel, thy mother’s father,—and take thee from thence a wife, of the daughters of Laban, thy mother’s brother.
texts.gen.28.3: And, GOD Almighty, bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, so shalt thou become a multitude of peoples.
texts.gen.28.4: And may he give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee,—that thou mayest possess the land of thy sojournings, which God gave to Abraham.
texts.gen.28.5: So Isaac sent away Jacob, and he took his journey to Padan-aram,—unto Laban son of Bethuel, the Syrian, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.
texts.gen.28.6: And Esau beheld that Isaac, when he blessed Jacob, and sent him to Padan-aram, to take to himself from thence a wife, that in blessing him, he laid command upon him, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
texts.gen.28.7: And that Jacob hearkened unto his father and unto his mother,—and took his journey to Padan-aram.
texts.gen.28.8: So then Esau beheld that displeasing, were the daughters of Caanan,—in the eyes of Isaac his father:
texts.gen.28.9: Esau therefore went unto Ishmael,—and took Mahalath daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham sister of Nebaioth, to himself to wife, in addition to the wives that he had.
texts.gen.28.10: So Jacob went forth from Beer-sheba, and journeyed towards Haran.
texts.gen.28.11: And he lighted on a place, and tarried the night there, because the sun had gone in,—and he took of the stones of the place, and put for his pillow, and lay down in that place,
texts.gen.28.12: And he dreamed, and lo! a stairway, planted earthwards, with, its top, reaching towards the heavens,—and lo! messengers of God, ascending and descending thereon;
texts.gen.28.13: and lo! Yahweh, standing by him,—and he said, I, am Yahweh, God of Abraham thy father and God of Isaac,—The land whereon, thou, art lying, to thee, will I give it and to thy seed;
texts.gen.28.14: And thy seed shall become as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt break forth westward and eastward, and northward and southward,—And all the families of the ground shall be blessed in thee and in thy seed.
texts.gen.28.15: Lo! then, I, am with thee, so will I keep thee in every place whithersoever thou mayest go, and will bring thee back unto this soil,—For I will not forsake thee until I have done that of which I have spoken to thee.
texts.gen.28.16: And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and said. Surely, Yahweh was in this place, And I, knew it not.
texts.gen.28.17: And he feared and said, How fearful is this place! None other this, than the house of God! Nor this than the gate of the heavens
texts.gen.28.18: So Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone which he had put for his pillow, and put it for a pillar,—and poured out oil upon the top thereof;
texts.gen.28.19: and called the name of that place—Beth-el,—nevertheless, Luz, was the name of the city, aforetime.
texts.gen.28.20: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying,—If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way whereon, I, am going, and give me bread to eat and raiment to put on;
texts.gen.28.21: and I come back in prosperity unto the house of my father, Then will Yahweh prove to be my God,—
texts.gen.28.22: And, this stone which I have put for a pillar, shall be the house of God,—And, of all which thou shalt give me, a tenth, will I tithe unto thee.
texts.gen.29.1: Then Jacob lifted up his feet,—and went his way towards the land of the sons of the East.
texts.gen.29.2: And he looked, and lo! a well, in the field and lo! there, three flocks of sheep, lying down near it, for out of that well, do they water the flocks, but, the stone, is great, on the mouth of the well:
texts.gen.29.3: so they gather together thither all the flocks, and roll away the stone from off the mouth of the well, and water the sheep,—and put back the stone upon the mouth of the well, to its place.
texts.gen.29.4: And Jacob said to them, My brethren, whence are ye? And they said: From haran, are we.
texts.gen.29.5: And he said to them, Know ye Laban, son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.
texts.gen.29.6: And he said to them, Is it well with him? And they said, Well, but lo! Rachel his daughter, coming in with the sheep.
texts.gen.29.7: And he said Lo! the day is yet high, it is not time for gathering together the cattle,—water the sheep, and go feed.
texts.gen.29.8: And they said, We cannot, until that all the flocks are gathered together, and they roll away the stone, from off the mouth of the well,—and then can we water the sheep.
texts.gen.29.9: While yet he was speaking with them, Rachel, had come in with the sheep which belonged to her father, for a shepherdess, was she.
texts.gen.29.10: And it came to pass when Jacob saw Rachel daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled away the stone from off the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother,
texts.gen.29.11: And Jacob kissed Rachel,—and lifted up his voice, and wept.
texts.gen.29.12: And when Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rebekah’s son, then ran she, and told her father.
texts.gen.29.13: And it came to pass when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fondly kissed him, and brought him into his house,—when he recounted to Laban all these things.
texts.gen.29.14: And Laban said to him, Surely, my bone and my flesh, art thou. So he abode with him a month of days.
texts.gen.29.15: Then said Laban to Jacob, Is it because my brother, thou art, that thou shouldst serve me for naught? Come tell me! What shall be thy wages?
texts.gen.29.16: Now, Laban, had two daughters,—the name of the elder, Leah, and the name of the younger, Rachel,
texts.gen.29.17: But, the eyes of Leah were weak,—whereas, Rachel, was comely in form and comely in countenance.
texts.gen.29.18: So Jacob loved Rachel,—and he said, I will serve thee seven years, for Rachel thy younger daughter.
texts.gen.29.19: And Laban said, Better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man,—Abide with me!
texts.gen.29.20: So Jacob served for Rachel—seven years,—and they became, in his eyes, as single days, for his love to her.
texts.gen.29.21: Then said Jacob unto Laban: Come give me my wife, for fulfilled are my days,—that I may go in unto her.
texts.gen.29.22: So Laban gathered together all the men of the place and made a banquet,
texts.gen.29.23: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter and brought her in unto him,—and he went in unto her.
texts.gen.29.24: And Laban gave her Zilpah, his handmaid, unto Leah his daughter. as handmaid.
texts.gen.29.25: And it came to pass in the morning, that lo! it was Leah,—and he said unto Laban, What is this thou hast done to me? Was it not, for Rachel, I served with thee? Wherefore then hast thou deceived me?
texts.gen.29.26: And Laban said, It must not be done so in our place,—to give the later-born before the firstborn.
texts.gen.29.27: Fulfil the week of this one,—then must we give thee, the other one also, for the service wherewith thou shalt serve with me, yet seven years more.
texts.gen.29.28: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled the week of this one,—and he gave him Rachel his daughter—to him to wife.
texts.gen.29.29: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid,—to be hers as a handmaid.
texts.gen.29.30: So he went in, unto Rachel also, and loved, Rachel also, more than Leah,—and he served with him, yet seven years more.
texts.gen.29.31: And, when Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, he granted her to bear children,—whereas, Rachel, was barren.
texts.gen.29.32: So Leah conceived, and bare a son, and called his name Reuben,—for she said, Because, Yahweh hath looked upon my humiliation, For, now, will my husband love me.
texts.gen.29.33: And she conceived again, and bare a son, and said. Because Yahweh heard that, I, was hated, he gave me, this one also. So she called his name Simeon.
texts.gen.29.34: And she conceived again and bare a son, and said, Now—this time, will my husband be bound unto me, For I have borne him three sons,—For this cause, called she his name Levi.
texts.gen.29.35: And she conceived again and bare a son, and said This time, will I praise Yahweh, For which cause, she called his name Judah. And she left off bearing.
texts.gen.30.1: And Rachel saw she had borne no children unto Jacob, so Rachel became envious of her sister,—and said unto Jacob, Come! give me children, or else, I die.
texts.gen.30.2: Then kindled the anger of Jacob with Rachel,—and he said, Am I, in the place of God, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?
texts.gen.30.3: And she said, Lo! my handmaid, Bilhah. Go in unto her,—that she may bear upon my knees, so that, I also, may be builded up by her!
texts.gen.30.4: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid, to wife,—and Jacob went in unto her;
texts.gen.30.5: and Bilhah conceived, and bare unto Jacob a son;
texts.gen.30.6: and Rachel said God hath vindicated me. Moreover also he hath hearkened unto my voice, and hath given me a son. For this cause, called she his name Dan.
texts.gen.30.7: And Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid conceived again, and bare a second son to Jacob.
texts.gen.30.8: Then said Rachel With wrestlings of God, have I wrestled with my sister Yea I have prevailed. So she called his name, Naphtali.
texts.gen.30.9: Then saw Leah, that she had left off bearing,—so she took Zilpah, her handmaid, and gave her to Jacob to wife.
texts.gen.30.10: And Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, bare to Jacob a son:
texts.gen.30.11: and Leah said, Victory hath come! So she called his name Gad.
texts.gen.30.12: And Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid bare a second son to Jacob;
texts.gen.30.13: and Leah said, For my happiness, surely happy have daughters pronounced me. So she called his name, Asher.
texts.gen.30.14: Then went Reuben, in the days of the wheat harvest, and found mandrakes, in the field, and brought them in unto Leah his mother, and Rachel said unto Leah, Pray give me, some of the mandrakes of thy son
texts.gen.30.15: And she said to her, Is it, a small thing, that thou hast taken away my husband? And wouldst thou take away, even the mandrakes of my son? Then said Rachel, Therefore, shall he lie with thee to-night, for the mandrakes of thy son.
texts.gen.30.16: And Jacob came in from the field, in the evening, so Leah went out to meet him and said: Unto me, shalt thou come in, for I have hired, thee, even with the mandrakes of my son. And he lay with her that night,
texts.gen.30.17: And God hearkened unto Leah,—and she conceived and bare to Jacob a fifth son.
texts.gen.30.18: Then said Leah. God hath given my hire, in that I gave my handmaid to my husband. So she called his name, Issachar.
texts.gen.30.19: And Leah conceived again and bare a sixth son to Jacob.
texts.gen.30.20: Then said Leah, God hath dowered me even me with a hand-some dowry, Now! will my husband dwell with me, for I have borne him six sons. So she called his name, Zebulon.
texts.gen.30.21: And afterwards she bare a daughter,—so she called her name, Dinah.
texts.gen.30.22: Then God remembered Rachel,—and God hearkened unto her, and granted her to bear.
texts.gen.30.23: So she conceived and bare a son,—and said, God hath taken away my reproach;
texts.gen.30.24: So she called his name Joseph, saying, Yahweh is adding unto me another son.
texts.gen.30.25: And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban, Let me go that I may take my journey, unto my place, and to my land.
texts.gen.30.26: Come, give me my wives and my children for whom I have served thee and let me take my journey,—for, thou, knowest my service wherewith I have served thee.
texts.gen.30.27: And Laban said unto him, If, I pray thee, I have found favour in thine eyes, …I have divined that Yahweh hath blessed me for thy sake.
texts.gen.30.28: And he said,—Come, fix thy wages for me, that I may give it!
texts.gen.30.29: And he said unto him, Thou, knowest how I have served thee,—and how thy cattle have fared, with me.
texts.gen.30.30: For it was, little, that thou hadst—before I came and then it brake forth into multitude, and Yahweh blessed thee at my every step. Now, therefore, when am, I, also to do something for my own house?
texts.gen.30.31: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said: Thou shall give me, nothing at all, If thou wilt do for me this thing, I will return, I will shepherd thy flock I will keep it:
texts.gen.30.32: Let me pass through all thy flock to-day, removing from thence every young one that is speckled and spotted and every young one that is dark-coloured among the young sheep, and spotted and speckled among the goats, and they shall be my wages.
texts.gen.30.33: And my righteousness shall answer for me on a future day, when thou shall come in respecting my hire that is before thee, Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats and dark-coloured among the young sheep, stolen, shall it be accounted, if found with me.
texts.gen.30.34: Then said Laban, Lo! would it might be according to thy word!
texts.gen.30.35: So he removed, on that day, the he-goats that were striped and spotted and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and every dark-coloured one among the young sheep,—and delivered them into the hand of his sons;
texts.gen.30.36: then put he a journey of three days between himself and Jacob,—but, Jacob himself, continued tending the flocks of Laban that were left.
texts.gen.30.37: So then Jacob took him rods of young storax, and hazel and maple,—and peeled in them white stripes, laying bare the white which was on the rods.
texts.gen.30.38: And he set the rods which he had peeled, in the channels in the troughs of water,—where the flocks came in to drink straight before the flocks, and the females of the flock used to be in heat when they came in to drink;
texts.gen.30.39: and the males of the flock were in heat before the rods,—so the flocks brought forth ring-straked, speckled, and spotted.
texts.gen.30.40: The rams also, did Jacob separate, and then set the faces of the flocks towards the ring-straked and all the dark-coloured, among the flocks of Laban,—and he put his own droves by themselves, and put them not with the flocks of Laban.
texts.gen.30.41: So it came to pass whensoever the stronger of the flocks were in heat, that Jacob set the rods before the eyes of the flocks in the channels,—that the females might be in heat among the rods;
texts.gen.30.42: but, when the flocks were late in bearing, he did not set them,—and so the late-born were Laban’s, but the strong ones Jacob’s.
texts.gen.30.43: Thus did the man break forth, exceedingly,—thus came he to have flocks in abundance, and maid-servants, and men-servants and camels and asses.
texts.gen.31.1: Then heard he the words of the sons of Laban, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that belonged to our father; Yea out of what belonged to our father, hath he made all this wealth.
texts.gen.31.2: And Jacob looked upon the face of Laban,—and lo! it was not with him as afore-time.
texts.gen.31.3: Then said Yahweh unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers and to thy kindred,—that I may be with thee.
texts.gen.31.4: So Jacob sent, and called for Rachel and for Leah, to the field unto his flock;
texts.gen.31.5: and said to them, Beholding, am I the face of your father, that it is not towards me as aforetime,—nevertheless, the God of my father, hath been with me;
texts.gen.31.6: and, ye, know that with all my vigour, have I served your father.
texts.gen.31.7: But, your father, hath deceived me, and hath changed my wages ten times,—yet God hath not suffered him to deal harmfully with me.
texts.gen.31.8: If thus he saith, The speckled, shall be thy wages, then do all the flock bring forth speckled,—But if thus he saith, The ring-straked, shall be thy wages, then do all the flock bring forth ring-straked.
texts.gen.31.9: So hath God stripped away the herds of your father, and given them to me.
texts.gen.31.10: And it came to pass in the season when the flock were in heat, then lifted I mine eyes and beheld in a dream,—and lo! the he-goats that were leaping upon the flock, were ring-straked speckled and dappled.
texts.gen.31.11: And the messenger of God said unto me in a dream, Jacob! and I said, Behold me!
texts.gen.31.12: Then he said Lift, I pray thee, thine eyes and behold All, the he-goats that are leaping upon the flock are ring-straked, speckled, and dappled,—for I have seen all that Laban, has been doing to thee.
texts.gen.31.13: I, am the GOD of Beth-el, where thou didst anoint a pillar, where thou didst vow to me a vow,—Now, rise, go forth out of this land, and return unto the land of thy kindred.
texts.gen.31.14: Then responded Rachel and Leah, and said to him,—Have we any longer a portion or an inheritance in the house of our father?
texts.gen.31.15: Are we not accounted, aliens, to him seeing that having sold us, he hath then gone on devouring, our silver?
texts.gen.31.16: Surely all the riches which God hath stripped off from our father, unto us, it belongeth, and unto our sons,—Now, therefore, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do.
texts.gen.31.17: So Jacob arose,—and mounted his sons and his wives on the camels;
texts.gen.31.18: and drave away all his herds and all his goods which he had gathered, the gains he had gained, which he had gathered in Padan-aram; that he might go in unto Isaac his father unto the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.31.19: Now, Laban, had gone, to shear his sheep,—so Rachel stole the household gods that belonged to her father,
texts.gen.31.20: Thus Jacob stole away unawares to Laban, the Syrian,—in that he had not told him that he was about to flee.
texts.gen.31.21: So he fled, he—and all that he had, and he arose, and passed over the River,—and set his face towards the mountain of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.22: And it was told Laban, on the third day,—that Jacob had fled.
texts.gen.31.23: So he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him a journey of seven days—and overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.24: And God went in unto Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night,—and said to him Take heed to thyself that thou speak not with Jacob either good or bad.
texts.gen.31.25: So then Laban came up with Jacob,—Jacob, having pitched his tent in the mountain, Laban, also, with his brethren pitched in the mountain of Gilead.
texts.gen.31.26: Then said Laban to Jacob, What hadst thou done, that thou shouldst steal away unawares to me,—and shouldst carry off my daughters, as captives of the sword?
texts.gen.31.27: Wherefore didst thou secretly flee, and rob me,—and didst not tell me, that I might send thee away with rejoicing and with songs, with timbrel and with lyre;
texts.gen.31.28: and didst not suffer me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now, hast thou done, foolishly.
texts.gen.31.29: It is in the power of my hand, to deal with thee for harm,—but the God of your father, last night, spake unto me, saying, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not with Jacob, either good or bad.
texts.gen.31.30: But, now, though thou, didst even take thy journey, because thou, didst sorely long, for the house of thy father, wherefore didst thou steal away my gods?
texts.gen.31.31: And Jacob answered and said unto Laban,—Because I was afraid, for I said, Lest thou take by force thy daughters from me!
texts.gen.31.32: He with whom thou find thy gods, shall not live! Before our brethren, note thou for thyself what is with me and take what is thine. Neither did Jacob know that, Rachel, had stolen them.
texts.gen.31.33: Then entered Laban into the tent of Jacob and into the tent of Leah and into the tent of the two handmaids, and found nothing,—then went he forth out of the tent of Leah, and entered into the tent of Rachel.
texts.gen.31.34: Now Rachel, had taken the household gods and put them in the basket-saddle of the camel, and taken her seat upon them. And Laban felt about throughout all the tent, and found them not.
texts.gen.31.35: And she said unto her father, Let it not be vexing in the eyes of my lord that I cannot rise up at thy presence, for, the way of women, is upon me. So he made search, but found not the household gods,
texts.gen.31.36: And it was vexing to Jacob and he contended with Laban,—and Jacob responded and said to Laban, What was my trespass, what my sin, that thou shouldst have come burning after me?
texts.gen.31.37: Now that thou hast felt about among all my goods, what hast thou found of the goods of thine own house? Set it out here, right before my brethren and thy brethren,—that they may give sentence betwixt us two.
texts.gen.31.38: This twenty years’ time, have, I, been with thee—Thy ewes and thy she-goats, have not cast their young,—And the rams of thy flock, have I not eaten,
texts.gen.31.39: The torn, have I not brought in unto thee—I bare the loss, At my hand, didst thou require it,—Stolen by day, or stolen by night.
texts.gen.31.40: Thus have I been—By day, drought hath consumed me, And, frost, by, night,—So that my sleep fled away from mine eyes.
texts.gen.31.41: This, hath been my lot twenty years in thy house,—I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, And six years for thy sheep—And thou didst change my wages ten times:—
texts.gen.31.42: But that the God of my father—The God of Abraham, and the Dread of Isaac—Proved to be mine, Surely even now, empty, hadst thou let me go? My humiliation and the wearying toil of my hands, God had seen, And therefore gave sentence last night!
texts.gen.31.43: Then responded Laban and said unto Jacob—the daughters, are my daughters, And the sons, are my sons, And the sheep are my sheep, And, all that, thou, beholdest, To me doth it belong! But to my daughters, what can I do to these this day, Or to their sons whom they have borne?
texts.gen.31.44: Now, therefore, come on! Let us solemnise a covenant, I and thou,—So shall it be a witness betwixt me and thee.
texts.gen.31.45: So Jacob took a stone,—and set it up as a pillar.
texts.gen.31.46: Then said Jacob to his brethren—Gather stones. And they took stones and made a heap,—and they did eat there, by the heap.
texts.gen.31.47: And Laban called it, Jegar-sahadutha,—but, Jacob, called it, Galeed.
texts.gen.31.48: Then said Laban: This heap, be witness betwixt me, and thee, to-day. For this cause, is the name thereof called Galeed;
texts.gen.31.49: also, The Watch Tower, as to which it is said, Yahweh watch betwixt me and thee, when we are parted one from another.
texts.gen.31.50: If thou oppress my daughters, or if thou take wives besides my daughters,—there may be no man with us—see! God, be witness betwixt me, and thee!
texts.gen.31.51: And Laban said to Jacob—Behold this heap, and behold this pillar, which I have set betwixt me, and thee:
texts.gen.31.52: A witness, be this heap, and, a witness, the pillar,—That, I, am not to pass, unto thee, over this heap, And, thou, art not to pass, unto me, over this heap and this pillar for harm.
texts.gen.31.53: The Gods of Abraham and the Gods of Nahor judge betwixt us—the Gods of their fathers. And Jacob sware by the Dread of his father Isaac:
texts.gen.31.54: and Jacob offered sacrifice in the mountain, and called on his brethren to eat bread. So they did eat bread, and tarried the night in the mountain.
texts.gen.31.55: And Laban rose up early in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them: and Laban went his way and returned to his place.
texts.gen.32.1: When, Jacob, had gone on his way, there met him, messengers of God.
texts.gen.32.2: And Jacob said, when he saw them, the camp of God, is this! So he called the name of that place, Mahanaim.
texts.gen.32.3: Then did Jacob send messengers before him unto Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
texts.gen.32.4: And he commanded them, saying, Thus, shall ye say to my lord to Esau, Thus, saith thy servant Jacob, With Laban, have I sojourned, and tarried until now:
texts.gen.32.5: And I have oxen and asses, flocks and men-servants, and maid-servants, So I must needs send to tell my lord, that I might find favour in thine eyes.
texts.gen.32.6: And the messengers returned unto Jacob, saying,—We came in unto thy brother unto Esau, moreover also he is on his way to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.
texts.gen.32.7: Then was Jacob greatly afraid, and in distress. So he divided the people that were with him and the flocks and the herds and the camels into two camps,
texts.gen.32.8: And he said. Should Esau come upon the one camp, and smite it, yet shall the camp that is left escape.
texts.gen.32.9: And Jacob said, God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac,—Yahweh, who wast saying unto me,—Return to thy land and to thy kindred that I may deal well with thee:
texts.gen.32.10: I am too small for all the lovingkindnesses and for all the faithfulness, which thou hast done unto thy servant,—For with my staff, passed I over this Jordan, But, now, have I become two camps.
texts.gen.32.11: Deliver me I pray thee out of the hand of my brother out of the hand of Esau, for I, am afraid of him, lest he come in and smite mother as well as sons
texts.gen.32.12: But, thou thyself, saidst,—I will deal well with thee. So will I make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which is not to be counted, for multitude.
texts.gen.32.13: And he tarried there that night, and took of that which came to his hand a present for Esau his brother:
texts.gen.32.14: She-goats, two hundred; And he-goats, twenty; Ewes, two hundred; And rams, twenty;
texts.gen.32.15: Milch camels, with their colts, thirty; Cows, forty; And bulls, ten; She-asses, twenty; And young he asses ten.
texts.gen.32.16: And he gave them into the hand of his Servants, each drove by itself, and said unto his servants—Pass over before me, and, a breathing-space, shall ye put betwixt drove and drove.
texts.gen.32.17: And he commanded the first one saying: When Esau my brother shall fall in with thee, and shall ask thee, saying Whose art thou? and whither wouldst thou go? and to whom belong these before thee?
texts.gen.32.18: then shalt thou say, To thy servant Jacob: It is, a present, sent to my lord, to Esau; And behold he himself also is behind us,
texts.gen.32.19: And he commanded the second also, and the third yea all that were going on behind the droves, saying,—According to this word, shall ye speak unto Esau, when ye find him.
texts.gen.32.20: Then shall ye say, Also, lo! thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said: I must pacify him with the present that goeth on before me. And, after that, will I see his face: Peradventure he will accept me.
texts.gen.32.21: So the present passed over before him,—whereas he himself tarried that night in the camp.
texts.gen.32.22: And he arose in that night and took his two wives, and his two handmaids, and his eleven sons,—and passed over the ford of Jabbok.
texts.gen.32.23: So he took them, and sent them over the brook,—and sent over that which he had.
texts.gen.32.24: And Jacob was left alone,—and there wrestled a man with him, until the uprisings of the dawn.
texts.gen.32.25: And when he saw, that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh,—and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was put out of joint, as he wrestled with him.
texts.gen.32.26: Then said he—Let me go, for uprisen hath the dawn. And he said: I will not let thee go, except thou have blessed me
texts.gen.32.27: Then he said unto him—What is thy name? And he said—Jacob.
texts.gen.32.28: Then he said—Not Jacob, shall thy name be called any more, but Israel,—For thou hast contended with God and with men and hast prevailed.
texts.gen.32.29: Then asked Jacob and said, Do, I pray thee, tell me thy name! And he said—Wherefore now, shouldest thou ask for my name? And he blessed him there,
texts.gen.32.30: So Jacob called the name of the place Peniel; For I saw God face to face; and my soul was delivered,
texts.gen.32.31: And the sun rose on him as soon as he had passed over Penuel,—he, moreover was halting upon his thigh,
texts.gen.32.32: For this cause, the sons of Israel eat not of the nerve of the large hip-sinew, which is by the hollow of the thigh, until this day,—because he touched the hollow of the thigh of Jacob, in the nerve of the hip-sinew.
texts.gen.33.1: Then Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and lo! Esau, coming in,—and with him, four hundred men. So he divided the children—unto Leah and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids;
texts.gen.33.2: and put the handmaids and their children first,—and Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph next;
texts.gen.33.3: but he himself, passed over before them, and bowed himself to the earth seven times, until he had come near unto his brother.
texts.gen.33.4: Then ran Esau to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck,—and they wept.
texts.gen.33.5: Then lifted he up his eyes, and beheld the women and the children, and said What are these to thee? And he said—The children wherewith God hath favoured thy servant,
texts.gen.33.6: Then came near the handmaids, they—and their children,—and bowed themselves.
texts.gen.33.7: Then came near Leah also with her children,—and they bowed themselves. And afterwards, came near Joseph with Rachel, and they bowed themselves,
texts.gen.33.8: Then said he, What to thee is all this camp, which I have fallen in with? And he said,—To find favour in the eyes of my lord.
texts.gen.33.9: Then said Esau, I have an abundance,—my brother, be thine what thou hast!
texts.gen.33.10: Then said Jacob, Nay, I pray thee, if, I pray thee, I have found favour in thine eyes, then thou wilt take my present at my hand,—For on this account, hath my seeing thy face been like seeing the face of God in that thou wast well-pleased with me.
texts.gen.33.11: Take, I pray thee my blessing which hath been brought in to thee, because God hath shewed me favour and because I have everything. So he was urgent with him and he took it.
texts.gen.33.12: Then he said, Let us break up and go, and let me go on before thee.
texts.gen.33.13: And he said unto him, My lord, is taking note, that, the children are tender,—and the flocks and the herds are giving suck with me,—and, should I overdrive them a single day, then would all the flocks die.
texts.gen.33.14: Let my lord, I pray thee pass over before his servant, and let, me, lead on in my own easy way, at the pace of the cattle that are before me, and at the pace of the children, until that I come in unto my lord, towards Seir.
texts.gen.33.15: Then said Esau: Let me leave, I pray thee, along with thee, some of the people who are with me! And he said—Why so? let me find favour in the eyes of my lord!
texts.gen.33.16: So Esau returned, that day, to his journey towards Mount Seir.
texts.gen.33.17: But, Jacob, brake up towards Succoth, and built for himself a house, for his cattle, made he places of shelter, for which cause, the name of the place was called, Succoth.
texts.gen.33.18: And Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan,—when he came in from Padan-aram,—and he encamped before the city.
texts.gen.33.19: And he bought the portion of the field where he had spread out his tent, at the hand of the sons of Hamor, father of Shechem,—for a hundred kesitahs.
texts.gen.33.20: And he set up there an altar,—and called it, El-elohe-Israel.
texts.gen.34.1: Then went forth Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob,—to see the daughters of the land.
texts.gen.34.2: And Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the land, saw her,—so he took her, and lay with her, and humbled her.
texts.gen.34.3: And his soul clave unto Dinah, daughter of Jacob,—and he loved the young woman, and spake to the heart of the young woman.
texts.gen.34.4: Then spake Shechem unto Hamor his father, saying,—Take me this girl to wife!
texts.gen.34.5: Now, Jacob, had heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter, but, his sons, happened to be with his cattle in the field,—so Jacob kept quiet until they came in.
texts.gen.34.6: Then came forth Hamor, father of Shechem, unto Jacob,—to speak with him.
texts.gen.34.7: Now the sons of Jacob came in from the field as soon as they heard, and the men were grieved, and it was vexing to them exceedingly,—for, a disgraceful deed, had he done with Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter, seeing that so, it should not be done.
texts.gen.34.8: So then Hamor spake with them saying—As for Shechem my son, his soul hath become attached to your daughter,—I pray you give her to him, to wife.
texts.gen.34.9: And exchange ye daughters with us in marriage,—your daughters, shall ye give to us, and our daughters, shall ye take to you.
texts.gen.34.10: And with us, shall ye dwell,—and, the land, shall be before you, tarry, and go through it, and get possessions therein.
texts.gen.34.11: Then said Shechem unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find favour in your eyes,—and, whatsoever ye may say unto me, will I give:
texts.gen.34.12: Heap on me, exceedingly, dowry and gift, and I will give, just as ye may say unto me,—but give me the young woman, to wife.
texts.gen.34.13: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and spake (because he had defiled Dinah their sister)—
texts.gen.34.14: and said unto them—We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man that is uncircumcised,—for a reproach, it would be to us.
texts.gen.34.15: Only herein, can we consent to you,—If ye will become like us, by circumcising to you every male,
texts.gen.34.16: then will we give our daughters to you, and your daughters, will we take to us,—and we will dwell with you, and become one people.
texts.gen.34.17: But if ye will not hearken unto us, to be circumcised, then will we take our daughter and be gone.
texts.gen.34.18: And their words looked fair in the eyes of Hamor,—and in the eyes of Shechem, Hamor’s son;
texts.gen.34.19: and the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter,—he, moreover being more honourable than all the house of his father.
texts.gen.34.20: So Hamor entered with Shechem his son into the gate of their city,—and they spake unto the men of their city, saying:
texts.gen.34.21: As for these men, in peace, they are with us—let them therefore dwell in the land and go through it, for, the land, lo! it is roomy on both hands before them,—their daughters, let us take to us for wives, and our daughters, let us give to them.
texts.gen.34.22: Only herein, will the men consent to us, to dwell with us, to become one people,—If we circumcise to us every male, even as they are circumcised.
texts.gen.34.23: Their herds and their substance, and all their beasts, shall they, not be, ours? Only, we must consent to them, that they may dwell with us.
texts.gen.34.24: And they hearkened unto Hamor, and unto Shechem his son, even all that were going forth out of the gate of his city,—and every male was circumcised, all that were going forth out of the gate of his city.
texts.gen.34.25: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Jacob Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, took each man his sword, and came in upon the city, boldly,—and slew every, male;
texts.gen.34.26: Hamor also, and Shechem his son, slew they with the edge of the sword,—and took Dinah out of the house of Shechem, and came forth,
texts.gen.34.27: The sons of Jacob, came in upon the slain and plundered the city,—because they had defiled their sister:
texts.gen.34.28: their flocks, and their herds and their asses,—and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field, they took;
texts.gen.34.29: and all their wealth and all their little ones, and their women, took they captive, and seized as plunder,—even all that was in their houses.
texts.gen.34.30: Then said Jacob unto Simeon and unto Levi—Ye have troubled me by making me odious among them that dwell in the land, among the Canaanites, and among the Perizzites,—I, having only men that may be counted, they will gather themselves, together against me and smite me,—and I shall be destroyed both I and my house.
texts.gen.34.31: And they said,—As with a harlot, was he to deal with our sister.
texts.gen.35.1: Then said God unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Bethel, and dwell there,—and make there an altar, to the GOD who appeared unto thee, when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
texts.gen.35.2: And Jacob said unto his house, and unto all who were with him,—Put away the gods of the alien which are in your midst, and purify yourselves, and change your garments;
texts.gen.35.3: And let us arise, and go up to Beth-el,—that I may make there an altar to the GOD who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way that I went.
texts.gen.35.4: So they gave unto Jacob all the gods of the alien which were in their hand, and the earrings which were in their ears,—and Jacob hid them under the oak, which was by Shechem.
texts.gen.35.5: And they brake up,—and it came to pass that the terror of God, was on the cities which were round about them, so that they pursued not after the sons of Jacob.
texts.gen.35.6: And Jacob came in towards Luz, which was in the land of Canaan, the same, is Beth-el,—he and all the people who were with him.
texts.gen.35.7: And he built there an altar, and called the place El-Beth-el,—because, there, God revealed himself unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother,
texts.gen.35.8: And Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse died, and was buried below Beth-el, under the oak,—so the name thereof was called, Allon-bacuth.
texts.gen.35.9: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came in from Padan-aram,—and blessed him.
texts.gen.35.10: And God said to him, Thy name, is Jacob,—Thy name shall no longer be called Jacob But, Israel, shall be thy name. So he called his name, Israel.
texts.gen.35.11: And God said to him—I, am GOD Almighty! Be fruitful and multiply, A nation, and a multitude of nations shall spring from thee,—And, kings, from thy loins, shall come forth;
texts.gen.35.12: And, the land which I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, To thee, will I give it,—And to thy seed after thee, will I give the land.
texts.gen.35.13: And God went up from him at the place where he had spoken with him.
texts.gen.35.14: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone,—and he poured out thereon a drink-offering, and poured thereon oil.
texts.gen.35.15: And Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him, Beth-el.
texts.gen.35.16: Then brake they up from Beth-el, and it came to pass when there was yet a stretch of country, to enter into Ephrath, that Rachel was in childbirth, and had hard-labour in her child-birth.
texts.gen.35.17: So it came to pass when she was in hard-labour in her child-birth, that the midwife said to her—Do not fear, for this also of thine, is, a son.
texts.gen.35.18: And it came to pass when her soul was going forth—for she died, that she called his name Ben-oni,—but, his father, called him, Ben-jamin.
texts.gen.35.19: So Rachel died,—and was buried on the way to Ephrath, the same, is Bethlehem.
texts.gen.35.20: And Jacob set up a pillar, over her grave,—the same, is—The Pillar of the Grave of Rachel until this day.
texts.gen.35.21: Then Israel brake up,—and spread his tent at a distance from Migdal Eder.
texts.gen.35.22: And it came to pass while Israel inhabited that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine; and Israel heard of it. And so the Sons of Israel came to be Twelve.
texts.gen.35.23: The sons of Leah, the firstborn of Jacob, Reuben,—And Simeon and Levi and Judah, and Issachar and Zebulon:
texts.gen.35.24: The sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin:
texts.gen.35.25: And the sons of Bilhah, handmaid of Rachel, Dan, and Naphtali:
texts.gen.35.26: And the sons of Zilpah, handmaid of Leah, Gad and Asher: These, are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him, in Padan-aram.
texts.gen.35.27: Then came Jacob unto Isaac his father, to Mamre, the city of Arba,—the same, is Hebron, where had sojourned Abraham and Isaac.
texts.gen.35.28: And the days of Isaac came to be—a hundred and eighty years.
texts.gen.35.29: And Isaac breathed his last, and died and was added unto his people, old, and satisfied with days,—and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.
texts.gen.36.1: Now these, are the generations of Esau the same, is Edom.
texts.gen.36.2: Esau, took his wives of the daughters of Canaan,—Even Adah, daughter of Elon, the Hittite, And Oholibamah daughter of Anah, son of Zibeon, the Hivite;
texts.gen.36.3: And Basemath daughter of Ishmael sister of Nebaioth.
texts.gen.36.4: So Adah bare to Esau, Eliphaz, and, Basemath, bare Reuel;
texts.gen.36.5: and Oholibamah, bare Jeush and Jalam and Korah. These, are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.36.6: Then took Esau his wives, and his sons, and his daughters and all the souls of his house, and his herds and all his beasts, and all his possessions whatsoever he had gathered in the land of Canaan,—and went into a land, away from the face of Jacob his brother,
texts.gen.36.7: For their substance had become too great for them to dwell together,—neither could the land of their sojournings sustain them, because of their herds,
texts.gen.36.8: So Esau dwelt in Mount Seir, Esau, is Edom.
texts.gen.36.9: And, these, are the generations of Esau father of Edom,—in Mount Seir.
texts.gen.36.10: These, are the name of the sons of Esau,—Eliphaz son of Adah wife of Esau, Reuel son of Basemath wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.11: Then came the sons of Eliphaz to be,—Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
texts.gen.36.12: Now, Timna, became the concubine of Eliphaz son of Esau, and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek. These, are the sons of Adah, wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.13: And, these, are the sons of Reuel, Nahath and Zerah Shammah and Mizzah,—These were the sons of Basemath wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.14: And, these, were the sons of Oholibamah daughter of Anah, son of Zibeon, wife of—Esau,—she bare to Esau Jeush, and Jalam, and Korah.
texts.gen.36.15: These, are the chiefs of the sons of Esau:—The sons of Eliphaz, firstborn of Esau,—Chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
texts.gen.36.16: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom, these, the sons of Adah.
texts.gen.36.17: And these, are the sons of Reuel, son of Esau—Chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah,—These are the chiefs of Reuel, in the land of Edom, these, the sons of Basemath wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.18: And these, are the sons of Oholibamah wife of Esau, Chief Jeush chief Jalam, chief Korah,—These are the chiefs of Oholibamah daughter of Anah wife of Esau.
texts.gen.36.19: These, are the sons of Esau, and, these, their chiefs—the same, is Edom.
texts.gen.36.20: These, are the sons of Seir, the Horite, who were dwelling in the land,—Lotan and Shobal and Zibeon and Anah;
texts.gen.36.21: and Dishon and Ezer and Dishan,—These, are the chiefs of the Horites the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
texts.gen.36.22: Then came the sons of Lotan to be, Hori and Hemam,—And, the sister of Lotan was Timna.
texts.gen.36.23: And, these, are the sons of Shobal, Alvan and Manahath, and Ebal,—Shepho, and Onam.
texts.gen.36.24: And, these, are the sons of Zibeon: Both Aiah and Anah,—The same, is the Anah that found the warm springs in the desert, as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father.
texts.gen.36.25: And these are the sons of Anah Dishon,—and Oholibamah, is daughter of Anah.
texts.gen.36.26: And, these, are the sons of Dishon,—Hemdan and Eshban, and Ithran and Cheran.
texts.gen.36.27: These, are the sons of Ezer,—Bilhan and Zaavan, and Akan.
texts.gen.36.28: These, are the sons of Dishan,—Uz and Aran.
texts.gen.36.29: These, are the chiefs of the Horites,—Chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah;
texts.gen.36.30: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan. These, are the chiefs of the Horites, after their chiefs in the land of Seir.
texts.gen.36.31: And, these, are the kings, who reigned in the land of Edom,—before there reigned a king of the sons of Israel:
texts.gen.36.32: There reigned in Edom, Bela, son of Beor,—and the name of his city, was Dinhabah.
texts.gen.36.33: Then died Bela,—and there reigned in his stead, Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah.
texts.gen.36.34: Then died Jobab,—and there reigned in his stead, Husham, from the land of the Temanites.
texts.gen.36.35: Then died Husham,—and there reigned in his stead, Hadad, son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, and, the name of his city, was Avith.
texts.gen.36.36: Then died Hadad,—and there reigned in his stead, Samlah from Masrekah.
texts.gen.36.37: Then died Samlah,—and there reigned in his stead, Shaul, from Rohoboth of the River.
texts.gen.36.38: Then died Shaul,—and there reigned in his stead, Baal-hanan, son of Achbor.
texts.gen.36.39: Then died Baal-hanan son of Achbor, and there reigned in his stead Hadar, and the name of his city, was Pau,—and, the name of his wife, Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
texts.gen.36.40: These then are the names of the chiefs of Esau after their families, after their places by their names,—Chief Timnah, chief Alvah chief Jetheth;
texts.gen.36.41: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon;
texts.gen.36.42: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar;
texts.gen.36.43: chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These, are the chiefs of Edom—after their dwellings in the land of their possession, the same, is Esau, father of Edom.
texts.gen.37.1: So Jacob dwelt in the land of the sojournings of his father,—in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.37.2: These, are the generations of Jacob—Joseph, when seventeen years old, was shepherding with his brethren among the flocks, and, he, being a youth, was with the sons of Bilhah and with the sons of Zilpah wives of his father,—so then Joseph brought in the talk about them—something bad, unto their father.
texts.gen.37.3: Now, Israel, loved Joseph more than any of his sons, because he was to him, the son of his old age, and he had made him, a long tunic.
texts.gen.37.4: So his brethren saw that their father loved him, more than any of his brethren, and they hated him, and could not bid him prosper,
texts.gen.37.5: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and told it to his brethren, and they went on yet more to hate him.
texts.gen.37.6: And he said unto them, Hear ye I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:
texts.gen.37.7: Lo! then, we, were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, when lo my sheaf rose up, yea and took its stand,—and lo! round about came your sheaves, and bowed themselves down to my sheaf.
texts.gen.37.8: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou, reign, over us, shalt thou, have dominion over us? So they went on yet more to hate him, because of his dreams and because of his words.
texts.gen.37.9: Then dreamed he, yet another, dream, and related it to his brethren, and said:—Lo! I have dreamed a dream, yet again, Lo! then, the sun and the moon, and eleven stars, were bowing themselves down to me.
texts.gen.37.10: So he related it unto his father, and unto his brethren,—and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream which thou hast dreamed? Shall we, indeed come in, I, and thy mother and thy brethren, to bow ourselves down to thee to the earth?
texts.gen.37.11: Then were his brethren jealous of him, but his father, marked the word.
texts.gen.37.12: Now his brethren went their way,—to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.
texts.gen.37.13: So Israel said unto Joseph Are not, thy brethren, feeding the flock in Shechem? Come on! and let me send thee unto them. And he said to him Behold me!
texts.gen.37.14: So he said to him—Go, I pray thee, look after the welfare of thy brethren, and the welfare of the flock, and bring me back word. And he sent him from the vale of Hebron, and he came in towards Shechem.
texts.gen.37.15: And a man found him, and lo! he was wandering about in the field, so the man asked him saying—What seekest thou?
texts.gen.37.16: And he said, My brethren, am, I, seeking,—do tell me, I pray thee, where they are feeding their flock.
texts.gen.37.17: And the man said, They have broken up from hence, for I heard them saying Let us go our way towards Dothan. So Joseph went after his brethren, and found them, in Dothan.
texts.gen.37.18: And they saw him afar off,—and, ere yet he drew near unto them, they conspired against him, to put him to death.
texts.gen.37.19: And they said each man unto his brother, Lo! that master of dreams yonder, coming in!
texts.gen.37.20: Now, therefore, come! let us slay him and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say A cruel beast, hath devoured him,—And let us see what will become of his dreams.
texts.gen.37.21: And Reuben heard it, and rescued him out of their hand, and said Let us not smite him, so as to take his life!
texts.gen.37.22: And Reuben said unto them Do not shed blood! Cast him into this pit, which is in the wilderness, but put not forth, a hand, against him! that he might rescue him out of their hand, to restore him unto his father.
texts.gen.37.23: So it came to pass, when Joseph had come in unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph of his tunic, the long tunic which was upon him,
texts.gen.37.24: and took him, and cast him into the pit, but the pit, was empty, there was in it no water.
texts.gen.37.25: And when they had sat down to eat bread, they lifted up their eyes and looked, and lo! a caravan of Ishmaelites, coming in from Gilead,—and, their camels, were bearing tragacanth gum, and balsam and cistus-gum, they were going their way, to take them down to Egypt.
texts.gen.37.26: So Judah said unto his brethren,—What profit that we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
texts.gen.37.27: Come and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites; but let not, our own hand, be upon him, for our own brother, our own flesh, is he And his brethren hearkened.
texts.gen.37.28: And there passed by certain Midianites travelling merchants, so they drew forth and uplifted Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites, for twenty pieces of silver,—and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
texts.gen.37.29: And Reuben returned unto the pit, and lo Joseph was not in the pit, so he rent his clothes;
texts.gen.37.30: and returned unto his brethren, and said,—The, lad, is not! And, I, oh where can I, go?
texts.gen.37.31: And they took Joseph’s tunic,—and slaughtered a buck of the goats, and dipped the tunic in the blood;
texts.gen.37.32: and sent the long tunic and brought it in unto their father, and said This, have we found! Examine, we pray thee, whether it is the tunic of thy son, or not!
texts.gen.37.33: So he examined it, and said—The tunic of my son! A cruel beast hath devoured him,—torn in pieces—torn in pieces, is Joseph!
texts.gen.37.34: And Jacob rent his garments, and put sackcloth upon his loins,—and mourned over his son many days.
texts.gen.37.35: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to console him but he refused to be consoled, and said—Surely I will go down unto my son mourning to hades! And his father wept for him.
texts.gen.37.36: Now, the Midianites, sold him into Egypt,—to Potiphar courtier of Pharaoh, chief of the royal executioners.
texts.gen.38.1: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down away from his brethren,—and turned aside unto a certain Adullamite, whose, name, was Hirah.
texts.gen.38.2: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite whose, name, was Shua,—and he took her, and went in unto her;
texts.gen.38.3: and she conceived and bare a son,—and he called his name Er.
texts.gen.38.4: And she conceived again and bare a son,—and she called his name Onan.
texts.gen.38.5: And she, yet again, bare a son, and called his name Shelah,—and she, was at Chezib, when she bare him.
texts.gen.38.6: And Judah took a wife, for Er his firstborn,—and, her name, was Tamar.
texts.gen.38.7: And it came to pass that Er, Judah’s firstborn was displeasing in the eyes of Yahweh,—so Yahweh put him to death,
texts.gen.38.8: Then said Judah to Onan, Go in unto thy brother’s wife, and fulfil the duty of a brother-in-law unto her,—and raise up seed, to thy brother.
texts.gen.38.9: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his,—and so although he did go in unto his brother’s wife, yet made he waste upon the ground, so as not to give seed to his brother.
texts.gen.38.10: And it was displeasing, in the eyes of Yahweh what he had done,—so he put, him also, to death,
texts.gen.38.11: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter-in-law—Remain a widow in the house of thy father until Shelah my son grow up. For he said, Lest, he also, die, like his brethren. So Tamar went her way, and remained in the house of her father.
texts.gen.38.12: And when the days were multiplied, then died Shua’s daughter, Judah’s wife,—and Judah consoled himself and went up unto his sheep shearers, he and Hirah his friend the Adullamite, towards Timnah.
texts.gen.38.13: And it was told Tamar saying,—Lo! thy father-in-law is going up towards Timnah, to the shearing of his sheep.
texts.gen.38.14: So she put off from her the garments of her widowhood and covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself up, and sat down in the entrance of, Enaim, which is by the way towards Timnah,—for she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she, had not been given him to wife.
texts.gen.38.15: And Judah, seeing her, reckoned her to be an unchaste woman,—for she had covered her face.
texts.gen.38.16: So he turned aside unto her. by the way, and said Grant it! I pray thee, let me come in unto thee! For he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, What wilt thou give me, if thou shouldst come in unto me?
texts.gen.38.17: And he said, I, will send a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give a pledge until thou send it?
texts.gen.38.18: And he said—What is the pledge that I shall give thee? And She said—Thy signet-ring, and thy guard, and thy staff that is in thy hand. So he gave them to her and came in unto her and she conceived by him.
texts.gen.38.19: Then she arose and went her way, and put off her veil from her,—and put on the garments of her widowhood.
texts.gen.38.20: And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge at the hand of the woman,—but he found her not.
texts.gen.38.21: So he asked the men of her place saying. Where is the devotee, she that was in Enaim, by the way? And they said,—There hath been here no devotee.
texts.gen.38.22: Then returned he unto Judah, and said—I found her not,—moreover also, the men of the place said, There hath been here no devotee.
texts.gen.38.23: And Judah said: Thou must take it to her, lest we become a contempt,—lo! I sent this kid, and, thou, hast not found her.
texts.gen.38.24: And it came to pass that about three months after, it was told Judah, saying—Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath been guilty of unchastity, moreover also lo! she hath conceived by unchastity. Then said Judah, Bring her forth and let her be burnt.
texts.gen.38.25: When, she, was about to be brought forth, then, she herself, sent unto her father-in-law saying, By the man to whom these belong, have I, conceived! And she said—Examine, I pray thee, to whom belong the signet-ring, and the guard, and the staff—these!
texts.gen.38.26: So Judah examined them and said—More righteous than I! forasmuch, as I had not given her to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.
texts.gen.38.27: And, it came to pass at the time of her travail, that lo! twins, were in her womb.
texts.gen.38.28: And it came to pass when she was in travail, that one put forth a hand,—so the midwife took and bound upon his hand a crimson thread, saying—This came first!
texts.gen.38.29: And so it was that, no sooner had he withdrawn his hand, than lo! his brother had come. And she said, Wherefore hast thou made for thyself a breach? So his name was called Perez.
texts.gen.38.30: And afterwards, came his brother, on whose hand was the crimson thread,—so his name was called, Zerah.
texts.gen.39.1: Now, Joseph, was taken down to Egypt,—and Potiphar, courtier of Pharaoh, chief of the royal executioners, an Egyptian bought him, at the hand of the Ishmaelites, who had brought him down thither.
texts.gen.39.2: And it came to pass that Yahweh, was with Joseph, so that he became a prosperous man,—and was in the house of his lord the Egyptian.
texts.gen.39.3: And his lord saw, that, Yahweh, was with him—and that whatsoever, he was doing, Yahweh, was causing to prosper in his hand.
texts.gen.39.4: So Joseph found favour in his eyes and waited upon him,—and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had, gave he into his hand.
texts.gen.39.5: And it came to pass from the time that he made him overseer in his house and over all that he had, that Yahweh blessed the house of the Egyptian, for Joseph’s sake,—yea it came to pass, that the blessing of Yahweh, was with all that he had, in the house and in the field;
texts.gen.39.6: so that he left all that he had in the hand of Joseph, and took note with him of nothing, save only the bread which, he himself, was eating. And so it was that Joseph was comely in form and comely in countenance.
texts.gen.39.7: And it came to pass after these things, that his lord’s wife lifted up her eyes unto Joseph,—and she said—Come! lie with me.
texts.gen.39.8: And he refused and said unto his lord’s wife, Lo! my lord, taketh no note with me as to what is in the house,—but, all that pertaineth to him, hath he delivered into my hand:
texts.gen.39.9: There is no one greater in this house than I, neither hath he withheld from me anything, save only thyself in that thou, art his wife,—how, then could I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
texts.gen.39.10: And it came to pass, that although she Spake unto Joseph day after day, yet hearkened he not unto her to lie beside her to be with her.
texts.gen.39.11: And it came to pass, when, on a certain day, he went into the house to attend to his business,—and there was no man of the household, there in the house,
texts.gen.39.12: that she caught him by his garment, saying—Come! lie with me. Then left he his garment in her hand, and fled and gat forth outside,
texts.gen.39.13: And it came to pass when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand,—and fled forth outside,
texts.gen.39.14: that she cried out to the men of her house and spake to them, saying, Look ye! he hath brought in to us a Hebrew man to insult us,—He came in unto me, to lie with me, so I cried out with a loud voice.
texts.gen.39.15: And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted high my voice, and cried out, then left he his garment beside me, and fled and gat forth outside.
texts.gen.39.16: So she laid by his garment beside her,—until his lord should come into his house,
texts.gen.39.17: Then spake she unto him, according to these words, saying,—He hath been in unto me—the Hebrew servant whom thou didst bring in to us—to insult me.
texts.gen.39.18: And it came to pass when I lifted high my voice and cried out, then left he his garment beside me, and fled outside.
texts.gen.39.19: And it came to pass, when his lord heard the words of his wife which she spake unto him saying, According to these words, hath thy servant done to me, Then was kindled his anger.
texts.gen.39.20: So Joseph’s lord took him and delivered him up to the prison,: the place where, the prisoners of the king, were imprisoned,—so he was there, in the prison.
texts.gen.39.21: And it came to pass that, Yahweh, was with Joseph, and extended unto him lovingkindness,—and gave him his favour in the eyes of the chief of the prison.
texts.gen.39.22: So the chief of the prison delivered up, into Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison,—and of all that was doing there, he, was the doer.
texts.gen.39.23: After nothing, was the chief of the prison looking, of whatever was in his hand,—in that Yahweh, was with him, and whatsoever, he was doing, Yahweh, was causing to prosper.
texts.gen.40.1: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt, and the baker, had sinned against their lord the king of Egypt.
texts.gen.40.2: Then fell the wroth of Pharaoh upon his two courtiers, upon the chief of the butlers, and upon the chief of the bakers;
texts.gen.40.3: so he delivered them up into the ward of the house of the chief of the royal executioners, into the prison,—the place where Joseph was imprisoned.
texts.gen.40.4: And the chief of the royal executioners charged Joseph with them and he waited upon them, and they were some days in ward.
texts.gen.40.5: And they dreamed a dream they two, each man, his dream in one night, each man, according to the interpretation of his dream,—the butler and the baker who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were imprisoned in the prison.
texts.gen.40.6: And Joseph came in unto them in the morning,—and looked at them, and lo! they were sad.
texts.gen.40.7: So he asked Pharaoh’s courtiers who were with him in the ward of his lord’s house, saying, Why are your faces troubled to-day!
texts.gen.40.8: And they said unto him, A dream, have we dreamed, but there is none, to interpret, it. Then said Joseph unto them—Is it not unto God, that interpretations belong? Relate it. I pray you, to me.
texts.gen.40.9: And the chief of the butlers related his dream to Joseph,—and said to him, In my dream, then lo! a vine, before me;
texts.gen.40.10: and, in the vine, three shoots,—and the same at sprouting time, had shot up her blossom, and her clusters had brought to perfection ripe grapes.
texts.gen.40.11: Now, the cup of Pharaoh, being in my hand, I took the ripe grapes and pressed them out into the cup of Pharaoh, and set the cup upon Pharaoh’s palm.
texts.gen.40.12: And Joseph said to him, This, is the interpretation thereof,—The three shoots are three days:
texts.gen.40.13: In three days more, will Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee to thine office, and thou shalt set the cup of Pharaoh in his hand, according to the former custom when thou wast his butler.
texts.gen.40.14: But if thou remember how I was with thee when it shall go well with thee, then wilt thou I pray thee do me a lovingkindness,—and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me forth out of this house;
texts.gen.40.15: For I was, stolen, out of the land of the Hebrews,—and, even here, had I done nothing, that they should have put me in the dungeon,
texts.gen.40.16: Then the chief of the bakers, seeing that he had well interpreted, said unto Joseph, I, too, was in my dream, when lo! three wicker baskets of fine bread were on my head;
texts.gen.40.17: and, in the uppermost basket, was some of every kind of food for Pharaoh that a baker could make,—but, the birds, kept eating them out of the basket from off my head.
texts.gen.40.18: And Joseph responded and said, This, is the interpretation thereof, The three baskets, are, three days:
texts.gen.40.19: In three days more, will Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and hang thee upon a tree, and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.
texts.gen.40.20: And it came to pass on the third day the birthday of Pharaoh, that he made a banquet for all his servants, and uplifted the head of the chief of the butlers and the head of the chief of the bakers in the midst of his servants;
texts.gen.40.21: and restored the chief of the butlers to his butlership, so that he set the cup upon the palm of Pharaoh;
texts.gen.40.22: but, the chief of the bakers, he hanged,—as, Joseph, had interpreted unto them.
texts.gen.40.23: Yet the chief of the butlers made no mention of Joseph but did forget him.
texts.gen.41.1: And it came to pass at the end of two years of days, that, Pharaoh, was dreaming, when lo! he was standing by the river (Nile);
texts.gen.41.2: and lo! from the river, were coming up seven heifers, comely in appearance and fat in flesh,—and they fed among the rushes.
texts.gen.41.3: And lo! seven heifers more coming up after them out of the river, uncomely in appearance and lean in flesh,—and they came and stood beside the heifers, by the lip of the river.
texts.gen.41.4: Then did the heifers that were uncomely in appearance, and lean in flesh, eat up, the seven heifers that were comely in appearance and fat. So Pharaoh awoke.
texts.gen.41.5: And he fell asleep, and dreamed a second time, when lo! seven ears, coming up on one stalk fat and good;
texts.gen.41.6: and lo! seven ears, lean and shrivelled by an east wind, coming up after them.
texts.gen.41.7: Then did the lean ears swallow up the seven fat and full ears. So Pharaoh awoke and lo! it was a dream.
texts.gen.41.8: And it came to pass in the morning, that his spirit became restless, so he sent and called for all the sacred scribes of Egypt and all her wise men,—and Pharaoh related to them his dreams, but there was no one that could interpret them. to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.9: Then spake the chief of the butlers with Pharaoh saying, My faults, would, I, mention this day.
texts.gen.41.10: Pharaoh, was wroth with his servants,—and put them in the ward of the house of the chief of the royal executioners, me, and the chief of the bakers.
texts.gen.41.11: Then must we needs dream, a dream in one night, I and he,—each man, according to the interpretation of his dream, did we dream.
texts.gen.41.12: And, there with us, was a young man, a Hebrew servant to the chief of the royal executioners, and we related to him, and he interpreted to us our dreams,—to each man—according to his dream, did he interpret,
texts.gen.41.13: And it came to pass as he interpreted to us, so, it happened,—me, he restored to mine office but him, he hanged.
texts.gen.41.14: Then sent Pharaoh and summoned Joseph, and they hastened him out of the dungeon,—so he shaved himself and changed his garments, and came in unto Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.15: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, A dream, have I dreamed, but none can interpret it,—but, I, have heard say concerning thee, that on hearing a dream, thou canst interpret it.
texts.gen.41.16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh saying, Not to me, doth it pertain! May, God grant in answer, the prosperity of Pharaoh!
texts.gen.41.17: Then spake Pharaoh unto Joseph,—In my dream, there was I, standing on the lip of the river;
texts.gen.41.18: When lo! out of the river, were coming up seven heifers, fat in flesh and comely in form,—and they fed among the rushes.
texts.gen.41.19: And lo! seven other heifers, coming up after them, poor and very uncomely in form and lean in flesh,—I had never seen such in all the land of Egypt, for uncomeliness.
texts.gen.41.20: Then did the lean and uncomely heifers eat up the first seven fat heifers;
