texts.gen.41.21: and they passed into their stomach yet could it not be known that they had passed into them, their appearance, being uncomely, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
texts.gen.41.22: Then looked I in my dream,—And lo! seven ears, coming up on one stalk, full and good;
texts.gen.41.23: And lo! seven ears, withered lean shrivelled by an east wind growing up after them.
texts.gen.41.24: Then did the lean ears swallow up, the seven good ears. So I told [these things] unto the sacred scribes, but there was none that could explain [them] to me.
texts.gen.41.25: Then said Joseph unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh, is, one. What God is about to do hath he announced to Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.26: The seven good heifers, are, seven years, and, the seven good ears are, seven years,—the dream, is, one.
texts.gen.41.27: And the seven lean and uncomely heifers that were coming up after them, are seven years, and the seven lean ears, shrivelled by an east wind, will turn out to be—seven years of famine.
texts.gen.41.28: The very word that I spake unto Pharaoh, what, God, is about to do, hath he showed unto Pharaoh.
texts.gen.41.29: Lo! seven years, coming in,—of great plenty, in all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.30: Then shall arise seven years of famine, after them, so shall be forgotten all the plenty in the land of Egypt,—and the famine shall consume the land;
texts.gen.41.31: neither shall the plenty in the land be discernible, because of that famine coming after,—for it shall be, very severe.
texts.gen.41.32: And for that there was a repeating of the dream unto Pharaoh, twice, it is because the thing, is established, from God, and God is hastening to do it.
texts.gen.41.33: Now, therefore, let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise,—and set him over the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.34: Let Pharaoh do this, that he may appoint overseers over the land,—so shall he take up a fifth of the land of Egypt, during the seven years of plenty.
texts.gen.41.35: And let them gather up all the food of these seven good years that are coming in,—and let them heap up corn under the hand of Pharaoh as food in cities so shall they keep it.
texts.gen.41.36: So shall the food become a store for the land, for the seven years of famine which shall come about in the land of Egypt,—and the land shall not be cut off in the famine.
texts.gen.41.37: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh,—and in the eyes of all his servants;
texts.gen.41.38: and Pharaoh said unto his servants,—Can we find such a one, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?
texts.gen.41.39: So Pharaoh said unto Joseph, After God hath made known unto thee all this, there is no one discreet and wise like thee.
texts.gen.41.40: Thou, shalt be over my house, and on thy mouth, shall all my people kiss,—only as to the throne, will I be greater than thou.
texts.gen.41.41: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph,—See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.42: So Pharaoh took his ring from off his hand and put it upon Joseph’s hand,—and clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put the chain of gold upon his neck;
texts.gen.41.43: and made him ride in the second chariot which belonged to him, and they cried out before him. Bow the knee! thus setting him over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.44: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph. I, am Pharaoh, Without thee, therefore shall no man raise his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.45: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-paneah, and gave him Asenath daughter of Poti-phera priest of On, to wife,—and Joseph went forth over the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.46: Now, Joseph, was thirty years old, when he took his station, before Pharaoh king of Egypt. So Joseph went forth from before Pharaoh, and passed along through all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.47: And the land produced, in the seven years of plenty, by handfuls,
texts.gen.41.48: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years in which there was plenty in the land of Egypt, and laid up food in cities—the food of the fields of the city. which were round about it, laid he up within it.
texts.gen.41.49: Thus did Joseph heap up corn like the sand of the sea making it exceeding abundant,—until one hath left off reckoning, because it cannot be reckoned.
texts.gen.41.50: Now to Joseph, were born two sons, ere yet came in the year of famine,—whom Asenath daughter of Poti-phera priest of On, bare to him.
texts.gen.41.51: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh,—For God hath made me forget all my trouble, and all the house of my father.
texts.gen.41.52: And, the name of the second, called he Ephraim, For God hath made me fruitful in the land of my humiliation.
texts.gen.41.53: Then came to an end the seven years of the plenty,—which was in the land of Egypt;
texts.gen.41.54: and the seven years of famine began to come in, according as Joseph had said,—and it came to pass that there was a famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt, there was bread.
texts.gen.41.55: Yet was famine felt in all the land of Egypt, and the people made outcry; unto Pharaoh for bread,—and Pharaoh said to all Egypt,—Go ye unto Joseph, that which he saith to you, shall ye do.
texts.gen.41.56: Now, the famine, was over all the face of the land,—so Joseph opened all [places] wherein it was and sold corn to the Egyptians, and the famine laid fast hold of the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.41.57: All the earth also, came in to Egypt to buy corn, unto Joseph,—because the famine had laid fast hold on all the earth.
texts.gen.42.1: Then saw Jacob that there was corn in Egypt,—and Jacob said to his sons, Wherefore look ye one at another?
texts.gen.42.2: And he said, Lo I have heard that there is corn in Egypt,—Go down thither and buy corn for us from thence, that we may live and not die.
texts.gen.42.3: So Joseph’s ten brethren went down,—to buy corn from the Egyptians;
texts.gen.42.4: but, Benjamin, Joseph’s own brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren,—for he said, Lest there befall him any mischief.
texts.gen.42.5: Thus came in the sons of Israel, to buy corn in the midst of them that came—for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.6: Now, Joseph—he, it was, that was in power over the land, he, it was that was selling corn to all the people of the land,—so Joseph’s brethren came in, and bowed themselves down to him, with their faces to the earth.
texts.gen.42.7: And Joseph beheld his brethren and recognised them,—and made himself a stranger unto them and spake with them harsh things and said unto them—Whence have ye come in? And they said, From the land of Canaan, to buy food.
texts.gen.42.8: And Joseph recognised his brethren,—whereas they, recognised him not.
texts.gen.42.9: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed regarding them,—so he said unto them—Spies, are, ye! to see the nakedness of the land, have ye come in!
texts.gen.42.10: And they said unto him, Nay, my lord,—but, thy servants, are come to buy food.
texts.gen.42.11: All of us, are, sons of one man,—honest men, are we: thy servants are not, spies.
texts.gen.42.12: And he said unto him,—Nay! but, the nakedness of the land, are ye come in to see.
texts.gen.42.13: And they said: We, thy twelve servants, are, brethren, sons of one man in the and of Canaan,—and lo! the youngest: is with our father this day, and, the one, is not!
texts.gen.42.14: And Joseph said unto them,—The very thing, that I spake unto you, saying—Spies, are, ye.
texts.gen.42.15: Hereby, shall ye be proved,—By the life of Pharaoh, ye shall not go forth from hence, save only by the coming in of your youngest brother hither.
texts.gen.42.16: Send—from among you—one that he may fetch your brother, but be, ye, held as prisoners, that your words may be proved whether, truth, is with you,—and, if not, by the life of Pharaoh, surely, spies, ye are.
texts.gen.42.17: So he drew them all together into ward, for three days.
texts.gen.42.18: And Joseph said unto them on the third day, This, do and live,—God himself, do, I, revere.
texts.gen.42.19: If ye, are, honest men, one brother of you shall be kept as a prisoner in your house of ward,—but, ye, go, take in corn for the famine of your houses;
texts.gen.42.20: and your youngest brother, shall ye bring in unto me, that your words may be confirmed, and ye die not. And they did so.
texts.gen.42.21: And they said each man unto his brother—Verily guilty, we are, respecting our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul when he appealed unto us for favour and we hearkened not,—therefore, hath come in unto us this distress.
texts.gen.42.22: And Reuben responded to them, saying—Spake I not unto you saying, Do not sin against the child! And ye hearkened not? His very blood, therefore lo! it is required.
texts.gen.42.23: But, they, knew not that Joseph was hearkening,—for, the interpreter, was between them.
texts.gen.42.24: So he turned away from them, and wept,—then came back unto them and spake unto them, and took away from them Simeon, and bound him prisoner before their eyes.
texts.gen.42.25: Then commanded Joseph that their bags should be filled with corn, and their silver be returned each man’s into his sack, and provision be given for the journey,—and it was done to them thus.
texts.gen.42.26: So they lifted up their corn on their asses,—and went their way, from thence.
texts.gen.42.27: And the first opened his sack to give fodder to his ass at the inn,—and beheld his silver, yea there, it was in the mouth of his sack!
texts.gen.42.28: So he said unto his brethren My silver hath been returned, yea verily, there it is in my sack! Then went forth their heart and they turned trembling—each man unto his brother saying. What is this that God hath done to us?
texts.gen.42.29: So they came in unto Jacob their father to the land of Canaan,—and told him all that had befallen them saying:
texts.gen.42.30: The man that is lord of the land spake unto us harsh things,—and then delivered us up. as spies of the land.
texts.gen.42.31: And we said unto him Honest men, are, we,—we are not spies!
texts.gen.42.32: Twelve brethren, are, we, sons of our father,—the one, is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
texts.gen.42.33: Then said the man the lord of the land unto us, Hereby, shall I get to know that honest men, ye are,—One brother of you, leave ye remaining with me, and corn for the famine of your houses, take ye and go your way;
texts.gen.42.34: And bring ye in your youngest brother unto me, So must I get to know that ye are, not spies, but are honest men: Your brother, will I give up to you, and with the land, shall ye traffic.
texts.gen.42.35: And it came to pass when, they, were emptying their, sacks then lo! each man’s bundle of silver, was in his sack,—and when they beheld their bundles of silver—they and their father, they were afraid,
texts.gen.42.36: And Jacob their father said unto them, Me, have ye bereaved,—Joseph, is not, and, Simeon, is not, and Benjamin, ye would take! Against me, have happened all these things.
texts.gen.42.37: Then spake Reuben unto his father saying, My two sons, shalt thou put to death, if I bring him not unto thee,—Come give him up upon my hand, and I, will restore him unto thee.
texts.gen.42.38: And he said, My son shall not go down with you,—For, his brother, is dead and, he alone, is left, and as surely as there befall him any mischief by the way wherein ye go, so surely shall ye bring down my grey hairs with sorrow unto hades.
texts.gen.43.1: But the famine, was severe in the land.
texts.gen.43.2: So it came to pass when they had made an end of eating the corn which they had brought in out of Egypt, that their father said unto them,—Return buy for us a little food.
texts.gen.43.3: Then spake Judah unto him saying,—The man, did protest, to us saying—Ye shall not see my face, except, your brother, is with you.
texts.gen.43.4: If thou art sending our brother with us, we will certainly go down, and buy for thee food;
texts.gen.43.5: but, if thou art not sending him, we will not go down, for the man, said unto us Ye shall not see my face, except, your brother, is with you.
texts.gen.43.6: And Israel said, Wherefore did ye ill to me,—to tell the man, there yet remained to you a brother?
texts.gen.43.7: And they said, The man, did ask, concerning ourselves and concerning our kindred saying—Is your father yet alive? Have ye a brother? So we told him according to the tenor of these words. Could we, at all know, that he would say, Bring down your brother?
texts.gen.43.8: Then said Judah unto Israel his father—Come! send thou down the young man with me that we may arise and go our way,—and live and not die, both we and thou and our little ones.
texts.gen.43.9: I, will be surety for him, at my hand, shalt thou require him,—as surely as I bring him not in unto thee, and set him down before thee, so surely will I be counted a sinner against thee all the days,
texts.gen.43.10: For, if we had not lingered, surely now, had we come back here a second time.
texts.gen.43.11: Then Israel their father said unto them—If so, then do this,—Take of the song of the land in your vessels, and carry down to the man a present,—A little balsam and a little honey, tragacanth gum and cistus gum, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
texts.gen.43.12: And double silver, take in your hand,—also the silver that was put back in the mouth of your sacks, carry ye back in your hand, peradventure it was an error,
texts.gen.43.13: Your brother also, take ye,—and arise go again unto the man.
texts.gen.43.14: And, God Almighty, give you compassion before the man, so shall he send with you, your other brother, and Benjamin. But, as for me, when I am bereaved, I am bereaved!
texts.gen.43.15: So the men took this present, double silver also, took they in their hand and Benjamin,—and arose and went down into Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
texts.gen.43.16: And Joseph saw—with them—Benjamin, so he said to him that was over his house Bring the men into the house,—and slay meat and make ready, for with me, shall the men eat at noon.
texts.gen.43.17: So the men did as Joseph had said, and the man brought the men into Joseph’s house,
texts.gen.43.18: Then were the men afraid because they had been brought into the house of Joseph, and they said—For the matter of the silver that came back in our sacks at the beginning, have, we, been brought in,—that he may turn round upon us and fall upon us, and take us for servants and our asses.
texts.gen.43.19: So they drew near unto the man that was over Joseph’s house,—and spake unto him at the entrance of the house;
texts.gen.43.20: and said, May it please my lord! We, did indeed come down, at the beginning to buy food.
texts.gen.43.21: And it came to pass when we had entered into the inn, that we opened our sacks, and lo! the silver of each man, in the mouth of his sack,—our silver in its full weight,—so we have bought it back in our hand!
texts.gen.43.22: And, more silver, have we brought down in our hand, to buy food,—we know not who put our silver in our sacks.
texts.gen.43.23: And he said—Peace to you do not fear! Your God, and the God of your father, hath given you secret treasure, in your sacks, as for your silver, it came in unto me. And he brought forth unto them Simeon.
texts.gen.43.24: So the man brought the men into Joseph’s house,—and gave them water and they bathed their feet, and he gave them provender for their asses.
texts.gen.43.25: And they made ready the present, against the coming in of Joseph at noon,—for they heard that it was there they should eat bread.
texts.gen.43.26: So when Joseph came into the house, they brought in to him the present which was in their hand into the house,—and bowed themselves down to him to the earth.
texts.gen.43.27: Then asked he after their welfare, and said—Is it well with your aged father, of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?
texts.gen.43.28: And they said—It is well with thy servant our father, he is yet alive. And they bent their heads and bowed them-selves down.
texts.gen.43.29: Then lifted he up his eyes, and saw Benjamin his brother son of his mother, and said—Is, this, your youngest brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, God, grant thee favour my son!
texts.gen.43.30: And Joseph made haste for his compassions towards his brother were pent up, and he sought to weep,—so he went into the inner chamber and wept there,
texts.gen.43.31: Then bathed he his face and came forth,—and restrained himself, and said Set on bread!
texts.gen.43.32: So they set on for him—by himself, and for them—by themselves,—and for the Egyptians that were eating with him—by themselves, for the Egyptians might not eat, bread, with the Hebrews for an abomination, had that been to Egyptians.
texts.gen.43.33: So they took their seats before him, the firstborn, according to his birthright and the youngest, according to his youth,—and the men looked with amazement, each one at his companion.
texts.gen.43.34: And he sent portions from before him unto them, and the portion of Benjamin exceeded the portions of them all, five-fold. And they drank and made merry with him.
texts.gen.44.1: Then commanded he him who was over his house saying—Fill the sacks of the men, with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s silver in the mouth of his sack;
texts.gen.44.2: and my cup—the cup of silver, shalt thou put in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, with his corn-silver. So he did, according to the word of Joseph, which he had spoken.
texts.gen.44.3: By the time, the morning, was light, the men, had been sent away, they, and their asses.
texts.gen.44.4: They themselves, had gone out of the city—they had not gone far, when Joseph said to him who was over his house, Rise chase after the men,—so shalt thou overtake them and shalt say unto them, Wherefore have ye requited evil for good?
texts.gen.44.5: Is not this that in which my lord drinketh, and whereby, he himself, doth divine? Ye have done evil in what ye have done.
texts.gen.44.6: So he overtook them,—and spake unto them these words.
texts.gen.44.7: And they said unto him, Wherefore should my lord speak such words as these? Far be thy servants, from doing such a thing as this!
texts.gen.44.8: Lo! the silver that we found in the mouth of our sacks, we brought back unto thee out of the land of Canaan,—how then could we steal out of the house of thy lord, silver or gold?
texts.gen.44.9: With whomsoever of thy servants it can be found, he shall die,—and, we also, will become my lord’s servants.
texts.gen.44.10: And he said, Yea, now, according to your words, so, let it be,—he with whom it is found, shall be my servant, Ye, however, shall be clear.
texts.gen.44.11: So they hastened and took down each man his sack to the ground,—and opened each man his sack.
texts.gen.44.12: Then made he thorough search, with the eldest, he began, and with the youngest, he ended,—and the cup was found in the sack of Benjamin!
texts.gen.44.13: And they rent their mantles,—and laded each man his ass, and returned to the city.
texts.gen.44.14: And Judah and his brethren came into the house of Joseph, he, yet being there,—and fell down before him to the earth.
texts.gen.44.15: And Joseph said to them, What is this deed which ye have done? Know ye not that such a man as I, can even divine?
texts.gen.44.16: Then said Judah—What shall we say to my lord, how shall we speak and how shall we justify ourselves,—when, God himself, hath found out the iniquity of thy servants? Behold us! my lord’s servants, both we, and he in whose hand the cup hath been found.
texts.gen.44.17: And he said, Far be it from me to do this thing! The man in whose hand the cup hath been found, he, shall be my servant, but as for you, go ye up in peace unto your father.
texts.gen.44.18: Then Judah drew near unto him, and said—Pardon my lord! Pray let thy servant speak a word in the ears of my lord, and do not let thine anger be kindled against thy servant,—for, thus, art, thou as Pharaoh!
texts.gen.44.19: It was, my lord, who asked his servants, saying,—Have ye a father, or a brother?
texts.gen.44.20: So we said unto my lord, We have an aged father, and the child of his old age a youth,—his brother, being dead, he alone, is left of his mother and, his father, loveth him.
texts.gen.44.21: So then thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me,—that I may set mine eyes upon him.
texts.gen.44.22: And we said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father,—as surely as he leaveth his father, so surely will he, die.
texts.gen.44.23: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother do come down with you, ye shall not again behold my face.
texts.gen.44.24: So it came to pass when we had gone up unto thy servant, my father, that we told him the words of my lord.
texts.gen.44.25: Then said our father,—Go again buy us a little food,
texts.gen.44.26: And we said, We cannot go down,—If our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down, for we cannot see the face of the man if, our youngest brother, is not with us.
texts.gen.44.27: Then said thy servant my father, unto us,—Ye yourselves, know, that, two, did my wife bear to me,
texts.gen.44.28: and the one went forth from me, and I said—Certainly he hath been, torn in pieces,—And I have never seen him since.
texts.gen.44.29: As surely as ye take, this one also, away from before my face and there befall him any mischief, so surely shall ye bring down my grey hairs, with misfortune to hades.
texts.gen.44.30: Now, therefore, as surely as I go in unto thy servant my father, and, the lad, is not with us,—seeing that his soul is bound up with the lad’s soul,
texts.gen.44.31: so surely shall it come to pass that when he seeth that the lad is not with us, then will he die. So shall thy servants bring down the grey hairs of thy servant our father, with sorrow to hades.
texts.gen.44.32: For thy servant, became surety for the lad, while away from my father saying,—If I bring him not unto thee, then will I count myself a sinner against my father all the days.
texts.gen.44.33: Now, therefore, I pray thee let thy servant remain instead of the lad, as servant to my lord,—but as for the lad, let him go up with his brethren.
texts.gen.44.34: For how can I go up unto my father, should the lad, not be with me? lest I look on the calamity, that shall find out my father,
texts.gen.45.1: And Joseph could not restrain himself before all who were stationed near him, so he cried out—Have forth every man from me! And there stood no man with him, when Joseph made himself known unto his brethren,
texts.gen.45.2: Then gave he forth his voice in weeping,—and the Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
texts.gen.45.3: Then said Joseph unto his brethren: I, am Joseph, is my father yet alive? But his brethren could not answer him, for they were terrified because of him.
texts.gen.45.4: Then said Joseph unto his brethren—Draw near I pray you, unto me. And they drew near. And he said—I, am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
texts.gen.45.5: But, now, do not grieve, neither let it be vexing in your eyes, that ye sold me hither,—for, to save life, did God send me before you.
texts.gen.45.6: For these two years, hath the famine been in the midst of the land,—and, yet five years, are there, in which there shall be neither ploughing, nor harvest.
texts.gen.45.7: So then God sent me before you, to plant for you a remainder in the earth,—and to save you alive, by a great deliverance,
texts.gen.45.8: Now, therefore it was not ye, who sent me hither, but, God, himself,—who also appointed me to be a father to Pharaoh, and a lord to all his house, and a ruler over all the land of Egypt.
texts.gen.45.9: Haste ye and go up unto my father, then shall ye say unto him—Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath appointed me lord to all Egypt,—come down unto me do not delay;
texts.gen.45.10: so shalt thou dwell in the land of Goshen, and shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy sons, and thy sons’ sons,—and thy flocks and thy herds and all that is thine;
texts.gen.45.11: so will I sustain thee, there, for there are yet five years of famine,—lest thou come to poverty—thou and thy house and all who are thine.
texts.gen.45.12: Now lo! your own eyes do see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin,—that it is my own mouth, that doth speak unto you.
texts.gen.45.13: As soon as ye have told my father all my honour in Egypt, and all that ye have seen, so soon shall ye hasten and bring down my father hither.
texts.gen.45.14: Then fell he upon the neck of Benjamin his brother, and wept,—and Benjamin wept on his neck.
texts.gen.45.15: Then kissed he all his brethren, and wept upon them,—and, thereafter, his brethren spake with him.
texts.gen.45.16: Now, the report, was heard by the house of Pharaoh, saying, The brethren of Joseph have come in, And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
texts.gen.45.17: So then Pharaoh said unto Joseph—Say unto thy brethren This, do,—lade your asses, and go enter into the land of Canaan;
texts.gen.45.18: and fetch your father and your households and come in unto me,—that I may give you the best of the land of Egypt, and eat ye the fat of the land.
texts.gen.45.19: Thou, therefore command them, This, do ye,—Take you out of the land of Egypt, waggons for your little ones and for your wives, so shall ye bring your father and come in.
texts.gen.45.20: Your eye, moreover, let it not look with pity upon your goods,—for, the best of all the land of Egypt, is, yours.
texts.gen.45.21: And the sons of Israel did so, and Joseph gave them waggons, at the bidding of Pharaoh,—and gave them provisions for the way:
texts.gen.45.22: to all of them, gave he to each man changes of raiment,—but, to Benjamin, he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment.
texts.gen.45.23: Moreover, to his father, sent he as followeth—ten he-asses, laden from the best of Egypt,—and ten she-asses laden with corn and bread and nourishing food for his father for the way.
texts.gen.45.24: Thus sent he forth his brethren and they departed,—and he said unto them, Do not fall out by the way.
texts.gen.45.25: And they went up out of Egypt,—and came into the land of Canaan, unto Jacob their father.
texts.gen.45.26: And they told him saying—Joseph: is, yet alive, yea, indeed, he, is ruler in all the land of Egypt. And his heart became faint, for he believed them not.
texts.gen.45.27: So they spake unto him all the words of Joseph which he had spoken unto them h then saw he the waggons, which Joseph had sent to carry him,—and the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
texts.gen.45.28: And Israel said, Enough! Joseph my son is, yet alive, I must go and see him before I die!
texts.gen.46.1: So Israel brake up, with all that he had, and came in to Beer-sheba,—and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
texts.gen.46.2: And God said to Israel in the visions of the night, and he said—Jacob! Jacob! And he said—Behold me!
texts.gen.46.3: And he said: I, am GOD himself, the God of thy father,—Be not afraid of going down to Egypt, seeing that for a great nation, will I plant thee there.
texts.gen.46.4: I will go down with thee to Egypt, and I will bring thee up, yea wholly up,—and, Joseph, shall lay his own hand upon thine eyes.
texts.gen.46.5: So Jacob rose up from Beer-sheba,—and the sons of Israel brought Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the waggons which Pharaoh had sent to bring him;
texts.gen.46.6: and they took their cattle and the gains which they had gained in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt,—Jacob and all his seed with him:
texts.gen.46.7: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and all his seed, brought he with him into Egypt.
texts.gen.46.8: Now, these, are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt—Jacob and his sons,—the firstborn of Jacob, Reuben:
texts.gen.46.9: And, the sons of Reuben,—Hanoch and Pallu, and Hezron and Carmi;
texts.gen.46.10: And, the sons of Simeon,—Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar,—and Shaul, son of the Canaanitess;
texts.gen.46.11: And the sons of Levi,—Gershon, Kohath and Merari;
texts.gen.46.12: And the sons of Judah,—Er and Onan and Shelah, and Perez and Zerah,—but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan, and the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul;
texts.gen.46.13: And, the sons of Issachar,—Tola and Puvah, and Iob and Shimron;
texts.gen.46.14: And the sons of Zebulon,—Sered and Elon, and Jahleel.
texts.gen.46.15: These, are the sons of Leah whom she bare to Jacob in Padan-aram, with Dinah also his daughter,—All the souls of his sons and of his daughters, were thirty-three.
texts.gen.46.16: And, the sons of Gad,—Zaphon and Haggi, Shuni and Ezbon,—Eri and Arodi and Areli;
texts.gen.46.17: And, the sons of Asher,—Imnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister,—and the sons of Beriah, Heber and Malchiel.
texts.gen.46.18: These, are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter,—so she bare these to Jacob,—sixteen souls.
texts.gen.46.19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife,—Joseph and Benjamin;
texts.gen.46.20: And there were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, bare to him,: Manasseh and Ephraim;
texts.gen.46.21: And the sons of Benjamin—Bela and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera and Naaman, Ehi and Rosh,—Muppim and Huppim, and Ard.
texts.gen.46.22: These, are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob,—all the souls, were fourteen.
texts.gen.46.24: And the sons of Naphtali,—Jahzeel and Guni, and Jezer and Shillem.
texts.gen.46.25: These, are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter,—so she bare these to Jacob,—all the souls, were seven.
texts.gen.46.26: All the souls that came in with Jacob to Egypt that had come forth of his loins, besides Jacob’s sons’ wives,—all the souls, were sixty-six;
texts.gen.46.27: and, the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls: All the souls of the house of Jacob that came into Egypt, were seventy.
texts.gen.46.28: And he sent, Judah, before him unto Joseph, to direct his face to Goshen,—so they came in towards the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.46.29: Then yoked Joseph his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father towards Goshen,—and he appeared unto him, and fell upon his neck, and wept upon his neck a good while.
texts.gen.46.30: Then said Israel unto Joseph I am ready to die at last,—now that I have seen thy face, in that thou art, yet alive.
texts.gen.46.31: Then said Joseph unto his brethren and unto the house of his father, I must go up, and must tell Pharaoh—and must say unto him, My brethren, and the house of my father, who were in the land of Canaan, have come in unto me.
texts.gen.46.32: Now, the men, are feeders of flocks, for men of cattle, they are,—and their flocks and their herds and all that they have, have they brought in.
texts.gen.46.33: So shall it come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call for you,—and shall say—What is your occupation?
texts.gen.46.34: Then shall ye say—Men of cattle, have thy servants been from our youth even until now, both we and our fathers,—To the end ye may dwell in the land of Goshen, for an abomination to Egyptians, is every feeder of a flock,
texts.gen.47.1: So then Joseph went in, and told Pharaoh, and said—My father and my brethren, and their flocks and their herds and all that they have, are come in from the land of Canaan,—and, here they are, in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.47.2: Moreover out of the whole number of his brethren, he took with him five men,—and set them before Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.3: And Pharaoh said unto the brethren of Joseph—What is your occupation? And they said unto Pharaoh—Feeders of flocks, are thy servants, both we and our fathers.
texts.gen.47.4: And they said unto Pharaoh—To sojourn in the land, are we come in, for there is no pasture for the flocks which pertain to thy servants, for, severe, is the famine in the land of Canaan. Now, therefore, let thy servants dwell we pray thee in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.47.5: Then spake Pharaoh unto Joseph saying,—Thy father and thy brethren, are come in unto thee.
texts.gen.47.6: The land of Egypt, is, before thee, in the best of the land, cause thou thy father and thy brethren to dwell,—let them dwell in the land of Goshen, And if thou knowest that there are among them men of ability, then shalt thou set them as chieftains of cattle over mine.
texts.gen.47.7: So Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and caused him to stand before Pharaoh,—and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.8: And Pharaoh said unto Jacob: About how many, have been the days of the years of thy life?
texts.gen.47.9: And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my sojournings, have been a hundred and thirty years,—Few and evil, have been the days of the years of my life, neither have they attained unto the days of the years of the lives of my fathers, in the days of their sojournings.
texts.gen.47.10: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh,—and came forth from the presence of Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.11: So then Joseph fixed the dwelling of his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt in the best of the land. in the land of Rameses,—as Pharaoh had commanded.
texts.gen.47.12: And Joseph nourished his father and his brethren, and all his father’s house,—with bread, according to the need of their little ones.
texts.gen.47.13: But, bread, was there none in all the land,—for the famine was, very severe,—so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine,
texts.gen.47.14: So Joseph gathered up all the silver that was found in the land of Egypt. and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which, they, were buying,—and Joseph brought the silver into the house of Pharaoh.
texts.gen.47.15: And the silver was spent out of the land of Egypt and out of the land of Canaan, so all the Egyptians came in unto Joseph, saying—Do give us bread, for why should we die before thee, although, silver, hath failed?
texts.gen.47.16: Then said Joseph: Give your cattle, and I will give you for your cattle,—if silver hath failed.
texts.gen.47.17: So they brought in their cattle unto Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses and for the cattle of the flock and for the cattle of the herd, and for the asses,—and he provided them with bread for all their cattle, throughout that year.
texts.gen.47.18: When that year was ended, then came they unto him in the second year and said to him—We will not hide from my lord, how that the silver and the herds of beasts for my lord are come to an end,—there is nothing left before my lord, save only our bodies and our ground:
texts.gen.47.19: Wherefore should we die before thine eyes both we, and our ground? Buy thou us and our ground, for bread,—and we and our ground will become servants to Pharaoh, and give seed, that we may live, and not die, and the ground, not lie waste.
texts.gen.47.20: So Joseph bought all the ground of the Egyptians for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine had laid fast hold upon them,—so the land became Pharaoh’s.
texts.gen.47.21: And as for the people, he brought them into bondage as servants,—from one end of the boundary of Egypt unto the other end thereof.
texts.gen.47.22: Only, the ground of the priests, bought he not,—for the priests had a statutory-portion, from Pharaoh and they had been eating their statutory-portion, which Pharaoh had given them, for which cause, they had not sold their ground.
texts.gen.47.23: And Joseph said unto the people, Lo! I have bought you this day, and your ground for Pharaoh,—see, here is seed for you, so shall ye sow the ground;
texts.gen.47.24: and it shall come to pass that, of the yield, ye shall give a fifth to Pharaoh,—but the four parts, shall be your own—for seed for the field, and for your food and for them who are in your households and for food for your little ones.
texts.gen.47.25: And they said—Thou hast saved our lives! let us find favour in the eyes of my lord, so will we become Pharaoh’s servants.
texts.gen.47.26: And Joseph appointed it for a statute—until this day, regarding the ground of Egypt, that Pharaoh, should take a fifth,—only, the ground of the priests, was, theirs alone, it had not become Pharaoh’s.
texts.gen.47.27: Thus Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt in the land of Goshen,—and gained possessions therein, and became fruitful and multiplied exceedingly.
texts.gen.47.28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years,—so it came to pass that the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years.
texts.gen.47.29: And the days of Israel drew near that he must die, so he called for his son for Joseph and said to him—If, I pray thee I have found favour in thine eyes, place, I pray thee thy hand under my thigh,—so shalt thou deal with me in lovingkindness and faithfulness—Do not I pray thee, bury me in Egypt.
texts.gen.47.30: When I shall lie down with my fathers, then shalt thou carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their buryingplace. And he said: I, will do according to thy word.
texts.gen.47.31: Then he said: Come, swear to me! And he sware to him. Then did Israel bow himself down on the head of the couch.
texts.gen.48.1: And it came to pass after these things, that one said to Joseph, Lo! thy father, is sick. So he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
texts.gen.48.2: And one told Jacob, and said—Lo! thy son Joseph, coming in unto thee. So Israel strengthened himself, and sat up on the couch.
texts.gen.48.3: Then said Jacob unto Joseph, GOD Almighty, appeared unto me in Luz in the land of Canaan,—and blessed me;
texts.gen.48.4: and said unto me—Behold me! about to make thee fruitful, so will I multiply thee, and give thee to become a multitude of peoples,—so will I give this land to thy seed after thee, as an age-abiding possession.
texts.gen.48.5: Now, therefore thy two sons who were born to thee in the land of Egypt, before I came in unto thee in Egypt, are mine! Ephraim and Manasseh, like Reuben and Simeon, shall be mine!
texts.gen.48.6: But thine offspring which thou hast begotten after them, thine own shall they be,—after the name of their brethren, shall they be called in their inheritance.
texts.gen.48.7: But, as for me, when I came in from Padan, Rachel died by me, in the land of Canaan, in the way, while yet there was a stretch of country to come into Ephrath,—so I buried her there in the way to Ephrath, the same, is Bethlehem.
texts.gen.48.8: Then Israel saw Joseph’s sons,—and said—Who are these?
texts.gen.48.9: And Joseph said unto his father, My sons, they are, whom God hath given me, in this place. And he said—Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, that I may bless them.
texts.gen.48.10: Now, the eyes of Israel, had become dim from old age,—he could not see,—so he drew them near unto him, and kissed them, and embraced them.
texts.gen.48.11: And Israel said unto Joseph, To see thine own face, had I not thought,—and lo! God hath caused me to see even thy seed!
texts.gen.48.12: And Joseph brought them out from beside his knees, and bowed himself down with his face towards the earth.
texts.gen.48.13: And Joseph took them both,—Ephraim in his right hand on Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand, on Israel’s right hand, and drew them near unto him.
texts.gen.48.14: Then Israel put forth his right hand and laid it upon the head of Ephraim, though, he, was the younger, and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh,—crossing his hands, although, Manasseh, was the first-born.
texts.gen.48.15: Thus blessed he Joseph, and said,—God himself—before whom walked my fathers. Abraham and Isaac, God himself—who hath been my shepherd, since I came into being until this day;—
texts.gen.48.16: The Messenger—who hath been my redeemer from all evil—bless the lads! And may there be called upon them, my name, and the name of my fathers. Abraham and Isaac; And may they swarm into a multitude, in the midst of the earth!
texts.gen.48.17: And Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim and it was displeasing in his eyes,—so he took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from off the head of Ephraim, on to the head of Manasseh.
texts.gen.48.18: And Joseph said unto his father—Not so, my father! for, this, is the firstborn, lay thy right hand upon his head.
texts.gen.48.19: And his father refused, and said—I know—my son, I know! He also, shall become a people, and he also, shall become great,—but nevertheless, his younger brother, shall become greater than he, and his seed, shall become a filling up of the nations.
texts.gen.48.20: And he blessed them on that day, saying—In thee, let Israel bless himself saying, God set thee as Ephraim, and as Manasseh! So he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
texts.gen.48.21: And Israel said unto Joseph: Lo! I, am about to die,—but it shall come to pass that, God will be with you, and will take you back into the land of your fathers.
texts.gen.48.22: But, I, have given to thee one mountain-track above thy brethren,—which I took out of the hand of the Amorite, with my sword and with my bow.
texts.gen.49.1: Then called Jacob unto his sons,—and said—Gather yourselves together, and let me tell you, that which shall befall you in the afterpart of the days.
texts.gen.49.2: Assemble yourselves and hear ye sons of Jacob,—And hearken unto Israel your father!
texts.gen.49.3: Reuben, my first-born, thou, My vigour, and the first-fruit of my strength,—Pre-eminence of elevation and pre-eminence of power:
texts.gen.49.4: Boiling over like water, thou mayest not have pre-eminence, Because thou didst mount the bed of thy father,—Then, wast thou profane—My marriage-bed, he mounted!
texts.gen.49.5: Simeon and Levi, are brethren,—Instruments of violence, are their agreements:
texts.gen.49.6: Into their circle, do not thou enter my soul! In their convocation, do not thou join mine honour! For in their anger, they slew brave men, And in their wantonness, they ham-strung oxen.
texts.gen.49.7: Accursed, be their anger, because fierce, And their wrath because cruel,—I divide them in Jacob, And I disperse them in Israel.
texts.gen.49.8: Judah, as for thee, thy brethren shall praise thee when thy hand is on the neck of thy foes,—The sons of thy father, shall bow them-selves down to thee:
texts.gen.49.9: A lion’s whelp, is Judah, From the prey, my son hast thou come up! He hath stooped—hath crouched As a lion—or as a lioness, Who shall rouse him?
texts.gen.49.10: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, Nor the commander’s staff from between his feet,—Until that he come in as a Shiloh, And, his, be the obedience of the peoples:
texts.gen.49.11: Binding, to the vine, his ass, And to the choice vine his ass’s colt, He hath washed in wine his raiment, And in the blood of grapes, his mantle:
texts.gen.49.12: Darker—his eyes, than wine,—Whiter—his teeth than milk!
texts.gen.49.13: Zebulon, by a haven of seas, shall he settle down,—Even he, by a haven of ships, With his utmost part upon Zidon.
texts.gen.49.14: Issachar, an ass of strength,—couching between the pens;
texts.gen.49.15: Then beholdeth he rest, that it is good, And the ground that it is pleasant,—So he bendeth his shoulder to bear, And becometh a tributary servant.
texts.gen.49.16: Dan, shall vindicate his people,—as one of the tribes of Israel;
texts.gen.49.17: It cometh to pass that, Dan, is a serpent upon the way, A horned viper, upon the path,—That biteth the heels of the horse, And his rider falleth backwards:—
texts.gen.49.18: For thy salvation, have I waited O Yahweh!
texts.gen.49.19: Gad! a troop shall troop on him,—But, he, shall troop on the rear.
texts.gen.49.20: Out of Asher, fatness, is his food,—So, he, setteth forth dainties for a king.
texts.gen.49.21: Naphtali, is a slender hind,—That putteth forth antlers of beauty.
texts.gen.49.22: A fruitful bough, is Joseph, A fruitful bough over a fountain,—Branches creeping over a wall.
texts.gen.49.23: So they attack him and have shot,—So they enclose him, do the masters of arrows.
texts.gen.49.24: But abideth, as an enduring one, his bow, And supple are the arms of his hands,—From the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, From thence, is the Shepherd the Stone of Israel:
texts.gen.49.25: From the GOD of thy father who doth help thee And GOD Almighty who doth bless thee, Blessings of the heavens, above, Blessings of the abyss, couching beneath,—Blessings of breasts and womb:
texts.gen.49.26: The blessings of thy father, have prevailed, Over the blessings of the perpetual mountains, The charm of the age-abiding hills,—They turn out to be, for the head of Joseph, And for the crown of the head of him who was set apart from his brethren.
texts.gen.49.27: Benjamin a wolf that teareth in pieces, In the morning, he eateth prey, And at eventide, he divideth spoil.
texts.gen.49.28: All these, are the twelve tribes of Israel,—And this, is that which their father spake to them when he blessed them, Each man severally according to the blessing wherewith he blessed them.
texts.gen.49.29: Then commanded he them and said unto them—I, am about to be gathered unto my people, Bury me among my fathers,—within the cave, that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite:
texts.gen.49.30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah which is over against Mamre, in the land of Canaan,—which Abraham bought, along with the field, from Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a buryingplace:—
texts.gen.49.31: There, buried they Abraham, and Sarah his wife, There, buried they Isaac, and Rebekah his wife,—And there, buried I Leah:—
texts.gen.49.32: buying the field and the cave that is therein, from the sons of Heth.
texts.gen.49.33: So Jacob made an end of commanding his sons, and gathered up his feet into the couch,—and ceased to breathe and was gathered unto his people.
texts.gen.50.1: And Joseph fell upon the face of his father, and wept upon him and kissed him.
texts.gen.50.2: Then Joseph commanded his servants the physicians, to embalm his father,—so the physicians embalmed Israel.
texts.gen.50.3: And they fulfilled for him forty days, for so, are they wont to fulfil the days of the embalmed,—and the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.
texts.gen.50.4: And, when the days of weeping for him were passed, Joseph spake unto the house of Pharaoh saying,—If I pray you, I have found favour in your eyes, speak ye I pray you in the ears of Pharaoh saying:
texts.gen.50.5: My father, made me swear saying,—Lo! I, am about to die,—in my grave which I digged for myself in the land of Canaan, there, shalt thou bury me. Now, therefore, let me go up, I pray thee and bury my father, and return.
texts.gen.50.6: And Pharaoh said,—Go up., and bury thy father according as he made thee swear.
texts.gen.50.7: So Joseph went up. to bury his father,—and there went up with him all the servants of Pharaoh the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt;
texts.gen.50.8: and all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and the house of his father,—only their little ones and their flocks and their herds, left they. in the land of Goshen.
texts.gen.50.9: And there went up with him, both chariots and horsemen,—so it came to pass that, the company, was exceeding great,
texts.gen.50.10: And they came in, as far as the threshing-floor of the Buckthorn, which is beyond the Jordan, then wailed they there—an exceeding great and grievous wailing,—and he made for his father a mourning, of seven days.
texts.gen.50.11: And when the dwellers in the land—the Canaanites—saw the mourning in the threshing-floor of the Buckthorn, they said,—A grievous mourning, this! for the Egyptians. For this cause, was the name thereof called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
texts.gen.50.12: And his sons did for him thus as he had commanded them;
texts.gen.50.13: so his sons carried him to the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah,—which Abraham bought—with the field—for a possession of a buryingplace from Ephron the Hittite over against Mamre.
texts.gen.50.14: Then Joseph returned to Egypt he and his brethren and all who had been up with him to bury his father,—after he had buried his father.
texts.gen.50.15: Now when the brethren of Joseph saw that their father was dead, they said—Oh! if Joseph should lie in wait for us,—and should return, to us, all the evil wherewith we requited him!
texts.gen.50.16: So they sent in charge unto Joseph saying,—Thy father, gave command before he died saying:
texts.gen.50.17: Thus, shall ye say to Joseph—Ah now! do forgive we pray thee the transgression of thy brethren and their sin in that with evil, they requited thee. Now, therefore grant forgiveness we pray thee, for the transgression of the servants of the God of thy father! And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.
texts.gen.50.18: Then went his brethren also, and fell down before him,—and said, Behold us! thine for servants.
texts.gen.50.19: And Joseph said unto them—Do not fear,—although in place of God, I am.
texts.gen.50.20: Ye, indeed, planned against me, evil,—God, planned it, for good, for the sake of doing, as at this day, to save alive much people.
texts.gen.50.21: Now, therefore do not fear! I will nourish you and your little ones. Thus he consoled them, and spake unto their heart.
texts.gen.50.22: And Joseph abode in Egypt, he, and his father’s house,—and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
texts.gen.50.23: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s, sons of three generations—moreover the sons of Machir, son of Manasseh, were born upon Joseph’s knees.
texts.gen.50.24: Then said Joseph unto his brethren, I, am about to die,—but God will surely concern, himself for you, so will he take you up out of this land, into the land which he sware to Abraham to Isaac and to Jacob.
texts.gen.50.25: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear saying,—God will, surely concern, himself for you, So shall ye carry up my bones, from hence.
texts.gen.50.26: So Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old,—and they embalmed him, and put him in a coffin in Egypt.

texts.gen.1.1: En el principio, Dios creó los cielos y la tierra.
texts.gen.1.2: La tierra estaba sin forma y vacía. Las tinieblas cubrían la superficie del abismo y el Espíritu de Dios se cernía sobre la superficie de las aguas.
texts.gen.1.3: Dios dijo: «Hágase la luz», y la luz se hizo.
texts.gen.1.4: Dios vio que la luz era buena y separó Dios la luz de las tinieblas.
texts.gen.1.5: Dios llamó a la luz «día», y a las tinieblas las llamó «noche». Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: el primer día.
texts.gen.1.6: Dios dijo: «Haya un firmamento en medio de las aguas, y que separe las aguas de las aguas».
texts.gen.1.7: Dios hizo el firmamento y separó las aguas que estaban debajo del firmamento de las aguas que estaban por encima del firmamento; y así fue.
texts.gen.1.8: Dios llamó al firmamento «cielo». Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: el segundo día.
texts.gen.1.9: Dios dijo: «Que las aguas que están bajo el cielo se reúnan en un solo lugar, y que aparezca lo seco»; y así fue.
texts.gen.1.10: Dios llamó a lo seco «tierra», y a la reunión de las aguas la llamó «mares». Y vio Dios que era bueno.
texts.gen.1.11: Dijo Dios: «Produzca la tierra hierba verde, plantas que den semilla y árboles frutales que den fruto según su especie, cuya semilla esté en ellos, sobre la tierra»; y así fue.
texts.gen.1.12: La tierra produjo hierba verde, plantas que dan semilla según su especie, y árboles que dan fruto, cuya semilla está en ellos, según su especie; y vio Dios que era bueno.
texts.gen.1.13: Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: el tercer día.
texts.gen.1.14: Dios dijo: «Haya lumbreras en el firmamento del cielo para separar el día de la noche; y sirvan de señales para las estaciones, para los días y los años;
texts.gen.1.15: y sean por lumbreras en el firmamento del cielo para alumbrar sobre la tierra»; y así fue.
texts.gen.1.16: Dios hizo las dos grandes lumbreras: la lumbrera mayor para que dominase en el día, y la lumbrera menor para que dominase en la noche. Hizo también las estrellas.
texts.gen.1.17: Dios las puso en el firmamento del cielo para alumbrar sobre la tierra,
texts.gen.1.18: y para dominar en el día y en la noche, y para separar la luz de las tinieblas. Y vio Dios que era bueno.
texts.gen.1.19: Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: el cuarto día.
texts.gen.1.20: Dios dijo: «Produzcan las aguas seres vivientes en abundancia, y vuelen las aves sobre la tierra en el ancho firmamento del cielo».
texts.gen.1.21: Dios creó los grandes monstruos marinos y todo ser viviente que se mueve, que las aguas produjeron según su especie, y toda ave alada según su especie. Y vio Dios que era bueno.
texts.gen.1.22: Dios los bendijo, diciendo: «Sed fecundos y multiplicaos, y llenad las aguas de los mares, y multiplíquense las aves en la tierra».
texts.gen.1.23: Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: el quinto día.
texts.gen.1.24: Dios dijo: «Produzca la tierra seres vivientes según su especie: ganado, reptiles y animales de la tierra según su especie»; y así fue.
texts.gen.1.25: Dios hizo los animales de la tierra según su especie, el ganado según su especie y todo lo que se arrastra sobre la tierra según su especie. Y vio Dios que era bueno.
texts.gen.1.26: Dios dijo: «Hagamos al hombre a nuestra imagen, conforme a nuestra semejanza; y tenga dominio sobre los peces del mar, sobre las aves del cielo, sobre el ganado, sobre toda la tierra y sobre todo reptil que se arrastra sobre la tierra».
texts.gen.1.27: Dios creó al hombre a su imagen, a imagen de Dios lo creó; varón y mujer los creó.
texts.gen.1.28: Dios los bendijo y les dijo: «Sed fecundos y multiplicaos; llenad la tierra y sometedla; dominad sobre los peces del mar, sobre las aves del cielo y sobre todo ser viviente que se mueve sobre la tierra».
texts.gen.1.29: Dios dijo: “Mirad, os he dado toda planta que da semilla, que está sobre la superficie de toda la tierra, y todo árbol en el que hay fruto que da semilla. Os servirán de alimento.
texts.gen.1.30: Y a toda bestia de la tierra, a toda ave de los cielos y a todo lo que se arrastra sobre la tierra, en que hay vida, toda hierba verde les servirá de alimento”; y así fue.
texts.gen.1.31: Dios vio todo lo que había hecho, y he aquí que era muy bueno. Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana: el sexto día.
texts.gen.2.1: Así fueron terminados los cielos y la tierra y todo su ornato.
texts.gen.2.2: Y acabó Dios en el séptimo día la obra que hizo; y descansó el día séptimo de toda la obra que había realizado.
texts.gen.2.3: Y bendijo Dios el día séptimo y lo santificó, porque en él descansó de toda la obra que había creado y hecho.
texts.gen.2.4: Éstos son los orígenes de los cielos y de la tierra cuando fueron creados, el día en que Yahvé Dios hizo la tierra y los cielos.
texts.gen.2.5: Y toda planta del campo antes que fuese en la tierra, y toda hierba del campo antes que germinase; porque Yahvé Dios aún no había hecho llover sobre la tierra, ni había hombre para que labrase el suelo,
texts.gen.2.6: sino que subía de la tierra un vapor que regaba toda la faz de la tierra.
texts.gen.2.7: Formó, pues, Yahvé Dios al hombre del polvo de la tierra, y sopló en su nariz aliento de vida, y fue el hombre un ser viviente.
texts.gen.2.8: Y Yahvé Dios plantó un huerto en Edén, al oriente; y puso allí al hombre que había formado.
texts.gen.2.9: Y Yahvé Dios hizo nacer de la tierra todo árbol delicioso a la vista y bueno para comer; también el árbol de la vida en medio del huerto, y el árbol del conocimiento del bien y del mal.
texts.gen.2.10: Y salía de Edén un río para regar el huerto, y de allí se repartía en cuatro brazos.
texts.gen.2.11: El nombre del uno era Pisón; éste es el que rodea toda la tierra de Havila, donde hay oro;
texts.gen.2.12: y el oro de aquella tierra es bueno; hay allí también bedelio y ónice.
texts.gen.2.13: El nombre del segundo río es Gihón; éste es el que rodea toda la tierra de Cus.
texts.gen.2.14: Y el nombre del tercer río es Hidekel; éste es el que va al oriente de Asiria. Y el cuarto río es el Éufrates.
texts.gen.2.15: Tomó, pues, Yahvé Dios al hombre y lo puso en el huerto de Edén, para que lo labrase y lo guardase.
texts.gen.2.16: Y mandó Yahvé Dios al hombre, diciendo: «De todo árbol del huerto podrás comer;
texts.gen.2.17: mas del árbol del conocimiento del bien y del mal no comerás; porque el día que de él comas, ciertamente morirás».
texts.gen.2.18: Y dijo Yahvé Dios: «No es bueno que el hombre esté solo; le haré ayuda idónea para él».
texts.gen.2.19: Yahvé Dios formó, pues, de la tierra toda bestia del campo y toda ave de los cielos, y las trajo a Adán para que viese cómo las había de llamar; y lo que Adán llamó a los animales vivientes, ése es su nombre.
texts.gen.2.20: Y puso Adán nombres a toda bestia y ave de los cielos y a todo ganado del campo; mas para Adán no se halló ayuda idónea para él.
texts.gen.2.21: Entonces Yahvé Dios hizo caer sueño profundo sobre Adán, y mientras éste dormía, tomó una de sus costillas y cerró la carne en su lugar.
texts.gen.2.22: Y de la costilla que Yahvé Dios tomó del hombre, hizo una mujer, y la trajo al hombre.
texts.gen.2.23: Dijo entonces Adán: «Ésta es ahora hueso de mis huesos y carne de mi carne; ésta será llamada Varona, porque del varón fue tomada».
texts.gen.2.24: Por tanto, dejará el hombre a su padre y a su madre, y se unirá a su mujer, y serán una sola carne.
texts.gen.2.25: Y estaban ambos desnudos, Adán y su mujer, y no se avergonzaban.
texts.gen.3.1: Pero la serpiente era astuta, más que todos los animales del campo que Yahvé Dios había hecho; la cual dijo a la mujer: “¿Conque Dios os ha dicho: ‘No comáis de todo árbol del huerto’?”
texts.gen.3.2: Y la mujer respondió a la serpiente: “Del fruto de los árboles del huerto podemos comer;
texts.gen.3.3: pero del fruto del árbol que está en medio del huerto dijo Dios: ‘No comeréis de él, ni lo tocaréis, para que no muráis’”.
texts.gen.3.4: Entonces la serpiente dijo a la mujer: «No moriréis;
texts.gen.3.5: sino que sabe Dios que el día que comáis de él, serán abiertos vuestros ojos, y seréis como Dios, conociendo el bien y el mal».
texts.gen.3.6: Y vio la mujer que el árbol era bueno para comer, y que era agradable a los ojos, y árbol codiciable para alcanzar la sabiduría; y tomó de su fruto y comió; y dio también a su marido, el cual comió así como ella.
texts.gen.3.7: Entonces fueron abiertos los ojos de ambos, y conocieron que estaban desnudos; entonces cosieron hojas de higuera y se hicieron delantales.
texts.gen.3.8: Y oyeron la voz de Yahvé Dios que se paseaba en el huerto, al aire del día; y el hombre y su mujer se escondieron de la presencia de Yahvé Dios entre los árboles del huerto.
texts.gen.3.9: Mas Yahvé Dios llamó al hombre, y le dijo: «¿Dónde estás tú?»
texts.gen.3.10: Y él respondió: «Oí tu voz en el huerto, y tuve miedo, porque estaba desnudo; y me escondí».
texts.gen.3.11: Y Dios le dijo: «¿Quién te enseñó que estabas desnudo? ¿Has comido del árbol de que yo te mandé no comieses?»
texts.gen.3.12: Y el hombre respondió: «La mujer que me diste por compañera me dio del árbol, y yo comí».
texts.gen.3.13: Entonces Yahvé Dios dijo a la mujer: «¿Qué es lo que has hecho?» Y dijo la mujer: «La serpiente me engañó, y comí».
texts.gen.3.14: Y Yahvé Dios dijo a la serpiente: «Por cuanto esto hiciste, maldita serás entre todas las bestias y entre todos los animales del campo; sobre tu pecho andarás, y polvo comerás todos los días de tu vida.
texts.gen.3.15: Y pondré enemistad entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu simiente y la simiente suya; ésta te herirá en la cabeza, y tú le herirás en el calcañar».
texts.gen.3.16: A la mujer dijo: «Multiplicaré en gran manera tus dolores en tus preñeces; con dolor darás a luz los hijos; y tu deseo será para tu marido, y él se enseñoreará de ti».
texts.gen.3.17: Y al hombre dijo: “Por cuanto obedeciste a la voz de tu mujer, y comiste del árbol de que te mandé diciendo: ‘No comerás de él’; maldita será la tierra por tu causa; con dolor comerás de ella todos los días de tu vida.
texts.gen.3.18: Espinos y cardos te producirá, y comerás hierba del campo.
texts.gen.3.19: Con el sudor de tu rostro comerás el pan hasta que vuelvas a la tierra, porque de ella fuiste tomado; pues polvo eres, y al polvo volverás”.
texts.gen.3.20: Y llamó Adán el nombre de su mujer, Eva, por cuanto ella era madre de todos los vivientes.
texts.gen.3.21: Y Yahvé Dios hizo al hombre y a su mujer túnicas de pieles, y los vistió.
texts.gen.3.22: Y dijo Yahvé Dios: «He aquí el hombre es como uno de nosotros, sabiendo el bien y el mal; ahora, pues, que no alargue su mano, y tome también del árbol de la vida, y coma, y viva para siempre».
texts.gen.3.23: Y lo sacó Yahvé Dios del huerto de Edén, para que labrase la tierra de que fue tomado.
texts.gen.3.24: Echó, pues, fuera al hombre, y puso al oriente del huerto de Edén querubines y una espada encendida que se revolvía a todas partes, para guardar el camino del árbol de la vida.
texts.gen.4.1: Conoció Adán a su mujer Eva, la cual concibió y dio a luz a Caín, y dijo: «He alcanzado varón de parte de Yahvé».
texts.gen.4.2: Después dio a luz a su hermano Abel. Y Abel fue pastor de ovejas, y Caín fue labrador de la tierra.
texts.gen.4.3: Y aconteció andando el tiempo, que Caín trajo del fruto de la tierra una ofrenda a Yahvé.
texts.gen.4.4: Y Abel trajo también de los primogénitos de sus ovejas, de lo más gordo de ellas. Y miró Yahvé con agrado a Abel y a su ofrenda;
texts.gen.4.5: pero no miró con agrado a Caín y a la ofrenda suya. Y se ensañó Caín en gran manera, y decayó su semblante.
texts.gen.4.6: Entonces Yahvé dijo a Caín: «¿Por qué te has ensañado, y por qué ha decaído tu semblante?
texts.gen.4.7: Si bien hicieres, ¿no serás enaltecido? y si no hicieres bien, el pecado está a la puerta; con todo esto, a ti será su deseo, y tú te enseñorearás de él».
texts.gen.4.8: Y dijo Caín a su hermano Abel: «Salgamos al campo». Y aconteció que estando ellos en el campo, Caín se levantó contra su hermano Abel, y lo mató.
texts.gen.4.9: Y Yahvé dijo a Caín: «¿Dónde está Abel tu hermano?» Y él respondió: «No sé. ¿Soy yo acaso guarda de mi hermano?»
texts.gen.4.10: Y él le dijo: «¿Qué has hecho? La voz de la sangre de tu hermano clama a mí desde la tierra.
texts.gen.4.11: Ahora, pues, maldito seas tú de la tierra, que abrió su boca para recibir de tu mano la sangre de tu hermano.
texts.gen.4.12: Cuando labres la tierra, no te volverá a dar su fuerza; errante y extranjero serás en la tierra».
texts.gen.4.13: Y dijo Caín a Yahvé: «Grande es mi castigo para ser soportado.
texts.gen.4.14: He aquí me echas hoy de la faz de la tierra, y de tu presencia me esconderé, y seré errante y extranjero en la tierra; y sucederá que cualquiera que me hallare, me matará».
texts.gen.4.15: Y le respondió Yahvé: «Ciertamente cualquiera que matare a Caín, siete veces será castigado». Entonces Yahvé puso señal en Caín, para que no lo matase cualquiera que le hallara.
texts.gen.4.16: Salió, pues, Caín de delante de Yahvé, y habitó en tierra de Nod, al oriente de Edén.
texts.gen.4.17: Y conoció Caín a su mujer, la cual concibió y dio a luz a Enoc; y edificó una ciudad, y llamó el nombre de la ciudad del nombre de su hijo, Enoc.
texts.gen.4.18: Y a Enoc nació Irad, e Irad engendró a Mehujael, y Mehujael engendró a Matusael, y Matusael engendró a Lamec.
texts.gen.4.19: Y tomó Lamec para sí dos mujeres; el nombre de la una fue Ada, y el nombre de la otra, Zila.
texts.gen.4.20: Y Ada dio a luz a Jabal, el cual fue padre de los que habitan en tiendas y crían ganados.
texts.gen.4.21: Y el nombre de su hermano fue Jubal, el cual fue padre de todos los que tocan arpa y flauta.
texts.gen.4.22: Y Zila también dio a luz a Tubal Caín, artífice de toda obra de bronce y de hierro; y la hermana de Tubal Caín fue Naama.
texts.gen.4.23: Y dijo Lamec a sus mujeres: «Ada y Zila, oíd mi voz; mujeres de Lamec, escuchad mi dicho: que un varón maté por mi herida, y un joven por mi golpe.
texts.gen.4.24: Si siete veces será vengado Caín, Lamec en verdad setenta veces siete lo será».
texts.gen.4.25: Y conoció de nuevo Adán a su mujer, la cual dio a luz un hijo, y llamó su nombre Set: «Porque Dios —dijo ella— me ha sustituido otra simiente en lugar de Abel, a quien mató Caín».
texts.gen.4.26: Y a Set también le nació un hijo, y llamó su nombre Enós. Entonces los hombres comenzaron a invocar el nombre de Yahvé.
texts.gen.5.1: Éste es el libro de las generaciones de Adán. El día en que creó Dios al hombre, a la semejanza de Dios lo hizo.
texts.gen.5.2: Varón y mujer los creó; y los bendijo, y llamó el nombre de ellos Adán, el día en que fueron creados.
texts.gen.5.3: Y vivió Adán ciento treinta años, y engendró un hijo a su semejanza, conforme a su imagen, y llamó su nombre Set.
texts.gen.5.4: Y fueron los días de Adán después que engendró a Set, ochocientos años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.5: Y fueron todos los días que vivió Adán novecientos treinta años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.6: Vivió Set ciento cinco años, y engendró a Enós.
texts.gen.5.7: Y vivió Set, después que engendró a Enós, ochocientos siete años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.8: Y fueron todos los días de Set novecientos doce años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.9: Vivió Enós noventa años, y engendró a Cainán.
texts.gen.5.10: Y vivió Enós, después que engendró a Cainán, ochocientos quince años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.11: Y fueron todos los días de Enós novecientos cinco años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.12: Vivió Cainán setenta años, y engendró a Mahalaleel.
texts.gen.5.13: Y vivió Cainán, después que engendró a Mahalaleel, ochocientos cuarenta años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.14: Y fueron todos los días de Cainán novecientos diez años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.15: Vivió Mahalaleel sesenta y cinco años, y engendró a Jared.
texts.gen.5.16: Y vivió Mahalaleel, después que engendró a Jared, ochocientos treinta años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.17: Y fueron todos los días de Mahalaleel ochocientos noventa y cinco años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.18: Vivió Jared ciento sesenta y dos años, y engendró a Enoc.
texts.gen.5.19: Y vivió Jared, después que engendró a Enoc, ochocientos años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.20: Y fueron todos los días de Jared novecientos sesenta y dos años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.21: Vivió Enoc sesenta y cinco años, y engendró a Matusalén.
texts.gen.5.22: Y caminó Enoc con Dios, después que engendró a Matusalén, trescientos años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.23: Y fueron todos los días de Enoc trescientos sesenta y cinco años.
texts.gen.5.24: Caminó, pues, Enoc con Dios, y desapareció, porque le llevó Dios.
texts.gen.5.25: Vivió Matusalén ciento ochenta y siete años, y engendró a Lamec.
texts.gen.5.26: Y vivió Matusalén, después que engendró a Lamec, setecientos ochenta y dos años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.27: Fueron, pues, todos los días de Matusalén novecientos sesenta y nueve años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.28: Vivió Lamec ciento ochenta y dos años, y engendró un hijo;
texts.gen.5.29: y llamó su nombre Noé, diciendo: «Éste nos aliviará de nuestras obras y del trabajo de nuestras manos, a causa de la tierra que Yahvé maldijo».
texts.gen.5.30: Y vivió Lamec, después que engendró a Noé, quinientos noventa y cinco años, y engendró hijos e hijas.
texts.gen.5.31: Y fueron todos los días de Lamec setecientos setenta y siete años; y murió.
texts.gen.5.32: Y siendo Noé de quinientos años, engendró a Sem, a Cam y a Jafet.
texts.gen.6.1: Aconteció que cuando comenzaron los hombres a multiplicarse sobre la faz de la tierra, y les nacieron hijas,
texts.gen.6.2: viendo los hijos de Dios que las hijas de los hombres eran hermosas, tomaron para sí mujeres, escogiendo entre todas.
texts.gen.6.3: Y dijo Yahvé: «No contenderá mi espíritu con el hombre para siempre, porque ciertamente él es carne; mas serán sus días ciento veinte años».
texts.gen.6.4: Había Nefilim en la tierra en aquellos días, y también después que se llegaron los hijos de Dios a las hijas de los hombres, y les engendraron hijos. Éstos fueron los valientes que desde la antigüedad fueron varones de renombre.
texts.gen.6.5: Y vio Yahvé que la maldad de los hombres era mucha en la tierra, y que todo designio de los pensamientos del corazón de ellos era de continuo solamente el mal.
texts.gen.6.6: Y se arrepintió Yahvé de haber hecho hombre en la tierra, y le dolió en su corazón.
texts.gen.6.7: Y dijo Yahvé: «Raeré de sobre la faz de la tierra a los hombres que he creado, desde el hombre hasta la bestia, y hasta el reptil y las aves del cielo; pues me arrepiento de haberlos hecho».
texts.gen.6.8: Pero Noé halló gracia ante los ojos de Yahvé.
texts.gen.6.9: Éstas son las generaciones de Noé: Noé, varón justo, era perfecto en sus generaciones; con Dios caminó Noé.
texts.gen.6.10: Y engendró Noé tres hijos: a Sem, a Cam y a Jafet.
texts.gen.6.11: Y se corrompió la tierra delante de Dios, y estaba la tierra llena de violencia.
texts.gen.6.12: Y miró Dios la tierra, y he aquí que estaba corrompida; porque toda carne había corrompido su camino sobre la tierra.
texts.gen.6.13: Dijo, pues, Dios a Noé: «He decidido el fin de todo ser, porque la tierra está llena de violencia a causa de ellos; y he aquí que yo los destruiré con la tierra.
texts.gen.6.14: Hazte un arca de madera de gofer; harás aposentos en el arca, y la calafatearás con brea por dentro y por fuera.
texts.gen.6.15: Y de esta manera la harás: de trescientos codos la longitud del arca, de cincuenta codos su anchura, y de treinta codos su altura.
texts.gen.6.16: Una ventana harás al arca, y la acabarás a un codo de elevación por la parte de arriba; y pondrás la puerta del arca a su lado; y le harás piso bajo, segundo y tercero.
texts.gen.6.17: Y yo, he aquí que yo traigo un diluvio de aguas sobre la tierra, para destruir toda carne en que haya espíritu de vida debajo del cielo; todo lo que hay en la tierra morirá.
texts.gen.6.18: Mas estableceré mi pacto contigo, y entrarás en el arca tú, tus hijos, tu mujer, y las mujeres de tus hijos contigo.
texts.gen.6.19: Y de todo lo que vive, de toda carne, dos de cada especie meterás en el arca, para que tengan vida contigo; macho y hembra serán.
texts.gen.6.20: De las aves según su especie, y de las bestias según su especie, de todo reptil de la tierra según su especie, dos de cada especie entrarán contigo, para que tengan vida.
texts.gen.6.21: Y toma contigo de todo alimento que se come, y almacénalo, y servirá de sustento para ti y para ellos».
texts.gen.6.22: E hizo Noé conforme a todo lo que Dios le mandó; así lo hizo.
texts.gen.7.1: Dijo luego Yahvé a Noé: «Entrad tú y toda tu casa en el arca; porque a ti he visto justo delante de mí en esta generación.
texts.gen.7.2: De todo animal limpio tomad siete parejas, macho y su hembra; mas de los animales que no son limpios, una pareja, el macho y su hembra.
texts.gen.7.3: También de las aves de los cielos, siete parejas, macho y hembra, para conservar viva la especie sobre la faz de toda la tierra.
texts.gen.7.4: Porque pasados aún siete días, yo haré llover sobre la tierra cuarenta días y cuarenta noches; y raeré de sobre la faz de la tierra a todo ser viviente que hice».
texts.gen.7.5: E hizo Noé conforme a todo lo que le mandó Yahvé.
texts.gen.7.6: Era Noé de seiscientos años cuando el diluvio de las aguas vino sobre la tierra.
texts.gen.7.7: Y por causa de las aguas del diluvio entró Noé en el arca, y con él sus hijos, su mujer y las mujeres de sus hijos.
texts.gen.7.8: De los animales limpios, y de los animales que no eran limpios, y de las aves, y de todo lo que se arrastra sobre la tierra,
texts.gen.7.9: de dos en dos entraron con Noé en el arca, macho y hembra, como mandó Dios a Noé.
texts.gen.7.10: Y sucedió que al séptimo día las aguas del diluvio vinieron sobre la tierra.
texts.gen.7.11: El año seiscientos de la vida de Noé, en el mes segundo, a los diecisiete días del mes, aquel día fueron rotas todas las fuentes del grande abismo, y las cataratas de los cielos fueron abiertas,
texts.gen.7.12: y hubo lluvia sobre la tierra cuarenta días y cuarenta noches.
texts.gen.7.13: En aquel mismo día entraron Noé, y Sem, Cam y Jafet hijos de Noé, la mujer de Noé, y las tres mujeres de sus hijos con ellos, en el arca;
texts.gen.7.14: ellos, y todos los animales silvestres según su especie, y todo ganado según su especie, y todo reptil que se arrastra sobre la tierra según su especie, y toda ave según su especie, y todo pájaro de toda especie.
texts.gen.7.15: Vinieron, pues, con Noé al arca, de dos en dos de toda carne en que había espíritu de vida.
texts.gen.7.16: Y los que vinieron, macho y hembra de toda carne vinieron, como le había mandado Dios; y Yahvé le cerró la puerta.
texts.gen.7.17: Y fue el diluvio cuarenta días sobre la tierra; y las aguas crecieron, y alzaron el arca, y se elevó sobre la tierra.
texts.gen.7.18: Y prevalecieron las aguas y crecieron en gran manera sobre la tierra; y flotaba el arca sobre la superficie de las aguas.
texts.gen.7.19: Y las aguas subieron mucho en extremo sobre la tierra; y todos los montes altos que había debajo de todos los cielos fueron cubiertos.
texts.gen.7.20: Quince codos más alto subieron las aguas, después que los montes fueron cubiertos.
texts.gen.7.21: Y murió toda carne que se mueve sobre la tierra, así de aves como de ganados y de bestias, y de todo reptil que se arrastra sobre la tierra, y todo hombre.
texts.gen.7.22: Todo lo que tenía aliento de espíritu de vida en sus narices, todo lo que había en la tierra, murió.
texts.gen.7.23: Así fue raído todo ser que vivía sobre la faz de la tierra, desde el hombre hasta la bestia, los reptiles, y las aves del cielo; y fueron raídos de la tierra, y quedó solamente Noé, y los que con él estaban en el arca.
texts.gen.7.24: Y prevalecieron las aguas sobre la tierra ciento cincuenta días.
texts.gen.8.1: Y se acordó Dios de Noé, y de todos los animales, y de todo el ganado que estaba con él en el arca; e hizo pasar Dios un viento sobre la tierra, y disminuyeron las aguas.
texts.gen.8.2: Y se cerraron las fuentes del abismo y las cataratas de los cielos; y la lluvia de los cielos fue detenida.
texts.gen.8.3: Y las aguas decayeron de sobre la tierra yendo y volviendo; y decrecieron las aguas al cabo de ciento cincuenta días.
texts.gen.8.4: Y reposó el arca en el mes séptimo, a los diecisiete días del mes, sobre los montes de Ararat.
texts.gen.8.5: Y las aguas fueron decreciendo hasta el mes décimo; en el décimo, al primero del mes, se descubrieron las cimas de los montes.
texts.gen.8.6: Sucedió que al cabo de cuarenta días abrió Noé la ventana del arca que había hecho,
texts.gen.8.7: y envió un cuervo, el cual salió, y estuvo yendo y volviendo hasta que las aguas se secaron sobre la tierra.
texts.gen.8.8: Envió también de sí una paloma, para ver si las aguas se habían retirado de sobre la faz de la tierra.
texts.gen.8.9: Y no halló la paloma donde sentar la planta de su pie, y volvió a él al arca, porque las aguas estaban aún sobre la faz de toda la tierra. Entonces él extendió su mano, y tomándola, la introdujo consigo en el arca.
texts.gen.8.10: Esperó aún otros siete días, y volvió a enviar la paloma fuera del arca.
texts.gen.8.11: Y la paloma volvió a él a la hora de la tarde; y he aquí que traía una hoja de olivo verde en el pico; y entendió Noé que las aguas se habían retirado de sobre la tierra.
texts.gen.8.12: Y esperó aún otros siete días, y envió la paloma, la cual no volvió a él más.
texts.gen.8.13: Y sucedió que en el año seiscientos uno de Noé, en el mes primero, al primero del mes, las aguas se secaron sobre la tierra; y quitó Noé la cubierta del arca y miró, y he aquí que la faz de la tierra estaba seca.
texts.gen.8.14: Y en el mes segundo, a los veintisiete días del mes, se secó la tierra.
texts.gen.8.15: Entonces habló Dios a Noé, diciendo:
texts.gen.8.16: «Salid del arca tú, y vuestra mujer, y vuestros hijos, y las mujeres de vuestros hijos con vosotros.
texts.gen.8.17: Todos los animales que están con vosotros de toda carne, de aves y de bestias y de todo reptil que se arrastra sobre la tierra, sacadlos con vosotros; y vayan por la tierra, y fructifiquen y multiplíquense sobre la tierra».
texts.gen.8.18: Entonces salió Noé, y sus hijos, su mujer, y las mujeres de sus hijos con él.
texts.gen.8.19: Todos los animales, y todo reptil y toda ave, todo lo que se mueve sobre la tierra según sus especies, salieron del arca.
texts.gen.8.20: Y edificó Noé un altar a Yahvé, y tomó de todo animal limpio y de toda ave limpia, y ofreció holocausto en el altar.
texts.gen.8.21: Y percibió Yahvé olor grato; y dijo Yahvé en su corazón: «No volveré más a maldecir la tierra por causa del hombre; porque el intento del corazón del hombre es malo desde su juventud; ni volveré más a destruir todo ser viviente, como he hecho.
texts.gen.8.22: Mientras la tierra permanezca, no cesarán la sementera y la siega, el frío y el calor, el verano y el invierno, y el día y la noche».
texts.gen.9.1: Bendijo Dios a Noé y a sus hijos, y les dijo: «Fructificad y multiplicaos, y llenad la tierra.
texts.gen.9.2: Vuestro temor y vuestro pavor estarán sobre todo animal de la tierra, y sobre toda ave de los cielos, en todo lo que se mueva sobre la tierra, y en todos los peces del mar; en vuestras manos son entregados.
texts.gen.9.3: Todo lo que se mueve y vive os será para mantenimiento: así como las legumbres y hierbas verdes, os lo he dado todo.
texts.gen.9.4: Pero carne con su vida, que es su sangre, no comeréis.
texts.gen.9.5: Porque ciertamente demandaré la sangre de vuestras vidas; de mano de toda bestia la demandaré, y de mano del hombre; de mano del varón su hermano demandaré la vida del hombre.
texts.gen.9.6: El que derramare sangre de hombre, por el hombre su sangre será derramada; porque a imagen de Dios es hecho el hombre.
texts.gen.9.7: Mas vosotros fructificad y multiplicaos; procread abundantemente en la tierra, y multiplicaos en ella».
texts.gen.9.8: Y habló Dios a Noé y a sus hijos con él, diciendo:
texts.gen.9.9: «He aquí que yo establezco mi pacto con vosotros, y con vuestra simiente después de vosotros;
texts.gen.9.10: y con todo ser viviente que está con vosotros, de aves, de animales y de toda bestia de la tierra que está con vosotros, desde todos los que salieron del arca hasta todo animal de la tierra.
texts.gen.9.11: Estableceré mi pacto con vosotros, y no exterminaré ya más toda carne con aguas de diluvio, ni habrá más diluvio para destruir la tierra».
texts.gen.9.12: Y dijo Dios: «Ésta es la señal del pacto que yo establezco entre mí y vosotros y todo ser viviente que está con vosotros, por siglos perpetuos:
texts.gen.9.13: Mi arco he puesto en las nubes, el cual será por señal del pacto entre mí y la tierra.
texts.gen.9.14: Y sucederá que cuando haga venir nubes sobre la tierra, se dejará ver entonces mi arco en las nubes.
texts.gen.9.15: Y me acordaré del pacto mío, que hay entre mí y vosotros y todo ser viviente de toda carne; y no habrá más aguas de diluvio para destruir toda carne.
texts.gen.9.16: Estará el arco en las nubes, y verlo he para acordarme del pacto perpetuo entre Dios y todo ser viviente, con toda carne que hay sobre la tierra».
texts.gen.9.17: Dijo, pues, Dios a Noé: «Ésta es la señal del pacto que he establecido entre mí y toda carne que está sobre la tierra».
texts.gen.9.18: Y los hijos de Noé que salieron del arca fueron Sem, Cam y Jafet; y Cam es el padre de Canaán.
texts.gen.9.19: Éstos tres son los hijos de Noé, y de ellos se pobló toda la tierra.
texts.gen.9.20: Después comenzó Noé a labrar la tierra, y plantó una viña;
texts.gen.9.21: y bebió del vino, y se embriagó, y estaba descubierto en medio de su tienda.
